Outside the church, the trekker is walking around a normal urban Cairo street. At most points, you will still see the church complex, its spires with crosses, and historic sandstone walls. But you will also see apartment buildings, shops, and normal pedestrian traffic.
This trekker can be found just east of Giza, near the map label Fustat.

title: Egypt - Hanging Church Interior (Plonkit)
description: At a certain point, the trekker moves from the street into the Hanging Church. Inside, you will see a beautiful courtyard with religious mosaics and two white church spires.

title: Egypt - Qaitbay Citadel (Plonkit)
description: The Qaitbay Citadel consists of a large castle surrounded by thick walls, which are both made of sandstone.

title: Egypt - Saint Mina Monastery (Plonkit)
description: The monastery complex of Saint Mina consists of several large, palace-like buildings in a somewhat modern, Arabic style. Most of the buildings have several spires crowned with Christian crosses.

title: Egypt - Abu Mena Excavation Site (Plonkit)
description: The Abu Mena Heritage Site is a major excavation area southwest of Alexandria, just south of the Saint Mina monastery. In the middle of the site, you can find a small, yellow wooden chapel.

title: Eswatini - Green Hills & Grass (Plonkit)
description: Eswatini’s landscape is known for its green, wooded hills and tall golden grass.

title: Eswatini - Wooden Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles in Eswatini are made of dark brown wood and follow a simple design. The insulators are mostly mounted on the side.

title: Eswatini - MR Roads (Plonkit)
description: Roads starting with the letters “MR” are exclusive to Eswatini.

title: Eswatini - Southern African Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Eswatini typically uses yellow outside lines and occasionally, triple white middle lines.

title: Eswatini - White Car No Antenna (Plonkit)
description: All of Eswatini was covered by a white Google car without an antenna.

title: Eswatini - Green License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Licence plates in Eswatini are long and green at the bottom.

title: Eswatini - Concrete Bus Shelters (Plonkit)
description: Concrete bus shelters are a common sight on roads in Eswatini.

title: Eswatini - Montane Grasslands (Plonkit)
description: Montane grasslands with long golden grass and a mountainous landscape are typical of Western Eswatini.

title: Eswatini - Pine Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Pine tree plantations are found in select areas in the West of the country.

title: Eswatini - MR9 Green Region (Plonkit)
description: This distinct region in the central South of the country, mostly along the MR9, can be recognized by the dark, overwhelming greenness and tall wooded mountains.

title: Eswatini - Eastern Flatlands (Plonkit)
description: You can recognise this region in the east of the country thanks to the unusual flatness and the mountains often visible in the distance.

title: Eswatini - Sugar Cane Fields (Plonkit)
description: Sugar cane is grown in several areas along the Eastern border.

title: Eswatini - MR3 South Ngomane (Plonkit)
description: The MR3 South of Ngomane can be recognized thanks to flatness, long dry grass and the dirt on the camera.

title: Eswatini - MR3 Divided Highway (Plonkit)
description: The MR3 from Manzini to the South African border is divided by metal and stone guardrails, making it recognisable.

title: Eswatini - MR8 Ridge (Plonkit)
description: The MR8 in Southeastern Eswatini straddling the South African border is recognisable because of this distinct ridge to the east.

title: Eswatini - Mlawula Nature Reserve (Plonkit)
description: You can recognise the Mlawula Nature Reserve thanks to the narrow dirt tracks, tall grass and overall savannah landscape.

title: Eswatini - Lomahasha Portuguese (Plonkit)
description: If you see Portuguese text in Eswatini, you are most likely in the small town of Lomahasha.

title: Ghana - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: All regular road generation 3 coverage in Ghana was made with a unique Google car. It has a visible roof rack with a piece of black tape on the right end of the front bar. In addition, the hood of the car is usually visible, showing a street view car wrapping that features a red rectangle and some other recognizable elements. Normally, this unique car is all you need to identify Ghana.

title: Ghana - White Pickup Meta (Plonkit)
description: Generation 4 coverage in Ghana was taken using a grey or white pickup truck with an antenna in the front. The truck will be either fully or partially blurred most of the time.

title: Ghana - Ghana License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Ghana uses white plates on normal vehicles, and yellow plates for commercial vehicles. They can be long or short. Because commercial vehicles are really common, you will often see a mix of both plate colours.

title: Ghana - Red Soil Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Ghana is mostly flat with red soil, however hills and mountains can be seen in some regions. Tropical vegetation is very common, and palms are common especially toward the south.

title: Ghana - Orange Fender Taxis (Plonkit)
description: Taxis in Ghana typically have multicoloured body panels. The fenders and quarter panels are always coloured orange-yellow.

title: Ghana - White Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Road lines in Ghana are always white. However, many paved roads do not have road lines at all.

title: Ghana - 3-Insulator Poles (Plonkit)
description: Ghana typically uses wooden poles with 3 insulators on a metallic crossbar.

title: Ghana - Flag Colors (Plonkit)
description: Ghana is a patriotic country, and you can often see things painted in the national flag’s colours: red, yellow, green, and sometimes including the black star.

title: Ghana - Striped Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Black and white striped signposts in Ghana are typically seen in cities. On rural roads, you will mostly see classic, non-painted, metal signposts.

title: Ghana - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in Ghana is limited and easy to memorize, as most of it was taken on its main roads and in major cities. The most dense coverage is located in the south, around the cities of Accra and Kumasi.

title: Ghana - Majority Generation 4 (Plonkit)
description: The majority of generation 4 coverage is close to Accra or Kumasi, with only a few major roads being covered.

title: Ghana - Paved vs Unpaved Map (Plonkit)
description:
This map shows the distribution of paved and unpaved roads across the country.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Ghana - Ghana Tape (Plonkit)
description:
Ghana features 3 distinct types of tape on the google car:
In the southwest, you can find the ‘unpeeled tape’, which is essentially a mostly intact tape, which is not peeling off.
In the east and north, you can find the ‘peeled tape’, which unlike the ‘unpeeled tape’, is slightly peeled off.
North of Kumasi, and west of Tamale, you can find this ‘scotched tape’, which has two distinct white spots on the left side of the tape.

title: Ghana - Northern Savannah (Plonkit)
description: Northern Ghana features a savannah landscape, which can be identified by its dry soil and less dense vegetation.

title: Ghana - Mountain Ranges (Plonkit)
description: Tall mountain ranges in Ghana are typically seen near Lake Volta in the highlighted area.

title: Ghana - Dense Forests (Plonkit)
description: Dense forests in Ghana are typically found in the southwest and east. You will usually see many naturally occurring palm trees, making the two regions recognizable.

title: Ghana - Coastal Palms (Plonkit)
description: Tall palm trees are commonly found along the coast. Most of them are located in the west.

title: Ghana - Wa Unpaved Roads (Plonkit)
description: Most unpaved roads in a dry savannah landscape are found north of Wa, as well as near the town itself.

title: Ghana - Sawla-N10 Road (Plonkit)
description: The road connecting the town of Sawla with the N10 has very crisp, new road lines. Most of the road runs in a general east-west direction, through a lush savannah landscape. The middle line can be solid or dashed.

title: Ghana - Salaga-Tamale Road (Plonkit)
description: The Salaga-Tamale road up to Kpalbusi is a dirt road with very moody overcast coverage. The soil tends to be very dark, with a purple or brown tinge to it. The road also has a unique tropical savannah feel. The soil is most dark near the town of Salaga.

title: Ghana - Nkwanta to Domanko Road (Plonkit)
description: The road between Nkwanta and Domanko is unpaved, with a powerline close to the road to your east or northeast. The road itself runs in a general SE-NW direction, through a lush savannah landscape that is typical of central Ghana.

title: Ghana - N2 Ridgeline (Plonkit)
description: On a section of the N2 east of Lake Volta, you can often see a ridgeline to your southeast, somewhat close to the road. The road itself also has a distinct angle, running in a general SW-NE direction. The sky is very overcast and grey.

title: Ghana - East Accra Coastal (Plonkit)
description: The coastal area just east of Accra, especially on the N1, has a distinct landscape: it is very flat and wide open, with significantly less vegetation than the rest of southern Ghana. Some parts can look somewhat dry.

title: Ghana - N1 Elubo New Road (Plonkit)
description: The section of the N1 road near the border town of Elubo is very new: it has dark and unblemished asphalt, a very crisp-looking middle line, and no outer lines. The vegetation is dense and occasionally features palm trees.

title: Ghana - Keta Lagoon (Plonkit)
description: The Keta Lagoon in the southeast of Ghana can be seen on the road that runs along it, with the lake being most visible in the northern section. You can sometimes see grey rocks on the side of the road. The soil is quite sandy in comparison to the rest of the country, and it should have a coastal feel.

title: Ghana - Nature Reserve Car (Plonkit)
description: Several nature reserves and sanctuaries have this unique car. A white car and side mirrors will be visible instead of the regular car, however, the ‘Ghana tape’ will still be there.

title: Ghana - Ankasa Game Reserve Car (Plonkit)
description: The Ankasa Game Reserve has a unique Google car. The entire front of the Google car can be seen, with only the actual camera blurred. The roof of the car will have a street view vinyl and the ‘Ghana tape’ will be present.

title: Ghana - Boabeng Fiema Car (Plonkit)
description: The Boabeng Fiema Monkey Sanctuary has a unique Google car. The ‘Ghana tape’ and roof rack will not be visible however, the black right side mirror will be slightly visible just outside the blur.

title: Ghana - Roof Rack Car (Plonkit)
description: All regular road coverage in Ghana was made with a unique Google car. It has a visible roof rack with a piece of black tape on the right end of the front bar. In addition, the hood of the car is usually visible, showing a street view car wrapping that features a red rectangle and some other recognizable elements. Normally, this unique car is all you need to identify Ghana.

title: Kenya - Pickup Truck Meta (Plonkit)
description: Kenya is mostly covered in Generation 4 pickup truck coverage. Most trucks are blurred out, but sometimes you can see parts of the car, which can be many different colors, or a snorkel.

title: Kenya - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Outer lines in Kenya will always be solid white, while inner lines will be yellow and either solid or dashed.

title: Kenya - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Kenyan poles are either made of concrete or wood, and have an L shaped crossbar.

title: Kenya - Follow Car (Plonkit)
description: On a lot of the coverage you will see a grey Toyota SUV following the Street View car.

title: Kenya - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Kenya uses long white front licence plates. The rear counterpart is square and yellow.

title: Kenya - Safaricom Ads (Plonkit)
description: This mobile network brand named Safaricom is unique to Kenya, and almost every city has one location.

title: Kenya - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Directional signs are green with a white border and text. They often display road numbers in white or yellow.

title: Kenya - Red Road Signs (Plonkit)
description: While infrequent, road signs in Kenya will mostly be red and white.

title: Kenya - Repurposed Vans (Plonkit)
description: These repurposed vans can be found all over Kenya.

title: Kenya - Eucalyptus Trees (Plonkit)
description: Many species of eucalyptus are commonly found in Kenya. They can be identified by their long, often clumped leaves, and smooth bark.

title: Kenya - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Generation 3 coverage in Kenya often features a visible roof rack and a snorkel. Some Generation 3 coverage has no visible car.

title: Kenya - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: You will often see pole markings with a skull and a danger message on it.

title: Kenya - County Names (Plonkit)
description:
Upon closer inspection of signs, billboards and posters, you will notice that the county name is often written. Therefore, knowledge of Kenyan counties can be extremely useful in region guessing.
You can practise Kenyan counties using the quiz in the resource section.

title: Kenya - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Most of the coverage in Kenya outside of the southwest is limited to main roads.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Kenya - Post Codes Kenya (Plonkit)
description:
Post codes in Kenya can be identified by signs in the format PO BOX XXX-YYYZZ, where the number YYY (usually 3 digits but sometimes 0) corresponds to a post code. This is the number which can be used to narrow down your guess. Often, the name of the city is listed after the PO BOX.
You can click on the image to enlarge it. Here is a quiz to help practice Kenyan post codes

title: Kenya - Topography Map (Plonkit)
description:
The natural formation of land has great diversity between regions. The east and large portions of the north are extremely flat. In contrast, the further southwest you travel, the higher the elevation becomes on average.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Kenya - Climate Map (Plonkit)
description:
Kenya has distinct regional climates. Some of these include:
- Humid
- Semi-Arid
- Arid
- Very-Arid
As regions vary, this means that there will be many transitional climates. Use this as a guide to quickly determine the general area to assist with region guessing.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Kenya - Far West Agriculture (Plonkit)
description: The far west areas of the country that are northwest and southwest of Kisumu are the most agricultural parts of the country. You will often see farms, grassy hills, and tall eucalyptus trees in this region of the country.

title: Kenya - Kitui Dry Hills (Plonkit)
description: The area around Kitui is semi-arid, usually mountainous, and has light orange, sandy dirt.

title: Kenya - Northwest Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The northwest part of the country has very limited coverage, most of which is on the A1 or in Sibiloi National Park. It has faintly tan soil and sparse low trees. A lot of the coverage in this area is very flat, but you can also see hills or mountains.

title: Kenya - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Coastal Kenya can be identified by the presence of coconut palms, with rare areas in Taita-Taveta County also containing them.

title: Kenya - White Flowers (Plonkit)
description: White flowers, especially when they are in large numbers, are commonly found east of Chyulu Hills National Park, as well as in Tsavo National Park and near the A109 south of Nairobi.

title: Kenya - Narok Features (Plonkit)
description: Stick fences which seem to go on forever are common in the area around Narok.

title: Kenya - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Red brick architecture is common in the western part of the country and a large area east of Nairobi.

title: Kenya - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Houses that are made of mud and sticks are commonly seen around the western part of the country and the coast.

title: Kenya - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: These light color bricks with excessive amounts of mortar are found along the coast. Walls made of these bricks are commonly seen in this area.

title: Kenya - National Parks Overview (Plonkit)
description:
Kenya has many unique Google cars in and around its National Parks and Reserves. These are still identifiable by the snorkel which is present in almost all of them.
Many of the National Park and Reserve cars must be used in conjunction with landscape, as they can be found in multiple areas.
You can learn more about these National Parks and Reserves in the spotlight section.

title: Kenya - B9 Red Dirt (Plonkit)
description: The B9 in the Northeast is entirely unpaved and has bright reddish orange dirt with many trees surrounding the road. Most of it is very flat, but the coverage at the western end of the road can have hills and mountains. The soil also transitions into a more sandy colour.

title: Kenya - A2 South Marsabit (Plonkit)
description: The A2 between Isiolo and Marsabit has many plants alongside the road and you will often see large mountains in the distance. The stretch going through Namunyak Wildlife Conservation Trust will have a very large mountain range to the west.

title: Kenya - A2 North Marsabit (Plonkit)
description: North of Marsabit will be much flatter, with some mountains in the distance. The stretch just north or Marsabit will have mountains visible to the south, while further north, a different range can be seen. It will also have much less vegetation.

title: Kenya - A3 North Garissa (Plonkit)
description: The A3 north of Garissa is very unique, with light coloured soil and many green trees on either side of the road.

title: Kenya - Western C34 (Plonkit)
description: The western part of the C34 is a flat, east to west road. There are two long, straight sections with an abundance of sugar cane. Furthermore, you will see a large mountain range north along the entire mentioned stretches of road.

title: Kenya - Nairobi City (Plonkit)
description: Nairobi is the largest city in the country, and capital of Kenya. It is the only city to have a considerable amount of skyscrapers, and is highly developed. It is densely populated, and is surrounded by small, poor settlements.

title: Kenya - Kilimanjaro View (Plonkit)
description: In a lot of the coverage north of Mt Kilimanjaro, the mountain is visible to the south, usually obscured by clouds. In the city of Oloitoktok, the mountain will often be visible directly to the south.

title: Kenya - Homa Bay Hill (Plonkit)
description: Homa Bay has this protruding hill to the east that is often visible.

title: Kenya - City Wajir Often (Plonkit)
description: The city of Wajir often has blinding white dirt roads, combined with extremely red soil on the roadside.

title: Kenya - Mara Triangle (Plonkit)
description: Mara Triangle has no considerable mountains and most of it is either flat or hilly. It has a white car that can be found in other Kenyan National Parks. Generation 4 coverage exists there as well.

title: Kenya - Amboseli NP (Plonkit)
description: Amboseli National Park has a grey car with a small snorkel. It is very flat with tan grass, few trees, and dried up lake beds. You can always see the base of Kilimanjaro to the south, with most of it obscured by clouds.

title: Kenya - Aberdare NP (Plonkit)
description: Aberdare National Park has a grey and brown car that features a large snorkel. Almost all of the coverage is outside of the National Park, with only two roads within the park covered. The main road through the park has these rubber bands on the roof rack, which can only be found in one other National Park in Kenya.

title: Kenya - Mt Elgon NP (Plonkit)
description: Between Kitale and Mt Elgon, you can find the Aberdare car as well, but it will always have rubber bands, unlike in Aberdare where it will only have them on the main roads through the park. It can be differentiated from Aberdare by its redder dirt, and greener landscape.

title: Kenya - Sibiloi NP (Plonkit)
description:
The area surrounding and between Kerio and Lodwar uses the same car as the Aberdare National Park, but with a vastly different landscape. It is very sandy, dry, and has little vegetation.
You may also find yourself in Generation 3 coverage without car meta.

title: Kenya - B8 Succulents (Plonkit)
description: This stretch of the B8 just north of Kibaoni has many succulents on the side of the road.

title: Kenya - Snorkel Cars (Plonkit)
description:
Kenya has many unique Google cars, almost all of which will have visible car meta. In Generation 3 you will typically see a car with a roof rack and a snorkel. In Generation 4 you will always have a large pickup truck, which will either be white or grey. The grey car comes in two slightly different variations, of which one can either be with or without a snorkel.

It is the only country other than Mongolia with a snorkel.

title: Kenya - Gen 3 No Car (Plonkit)
description: While the vast majority of Kenyan car coverage has a visible Street View car, it is possible to find Generation 3 coverage with no visible car.

title: Kenya - Big Snorkel Grey Car (Plonkit)
description: This Generation 3 grey car with a large snorkel is mostly found in the west, but can also be found in the Mombasa and Nairobi areas, and regions east of Nairobi near Kitui.

title: Kenya - Small Snorkel Black Car (Plonkit)
description: This Generation 3 black car with a small snorkel is mostly found in the east of the country. You can also see it north and south of Nairobi.

title: Kenya - Gen 4 Grey Car (Plonkit)
description:
Kenya has mostly Generation 4 coverage covered by a large grey Google car, with or without a snorkel. There are many metas regarding Generation 4, too many in fact to break down here.

RESOURCE: Therefore, please use this document. It covers this area in depth, and was created by snowf_lake#9088.

Key meta information can be found in the tips below. Other less extensive, but still noteworthy car meta, can be found in the spotlight section.

title: Kenya - Tape on Roof (Plonkit)
description: You can see pieces of white tape on the roof of the Google car in a lot of the coverage north and south of Nairobi.

title: Kenya - A109 Orange Dirt (Plonkit)
description:
The A109 between Mombasa and Nairobi has light orange dirt and many hills around the road and in the distance. You will additionally see many transportation trucks delivering various goods.

Most of the coverage between Mombasa and Emali also has a unique car, which has a cord on the left.

title: Kenya - Mombasa Coast (Plonkit)
description: Mombasa and the other coastal towns are easily identified from the white sandy soil, palm trees and coastal feel.

title: Kenya - Dirt-Speckled Car (Plonkit)
description: This car that is covered in specks of dirt is unique to these stretches of the A3, B9, and the Habaswein-Dadaab Road connecting the two.

title: Lesotho - Gen 2 Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
All coverage in Lesotho is Generation 3. In almost all locations, the back of a white Google car without an antenna is visible.
While Botswana and Eswatini only have Generation 3 coverage, South Africa also has Generation 2 and Generation 4 coverage. In addition, Generation 3 coverage is somewhat rare in South Africa.

title: Lesotho - Lesotho Mountains (Plonkit)
description:
One of the best ways to identify the country are the characteristic ‘Lesotho mountains’. They are bare and treeless, often have tabletop-like shapes, and recognizable horizontal rocky ridgelines.
Depending on where you are in the country, the mountains can vary a bit in appearance. Especially inland areas towards the southeast, where they appear more like rolling green hills rather than isolated tabletop mountains. However, you will still often be able to see the horizontal rocky ridges.

title: Lesotho - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Lesotho uses long white licence plates with blue text. If partially unblurred, you may see the Mokorotlo hat symbol on the left.

title: Lesotho - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Lesotho uses yellow outer lines and white inner lines.

title: Lesotho - Triple Middle Lines (Plonkit)
description: Some roads have unique triple middle lines, consisting of two solid lines with a dashed line in between.

title: Lesotho - Like Four Other (Plonkit)
description: Like the four other Southern African countries, Lesotho drives on the left.

title: Lesotho - Round Huts (Plonkit)
description: In rural areas, you will often see traditional round huts with thatched roofs.

title: Lesotho - Agave Plants (Plonkit)
description: These agave plants are common throughout the countryside and often a good clue for the country.

title: Lesotho - Short Grass (Plonkit)
description: Grasslands in Lesotho primarily consist of short grass.

title: Lesotho - Basotho Blankets (Plonkit)
description: Many people in Lesotho wear traditional clothing. Most recognizably, a lot of people can be seen wearing a Basotho woollen blanket.

title: Lesotho - Livestock (Plonkit)
description: Lesotho is a very rural society. You will often see a lot of free-roaming livestock on Lesotho’s roads: most commonly cows, but also horses, donkeys, and other farm animals.

title: Lesotho - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Coverage in Lesotho is very sparse, particularly in the southeastern half, where it’s mostly limited to yellow roads. All urban coverage is found in the northwest.

title: Lesotho - Flat Region (Plonkit)
description:
Lesotho can be roughly divided into two regions, based on landscape: flat and mountainous.
In the flat region, the road itself runs through a mostly flat or hilly landscape. “Flat” is a bit of a misnomer, as you will usually still see tabletop-like mountains around you. However they will usually be significantly further away from the road, giving you a more clear line of sight. This “flat” part is the region with the most coverage, settlements and agriculture.

title: Lesotho - Mountainous Region (Plonkit)
description:
Conversely, in the mountainous part, the road will usually be directly on the side of the mountain, instead of slightly away from it. The mountains are often large, closer to the road, and covered in green grass.
Coverage in the mountainous part of Lesotho is very sparse: there are only 6 main roads (and a couple of very small off-roads) with coverage, meaning that you can learn each road by heart if you feel so inclined.

title: Lesotho - Water Reservoirs (Plonkit)
description:
There are two large man-made water reservoirs in the mountainous part of Lesotho, which can be seen from several road sections.
The larger Katse reservoir is visible from parts of the A25. The smaller Mohale reservoir is visible from an off-road of the A3.

title: Lesotho - A2 Good Pavement (Plonkit)
description: The section of the A2 between Maseru and Mafeteng has by far the best road quality in all of Lesotho.

title: Lesotho - A25 Raindrop Camera (Plonkit)
description: On a section of the A25, just east of the big reservoir, the camera is covered in raindrops in one direction.

title: Lesotho - A5 Road Construction (Plonkit)
description:
Several sections of the A5 south of Nyakosoba are under construction. As a result, you will often see a sort of temporary “bollard” next to the road, consisting of a stick that is mostly painted white.
Even on sections without the bollard, you can often recognize this road, as it is a wide dirt road with very dark brown soil.

title: Lesotho - Sehlabathebe Road (Plonkit)
description:
The road going from Ramatsediso to Sehlabathebe NP, in the southeast on the border with South Africa, is very recognizable. Consider guessing there if the following three things are all true for your location:
- Unpaved road with light brown soil.
- Good weather with little fluffy clouds.
- Grassy landscape high in the mountains.
You will also often be able to see exposed, light-coloured rocks next to the road.

title: Lesotho - Maseru City (Plonkit)
description:
The only city with a significantly urbanised downtown area is Maseru, the capital. All other towns have a very provincial feel in comparison to Maseru.
Note that the suburbs of Maseru can still have a very rural feel.

title: Lesotho - Qacha's Nek (Plonkit)
description:
Qacha's Nek is a very recognizable town that is located far away from most other towns, on the southeastern border with South Africa.
It is situated right in the middle of green mountains, and it had noticeably bad weather when the Google car drove there.

title: Lesotho - Generation 3 White Car (Plonkit)
description: All coverage in Lesotho is Generation 3. In almost all locations, the back of a white Google car without an antenna is visible.

title: Lesotho - Left Hand Traffic (Plonkit)
description: Like the three other Southern African countries, Lesotho drives on the left.

title: Madagascar - Generation 3 Trekker (Plonkit)
description: All coverage in Madagascar was taken with a Generation 3 trekker camera.

title: Madagascar - Boat Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: Several boat trekkers can be found throughout the country.

title: Madagascar - People Following Trekker (Plonkit)
description: Most coverage features one or several people walking alongside the trekker. These people can be used both to recognise the country and to regionguess it.

title: Madagascar - Malagasy Language (Plonkit)
description: Madagascar has two official languages: French and Malagasy, which is written with the Latin alphabet and contains many long, multiple-syllable words.

title: Madagascar - Climate Variation (Plonkit)
description: The climate of Madagascar generally varies from extremely dry in the southern and central parts, to tropical in the north.

title: Madagascar - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Street View in Madagascar is very limited, with a mixture of land and boat coverage, most of which is on or near the west coast. It is worth noting that almost all the coverage was taken using trekkers, with only two exceptions, both of which have a visible, unique Street View car.
Because of the limited coverage, this guide will be structured differently than most other guides. It will be divided into two main sections: one for land coverage and one for boat coverage, which in turn is divided into subsections based on region.

title: Madagascar - Ambanja Person (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in Ambanja can be recognized by a person wearing a dark blue T-shirt and black sunglasses.

title: Madagascar - Nosy Ambariovato People (Plonkit)
description: The coverage on the island of Nosy Ambariovato can be recognized by the people, one wearing a blue T-shirt and sunglasses on their forehead, one with a light red T-shirt and one with a darker red tank top. There is also a fourth person in some of the coverage, wearing a light blue T-shirt. The coverage is very hilly and forested.

title: Madagascar - Nosy Ambariovato Village (Plonkit)
description: There is a village by the northern shore of Nosy Ambariovato.

title: Madagascar - Ambiky Palms (Plonkit)
description: Ambiky can be recognized by the large number of palms combined with the brown, sandy dirt road. In most of the coverage, there is a person walking in front of the trekker with a grey T-shirt and a brown backpack.

title: Madagascar - Beach West Ambiky (Plonkit)
description: A beach west of Ambiky can be recognized by the low trees combined with low mountains to the northwest.

title: Madagascar - South Ambiky Forest (Plonkit)
description: An area with coverage south of Ambiky can be recognized by the large, solitary green bushes combined with a very slight red tinge in the dirt. Certain parts of the coverage are quite wet.

title: Madagascar - Sambirano River Person (Plonkit)
description: There are three major sections of coverage along the Sambirano river, most of which can be identified with the single person, wearing a dark blue T-shirt and sunglasses on their forehead. The same person is also present on Nosy Ambariovato.

title: Madagascar - Sambirano River Group (Plonkit)
description: A small section of the coverage by the Sambirano river has two different people present on the coverage; one with a red T-shirt and white cap, and one with a spotted dress.

title: Madagascar - Northern Atoll (Plonkit)
description: A couple of atolls on the central west coast can be seen on Street View. The northernmost is the smallest, and is easily recognizable as it only consists of sand and you can always see from one shore to the other.

title: Madagascar - Southern Atolls (Plonkit)
description: The other atolls can be recognized by their small size relative to other landmasses and the broad leaved palms which is rarely found anywhere else in the country.

title: Madagascar - Antananarivo Hill (Plonkit)
description: Most of the coverage in Antananarivo was taken on the side of a hill looking out over the city, which leads up to the Queen’s Palace, which can be seen near the top of the hill.

title: Madagascar - RN8 Silver Roof Rack (Plonkit)
description: The coverage on the RN8 between Andriamena and Marofandilia can easily be recognized by the large silver roof rack on the Street View car. The coverage is very dry and sandy.

title: Madagascar - RN8 Trekker People (Plonkit)
description: The trekker next to the RN8 can be recognized by its extreme dryness, combined with the four people wearing red, blue, grey and light blue respectively.

title: Madagascar - Avenue of the Baobabs (Plonkit)
description: Baobab Avenue is easy to recognize by the extremely broad trunked baobab trees along the side of the road.

title: Madagascar - Morondava Town (Plonkit)
description: Morondava is most easily recognized by the bald person wearing either a light green or a light red striped shirt. It is also one of few towns where the trekker walks on a paved road.

title: Madagascar - Morondava Beach (Plonkit)
description: Morondava has a very smooth sand beach, with the ocean to the northwest. There are a large number of palms visible.

title: Madagascar - Belo Sur Mer Town (Plonkit)
description: Belo Sur Mer can be recognized by the large number of palms combined with the blanket of white sand on the ground.

title: Madagascar - Belo Sur Mer Beach (Plonkit)
description: The beach outside Belo Sur Mer can be recognized by the somewhat dirty sand and the curved shoreline with the ocean to the northwest.

title: Madagascar - Kirindy Mitea Soil (Plonkit)
description: Kirindy Mitea National Park can be most easily recognized by having the reddest soil present on Street View in Madagascar.

title: Madagascar - Manahy Car (Plonkit)
description: A car with a barely visible grey metal roof rack can be seen by Manahy. There are some locations where the car is completely blurred out, where the shape of the blur is the best indication of the area.

title: Madagascar - South Manahy Dune (Plonkit)
description: A piece of coverage, partly taken on a large grassy field, and partly on the side of a sand dune, can be found south of Manahy.

title: Madagascar - North Andavadoaka Village (Plonkit)
description: A village with the shore to the east can be found north of Andavadoaka.

title: Madagascar - Cape Village (Plonkit)
description: A small, very sandy village with the shore to the north can be seen on a small cape north of Andavadoaka. Part of the coverage was taken just outside the shoreline.

title: Madagascar - Andavadoaka People (Plonkit)
description: The town of Andavadoaka can be recognized by three different people appearing on the coverage; One wearing a greyish hat and a light blue shirt, and two with red and white T-shirts.

title: Madagascar - Andavadoaka Trekker 1 (Plonkit)
description: The main part of the trekker coverage surrounding Andavadoaka can be recognized by either the person wearing a greyish hat and light blue shirt or a person wearing a yellow T-shirt.

title: Madagascar - Andavadoaka Trekker 2 (Plonkit)
description: A second Trekker, going to the northeast of Andavadoaka can be recognized by a person with a light blue T-shirt.

title: Madagascar - Blue Cow Cart (Plonkit)
description: A blue cart dragged by a black cow on the left and a brown-white cow on the right can be found south of Andavadoaka.

title: Madagascar - Cow Cart (Andavadoaka) (Plonkit)
description: Another cart dragged by a white cow on the left and a black and white cow on the right can be found just south of Andavadoaka.

title: Madagascar - Velondriake Village (Plonkit)
description: A small seaside village, with little to no visible people can be found in the northern end of the bay, south of Andavadoaka.

title: Madagascar - Velondriake Rocky (Plonkit)
description: Coverage on a somewhat rocky ground with no people following the trekker can be found southwest of the bay.

title: Madagascar - Velondriake Shallow Water (Plonkit)
description: Coverage with multiple different people walking near and around the trekker, and with a small village to the west, can be found in the southeastern part of the bay. Part of the coverage goes through a very shallow body of water.

title: Madagascar - Velondriake Fishing Nets (Plonkit)
description: A cluster of fishing nets can be found in the bay.

title: Madagascar - Tsaranoro Massif (Plonkit)
description: The Tsaranoro Massif is a large monolithic mountain with trekker coverage. The steep mountainsides, combined with the mountainous area surrounding the coverage makes it very recognizable. The four people following the trekker can also occasionally be a useful clue.

title: Madagascar - Tsaranoro Forest (Plonkit)
description: A small part of the coverage in Tsaranoro was taken inside a forest, which occasionally hides the surrounding mountains. The best way to recognize this area is the relatively dark coverage, combined with the four people following the trekker.

title: Madagascar - Tsaranoro Camp (Plonkit)
description: A small settlement is found in the northeastern end of Tsaranoro. The mountains can typically be seen in the background.

title: Madagascar - Toliara Town (Plonkit)
description: Toliara can be recognized as being a generally quite busy-looking town and the only large town on Madagascar with no person following the trekker.

title: Madagascar - St Augustin People (Plonkit)
description: Two pieces of coverage can be recognized by two people following the trekker; one with a yellow tank top and one with a blue T-shirt. The first of these two parts is located in the town of St Augustin.

title: Madagascar - East St Augustin (Plonkit)
description: The second part with the same two people is found to the east of St Augustin, going through a hilly landscape with a lot of shrubs.

title: Madagascar - Nosy Ambariovato Boat (Plonkit)
description: A white boat, containing many people, can be found going around the island of Nosy Ambariovato.

title: Madagascar - Ankify Blue Boat (Plonkit)
description: A mainly blue boat can be found along the coast south of Nosy Ambariovato.

title: Madagascar - Ambohimena Row Boat (Plonkit)
description: A row boat containing five people with a wide wooden frame surrounding it can be found northwest of Ambohimena.

title: Madagascar - Sambirano River Boat (Plonkit)
description: A boat going up the Sambirano River can be seen with two people; a tourist with a blue T-shirt and a gondolier with a brown shirt. The northernmost part of the coverage is very dark, as it was taken during sunset.

title: Madagascar - West Coast Atoll Boat (Plonkit)
description: The boat covering some small atolls along the central parts of the west coast can be recognized by the driver, wearing a white cap and no shirt.

title: Madagascar - North Andavadoaka Boat (Plonkit)
description: The boat north of Andavadoaka can mostly be recognized by the large sail almost filling up the entire screen and the bow which is painted yellow and blue. Note that the sail is not present in the northern parts of the coverage.

title: Madagascar - South Andavadoaka Boat (Plonkit)
description: The boat in the bay south of Andavadoaka can be recognized by either the somewhat smaller sail than the one north of Andavadoaka, or the person sitting by the bow wearing a red T-shirt with the text “Diesel”. Beware that only one of the two will appear on most of the coverage.

title: Madagascar - St Augustin Boat (Plonkit)
description: Four people; one dressed in red, one in blue and one in yellow in the back, and one dressed in brown at the front, can be seen on a boat by the town of St Augustin.

title: Mali - Coverage Overview (Plonkit)
description: Mali has very limited coverage. There are only ten small trekkers, divided over seven locations. Instead of learning a lot of country-specific clues, it is more practical to simply memorise what the trekkers look like.

title: Mali - Tripod Camera (Plonkit)
description:
All this trekker coverage is made with a regular consumer-grade camera on a tripod. This gives all the coverage a very peculiar and recognizable look, which is different from the normal backpack trekkers. It can have a slightly ‘ethereal’ look to it, but it is recommended to simply click on a few of the locations to get a feeling for what it looks like. Objects in the image will usually have motion blur, and slightly saturated colours.
From here on, the Mali tripod trekkers will be simply referred to as “tripods”.

title: Mali - Mud Brick Mosques (Plonkit)
description:
Almost all the tripods focus on showing historical mosques. These tripods usually have an indoor part and an exterior part, which are sometimes not connected to each other.
These mosques have a recognizable look: they are made out of mud bricks and adobe plaster. The walls of the buildings are decorated with wooden sticks. Inside, you will usually see the same adobe walls, and prayer rugs on the floor.

title: Mali - Pinpointable Mosque Exteriors (Plonkit)
description:
The exterior parts of the mosque tripods can look like a normal street. These will sometimes have enough information available (when moving) to be included in pinpointable maps, like A Community World.
This guide has separate sections for the pinpointable and non-pinpointable coverage. You can choose to study only the coverage that is relevant for competitive maps, or all the coverage. Note, however, that the interiors of the mosques are not considered pinpointable, even though they are covered in the section next to their respective exteriors.

title: Mali - Arid Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Mali is generally an arid country. Seeing a sandy, dry landscape can help with immediately distinguishing the Mali tripods from most tripods in other countries.

title: Mali - Niono Mosque (Exterior) (Plonkit)
description:
The Niono mosque is located in a busy area by the side of a wide, sandy and fairly dirty road, with trees right by the walls of the mosque.
It is most easily located on the map by first looking for the “Centre Commercial” slightly north of the centre of Niono.

title: Mali - Niono Mosque (Interior) (Plonkit)
description: The inside of the Niono mosque can be recognized by its fairly detailed “European style” pillars, which is not found in any of the other Malinese mosques with coverage.

title: Mali - Sidi Yahiya Mosque (Exterior) (Plonkit)
description:
The roads around the Sidi Yahiya mosque are a mixture of sand and tiles shaped like slices of bread, which within Mali, is unique to this coverage.
The surrounding buildings are mostly built of bricks having a peachy orange colour with a brown undertone. This can also be found around the other two mosques with coverage in Timbuktu. The area generally looks busier than around the Djingareyber mosque.

title: Mali - Sidi Yahiya Mosque (Interior) (Plonkit)
description: The interior of Sidi Yahiya mosque is recognized by the yellow painted walls combined with the bottom of the walls, which consists of unpainted bricks. The mosque has a courtyard, with walls made of bricks and a floor made of bright, square tiles.

title: Mali - Djingareyber Mosque (Exterior) (Plonkit)
description: Coverage outside of the Djingareyber mosque in Timbuktu features brick buildings and a paved street with rectangular tiles.

title: Mali - Djingareyber Mosque (Interior) (Plonkit)
description: The inside of the Djingareyber mosque can be characterised by yellow painted walls, wide round archways, and red carpet.

title: Mali - Sankore Mosque (Exterior) (Plonkit)
description: The Sankoré Mosque is surrounded by very sandy ground. The mosque itself has a prominent pyramid-shaped tower.

title: Mali - Sankore Mosque Doors (Plonkit)
description: The Sankoré Mosque has richly decorated doors, which are made of wood adorned with metal details.

title: Mali - Sankore Mosque (Interior) (Plonkit)
description: The interior of the Sankoré Mosque has blue carpet, yellow painted walls, and a fairly low ceiling supported by wooden beams.

title: Mali - Gao Mosque (Exterior) (Plonkit)
description: The exterior of the mosque in Gao can be recognised by the large desolate space outside the walls, the ground consisting of reddish dirt, and some trees in the background.

title: Mali - Gao Mosque (Interior) (Plonkit)
description: The inside of the Gao mosque consists of undecorated corridors with low roofs. You can see the pyramid shaped structure, with a very large number of dry branches sticking out of it, from the courtyard.

title: Mali - Djenne Mosque (Exterior) (Plonkit)
description: The Djenné mosque has a very recognizable front, with some distant trees and a clear sky. The mosque is surrounded by low houses, making the area look fairly open.

title: Mali - Djenne Mosque (Interior) (Plonkit)
description: The interior of the Djenné mosque is quite dark, with a high roof and narrow corridors with gothic arches. There is also a large courtyard with sandy ground and brown wooden doors along the walls.

title: Mali - Mopti Mosque (Exterior) (Plonkit)
description: The Mopti mosque is similar in style to the Djenne mosque, but has trees growing closer to the walls and a slight amount of clouds in the sky. The streets with coverage around the walls of the mosque also appear more narrow than the ones in Djenne.

title: Mali - Mopti Mosque (Interior) (Plonkit)
description: The interior of the Mopti mosque can be recognised by the somewhat open space, with a high roof, no arches, and a blue carpet across the entire floor.

title: Mali - Misplaced Bamako Mosque (Plonkit)
description:
In the north west of Bamako, you can find a tripod inside an empty modern mosque. The interior’s light blue walls and pink floor make this location instantly recognizable.
The coverage on the exterior is in the mosque’s yard. The outside walls are made of concrete, and are painted yellow and orange.
This coverage is severely misplaced, being actually located in an unidentifiable rural area, rather than inside Bamako.

title: Mali - Bandiagara Gorge (Plonkit)
description: This natural rocky gorge is part of the Bandiagara Escarpment. It features dry trees and bushes following the path. It is located southwest of Sangha Ogol Leye, and is the only completely rural coverage in Mali.

title: Mali - Misplaced Tripods (Sankore) (Plonkit)
description: Inside the Sankore mosque coverage in Timbuktu (but not connected to it), there are several misplaced locations: The inside of a tour business actually located in Bamako, a classroom, a couple of streets and some other miscellaneous places.

title: Nigeria - Pickup Truck (Plonkit)
description: A visible Street View car is present in most of the coverage, being a pickup truck with the cab and bed visible. The colour of the cab and other features of it varies. In Generation 3, a roof rack is present. You may also find a large blur covering the entire pickup truck.

title: Nigeria - Police Follow Car (Plonkit)
description: A police car, most commonly white or black, can almost always be seen following the Street View car. The follow cars may differ slightly from the ones shown in the image.

title: Nigeria - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Nigeria uses short licence plates that appear somewhat green through the blur.

title: Nigeria - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Most Nigerian poles are made of concrete, have indents with a few horizontal supports, and are similar to the ones used in Brazil, but do not have holes through them.

title: Nigeria - Poor Road Quality (Plonkit)
description: Roads are not always well-maintained in Nigeria, so roads without roadlines or faded roads are common. Potholes, cracked roads and unpaved roads are also relatively common.

title: Nigeria - House Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Most Nigerian houses are single-storey, with steeply pitched roofs commonly made of metal sheets. Cinder block walls surrounding the houses are also common.

title: Nigeria - Storefront Signs (Plonkit)
description: City and state names are often found on storefronts or banners in Nigeria, so knowing them can be quite useful.

title: Nigeria - Shitcam Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Within mainland Africa, Nigeria is currently the only country to have this low-quality coverage, known as official ari, or “shitcam”.

title: Nigeria - Topography Map (Plonkit)
description: Nigeria is generally a fairly flat country with subtle elevation changes throughout. The south is relatively flat apart from some noticeable hills in the southeast, in Enugu state and in the southwest, between Ife and Lokoja. In the north, more prominent hills and mountains are found from Abuja and Jimeta. The largest mountains are found in the east, making up the Mandara mountain range and the Nigeria-Cameroon border. However, due to little coverage, the mountains are rarely visible.

title: Nigeria - Climate Map (Plonkit)
description: Shown is a Köppen climate map of Nigeria. The climate ranges from tropical rainforest in the far south, where you can find an abundance of palms with lush, green vegetation, to a more arid, savannah landscape in the centre, with more scattered trees. In the far north, it transitions to an arid steppe where the vegetation becomes even more sparse.

title: Nigeria - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Nigeria is a sparsely covered country, with very few roads in the northwest and east. Most of the coverage is centred around big cities and the highways that connect them.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Nigeria - Gen 3 Map (Plonkit)
description:
Knowing where you can find each generation is very useful. Notably, Generation 3 is not found north of Abuja.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Nigeria - Gen 4 Map (Plonkit)
description:
Generation 4 is not found in the northwest or far south. Shitcam is now found in most of Nigeria.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Nigeria - Map Shows States (Plonkit)
description:
This map shows states with unique vehicle and tuk tuk colours. If a vehicle is shown, the state will have yellow tuk tuks.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Nigeria - Religious Attire (Plonkit)
description: Nigeria is mainly Christian in the south, and Islamic in the north. As such, seeing women in hijabs and men in Muslim attire is more common in the north.

title: Nigeria - Kaduna Haystacks (Plonkit)
description: These haystacks are extremely common and are almost exclusively found in Kaduna state.

title: Nigeria - Kano Corn Fields (Plonkit)
description: If you find yourself in an arid, but green, agricultural landscape with an abundance of corn around, you are likely to be in Kano state. It is only covered by shitcam, without any Generation 3 or 4.

title: Nigeria - Benue Vegetation (Plonkit)
description: Benue state can be recognized by the lush, green grass covered ground, with reddish soil. The vegetation is somewhat scattered, with the grass making way for taller trees. Shorter trees and shrubs between the grass and taller trees are somewhat uncommon. Thatched huts are also common in comparison to other southern states.

title: Nigeria - Niger State Shitcam (Plonkit)
description: Niger state is the shitcam equivalent to Benue state. It is almost entirely covered by shitcam, and can be recognized by the scattered trees, reddish soil, and dry grass.

title: Nigeria - Northwest Arid Roads (Plonkit)
description: The highways that run through the northwestern states of Kebbi, Sokoto, Zamfara, and Katsina can be recognized by an even more open and arid landscape compared to Niger state. The tree coverage becomes even more sparse, or there may not be trees at all. These states are entirely covered by shitcam.

title: Nigeria - Northeast Hills (Plonkit)
description: A savannah landscape combined with rocky hills can most commonly be seen in the northeast in the states of Plateau, Bauchi, Gombe, Adamawa, and the north of Taraba. The hills in the far east and west of this region are typically greener and covered in more vegetation compared to the hills toward the middle of the range.

title: Nigeria - Abuja Monoliths (Plonkit)
description: These monolithic mountains with exposed, weathered rock are common in and around Abuja.

title: Nigeria - Lekki Palms (Plonkit)
description: A flat landscape with coastal vegetation and many palms can be seen east of Lekki. The ground is very sandy. Almost all of the coverage is old Generation 3, with a silver follow car.

title: Nigeria - A121 Highway (Plonkit)
description: The A121 can be recognized by the lush, tropical vegetation surrounding the divided highway, with a short, concrete median. Being a major highway, many vehicles, especially trucks, can be seen along it.

title: Nigeria - A3 Divided Highway (Plonkit)
description: The A3 going east of Potiskum to the Borno State border can be recognized by the Generation 4 coverage, mostly open arid landscape, and the highway being divided.

title: Nigeria - Dark Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: Dark red soil is most commonly found in and around Benin City and Enugu.

title: Nigeria - Obudu Plateau Road (Plonkit)
description: The Obudu Plateau road can be recognized by having the tallest mountains in Nigeria with street view coverage. The road winds up lush, green mountains and the coverage is slightly foggy and wet.

title: Nigeria - Blue Tint Shitcam (Plonkit)
description: This variant of shitcam with a distinct blue tint can be found in these areas.

title: Nigeria - Follow Car Map (Plonkit)
description: This map shows where each old Generation 3 follow car can be found. They are uncommon, but can still be useful to know.

title: Nigeria - Vehicle Tuktuk Colours (Plonkit)
description: This map shows states with unique vehicle and tuk tuk colours. If a vehicle is shown, the state will have yellow tuk tuks.

title: Réunion - French Overseas Department (Plonkit)
description: Réunion, officially the Department of Réunion, is an overseas department and region of France, east of Madagascar in the Indian Ocean. As such, for country streaks purposes, it is counted as France.

title: Réunion - Car (Black Tape/Roof Rack) (Plonkit)
description: Réunion has a Street View car with visible side mirrors, a roof rack, and black tape at the end of the rear right bar.

title: Réunion - French Infrastructure (Plonkit)
description: Being a French Department, you will see French infrastructure, such as signs, bollards and poles.

title: Réunion - Landscape (Volcanic/Tropical) (Plonkit)
description: Réunion is a mountainous volcanic island in the Indian Ocean on a similar latitude to Queensland, Australia. Most roads are along the coast, with lush green mountains visible close by. Vegetation consists of palms and ferns, pine trees at higher elevation, and flowering plants due to the island’s tropical savanna climate.

title: Réunion - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Only a handful of roads were covered without a trekker. Learning the general regions with coverage will help you get those extra 10 points.

title: Réunion - Bus Stops (Yellow/L-Shaped/Pink/Orange/Green/Red) (Plonkit)
description:
There are six distinct bus stop designs on Réunion:
- Yellow - This is the most common type and can be found all over the island. It is usually accompanied by another bus stop, meaning you can get a good region guess if you see it on its own.
- L Shaped - It can either be white, or an olive colour. It may also be in the form of a bus shelter. It is almost never accompanied by a yellow bus stop.
- Pink - Rarely accompanied by a yellow bus stop.
- Orange - Almost always accompanied by a yellow bus stop.
- Green - Almost always accompanied by a yellow bus stop.
- Red - Rarely accompanied by a yellow bus stop.
This infographic shows where each one can be found. The list above is ranked by how common each one is found.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Réunion - Sugarcane Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Sugarcane plantations on Réunion can be found in two regions: the northeast and the southwest. The southwest is generally more built up and densely populated, meaning you will see more buildings or cars around.

title: Réunion - Cilaos Caldera (Plonkit)
description: Cilaos is a town inside a caldera. It can be recognized by the wall of mountains surrounding the town with overcast coverage.

title: Réunion - Rectangular Front Blur (North of Saint-Louis) (Plonkit)
description: You can spot this rectangular blur on the front camera in all the coverage going north of Saint-Louis.

title: Réunion - Coastal N1 Highway (Divided) (Plonkit)
description:
The northwestern section of the N1 is divided, with a distinct ridge to the southeast and the ocean to the northwest.
Note that although a bridge appears on the map, the coverage was taken before the bridge was built, meaning you will not see the bridge.

title: Réunion - Route du Volcan (Martian Landscape) (Plonkit)
description: Route du Volcan can be recognized by the Martian landscape. The only vegetation is scattered shrubs and the soil is a distinct brown-red colour. These white stones lining the road are also a good clue.

title: Réunion - Route Forestiere 58 (Dirt Track/Dense Vegetation) (Plonkit)
description: La Route Forestière 58 de la Scierie et du Haut des Makes is a winding dirt track that can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding it, particularly pine trees and eucalyptus. The track itself is also dark in colour, with grass growing in the middle of it.

title: Réunion - Eastern N2 (Sparse/Vegetated) (Plonkit)
description: The eastern region of Réunion is the least densely populated, evident by the eastern part of the N2, which is a single carriageway passing through somewhat dense vegetation on both sides, or a vast landscape with little to no trees.

title: Réunion - City Bollards (Saint Paul Black / Saint Denis Green) (Plonkit)
description: The two largest towns in Réunion can be differentiated by their bollards, commonly seen at intersections. Saint Paul uses black bollards, while Saint Denis uses green bollards, often with white balls on top. Saint Denis is also more built up, being the capital.

title: Rwanda - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Rwanda uses long white front and yellow back licence plates.

title: Rwanda - Pickup Truck Meta (Plonkit)
description: All the coverage in Rwanda is made with a Generation 4 camera. In most of the coverage, the Google car is a pickup truck which will be covered entirely by a big blur.

title: Rwanda - White Pickup Meta (Plonkit)
description: Sometimes the Google car is entirely visible: it is a big white or brown pickup truck with a brakelight. The camera mount is visible.

title: Rwanda - Hazy Sky (Plonkit)
description: The coverage has a noticeable hazy tint to it, which is especially apparent in the sky.

title: Rwanda - Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Rwandan architecture features a lot of brick and concrete. Most houses in Rwanda are single family houses, which can have rather steep roofs. Houses also often have fences for protection. The most notable feature of Rwandan architecture are the ‘ventilation bricks,’ which are present in many houses.

title: Rwanda - Hilly Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Rwanda is generally quite hilly, but not very mountainous.

title: Rwanda - Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: Most of the soil in Rwanda has a noticeable red tint to it.

title: Rwanda - Rwanda Features (Plonkit)
description: Eucalyptus are very commonly found in Rwanda. They can be identified by their long, often clumped leaves, and smooth bark.

title: Rwanda - Banana Plants (Plonkit)
description: Banana plants are common throughout Rwanda.

title: Rwanda - Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Rwanda uses multiple different red and white cylindrical bollards.

title: Rwanda - Waystones (Plonkit)
description: Rwanda uses various different styles of white concrete waystones.

title: Rwanda - Clean Streets (Plonkit)
description: Streets in Rwanda are noticeably very clean and free of garbage.

title: Rwanda - Striped Kerbs (Plonkit)
description: Kerbs are often painted with black and white stripes.

title: Rwanda - Fences & Walls (Plonkit)
description: Villa neighbourhoods often have a lot of tall security fences and walls.

title: Rwanda - Driving Side (Plonkit)
description: Rwanda drives on the right.

title: Rwanda - Moto Vests (Plonkit)
description: All motorcyclists in Rwanda are required to wear red vests and helmets.

title: Rwanda - Limited Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Rwanda has quite limited coverage: street view is limited to Kigali, and a couple of other patches elsewhere in Rwanda.
You can check out the coverage in detail on this site.

title: Rwanda - District Codes (Plonkit)
description: Street names often have a two-letter code, which tells you the district you are in.

title: Rwanda - Lamp Types Map (Plonkit)
description:
Lamps are fairly consistent on National Roads in Rwanda, but other designs can be sometimes found on some sections.
- Roads marked in green mainly use lamps, with lamp arms that have a slight curve near the end and extend past the lamppost.
- Roads marked as red have lamps with shorter arms and a sharper bend near the top of the lamppost.
- Roads marked with blue use lamps with a longer arm that curves for the entire length.
- Grey roads rarely have lamps.

title: Rwanda - Lamp Post Numbers (Plonkit)
description: Lampposts along many national roads will have the road number painted in black letters. Below that, you will find the lamp number, which generally, but not always, increases the further from Kigali you get.

title: Rwanda - Tea Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Tea plantations are common in Western Rwanda, and a couple other pockets.

title: Rwanda - Northeast Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description: Northeastern Rwanda has less extreme elevation compared to the rest of Rwanda. It more so consists of rolling hills and open agricultural land or undeveloped grassland.

title: Rwanda - Northwest Volcanoes (Plonkit)
description: Volcanoes and volcanic rocks can be seen in northwestern Rwanda.

title: Rwanda - Akagera NP (Plonkit)
description:
The Akagera national park features a very vegetated yet dry landscape with wide unpaved roads that are reddish-brown in colour.
You can also find these rectangular waystones at intersections.
This coverage was taken with the brown Google car.

title: Rwanda - Nyungwe Forest NP (Plonkit)
description:
The Nyungwe Forest National Park goes through a lush and hilly landscape, which has 2 distinct covered roads; The yellow NR10 is paved, with roadlines. French style bollards and green lamp posts can be seen on the sides of the road. The white NR26 going south is mostly paved, except for the southernmost section. No roadlines are present.
This coverage was taken with the brown Google car.

title: Rwanda - NR11 White Lines (Plonkit)
description: The NR11 north of Mabanza uses all white road lines.

title: Rwanda - NR15 Poor Pavement (Plonkit)
description: The section of NR15 from Muhanga till the Western Province border has very poor pavement, with a lot of potholes and a lack of road lines.

title: Rwanda - NR15 Unpaved Section (Plonkit)
description: The section of NR15 from the Western Province border to this point is under construction, with no pavement at the moment; making it the only covered National Road to be unpaved for this long. Also, most of the road hugs a steep cliffside made of red dirt.

title: Rwanda - NR16 Dashed Lines (Plonkit)
description: The NR16 is the only road that predominantly uses dashed outer white lines.

title: Rwanda - Kigali River (Plonkit)
description: A wide river can be seen along the northeastern border of Kigali City.

title: Rwanda - Kigali Villas (Plonkit)
description: Much of the Kigali coverage is in the richer neighbourhoods. You will see a lot of luxury villas.

title: Rwanda - Butare Cobblestone (Plonkit)
description: Many roads in Butare feature cobblestone pavement.

title: Rwanda - Gen 4 Pickup (Plonkit)
description: All the coverage in Rwanda is made with a Generation 4 camera. In most of the coverage, the Google car is entirely visible: it is a big white, black, or brown pickup truck. The camera mount is visible.

title: Rwanda - Car Blur (Plonkit)
description: Occasionally, the Google car will be covered entirely by a big blur.

title: Rwanda - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Rwanda has quite limited coverage: street view is limited to Kigali, and a couple of other patches elsewhere in Rwanda.

title: Rwanda - Kigali Black Pickup (Plonkit)
description: The black pickup truck can be found in most of Kigali.

title: Rwanda - Dirty Car Cyangugu (Plonkit)
description: Around Cyangugu, the Google car is often exceptionally dirty.

title: Rwanda - NR10 Roof Specks (Plonkit)
description: On the NR10 between Butare and Mont Gabegi, there are two small specks on the bottom left side of the Google car roof.

title: Senegal - Blue License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Senegal is the only African country to use fully blue licence plates. A newer version exists in Generation 4 which looks like the standard European licence plate which is white with a blue strip on the left.

title: Senegal - Gen 4 Truck Cab (Plonkit)
description:
A silver or white truck cab is visible in the Generation 4 coverage. Several variants of each exist, most of which are region or road specific. The most useful and recognizable ones will be shown in the spotlight section. For a complete overview, see this document by Lupus.
In the area around Dakar and Thies you can also find a black pick up truck.

title: Senegal - Gen 3 Roof Rack (Plonkit)
description: A Google Car with a visible roof rack and the right side mirror is seen in Generation 3 coverage. Rifts can also be seen in the sky.

title: Senegal - Driving Side (Plonkit)
description: Senegal drives on the right.

title: Senegal - French Infrastructure (Plonkit)
description: Being a former French colony, Senegal uses French infrastructure such as bollards, poles, signs and road lines.

title: Senegal - Language (Plonkit)
description: The official and most common language seen in Senegal is French.

title: Senegal - Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: The road number and the distance to the nearest towns can be seen on these white kilometre markers with a red top.

title: Senegal - Town Entry Signs (Plonkit)
description: Most town entry signs in Senegal are white and feature a thick pink outline. The town is also written in a bold, black font.

title: Senegal - Solar Lamps (Plonkit)
description: These simple black lamps with a solar panel at the top are commonly seen in Senegal.

title: Senegal - Yellow-Orange Taxis (Plonkit)
description: Yellow-orange taxis with black fenders can commonly be seen in Senegal.

title: Senegal - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
This is a coverage map of Senegal. Most of the coverage is west of Touba, with very few roads apart from main roads covered in the east.
You can click on the image to enlarge it. Alternatively, you can look at the coverage in more detail on this site.

title: Senegal - Northern Savannah (Plonkit)
description: The landscape north of The Gambia and for Senegal generally is a flat, arid, savannah-desert landscape with sparse trees. The trees themselves will be somewhat short and have leaves that are faded in colour.

title: Senegal - Southern Greenery (Plonkit)
description: The vegetation in the region south of The Gambia is more lush and green compared to the rest of Senegal, and palm trees can be seen closer to the coast.

title: Senegal - Diourbel Rural (Plonkit)
description: Diourbel Region is the only region in Senegal with extensive rural coverage. The coverage in the region will look like this, with the Google Car driving on a sandy road with sparse trees. Some of the coverage extends to the west in the Thies region up to Babou.

title: Senegal - Coastal Dunes (Plonkit)
description: A very slightly rolling landscape consisting of vegetated sand dunes can be seen along the northwestern coast.

title: Senegal - Bakel Hills (Plonkit)
description: A dry landscape with slight hills can mostly be seen around Bakel, but also south to Nayé.

title: Senegal - Kedougou Hills (Plonkit)
description: A greener landscape with larger hills can be seen around Kedougou and Mako.

title: Senegal - Northern Rice Fields (Plonkit)
description: Irrigated rice fields can sometimes be seen in the region between St Louis and Richard Toll.

title: Senegal - Long Antenna Car (Plonkit)
description: The silver Generation 4 car with a long antenna at the front left can be seen on many roads, but none past the eastern border of Diourbel Region.

title: Senegal - White Gen 4 Car (Plonkit)
description: The regular Generation 4 white car is most commonly found south of The Gambia, but can also be found on the northeastern coast and a small region between Kaolack and Saly.

title: Senegal - Divided Highways (Plonkit)
description: Divided highways are found between Dakar and Touba. The two divided highways are between Dakar and Touba, and between Dakar and Saly.

title: Senegal - N1 Railway Parallel (Plonkit)
description: The N1 between Tambacounda and Nayé generally runs in a northeast east direction. A railway runs parallel to the road. The railway is to the south of the road between Tambacounda to just before Youpe Amadi, and is to the north from Youpe Amadi to Bellé.

title: Senegal - N2 Hazy Low Sun (Plonkit)
description: Hazy coverage with a low sun through a sometimes agricultural landscape can be seen on the N2 between St. Louis and Richard Toll.

title: Senegal - N2 Desert Road (Plonkit)
description: The N2 between Richard Toll and Matam is a wide road going through a flat desert landscape with very sparse trees. It can be recognized by the bright blue skies with no clouds. The road itself goes east-west and northeast-southwest.

title: Senegal - N3 Yellow Grass (Plonkit)
description: Distinct, tall patches of bright yellow grass can be seen along the N3, mostly to the east in the Matam Region.

title: Senegal - Bushfire Haze (Plonkit)
description: The road northeast of Kedougou to the Malian border can be recognized by the hazy bushfire coverage. Smoke trails can sometimes be seen in the distance. The road is paved south of Saraya.

title: Senegal - Saloum Delta (Plonkit)
description: A flat, slightly marshy landscape with low vegetation can be seen on a few sections of roads in the Saloum River Delta.

title: Senegal - Kola-Velingara Soil (Plonkit)
description: The Kola-Velingara road between Saré Amirou and Badion is a dirt road that can be recognized by the late afternoon to evening coverage. The coverage gets later toward the west.

title: Senegal - Forest of Thies (Plonkit)
description: The white road in the Forest of Thies can be recognized by the dry, slightly hilly landscape with brown vegetation. The road itself is made of bright orange dirt. There is also a noticeably haze in the coverage.

title: Senegal - Box Car (Plonkit)
description: The silver Generation 4 car with a box in the back right of the cab can mainly be seen on the road between Richard Toll and Louga, and the N3 between Tiourene and Matam. It can also be seen on the dirt road hugging the Mauritanian border, from Matam to Gassamberi. Finally, it can be seen on a few roads near Diolotène.

title: Senegal - Dirty Left Car (Plonkit)
description: The silver Generation 4 car with a stain at the back left of the cab can be seen on the N2 from Richard Toll to Matam and Bakel to Nayé. It can also be seen on the N1 between Tambacounda and Nayé.

title: Senegal - Dirty Left & Roof (Plonkit)
description: The silver Generation 4 car with a stain at the back left and a dirty roof can mainly be seen on the N1 between Kaffrine and Tambacounda, and the N7 between Tambacounda and Kedougou. It can also be seen between Dahra and Diakhao.

title: Senegal - Red Cloth Car (Plonkit)
description: The silver Generation 4 car with a red cloth at the front left can be seen on this eastern road between Ouro Sogui and Bakel.

title: Senegal - Antenna Down Car (Plonkit)
description: The white Generation 4 car but with the antenna down, parallel to the car’s roof, can be found on the N6 between Ziguinchor and Kolda.

title: Senegal - White Dirty Back Car (Plonkit)
description: The white Generation 4 car with a noticeably dirty back can be seen on the road going north of Kolda, up to Katonfara.

title: Senegal - Dakar City (Plonkit)
description: Dakar is the largest and capital city of Senegal. It can be recognized by the denseness of the city and taller, more modern buildings.

title: Senegal - Touba Mosque (Plonkit)
description: The infamous Great Mosque of Touba can be recognized by the five tall minarets, which can be seen from afar.

title: South Africa - Driving Side (Plonkit)
description: South Africa drives on the left.

title: South Africa - Most Roads South (Plonkit)
description:
On most roads, South Africa utilizes single yellow outer lines and white centre lines.
!!Australia practically never uses yellow outer lines.

title: South Africa - Triple Center Lines (Plonkit)
description:
South Africa occasionally features unique white triple centre lines with 2 solid lines on the outside and a dashed line on the inside.
You may also sometimes encounter another unique triple centre line, consisting of two white lines with one yellow line in the middle. These centre lines are usually found on larger main roads.

title: South Africa - Gen 2 Halo (Plonkit)
description:
Generation 2 coverage is quite common in the country.
It can be recognized by the large circular car blur and the halo-like colour distortion in the sky.

title: South Africa - Languages (Plonkit)
description:
South Africa has 11 official languages: English, Afrikaans, and various Bantu languages. English is the lingua franca and therefore appears most often on signage.
Afrikaans is a Germanic language that is closely related to Dutch. Common Afrikaans place name suffixes are -fontein, -kraal, -kop, -dorp, -nek, and -berg or -burg. While Afrikaans is most commonly spoken in the western half of the country, you will find Afrikaans place names all over South Africa, meaning that it is not useful for region-guessing.

title: South Africa - Bird Poles (Plonkit)
description: The most common type of pole in South Africa features 1 to 5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators that resemble rows of birds, which is why they are referred to as “bird poles” in the community.

title: South Africa - South Africa Uses (Plonkit)
description:
South Africa uses green directional signs with the road number in yellow.
- !!N and R-roads are exclusive to South Africa.
- !!A and B-roads are exclusive to Botswana, Lesotho and Namibia. In addition to this, Namibia uses C, D, M and F roads.
- !!MR-roads are exclusive to Eswatini.

title: South Africa - South Africa Utilizes (Plonkit)
description:
South Africa utilizes triangular warning signs with a red border and a white background.
!!Australia and New Zealand use yellow diamond-shaped warning signs.

title: South Africa - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description:
South Africa uses white-and-red chevrons. You can find a similar chevron pattern below directional signs.
In addition, unique-looking small, thin chevrons with one arrow are common next to roads.

title: South Africa - Walled Houses (Plonkit)
description: Suburban houses in and around large cities will often be surrounded by high walls, fences, and gates to deter criminals.

title: South Africa - Gen 4 Blue Car (Plonkit)
description: All Generation 4 coverage in South Africa was taken by a blue Street View car with a short antenna.

title: South Africa - Gen 4 Smallcam (Plonkit)
description: South Africa also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, but with a short antenna on the back.

title: South Africa - License Plates Map (Plonkit)
description:
Each province features a different licence plate design, which can be somewhat visible through the blur. Most notably Free State or KwaZulu-Natal, which have a slight green tint and blue tint respectively.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: South Africa - Highways Map (Plonkit)
description:
A map of major highways in South Africa. On road signs, the letter ‘N’ should appear in front of the highway number. On Google Maps, however, the letter ‘N’ will not be present. Instead, a blue pentagon with the number will be displayed.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: South Africa - R-Roads Map (Plonkit)
description:
Most of the R-roads with three-digit road numbers are geographically grouped. However, many roads go through multiple provinces and some, especially the 100s, are spread throughout the whole country. The map shows roughly where you can find each set of R-roads.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: South Africa - Area Code Map (Plonkit)
description:
Telephone numbers are 10 digits long. The first three digits of landline numbers are the area code. The first digit is always a zero; the second and third digits give you the area. The area codes are geographically grouped, so even learning just the first digit is useful.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.
Image provided by dbldk.

title: South Africa - Western Cape A-Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles with 3 bars forming the letter ‘A’, with the bottom insulators being attached at the edges of a horizontal bar, can be found almost exclusively in Western Cape, and rarely in bordering provinces.

title: South Africa - Eastern Cape A-Poles (Plonkit)
description: A similar poletop can be found in Eastern Cape, however the A-shape is noticeably wider and the bottom insulators are attached directly to the ‘A’ rather than a horizontal bar.

title: South Africa - KZN Trident Poles (Plonkit)
description: Trident pole tops are almost unique to KwaZulu-Natal.

title: South Africa - Northern Alternating Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles with 3 alternating insulators sticking out horizontally at the top are mostly seen in the four northern provinces of Limpopo, Gauteng, North West and Mpumalanga. They can also sometimes be found in Northern Cape. In the rest of the country, these pole tops are exceedingly rare.

title: South Africa - Triangle Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles with 2 diagonal bars forming a ‘<’ shape can be found mostly in the northeastern provinces, most commonly in Limpopo and North West.
