title: South Africa - Mpumalanga Metal Arms (Plonkit)
description: Poles with 1 or 2 metal arms holding up insulators are most commonly seen in Mpumalanga.

title: South Africa - Red Sign Stickers (Plonkit)
description: Square, red stickers on the back of regular signs are often found in Eastern cape and close to Eastern cape in Northern Cape and Free State. You may see them in the North West province as well, but to a lesser extent.

title: South Africa - White Chevron Stickers (Plonkit)
description: White stickers on the back of chevrons are often seen in the Cape provinces.

title: South Africa - Limpopo Pink Pavement (Plonkit)
description: You can find this grainy, almost Texas-like pavement with a hint of pink in Limpopo.

title: South Africa - Bird Nests (Plonkit)
description: Big bird nests on top of poles are commonly seen in the northern part of the Northern Cape Province.

title: South Africa - Power Plants (Plonkit)
description: Power plants are often seen in between the town of Secunda and eMalahleni in Mpumalanga.

title: South Africa - Northeast Arid (Plonkit)
description: The northeast of the country can look very dry and somewhat barren, with a lot of orange or red soil. You will often see hills or mountains covered in shrubs.

title: South Africa - Western Cape Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Unique rocky, treeless mountains can be seen in Western Cape, with most of the mountains having tall, steep sides and sharp peaks.

title: South Africa - Vineyards (Plonkit)
description: Vineyards are almost exclusively found in Western Cape, mostly in valleys near the coast. You can also commonly find them near Upington, in Northern Cape.

title: South Africa - Northern Cape Desert (Plonkit)
description: A dry landscape with red soil is typically found in the Northern Cape.

title: South Africa - Sugar Cane (Plonkit)
description: Sugarcane plantations are most commonly seen in KwaZulu-Natal, mostly along the coast. However, they can also be seen in Mpumalanga on the Mozambique border. For an overview, see this map.

title: South Africa - Cook Pines (Plonkit)
description: Uniquely tall Cook pine trees are found mostly between the cities of East London and Durban along the southeastern coast.

title: South Africa - Pine Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Tree plantations that consist mostly of pine are common to the west of Eswatini, and some to the south in KwaZulu-Natal.

title: South Africa - Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description: Grassy rolling hills are generally located in the coastal area of Western Cape between Cape Town and George, and just north of Cape Town. Tall ridges are usually visible to the north or east.

title: South Africa - Mozambique Border Flat (Plonkit)
description: The landscape near the Mozambique border in the highlighted area is noticeably flat, with green subtropical vegetation.

title: South Africa - Kruger Camo Car (Plonkit)
description: A camouflage car with black side mirrors and roof racks can be seen in Kruger National Park, on the Mozambique border.

title: South Africa - Kruger Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
The landscape around Kruger National Park is generally flat, with a savannah climate and dry vegetation. You will not see any agriculture and the vegetation is mostly made up of grasses, with small trees dotting the landscape. Red soil can also be seen below the grass.
In addition, this distinctive directional waystone is commonly found at many junctions.

title: South Africa - Metro Route Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Metropolitan Routes are major roads around cities. They are designated with the letter M.
These distinct and unique M route signs are commonly found in Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha) and Durban, respectively.

title: South Africa - Joburg Reflective Tape (Plonkit)
description: Traffic lights and pedestrian crossing poles in Johannesburg are encircled by three strips of reflective tape.

title: South Africa - Durban Lamps (Plonkit)
description: While this lamp and arm can be found uncommonly across the country, Durban uniquely has this bump on the top. You may, however, still see the standard lamp and arm.

title: South Africa - Pole Ads (Plonkit)
description: Poles or any public infrastructure will often be plastered with dodgy adverts for abortion services or penis enlargement pills in and around Gauteng, in particular in Johannesburg and Emalahleni.

title: South Africa - R360 Red Asphalt (Plonkit)
description: The section of the R360 north of Bokspits, next to the Botswana border, has asphalt with a recognizable reddish tint. The landscape is arid and features dry greyish trees, shrubs and long golden grass. The road runs in a general north to south direction.

title: South Africa - Table Mountain (Plonkit)
description: The distinct Table Mountain, located west of Cape Town, can be recognized by its prominent three-kilometre plateau. It is flanked by Devil’s Peak, which is more pyramidal.

title: South Africa - George's Peak (Plonkit)
description: Mountains in the Witfontein Nature Reserve, likely George’s Peak, will be visible north from the city of George.

title: South Africa - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: On most roads, South Africa utilizes single yellow outer lines and white centre lines.

title: South Africa - Green Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: South Africa uses green directional signs with the road number in yellow.

title: South Africa - Warning Signs (Plonkit)
description: South Africa utilizes triangular warning signs with a red border and a white background.

title: South Africa - Area Codes Map (Plonkit)
description: Telephone numbers are 10 digits long. The first three digits of landline numbers are the area code. The first digit is always a zero; the second and third digits give you the area. The area codes are geographically grouped, so even learning just the first digit is useful.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Low Quality Shitcam (Plonkit)
description: All the coverage was taken with a low quality camera that’s commonly referred to as “Shitcam”. The car will often be completely blurred, with a very large blur covering the back and a somewhat smaller blur covering the front.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Portuguese Language (Plonkit)
description: Portuguese is the main language used on São Tomé and Príncipe.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Portuguese Infrastructure (Ladder Poles) (Plonkit)
description: On top of the language, the Portuguese influence can also be seen in infrastructure, such as ladder poles and pedestrian signs with the same design as in Portugal.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Tropical Rainforest (Bananas) (Plonkit)
description: São Tomé and Príncipe are tropical islands, which are almost completely covered in rainforests. Banana plants are especially common throughout the islands.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Slanted Antenna (Plonkit)
description: In many locations, you will notice a slanted antenna protruding from the side of the car.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Blue Pole Paint (CST) (Plonkit)
description: Some wooden poles are painted blue on the bottom. You can also read the letters CST on them.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Yellow Taxis/Minibuses (Plonkit)
description: Taxis and minibuses are painted in a bright yellow colour.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Principe Dim Shitcam (Plonkit)
description: This desaturated and even dimmer variant of shitcam is most common on Príncipe.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Principe Car (Blue Roof/Silver Rails) (Plonkit)
description: The car used on Príncipe can be recognised by the blue roof and silver roof rails.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Sao Tome Car (Black Roof Rails) (Plonkit)
description: The car used on São Tomé is black with black roof rails. In most locations, it is blurred out.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Southern Oil Palms (Plonkit)
description: You can find oil palm plantations in southern São Tomé.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe - Trinidade Red/White Poles (Plonkit)
description: The town of Trinidade has poles with red and white pole paint.

title: Tanzania - Coverage Map (Gombe/Kilimanjaro) (Plonkit)
description:
Tanzania has extremely limited coverage:
- Several Generation 3 trekkers in Gombe National Park. There is also one small indoor tripod in this park.
- A couple of tripods on Mount Kilimanjaro.
- Some spill coverage, made with a regular Google car, on the border with Kenya.
This guide only discusses the trekkers and tripods. For the spills, see our spillover guide.
It should be noted that none of the trekkers and tripods are pinpointable, or even on a road, and therefore they typically do not appear in serious competitive maps. This guide describes them primarily for the sake of completeness. The spills however do appear in maps from time to time.
Due to the sparse nature of the coverage, that is also entirely not on any streets, it is not useful to learn any territory identification metas. Instead, it is better to just memorise what the trekkers and tripods look like.

title: Tanzania - Kilimanjaro Tripods (Ethereal) (Plonkit)
description:
On Mount Kilimanjaro, there are a couple of tripods.
This is a type of coverage made with a regular camera mounted on a tripod. As a result, this coverage has a distinct ethereal look, compared to normal street view: objects in the image will usually have motion blur, and slightly saturated colours.

title: Tanzania - Kilimanjaro Landscape (High Altitude) (Plonkit)
description: The Mount Kilimanjaro tripods show a high altitude landscape, with dark grey rock and in some places eternal snow in the distance. In some panos, you will see mountaineers and tents.

title: Tanzania - Gombe Trekker (Jungle/Lowland) (Plonkit)
description:
A walking trekker goes through a large part of Gombe National Park. The landscape varies somewhat from place to place.
In the lowland parts, you will see dense jungle and usually very little sunlight, leading to dark coverage. Sometimes, you can see chimpanzees.

title: Tanzania - Gombe Trekker (Savannah Trees) (Plonkit)
description: Higher up on the hills, the forest becomes more open and you will see savannah-like trees around you.

title: Tanzania - Gombe Trekker (Hill Tops) (Plonkit)
description: On top of the hills, the trees make way for a bare grassland landscape. Here, you have breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape and Lake Tanganyika.

title: Tanzania - Lake Tanganyika Boat Trekker (Plonkit)
description:
There is a boat trekker in Lake Tanganyika, that hugs the coast very closely, next to Gombe National Park. The coast is always to your east. You will see hills that are mostly covered in tropical forest, with some bare and grassy hilltops.
You can see the boat through the blur: it is painted olive green and white, and has some people in it. The boat and people are always pixelated due to the blur.

title: Tanzania - Jane Goodall's House (Plonkit)
description: There is one more tripod in Tanzania, inside Jane Goodall’s house. It is also located in Gombe National Park, adjacent to the normal Generation 3 trekker coverage.

title: Tunisia - Black Plates (Plonkit)
description: Tunisian licence plates are black with white text.

title: Tunisia - Follow Cars (Plonkit)
description:
One of the best ways to recognize Tunisia is that, in most coverage, the Google car is escorted by a follow car.
There are several different follow cars and these are four of the most commonly found ones.

title: Tunisia - Black Google Car (Plonkit)
description: The Google car in Tunisia is black with a medium-length, thin antenna.

title: Tunisia - Climate (Plonkit)
description: Tunisia has Mediterranean, dry and semidesert climates.

title: Tunisia - Olive Plantations (Plonkit)
description: These olive tree plantations can often be found along roads. They consist of nicely arranged rows of olive trees on an often raked, weedless soil.

title: Tunisia - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Tunisia usually has white road lines. Outer road lines can be dashed or solid.

title: Tunisia - Bilingual Signs (Plonkit)
description: In Tunisia, both French and Arabic are common. The Arabic script can be identified by its lines and dots. You can often see bilingual signs.

title: Tunisia - Direction Signs (Plonkit)
description: Most direction signs have a white background with towns listed in Arabic and Latin script. The font of the Latin script is usually quite distinctive.

title: Tunisia - Blue Doors (Plonkit)
description: Doors, windows, gates and other architectural elements are sometimes painted with this specific traditional shade of blue.

title: Tunisia - Striped Curbs (Plonkit)
description: Red and white striped curbs are common in Tunisia.

title: Tunisia - Km Markers (Plonkit)
description: These white concrete markers with a rounded red or yellow top can be found throughout Tunisia. The top can be red, yellow, or green.

title: Tunisia - Stop Sign (Plonkit)
description: Tunisia has a fairly unique stop sign with Arabic and Latin script.

title: Tunisia - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Coverage is mostly limited to the east coast, between Bizerte in the north and Medinine in the south. Most coverage is in bigger towns and on main roads. The biggest towns and the island of Djerba have quite extensive side road coverage.

title: Tunisia - North Toyota Follow Car (Plonkit)
description: This light green Toyota follow car can be found everywhere in the northernmost part of Tunisia. You will never see it south of Hammamet.

title: Tunisia - South Mazda Follow Car (Plonkit)
description: The dark green Mazda is the most common follow car in Tunisia. This becomes apparent if you look at the coverage map, it can be found all the way from Hammamet to Djerba. Aside from the darker colour, it can also be recognized by its military licence plate with a red strip on the left.

title: Tunisia - Tunis Follow Cars (Plonkit)
description: Tunis, the capital of Tunisia, has a lot of different follow cars. Most of them can be found all over the city. The light green Toyota can also be spotted here.

title: Tunisia - Kairouan Mitsubishi (Plonkit)
description: The city of Kairouan in central-northern Tunisia has this unique follow car, a white Mitsubishi with white mirrors. The dark green follow car can also sometimes be spotted following the Mitsubishi.

title: Tunisia - Djerba No Follow Car (Plonkit)
description:
The island of Djerba is the only region of Tunisia where you are usually not accompanied by a follow car. Most coverage completely lacks one.
While it is rare, this white Mercedes and the dark green follow car can be present.

title: Tunisia - North Tunis Hilly (Plonkit)
description: The area north of Tunis has a Mediterranean climate with hilly terrain. The region is very agricultural and at the time the coverage was captured, almost all fields laid fallow.

title: Tunisia - Tunis-Hammamet Hilly (Plonkit)
description: The area between Tunis and Hammamet looks similar to the area north of Tunis, but the hills tend to be higher and more vegetated.

title: Tunisia - Central Flat Arid (Plonkit)
description: The large middle region between Hammamet and Gabes is very flat, and more arid. Olive tree plantations are common and the more south you go, the drier the landscape becomes.

title: Tunisia - South Desert (Plonkit)
description: South of Gabes is where the landscape changes into something more akin to a desert. A lot more rubbish and small white rocks can be found along the roads. Olive tree plantations are still somewhat common. A mountain range far in the distance is often visible to the southwest.

title: Tunisia - Djerba Vibe (Plonkit)
description: The island of Djerba can sometimes have a distinct vibe. There tend to be a lot of palm trees. Whitewashed, traditional buildings with blue doors and windows are common.

title: Tunisia - Bizerte Lake (Plonkit)
description: Bizerte Lake is instantly recognizable due to its teal coloured waters. There are slight hills to its south, with the rest of the area around the lake being flat. The city of Bizerte is located on the northeast side of the lake.

title: Tunisia - Gabes Palms (Plonkit)
description: If you see a large amount of palm trees in a single place, you are probably in Gabes.

title: Tunisia - Medinine Sandy Hills (Plonkit)
description: On the P1 road northwest of Medinine, you can occasionally find sandy hills that look like this. These hills are quite unique, as most coverage in southern Tunisia is in very flat areas.

title: Tunisia - Sousse Offroad (Plonkit)
description: An offroad from road P12 southwest of Sousse can be recognised by the dark pavement surrounded by bright sandy soil combined with the east-west road angle. The eastern part of the road is fairly vegetated, with large numbers of prickly pears, while the western part of the road is very arid with little to no vegetation.

title: Tunisia - Djerba Causeway (Plonkit)
description: You can easily recognise the Djerba-Zarzis causeway thanks to the water on both sides and the pipeline that is always present to your west.

title: Tunisia - Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: Trekkers can be found all over the country, even in places far away from the area with car coverage. Coverage includes archaeological sites, forts, mosques, and a Star Wars set, among other things.

title: Uganda - Limited Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Uganda has very limited coverage, with most of the coverage in the capital city of Kampala and the nearby city of Entebbe. The rest of the coverage is located in the various national parks that will be covered below.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Uganda - Driving Side (Plonkit)
description: Uganda drives on the left hand side of the road.

title: Uganda - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Uganda uses white front plates with yellow rear plates. These plates can be long or tall.

title: Uganda - Kampala Car (Plonkit)
description: In all coverage in Kampala, a unique Google car is visible. This car is white with square side mirrors and a boxy look.

title: Uganda - Kampala Vibe (Plonkit)
description: Kampala is a fairly busy-looking city, with many signs, narrow unpaved roads and typically fairly small, one-storey houses. Like many African countries, houses will often be surrounded by tall walls, commonly with barbed wire on top.

title: Uganda - Kampala Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: Like most of the national park coverage, Kampalan soil is typically very red. Even paved roads normally have a noticeable red, purple or pink tinge.

title: Uganda - Kampala Hills (Plonkit)
description: Kampala is a very hilly city, and as such it is rare to get a round without elevation or noticeable hills.

title: Uganda - Taxi Buses (Plonkit)
description: Throughout Kampala, you will often see these taxi buses, with a blue blocky pattern on the sides. These are a good clue for the city if you are not able to see the Google car.

title: Uganda - City Centre Curbs (Plonkit)
description: In the city centre of Kampala, you will see paved roads with black-and-white curbs. In contrast to the rest of the city, the city centre looks richer and very built-up, with lots of multi-storey buildings.

title: Uganda - Entebbe Vibe (Plonkit)
description: The city of Entebbe, southwest of Kampala, can often be recognized by feeling slightly emptier than most of the capital, with more greenery and somewhat fancier houses. The area also has significantly more street signs than the rest of the capital.

title: Uganda - National Park Car (Plonkit)
description: Most coverage in the Ugandan national parks was taken with this Street View car, which is similar to the one seen in Kampala, but with a black bar along the front of the car. The visibility of the car varies greatly, and it is somewhat common for it to not be visible at all.

title: Uganda - Kidepo Savannah (Plonkit)
description: The National Park is located in the northeastern parts of the country and mostly consists of a large savannah with mountains being visible in most directions. The most recognizable mountain range can be seen to the east and is visible in most of the coverage.

title: Uganda - Kidepo South Forest (Plonkit)
description: The southern half of the north road in Kidepo is somewhat forested, and as such it may occasionally be hard to see the various mountains.

title: Uganda - Kidepo North Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The northern half of the north road in Kidepo is located in a savannah and can be easily recognised by the wide mountain to the north.

title: Uganda - Murchison Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The National Park is located by the northern end of Lake Albert and can commonly be recognized by the low dirt barriers along the side of the roads. A savannah can be seen in the western part, while the eastern parts contain many small trees and bushes. Apart from a fairly low and wide mountain range far away to the west, there are no mountains in the vicinity.

title: Uganda - Murchison Palms (Plonkit)
description: Seeing these palms in Uganda means you are extremely likely to be in the northern parts of Murchison Falls.

title: Uganda - Kibale Wide Road (Plonkit)
description: The National Park has three types of coverage, the first of which is a very wide dirt road going through a dense, tropical forest. It is by far the widest dirt road in the country outside of Kampala with Street View coverage.

title: Uganda - Kibale Small Road (Plonkit)
description: The second type of coverage in Kibale is on a small forest road, which is still large enough to be covered using a car. The forest appears to be quite dense, however it is typically not very dark. The area is mostly flat.

title: Uganda - Kibale Forest Paths (Plonkit)
description: The final type of coverage is a number of tiny forest paths. The coverage is somewhat dark, with the sun shining through every so often.

title: Uganda - Lake Mburo Dry Grass (Plonkit)
description: The park is located west of lake Victoria and has by far the driest coverage in the country. The grass is almost always completely dried out, which is normally enough to recognise it. Bushes and trees along the road also typically look very dry. The area is quite hilly, but not mountainous.

title: Uganda - Semuliki Forest (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in the national park consists of two small forest paths running parallel to each other. The forest appears very humid, and on much of the coverage, drops of water can be seen on the camera lens.

title: Uganda - Mt Elgon Forest (Plonkit)
description: The national park is located near the Kenyan border and has two stretches of paths covered, the first of which is in a forest with a fairly steep slope heading upwards to the east. The dirt typically has a very dark red colour.

title: Uganda - Mt Elgon Open Hilly (Plonkit)
description: The eastern stretch of path covered is easily recognized by its small palm-like trees on an open hilly field and a man following the photographer, who is dressed in green and holding a rifle.

title: Uganda - QE Brown Dirt (Plonkit)
description: Queen Elizabeth National Park, north of Lake Edward, is one of the only places in Uganda where you will commonly see dirt which is not red. Instead, the dirt will typically be either brown or greyish.

title: Uganda - QE Cacti (Plonkit)
description: On top of the brown dirt, the national park also contains large cacti with many branches going almost straight upwards, resembling the shape of trees.

title: Uganda - QE Craters (Plonkit)
description: On the northern coverage, it is common to see large, water-filled craters. Similar craters cannot be found elsewhere in the country.

title: Uganda - QE Paved Road (Plonkit)
description:
The only paved road with coverage outside Kampala can be found here. The pavement almost entirely lacks the red tinge which is typical for most roads in the country. The road has white, solid outer lines and a yellow middle line.
A power line runs parallel to the road, to your east. To your north, you will be able to see hills.

title: Uganda - Katwe Village (Plonkit)
description: Katwe village is the only significant settlement outside of Kampala with Street View coverage.

title: Uganda - Limited Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Uganda has very limited coverage, with most of the coverage in the capital city of Kampala and the nearby city of Entebbe. The rest of the coverage is located in the various national parks that will be covered below.

Note: Because the coverage in Uganda is limited, this guide is structured differently than most of the other country guides, with two separate sections for Kampala and the National Parks. These sections also include most of the tips needed to identify the country.

You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Antarctica - Snow and Ice (Plonkit)
description: Most of Antarctica is covered in snow and ice.

title: Antarctica - Dark Soil (Plonkit)
description: The soil will always be dark.

title: Antarctica - Penguins (Plonkit)
description: Penguins can be found on parts of the coverage.

title: Antarctica - Half Moon Island (Plonkit)
description: Half Moon Island was covered by a tripod. It can also be recognized by the numerous other people in red jackets.

title: Antarctica - Deception Island Bay (Plonkit)
description: The Deception Island Bay can be recognized by the blue and white ship in the bay, and the abandoned equipment on the beach.

title: Antarctica - Deception Island Trekker (Plonkit)
description: The trekker can be seen walking in a line on Deception Island.

title: Antarctica - Deception Island Beach (Plonkit)
description: A beach with black sand and many penguins can be seen on Deception Island.

title: Antarctica - Cuverville Island (Plonkit)
description: Cuverville Island can be recognised by the overcast weather combined with the coastline to the northwest. You’ll also see a decent number of penguins, particularly toward the east.

title: Antarctica - Danco Island (Plonkit)
description: Danco Island can be recognised by the beautiful sunset coverage over a snowy fjord.

title: Antarctica - Petermann Island (Plonkit)
description: Petermann Island can be recognized by the layer of snow with patches of exposed rocks, and the overexposed camera.

title: Antarctica - Ross Island West (Plonkit)
description: The coverage at the western tip of Ross Island can typically be recognised by the extremely dark, and mostly barren, rocky soil.

title: Antarctica - Ross Island Cabin (Plonkit)
description: A tripod featuring the exterior and interior of a small wooden cabin with a grey metal roof can be found south of the eastern tip of Ross Island.

title: Antarctica - McMurdo Station (Plonkit)
description: McMurdo Station is the largest research station on Antarctica, and can be recognized by the dark brown soil, many buildings, American infrastructure and sunset coverage.

title: Antarctica - McMurdo Interiors (Plonkit)
description: You can also find tripod coverage inside several buildings at McMurdo Station.

title: Antarctica - McMurdo Hut (Plonkit)
description: On the eastern side of McMurdo Station you can find a small wooden cabin, having a tripod going inside.

title: Antarctica - McMurdo Ice Trekker (Plonkit)
description: Southeast of McMurdo station, the trekker can be seen walking on a layer of ice around various machinery.

title: Antarctica - Mainland Valleys (Plonkit)
description: The trekker can be seen walking through a fantastical landscape consisting of many desolate valleys on mainland Antarctica, west of Ross Island.

title: Antarctica - South of McMurdo (Plonkit)
description: A vast, snowy landscape with spread out hills can be seen south of McMurdo station.

title: Antarctica - South Pole (Plonkit)
description:
The tripod at the south pole can be recognized by numerous countries’ flags around the tripod, and a sign with ‘Geographic South Pole’ written on it.
This location is often on community-made world maps for a better scoring range.

title: Antarctica - South Pole Observatory (Plonkit)
description: The South Pole Observatory has tripod coverage going around and inside of it.

title: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands are a British Overseas Territory east of the Falkland Islands. As such, for country streaks purposes, they are counted as the UK.
Coverage is very limited: there are only a couple of Generation 3 trekkers:
- One trekker in the abandoned town of Grytviken
- Three trekkers in the isolated fjords of the rest of the island.
Due to the sparse nature of the coverage, that is also entirely not on any streets, it is not useful to learn any territory identification metas. Instead, it is better to just memorise what the trekkers look like.

title: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands - Grytviken Machinery (Plonkit)
description:
Abandoned, rusted machinery can be seen in Grytviken.
Grytviken is the only pinpointable trekker in South Georgia. Therefore, this trekker appears in pinpointable maps like A Community World.

title: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands - Grytviken Church (Plonkit)
description: A church and another building made of white painted wood can also be seen in Grytviken.

title: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands - West Side Valley (Plonkit)
description: This wide open valley with lightly snow capped mountains can be seen on the west side of South Georgia Island.

title: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands - Prion Island (Plonkit)
description: Prion Island can be recognized by the wooden walkway, lush green plants and numerous seals which inhabit the island.

title: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands - Hercules Bay Boat (Plonkit)
description: This boat trekker in Hercules Bay can be recognized by a man in a red jacket and the MS National Geographic Explorer in the background.

title: Bangladesh - License Plates (White/Black/Turquoise) (Plonkit)
description: Bangladeshi licence plates are either white, black or turquoise.

title: Bangladesh - Bengali Script (Horizontal Line/Triangles) (Plonkit)
description: The Bengali script features a continuous horizontal line at the top of each word. It has a similar look to Devanagari (Hindi), however it can usually be recognised by the many letters featuring triangular shapes.

title: Bangladesh - Gen 3 Cars (Red Mirror/Classic/Striped) (Plonkit)
description: In Generation 3 coverage, these three cars can be seen in Bangladesh: the red mirror with bars, classic white and striped white car.

title: Bangladesh - Gen 4 Cars (Black/White) (Plonkit)
description: In Generation 4 coverage, two Street View cars can be seen in Bangladesh: a black car and a white car.

title: Bangladesh - Shitcam (Black/White Car) (Plonkit)
description: Bangladesh, as well as a variety of other countries, has received some poor quality coverage, also known as “Shitcam”. The Shitcam car colours are black and white.

title: Bangladesh - Rickshaws (Green Auto) (Plonkit)
description: Rickshaws are frequently found all around Bangladesh, especially the green auto rickshaws.

title: Bangladesh - Signposts (Black & White Stripes) (Plonkit)
description: Signposts in Bangladesh often have black-and-white stripes.

title: Bangladesh - Water Bodies and Fields (Plonkit)
description: Bodies of water and agricultural fields can be often seen beside the streets of Bangladesh.

title: Bangladesh - Tree Paint (White Bottoms) (Plonkit)
description: Streets in Bangladesh are often lined by trees, which sometimes have white paint on the bottom of their trunks.

title: Bangladesh - Concrete Bollards (Red & White) (Plonkit)
description: Bangladesh uses red-and-white concrete bollards throughout the whole country.

title: Bangladesh - Tin Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Tin roofs are commonly found in Bangladesh.

title: Bangladesh - Gen 4 Smoky Quality (Plonkit)
description: The Generation 4 coverage in Bangladesh will often have a smoky feel to it.

title: Bangladesh - Western Roofs (Hip/Sheet Metal) (Plonkit)
description:
Bangladesh has several distinct roof styles that create an east/west divide in the country.
The west, particularly the divisions of Rajshahi, Khulna and Dhaka, is dominated by hip roofs made of sheet metal. The states of Rangpur and Chittagong tend to have mixed roofs.

title: Bangladesh - Eastern Roofs (Triangular Window) (Plonkit)
description: In the east, you will commonly see sheet metal roofs with a triangular "window" just below the ridge of the roof. The state of Sylhet will exclusively have this style, which can also be seen in Chittagong, Mymensingh, eastern Rangpur and northern Dhaka.

title: Bangladesh - Tiled Roofs (Khulna/Indian Border) (Plonkit)
description: Tiled roofs are uncommon in Bangladesh, but the ones you do see are of West Bengal origin, and are thus only found on the Indian border in the state of Khulna.

title: Bangladesh - Rice: Early Growth (Short Green) (Plonkit)
description:
Rice is the main agricultural crop in Bangladesh and is planted twice a year. The different rice seasons can be told apart by the height and colour of the rice and are very useful for regionguessing.
Short green rice that is barely sticking out of the water is known as early growth rice. Early growth rice can be seen in the states of Khulna, Mymensingh and south of Padma River in Dhaka.

title: Bangladesh - Rice: Mid Growth (Green) (Plonkit)
description: Slightly taller rice, in the middle of growing, which still remains green, can be seen in the states of Rangpur, Barishal and Chittagong.

title: Bangladesh - Rice: Fully Grown (Yellow/Tall) (Plonkit)
description: Fully-grown rice is characterised by being noticeably taller, as well as having a yellow or orange colour and fluffier tips - the fluffiness signifies that the rice is ripe. Fully-grown rice is mostly seen in the state of Rajshahi, but it is also present in Rangpur and Chittagong.

title: Bangladesh - Rice: Harvested (Beige/Cut) (Plonkit)
description: Harvested rice can be identified by its beige or brown colour and shorter, cut down appearance. It can be seen alongside fully-grown, unharvested rice as well as freshly planted early growth rice in adjacent fields. This is most commonly seen in the states of Sylhet and southern Khulna.

title: Bangladesh - Rice: Off-Season (Barren Fields) (Plonkit)
description: Rice fields require some rest time, so it's natural to come across some off-season barren, empty fields without rice altogether. Off-season fields are mostly seen in the state of Dhaka, north of Padma River.

title: Bangladesh - Vast Empty Rice Fields (Plonkit)
description: Vast rice fields with almost nothing else in view can be seen in the border area between the states of Dhaka, Mymensingh and Sylhet.

title: Bangladesh - Chittagong Hills (Plonkit)
description: While most of Bangladesh is almost completely flat, in the eastern parts of Chittagong you may find fairly tall, forested and uncultivated hills.

title: Bangladesh - Sylhet Ridge (Indian Border) (Plonkit)
description: A sizable east-west ridge can be seen on the Indian border from the northern parts of Sylhet and eastern Mymensingh. It is often obscured or diminished by heavy haze.

title: Bangladesh - Corn Fields (West) (Plonkit)
description:
Corn tends to be planted in the west of Bangladesh - large and medium-sized fields can be found in Rajshahi, Rangpur, western Mymensingh and northern Khulna.
Smaller patches of corn can be found in the south of Barishal, usually adjacent to other crops.

title: Bangladesh - Jute (Rangpur) (Plonkit)
description: Jute is a tall-growing green crop which gets dried and used in the making of rugs, bags and other goods. Because of when the coverage was taken, jute can almost exclusively be found on Street View in Rangpur. In its dried state it can be found hanging off fences and drying on the roads anywhere in the country.

title: Bangladesh - Canola (Yellow Flowers) (Plonkit)
description: Canola is a low-growing crop with yellow flowers that is used to make cooking oil. It is usually planted during the off-season for rice, making it extremely common north of Padma river in the state of Dhaka.

title: Bangladesh - Tea Plantations (Sylhet) (Plonkit)
description: Tea production in Bangladesh is concentrated in the highlands of southern Sylhet and, rarely, Chittagong.

title: Bangladesh - Fruit Orchards (Rajshahi/Rangpur) (Plonkit)
description: Standalone fruit trees in Bangladesh are most commonly seen in the states of Rajshahi and Rangpur. Fruit orchards with systematically planted trees, however, are concentrated near the Indian border in both states.

title: Bangladesh - Sunflower Fields (Barishal) (Plonkit)
description: Sunflower fields are found in the south of Barishal state.

title: Bangladesh - Watermelon Fields (Barishal) (Plonkit)
description: Fields of watermelons can also be found in the south of Barishal.

title: Bangladesh - Eucalyptus Trees (North) (Plonkit)
description: Eucalyptus trees are tall trees with lush crowns and ivory-coloured trunks. In Bangladesh they are more common in the north, with Rangpur, Rajshahi and Mymensingh being the most likely states.

title: Bangladesh - Blossoming Trees (Spring Coverage) (Plonkit)
description: Blossoming trees are tied to coverage and seasonal metas in Bangladesh, and are only found in the states where coverage was taken during spring time - Khulna, Mymensingh and southern Dhaka.

title: Bangladesh - Beach Sheoaks (Coastal) (Plonkit)
description: Beach Sheoaks (Casuarina equisetifolia) are thin evergreen trees with thin, long, drooping branchlets. Like the name suggests, they are mostly observed in coastal regions - along the coast of the Teknaf Peninsula and around Noakhali city in Chittagong.

title: Bangladesh - Copyright 2022 (Mymensingh/Dhaka) (Plonkit)
description: For legal reasons, Google has added small labels noting their copyright on all Street View coverage. These labels contain a year, typically the year when the coverage was released, which can be used to regionguess Bangladesh. Generation 4 coverage with 2022 written on the copyright labels can be found in Mymensingh, Dhaka and less commonly Chittagong.

title: Bangladesh - Copyright 2023 (North/South/Sylhet) (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, Generation 4 coverage with 2023 written on the copyright labels can be found in Rangpur, Rajshahi, Khulna, Barishal, Sylhet and less commonly Chittagong.

title: Bangladesh - Shitcam Map (Dhaka) (Plonkit)
description: Shitcam coverage is only found in and around Dhaka.

title: Bangladesh - White Car Gen 3 Map (Plonkit)
description: Generation 3 coverage with the white Street View car can be found in Dhaka, Chattogram as well as on the highway connecting them.

title: Bangladesh - Striped Car Gen 3 Map (Plonkit)
description: Generation 3 coverage with the striped Street View car can be found mostly on yellow roads west of Dhaka.

title: Bangladesh - Sylhet Guard with Hayfork (Plonkit)
description: In the city of Sylhet there will often be a guard at the side of the car visible, usually holding a hayfork. Note that this only applies to Generation 3 coverage.

title: Bangladesh - Barishal Guard (Plonkit)
description: In the city of Barishal there can also be a guard at the side of the car visible, not to be confused with the Sylhet guard.

title: Bangladesh - Khulna Black Cover Trekker (Plonkit)
description: This interesting trekker with a black cover can be found in the city of Khulna.

title: Bangladesh - Nijhum Dwip Red Mirror Trekker (Plonkit)
description: The trekker with red colour in the mirrors is unique to the island of Nijhum Dwip.

title: Bangladesh - Hatiya Island Scooter (Plonkit)
description: A scooter trekker, where mostly the left mirror and some hair is visible, can be found on Hatiya Island.

title: Bangladesh - Saint Martin's Island Guard Trekker (Plonkit)
description: A trekker escorted by a security guard is found on Saint Martin's Island.

title: Bhutan - Red License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Licence plates in Bhutan are almost always red and can easily be seen on vehicles.

title: Bhutan - Grey Google Car (No Antenna) (Plonkit)
description: Coverage in Bhutan was taken by a grey Google car without an antenna.

title: Bhutan - Stone Block Barriers (Plonkit)
description:
Bhutan commonly uses these stone blocks as safety barriers on winding rural roads. These blocks are very common and often one of the best ways to recognize rural Bhutan rounds.
Guardrails, on the other hand, are rare.

title: Bhutan - Traditional Architecture (Tin Roofs/Wood) (Plonkit)
description: The traditional Bhutanese architecture is very distinct. Most of the houses have tin roofs and wooden painted frames, which give them a unique look.

title: Bhutan - Dzongkha Script (Plonkit)
description: Dzongkha is an official language in Bhutan and has unique-looking letters.

title: Bhutan - Mountainous Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Bhutan is a mountainous country and most of the coverage is located on its main mountain roads.

title: Bhutan - Prayer Flags (Plonkit)
description: Prayer flags near the road are typically seen in Bhutan.

title: Bhutan - Thin Metal Poles (Black Bottoms) (Plonkit)
description: Thin metal poles are occasionally found in Bhutan. They are often painted black at the bottom.

title: Bhutan - Bhutanese Road Markers (Plonkit)
description:
These are the Bhutanese road markers, notice the yellow top and the white bottom.
On national highways, the road number is found on the top of the marker, but is not labelled on the map. However, it can still be used to identify the road using this table.

title: Bhutan - Town Signs (Blue/Red) (Plonkit)
description: These signs are frequently found in the cities of Bhutan and are often coloured red or blue.

title: Bhutan - Taxis (Yellow Roof/Plate) (Plonkit)
description: Taxis in Bhutan have yellow licence plates and yellow roofs.

title: Bhutan - Signposts (Black & White Stripes) (Plonkit)
description: Signposts in Bhutan frequently have black-and-white stripes.

title: Bhutan - Coverage Map (Main Roads) (Plonkit)
description: Most of the Bhutanese street view coverage was taken on the main roads and cities.

title: Bhutan - Double White Lines (Plonkit)
description: Two solid white outside lines are only seen in western Bhutan south and close to the capital Thimphu.

title: Bhutan - Flat Southern Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Flat landscapes like this in Bhutan can only be found in the south.

title: Bhutan - Phobjikha Valley (Plonkit)
description: The Phobjikha Valley, south of Nubding, is a wide and relatively flat agricultural valley. It is by far the largest open valley with no major river visible on Street View.

title: Bhutan - Haa Vehicle Hook (Plonkit)
description: A hook can be seen on the back of the car in Haa District, mainly in the town of Ha.

title: Bhutan - Late Sunset (Mongar/Paro) (Plonkit)
description: Late sunset coverage can be found in two places in the country; on a small rural sideroad in the east of Mongar District and in a significantly more urban area around the town of Paro in the west.

title: Bhutan - Gelephu Airport (Plonkit)
description: Gelephu Airport is the only airport located in the flat south part of Bhutan, making it recognisable.

title: Bhutan - Paro Airport (Dry Valley) (Plonkit)
description: The Paro International Airport is located in a dry northwest valley and is one of the two northern airports.

title: Bhutan - Bumthang Airport (Wet Valley) (Plonkit)
description: While the Paro International Airport is located in a dry northwest valley, the Bumthang Domestic Airport is located in a wet northern valley.

title: Bhutan - Road Markers (Yellow Top/White Bottom) (Plonkit)
description: These are the Bhutanese road markers, notice the yellow top and the white bottom.

title: British Indian Ocean Territory - UK Overseas Territory (Plonkit)
description:
The British Indian Ocean Territory is an United Kingdom overseas territory in the Indian Ocean. As such, it is counted as the UK for country streaks purposes.
Beware that none of the coverage is considered pinpointable, and as a result you are unlikely to get it in most community-made maps. As such, this guide is mainly intended to give a general idea of what type of coverage you can find on the islands.

title: British Indian Ocean Territory - Gen 3 Trekker (Plonkit)
description: Coverage was taken with a Generation 3 trekker.

title: British Indian Ocean Territory - Northern Atolls Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Coverage is mostly found on small atolls in the northern half of the territory.

title: British Indian Ocean Territory - Sand Beaches (Palms) (Plonkit)
description: A large portion of the coverage is taken on sand beaches. You will typically see many palm trees along the beaches.

title: British Indian Ocean Territory - Coconut Palm Forests (Plonkit)
description: Coastal palm forests also comprise a significant portion of the coverage. They almost exclusively consist of coconut palms.

title: British Indian Ocean Territory - Mangroves (Plonkit)
description: Mangroves can be found on several of the atolls.

title: British Indian Ocean Territory - Grassy Fields (Plonkit)
description: Some of the larger islands with coverage have grassy fields surrounded by bushes and palms.

title: British Indian Ocean Territory - Offshore Water Trekker (Plonkit)
description: The trekker can occasionally be found walking offshore in the water.

title: British Indian Ocean Territory - Coin du Mire (Plonkit)
description: Coin du Mire is a small island with a dark rocky shore and a grassy field with no bushes or palm trees.

title: British Indian Ocean Territory - Nelsons Island Shipwreck (Plonkit)
description: A white medium-sized shipwreck can be found on the beach at the eastern tip of Nelsons Island.

title: Cambodia - License Plates (White/Blue Text) (Plonkit)
description:
Licence plates are white with blue letters. The blue sheen of the letters can be hard to see through the blur, and the plates might appear as plain white.
Plates on government vehicles are green.

title: Cambodia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
On the Generation 3 coverage you can find two different Google cars:
- A car with a short, stubby antenna. The antenna has three ridges. It can sometimes be hard to tell if the antenna has ridges.
- A white car with stripes and no antenna. There is a white stripe on the left, and a yellow stripe on the right. The stripes are sometimes poorly visible.
The car is not always as visible as shown in the example images.
The Latin American countries of Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador and Brazil also have cars with similar short antennas. However, these have a diagonally coiled ridge, instead of Cambodia’s three ridges.

title: Cambodia - Driving Side (Right) (Plonkit)
description: Cambodia drives on the right.

title: Cambodia - Khmer Script (Plonkit)
description:
Khmer is the official language of Cambodia. It has its own unique script, which is very distinct and recognizable. In most fonts, letters have an intricate, curvy look.
Khmer can look fairly different depending on the font used. A compilation of what this script looks like in street view can be found here.

title: Cambodia - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Two types of poles are common:
- Concrete ladder poles (so named because the indents and ridges resemble a ladder).
- Round concrete poles with small holes.
Rarely, you might see simple wooden poles.
You can easily distinguish between Thailand and Cambodia based on the poles. Thailand uses square concrete poles with rows of small pinholes on the sides. Such poles are very uncommon in Cambodia (but not completely absent).

title: Cambodia - Bollards (Red & White/Stone) (Plonkit)
description:
Cambodia has a variety of different bollards. The most common ones are:
- A stone bollard with red-and-white stripes.
- A stone bollard with a red top and a white base, usually with a reflector in the red part.
Some bollards are unique to a road or region. More details can be found in the region-guessing section.

title: Cambodia - Road Markers (White/Red Top) (Plonkit)
description: Cambodian road markers are made of stone, with a white-coloured base and a rounded red top. You will find the road number on the narrow side and a town name with a distance on the main side.

title: Cambodia - Chevrons (Black/Yellow Arrows) (Plonkit)
description:
Chevrons in Cambodia are black with yellow arrows.
Chevrons are somewhat rare. On many occasions, Cambodia prefers to use bollards instead of chevrons to mark curves in the road.

title: Cambodia - Road Lines (Yellow Middle/White Outer) (Plonkit)
description: Roads have dashed or solid yellow middle road lines. Outer road lines are somewhat rare, but when present, they are solid white.

title: Cambodia - Unpaved Roads (Plonkit)
description: Many roads are unpaved. Usually, only main roads and roads in and near urban areas are paved.

title: Cambodia - Stilt Houses (Plonkit)
description: Wooden houses on stilts are common. Walls are often made of vertical planks. Many homes have double or triple roofs.

title: Cambodia - House Colors (Red/Blue/Orange) (Plonkit)
description:
In addition, traditional Cambodian wooden stilt houses tend to have very recognizable colour schemes.
- Walls are commonly painted dark red-brown, light blue or an ochre orange.
- Doors, windows and other architectural details are often painted bright blue.

title: Cambodia - Roofs (Tiled/Metal) (Plonkit)
description:
Many traditional homes have tiled orange or red roofs, sometimes with ornaments on the ridges and corners. Corrugated and plain metal roofs are also common.
On other, more modern buildings, you can see a wider variety of roof colours and materials.

title: Cambodia - Buddhist Temples (Plonkit)
description: The majority of Cambodians are Buddhist. Temples are common throughout the country. Temple architecture is highly decorative, with ornamented roofs. You might also see Buddhist flags.

title: Cambodia - Beer Ads (Plonkit)
description: You will see a lot of advertisements for the beer brands Angkor, Anchor, and the very creatively named Cambodia Beer.

title: Cambodia - CPP Party Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Throughout the country, you can find distinct blue signs from the Cambodian People’s Party (CPP).
These signs occasionally feature the likenesses of major party politicians: usually three men side by side.

title: Cambodia - Shitcam (Ari) (Plonkit)
description: Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Cambodia. This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”). It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours. A good map will not usually include this coverage, but it is good to be aware of its existence, in order to not be caught off-guard by it.

title: Cambodia - Coverage Map (Cities) (Plonkit)
description:
Street view coverage is somewhat limited. Most of the coverage is located around the cities of Phnom Penh, Siem Reap and Battambang.
You can click on the image to enlarge it. You can also view the official street view coverage in more detail on this site.

title: Cambodia - Shitcam Map (Southwest) (Plonkit)
description: Shitcam in Cambodia is only found in the southwestern half.

title: Cambodia - Central Plain (Plonkit)
description: The low-lying central plain is home to most agricultural land. The landscape is flat, cultivated, and dotted with villages and farms.

title: Cambodia - Northeast Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Conversely, the northeast is much more uncultivated: there is less agriculture and more natural vegetation. Some areas are slightly hilly.

title: Cambodia - Southwest Landscape (Hills) (Plonkit)
description: The southwest is the area with the most elevation in Cambodia. This region is characterized by hills and low mountains. Some inland roads feature dense forest cover, but the coastal areas in particular are fairly densely populated.

title: Cambodia - White Sandy Soil (Southeast) (Plonkit)
description: Sandy, white soil is very common in the region southeast of Phnom Penh, as well as around the city itself. The colour can range from bright white to slightly beige.

title: Cambodia - Thai Border Mountains (Plonkit)
description:
Near the northern border with Thailand, you can often see a mountainous ridgeline to your north. The soil in this region tends to be red, ranging from a slight reddish tinge to deep dark red.
The ridgeline closely corresponds with the border with Thailand. The drop-off to the Cambodian lowland to its south is abrupt. This means that the roads you are on are themselves located in a very flat landscape (see inset map).

title: Cambodia - Rubber Plantations (Plonkit)
description:
Rubber tree plantations are found in three places:
- In a narrow belt northeast of Phnom Penh, mostly centred around the southern sections of Roads 7 and 71
- Around the town of Ban Lung in the far northeast, as well as east of it on and near Road 78.
- Around the town of Pech Sreada. This area has a distinct look. See the tip in the spotlight section.
Rubber trees can be recognized by their thin trunks and dark green crowns. The trees are neatly arranged in rows. They often have small taps near the bottom of the trunk.

title: Cambodia - Thai-Style Bollards (Road 48) (Plonkit)
description: Black-and-white bollards in Cambodia are only found on Road 48, between Tatai and the intersection with Road 4.

title: Cambodia - Kiri Sakor Construction (Plonkit)
description: The road between Road 48 and Kiri Sakor is under construction and only has one paved road side. The unpaved side has red soil.

title: Cambodia - Southwest Jungle Roads (Plonkit)
description: Several unpaved jungle offroads in the southwest of the country, northeast of Road 48, have a distinct look: red soil, dense jungle, and generally hilly terrain.

title: Cambodia - Phnum Samkos Area (Plonkit)
description: The coverage close to Phnum Samkos has a distinct look: overcast weather, and large, prominent mountains that are visible in the distance. The roads are unpaved and consist of brown soil. Wild, very green vegetation can be seen all around you.

title: Cambodia - Triangular Red Stripe Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
Unique triangular bollards with red stripes can be found in three places in Cambodia, all located in the same area in the southwest:
- On Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk. They are especially common in the section between Kirirom National Park and Preah Sihanouk.
- One small off-road of Road 4, in Ream National Park near Preah Sihanouk.
- In Preah Monivong National Park.

title: Cambodia - Road 4 Wide Red Shoulders (Plonkit)
description: There is another good way to recognize Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk: in most sections, it has a distinctive wide, red-brownish shoulder on both sides of the road.

title: Cambodia - Oil Palms (Road 4) (Plonkit)
description: Oil palm plantations can only be found on Road 4, as well as some of its rural offroads, just north of Preah Nob.

title: Cambodia - Preah Monivong NP (Plonkit)
description: Preah Monivong National Park in the south of the country has a unique and recognizable landscape. It is situated on a highland plateau. The soil is white and very rocky. The vegetation consists of stunted, windswept bushes and low trees. The foliage has a distinct dark green tint that contrasts with the white rocks. Some parts of the park are more forested but will still have the same rocky soil.

title: Cambodia - Road 41 (Gravelly/NNE) (Plonkit)
description:
Road 41, southwest of Phnom Penh, has a recognizable look and road angle:
- It is a wide road, with a grey and very gravelly road surface
- It runs in a general NNE direction
- The landscape close to the road is flat and agricultural. However, you can often see hills in the distance.

title: Cambodia - Unique Poles (1-Side Insulators) (Plonkit)
description: In the sections of Road 6 west of Siem Reap, to Sisophon, and Road 5, south of Sisophon to Krong Battambang, you can find power lines with unique poles that are found nowhere else in Cambodia. The pole tops have three horizontal beams, with hanging insulators on only one side. The bottom of the poles have indents.

title: Cambodia - Unique Poles (2-Side Insulators) (Plonkit)
description: The powerline from the previous tip continues on the section of Road 5 west of Sisophon. However, here the pole tops have insulators on both sides. The rest of the pole is identical however.

title: Cambodia - Road 76 South (Plonkit)
description: The southern section of Road 76, south of Krong Saen Monourom, has recognizable coverage: overcast weather, dark asphalt, the presence of outer road lines, and relatively crisp lines for Cambodian standards. Furthermore, a large part of the eastern half of this road runs through hilly terrain with dense jungle.

title: Cambodia - Road 76 North (Plonkit)
description:
Most of the northern section of Road 76, between Lumphat and Mayura Wild Park, is recognizable too: it is a wide, unpaved road, with brown soil, and a semi-open jungle forest all around you.
Weather conditions start off as overcast on the southern end of the road, and quickly improve the further north you go, with almost completely clear skies on the northern end.

title: Cambodia - Preah Features (Plonkit)
description: Bilingual signs with Chinese writing can commonly be found in Preah Sihanouk.

title: Cambodia - Pech Sreada Rubber (Plonkit)
description: Around the town of Pech Sreada, in the far east of Cambodia, you can find rubber tree plantations that were covered during the dry season, leading to a distinct look. In addition, the soil is very orange, making it easy to distinguish this area from other regions in Cambodia with rubber tree plantations.

title: Cambodia - Angkor Wat (Plonkit)
description: Angkor Wat is a massive temple complex built by the historical Khmer Empire. It is located just north of Siem Reap and has extensive trekker coverage. It can be recognized by its dark, weathered stone buildings. While this location is unlikely to show up in competitive maps, it is extremely common in GeoGuessr’s official Cambodia map.

title: Cambodia - Gen 3 Cars (Stubby Antenna/Striped) (Plonkit)
description:
On the Generation 3 coverage you can find two different Google cars:

A car with a short, stubby antenna. The antenna has three ridges. It can sometimes be hard to tell if the antenna has ridges.

A white car with stripes and no antenna. There is a white stripe on the left, and a yellow stripe on the right. The stripes are sometimes poorly visible.

The car is not always as visible as shown in the example images.

title: Cambodia - Poles (Ladder/Round with Holes) (Plonkit)
description:
Two types of poles are common:

Concrete ladder poles (so named because the indents and ridges resemble a ladder).

Round concrete poles with small holes.

Rarely, you might see simple wooden poles.

title: China - All Official Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
All official coverage in mainland China is taken with a tripod. Objects in the image will usually have motion blur, and slightly saturated colours.
A separate Plonk It guide to Hong Kong can be found here. The Macau guide can be found here.

title: China - Simplified Chinese (Plonkit)
description: Chinese writing consists of often complicated symbols made up of several strokes. On mainland China, you’ll typically find simplified Chinese, where the number of strokes of many symbols have been greatly reduced compared to traditional Chinese.

title: China - License Plates (Blue/White Text) (Plonkit)
description: Chinese licence plates are blue with white text.

title: China - Coverage Map (East Coast) (Plonkit)
description: Coverage in mainland China is limited to several small spots, mainly in or near major urban areas on the east coast. A significant portion of the coverage is considered hidden, which is also shown on this map. Hidden means it won’t show up on Google Maps, however you can still access it in the Map Making App.

title: China - Museums (Beijing/Shanghai) (Plonkit)
description: A significant portion of the coverage was taken inside museums and can be found in many cities, however a majority of the covered museums are located in and around Beijing and Shanghai.

title: China - Ancient Cities (Plonkit)
description: Ancient cities with coverage can be found along the east coast in Zhoucun, northeast of Xuzhou, in Yangzhou, west of Jiaxing and west of Zhangzhou.

title: China - Urban Coverage (Modern) (Plonkit)
description: Coverage taken outside in modern urban areas can be found in Beijing, Yangzhou, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Chengdu.

title: China - Forbidden City (Beijing) (Plonkit)
description: The Palace Museum (commonly referred to as the Forbidden City) is a massive palace in the centre of Beijing.

title: China - Today Art Museum (Beijing) (Plonkit)
description: By the Today Art Museum in Beijing you can find this modern urban street with several cafes and bars along the road. In front of the museum you can also find this uncanny statue.

title: China - Sichuan Museum (Chengdu) (Plonkit)
description: The parking area outside Sichuan Museum in Chengdu has a lot of greenery.

title: China - Hubei Museum (Wuhan) (Plonkit)
description: The Hubei Museum in Wuhan can be recognised by its palace-like architecture with grey roofs.

title: China - Silk Museum (Hangzhou) (Plonkit)
description: The Museum of silk production in Hangzhou can be recognised by the rounded glass facade and the fountain by the front.

title: China - Long Museum (Shanghai) (Plonkit)
description: Shanghai Long Museum can be recognised by the boxy concrete main building.

title: China - Suzhou Museum (Plonkit)
description: Suzhou Museum can be recognised by the white and grey symmetric angular architecture.

title: China - Yangzhou Museum (Plonkit)
description: The Yangzhou Museum can be recognised by the beige rounded stone building.

title: China - Zhoucun Ancient City (Plonkit)
description: The ancient city of Zhoucun is the only pinpointable ancient city in China, and can be recognised by the street going straight north to south.

title: China - Mainland Tripods (Motion Blur) (Plonkit)
description: All official coverage in mainland China is taken with a tripod. Objects in the image will usually have motion blur, and slightly saturated colours.

title: Hong Kong - Southern China SAR (Plonkit)
description:
Hong Kong is located in Southern China, sharing a border with the Guangdong province. It is a Chinese Special Administrative Region, so for country streaks purposes, it is counted as part of China.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Hong Kong - License Plates (White Front/Yellow Rear) (Plonkit)
description: Hong Kong has white front licence plates and yellow rear licence plates. The licence plates can be long or short. Some cars have an additional black mainland Chinese licence plate.

title: Hong Kong - Driving Side (Left) (Plonkit)
description: Hong Kong drives on the left.

title: Hong Kong - Urban Landscape (Dense/Skyscrapers) (Plonkit)
description:
Hong Kong is a densely populated city with millions of inhabitants. In urban areas, modern skyscrapers are common, with busy streets filled with vehicles and pedestrians.
The city has a unique vibe that you can quickly pick up on. In many cases, this vibe alone should be sufficient to identify urban Hong Kong locations.

title: Hong Kong - Rural Landscape (Mountainous/Green) (Plonkit)
description:
There is also a plethora of rural locations that are harder to identify.
Outside the urban areas, Hong Kong is generally quite mountainous, with green, subtropical vegetation. There is extensive coverage in rural areas outside the city, with many roads going through the mountains. You might see low-rise rural buildings, however usually you will not need to travel far to see tall apartment blocks.

title: Hong Kong - Tall Apartment Buildings (Plonkit)
description: One very striking aspect of Hong Kong architecture are the many extremely tall apartment buildings found throughout the city.

title: Hong Kong - Air Conditioners (Plonkit)
description: Because of the subtropical climate, air conditioners attached to the walls of apartments are very common in Hong Kong.

title: Hong Kong - Bilingual Signs (English/Chinese) (Plonkit)
description:
Hong Kong has two official languages: English and Chinese (legally, no variety is specified, but residents primarily speak Cantonese).
Bilingual signs are common, with English next to traditional Chinese characters.

title: Hong Kong - Grey Lamp Posts (Wide Base) (Plonkit)
description: Cylindrical grey lamp posts with a wide base are common. Many lamp posts have a white sticker.

title: Hong Kong - Rural Utility Poles (Wooden/Concrete) (Plonkit)
description: Utility poles will never be seen in urban rounds, however you might see cylindrical wooden poles in rural areas. The poles can be single or double, with electricity counters or transformers attached to them.

title: Hong Kong - No Striped Kerbs (Plonkit)
description: In Hong Kong, you will almost never see striped kerbs, which are extremely common in Singapore. In addition, grey pedestrian guardrails are also common.

title: Hong Kong - Yellow Road Markings (Crossings/Grids) (Plonkit)
description: Hong Kong uses yellow pedestrian crossings. Some intersections have yellow grids.

title: Hong Kong - Road Lines (White Center/Yellow Outer) (Plonkit)
description: Hong Kong usually uses white centre lines and white or yellow outer lines. These lines can be single, double or dashed. Roads are also commonly made of concrete. Yellow outer lines are most commonly found on small roads to indicate no-stopping.

title: Hong Kong - Road Signs (White Rectangular) (Plonkit)
description: Road signs are white and rectangular, with a thick black outline and bilingual text.

title: Hong Kong - Give Way Signs (Plonkit)
description: Give way signs feature a white upside down triangle with a thick red border and bilingual text.

title: Hong Kong - Rock Walls & Plaques (Plonkit)
description: Distinct weathered rock walls can be seen on the side of mountains. Some of them have nets, to prevent rockslides. In addition, green or blue plaques are a common sight.

title: Hong Kong - Fire Hydrants (Red/Yellow) (Plonkit)
description: Most fire hydrants are red, and usually have circular tops and three protrusions. There is also a pipe-like variant. Some fire hydrants have other colours, so make sure to look at their shape or other clues before guessing.

title: Hong Kong - Yellow Bollards (Blue Arrow) (Plonkit)
description: Yellow bollards with a white arrow in a blue circle are commonly seen at pedestrian crossings, but also elsewhere, indicating where cars should go. There is a flat and a cuboid version.

title: Hong Kong - Orange Bins (Plonkit)
description: Distinct bright orange bins can be found on sidewalks.

title: Hong Kong - Taxis (Red/Green/Blue) (Plonkit)
description:
Hong Kong taxis come in two variants: sedans or station wagons, with the sedans most commonly seen. They can be easily identified by their silver roofs, green stickers on the front and rear bumper, and the taxi sign on the roof.
Red taxis are most common on Hong Kong Island and Kowloon, green taxis in the New Territories in the northern region and blue taxis on Lantau Island and Chek Lap Kok. Keep in mind, Hong Kong is a small city and taxis travel all around it.

title: Hong Kong - Regional Buses (Plonkit)
description:
Buses in Hong Kong are mostly double-decker, with various colour schemes and adverts on the side. Single-decker versions do exist, but are less common. Smaller minibuses can also be seen, with a green or red roof.
Double-decker buses are also somewhat common in Singapore, but these will often have a recognizable light green colour scheme.

title: Hong Kong - Village Houses (Boxy) (Plonkit)
description: Boxy houses that are a few storeys high are a common sight in small villages, mostly to the north of Hong Kong.

title: Hong Kong - Double-Decker Trams (HK Island) (Plonkit)
description: A double-decker tram line runs along the north of Hong Kong Island. A full map of the route can be seen here.

title: Hong Kong - Light Rail (Northwest New Territories) (Plonkit)
description: The northwestern part of the New Territories is served by a distinct light rail system. It can be recognised by its green-and-orange platforms, single-level train cars and the fact that the tracks are separated from the street.

title: Hong Kong - Mong Kok (Dense/Gridded) (Plonkit)
description: Mong Kok and the surrounding districts in Kowloon can be recognized by the crowded, busy, gridded streets, with apartment blocks situated above the shops.

title: Hong Kong - Northwest New Territories (Flat/Paddies) (Plonkit)
description: The north-western area near the Mainland China border is mostly flat and features a patchwork of waterlogged rice paddies. The Shenzhen skyline is visible in the distance, to your north.

title: Hong Kong - Central District (Skyscrapers) (Plonkit)
description: The Central District can be recognized by the large concentration of modern skyscrapers. The district feels quite busy, affluent and well-kept, with lots of luxury brand stores and ads.

title: Hong Kong - IFC vs ICC Skyscrapers (Plonkit)
description:
You can use these two skyscrapers to determine whether you are on the Kowloon or Hong Kong Island side. The IFC is on the Hong Kong Island side and the ICC is on the Kowloon side.
The ICC has straighter edges and looks more like a cuboid, while the IFC is rounder. The IFC will also have noticeable vertical window frames, while the ICC has none.

title: Hong Kong - Mid-Levels (Hilly Residential) (Plonkit)
description: Mid-Levels is a residential district that is easily recognized by the non-identical tall modern apartments and hilliness.

title: Hong Kong - Residential District Quarry (Plonkit)
description: The residential district of Quarry Bay has a lot of identical white and brown apartment blocks, and tall glass office buildings.

title: Hong Kong - Chek Lap Kok (Construction) (Plonkit)
description: Chek Lap Kok Island and the Boundary Crossing Facilities can be recognized by the various large scale construction works going on in the area. From the outside, it can be identified by the many bridges that connect other parts of Hong Kong to the two islands.

title: Hong Kong - Tung Chung (Wall of Buildings) (Plonkit)
description: The residential district of Caribbean Coast and Tung Chung has identical apartment blocks that face the same direction, almost like a “wall” of buildings. There are a lot of planted palm trees in between and on the side of roads.

title: Hong Kong - Tsing Ma Bridge (Plonkit)
description: The Tsing Ma Bridge can be recognized by being the only major suspension bridge in Hong Kong. The bridge has two ladder-like support towers, and yellow and red guardrails.

title: Hong Kong - Ting Kau Bridge (Plonkit)
description: Ting Kau Bridge, a cable-stayed bridge connecting Ting Kau and Tsing Yi, can be identified by the generally clean asphalt and newer condition, three cylindrical support towers, hangers coming directly from the towers themselves, and yellow paint seen in the median and on the outsides.

title: Hong Kong - Ting Kau Bridge (Plonkit)
description: While similar to the Ting Kau Bridge, the cable-stayed Stonecutters Bridge can be identified by the lack of yellow paint, and its box beam guardrail design, as opposed to the cable design seen on the other two bridges.

title: Hong Kong - Lung Wo Road (Skylines) (Plonkit)
description: Lung Wo Road can be recognized by the Hong Kong Island skyline to the south and the Kowloon skyline to the north. The road is also in good condition and the sidewalks are clean.

title: Hong Kong - Tai Chung Kiu Road (Plonkit)
description: The Tai Chung Kiu Road is a divided road that runs in a north-east direction, and has views of the Shing Mun River to the west. The median has palm trees. In addition, a bicycle path runs alongside the road. Further north, Route 2 also runs alongside the river, but this road has more lanes.

title: Hong Kong - Fan Kam Road (Tropical) (Plonkit)
description: Fan Kam Road runs in a general north-east direction, and can be recognized by the dense tropical vegetation surrounding the road, and sometimes mountains in the background. The road is also quite narrow and does not have any outer lines. Many small villages branch off of the road, south and north of the country park.

title: Hong Kong - Lam Kam Road (Busy) (Plonkit)
description: Lam Kam Road is similar to Fan Kam Road, however it runs in a more east-west direction. The road should also feel busier with more cars driving along the road and more houses on the sides of the road. In addition, the road is usually wider and a median containing trees can be seen separating sidewalks near the villages.

title: Hong Kong - Kai Tak Cruise Terminal (Plonkit)
description: The Kai Tak Cruise Terminal can mainly be seen from the Eastern Corridor, north of Tsat Tsz Mui, and from the Kwun Tong bypass south-west of Kwun Tong. The cruise terminal can be recognized by its shiny, cylindrical appearance, with triangular windows along the side.

title: Hong Kong - HK-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge (Plonkit)
description: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge can be seen from the South Perimeter Road, on Chek Lap Kok Island. Its length stretches into the horizon, spanning across the ocean. The road itself can be recognized by the black and yellow concrete barriers on either side.

title: Hong Kong - Disneyland Roads (Plonkit)
description: The roads going to Disneyland are divided, with palm trees along the side of the road with teal coloured street lamps.

title: Hong Kong - Outlying Islands (Plonkit)
description: Between Hong Kong Island and Lantau Island, there are three unique islands: Peng Chau, Cheung Chau and Lamma Island, with trekker coverage. These islands can be identified by the lack of cars, narrow streets, and rural architecture. Lamma Island is also the hilliest of the three.

title: Hong Kong - Lugard Road Trekker (Plonkit)
description: The Lugard Road trekker around Victoria Peak can be recognized by the distinct black guardrail, view of the skyline and tourists walking along the path.

title: Hong Kong - Double-Decker Buses (Plonkit)
description: Buses in Hong Kong are mostly double-decker, with various colour schemes and adverts on the side. Single-decker versions do exist, but are less common. Smaller minibuses can also be seen, with a green or red roof.

title: Hong Kong - Sai Wan Ho (Residential) (Plonkit)
description: The residential district of Sai Wan Ho has a lot of identical white and brown apartment blocks, and tall glass office buildings.

title: Hong Kong - Tsing Ma Bridge (Suspension) (Plonkit)
description: The Tsing Ma Bridge can be recognized by being one of three suspension bridges in Hong Kong. The bridge has two ladder-like support towers, and yellow and red guardrails.

title: Hong Kong - Ting Kau Bridge (Yellow) (Plonkit)
description: Ting Kau Bridge, another suspension bridge connecting Ting Kau and Tsing Yi, can be identified by the generally clean asphalt and newer condition, three cylindrical support towers, hangers coming directly from the towers themselves, and yellow paint seen in the median and on the outsides.

title: Hong Kong - Stonecutters Bridge (Plonkit)
description: While similar to the Ting Kau Bridge, the Stonecutters Bridge can be identified by the lack of yellow paint, and its box beam guardrail design, as opposed to the cable design seen on the other two bridges.

title: India - Shitcam Coverage (Plonkit)
description: The vast majority of the coverage in India was taken with what’s commonly referred to as “shitcam”, which is a low-quality camera that can typically be recognised by the brownish colours and often, but not always, by a large circular blur covering the Street View car.

title: India - Gen 4 Smallcam (Plonkit)
description: All the Generation 4 coverage in India was taken using the smallcam, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: India - Gen 3 Trekker Coverage (Plonkit)
description: While most of India is covered in shitcam, there is also a significant amount of Generation 3 trekkers throughout the country.

title: India - Driving Side (Left) (Plonkit)
description: India drives on the left side of the road.

title: India - Scripts Variety (Plonkit)
description: A wide variety of scripts can be found in India. Most of them can be used to narrow down the region.

title: India - English Signage (Plonkit)
description: English is also an official language in India and can be seen on a lot of signage.

title: India - License Plates (Long/White/Yellow) (Plonkit)
description: Indian licence plates are typically fairly long, with the most common design being white. Commercial vehicles typically use yellow plates, while electric vehicles use green.

title: India - Signposts (Black & White Stripes) (Plonkit)
description: India typically has black and white striped signposts.

title: India - Utility Poles (Concrete/Trident) (Plonkit)
description:
The most common Indian utility pole is a concrete square pole with a trident pole top.
Beware that many regions have their own distinct poles and poletops.

title: India - Hindi (Devanagari Script) (Plonkit)
description: Hindi is the most common language in India and can be found in many central and northern regions. It uses the Devanagari script, which can be recognised by the line going through the top of each word and the straight vertical lines found in the majority of all letters.

title: India - Marathi (Devanagari with ळ) (Plonkit)
description: Marathi, found in Maharashtra, also uses the Devanagari script, however it sometimes uses the letter ळ which is not found in Hindi.

title: India - Punjabi (Gurmukhi Script) (Plonkit)
description: Punjabi can be found in Punjab in northwestern India. While the script looks somewhat similar to Hindi, it can generally be differentiated by the softer shape of the letters and the horizontal bar being broken over certain letters. It also has some distinctly different features, such as the letters ਨ, ਲ and ਅ as well as a diacritic in the shape of a soft curve beneath a letter.

title: India - Gujarati Script (No Top Line) (Plonkit)
description: Gujarati, found in Gujarat, has a script with several similarities to the Hindi script, however it notably lacks the horizontal line at the top of every word.

title: India - Bengali Script (Triangles) (Plonkit)
description: Bengali is found in northeastern India and has a similar look to Devanagari (Hindi), however it can usually be recognised by the many letters featuring left-facing triangular shapes.

title: India - Assamese (Bengali with ৰ/ৱ) (Plonkit)
description: Assamese, mainly found in Assam, also uses the Bengali script, with the addition of some characters, most notably ৰ and ৱ.

title: India - Kannada Script (Rounded/Squiggly Tail) (Plonkit)
description: Kannada is found in Karnataka and has a script with a lot of smooth curves and small circles. It is very similar to the Telugu script, with Telugu having one additional feature described in the next tip. Many characters also feature a distinct squiggly tail in the top right corner, which is less common in Telugu.

title: India - Telugu (Tick Marks) (Plonkit)
