title: Nepal - Striped Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Nepal mainly uses black-and-white striped concrete bollards that often have a red marking on the top. The amount of stripes vary from 3 to 5.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: You will see flat agricultural areas in the south as well as high altitude mountain roads in the northern half of Nepal.

title: Nepal - Most Buildings Either (Plonkit)
description: Most buildings are either colorful blocky multi-story structures or small houses with painted concrete, red brick, or thatched looking walls, with either a tiled or tin roof. As part of the building facade, you will often spot triangle shaped decorations.

title: Nepal - Nepal Uses Black-and-white (Plonkit)
description: Nepal uses black-and-white striped signposts.

title: Nepal - Nepal Features (Plonkit)
description: This type of white-painted Buddhist stupa, sometimes with painted eyes on the sides, are only found in Nepal.

title: Nepal - English Features (Plonkit)
description: Districts can show up on addresses, often in English as well.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The area in the far south close to the Indian border is almost completely flat, while the central and northern parts are very high altitude and very mountainous.

title: Nepal - Dense Vegetation (Plonkit)
description: The western hills can be recognised by the dry landscape, with a lot of exposed hillsides lacking vegetation.

title: Nepal - Areca Palms Be (Plonkit)
description: Areca Palms can be recognised by their very thin trunk and a small crown. They are mainly found in the southeast.

title: Nepal - Canola Crop With (Plonkit)
description: Canola, a crop with bright yellow flowers, is mostly found in a few southern pockets in the western half of Nepal.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Chir Pines, which can be identified from their generally smooth-looking conical or spherical crowns with very long needles, are found everywhere in the mountains, but are much more common in the west, and near Kathmandu.

title: Nepal - Grass With White (Plonkit)
description:
Grass with white and fluffy-looking tips is most commonly found just southeast of Kathmandu.
While it can be found in most of the country, it usually won’t look as white and fluffy outside the dark red coloured region.

title: Nepal - Japanese Cedar Trees (Plonkit)
description: Japanese cedar trees, which are only found in far eastern Nepal, can typically be recognised by their significant height combined with their narrow, fluffy-looking crowns.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Tea Plantations are also only found in far eastern Nepal. Both in the mountains, and in the flat region.

title: Nepal - Rounded Roof Tiles (Plonkit)
description: Rounded roof tiles are most common in the flat regions south of Kathmandu, but are also prevalent further west.

title: Nepal - West Bengal Style (Plonkit)
description: West Bengal style roof tiles, which are more organised and have small diamond shaped protrusions, are most common in the far west flat region. This hint also works for the half-rounded tiles.

title: Nepal - Birgunj Features (Plonkit)
description: Flat square shaped stone tiles that are grey in colour are common south of Kathmandu, more specifically around Birgunj and Janakpur.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Rectangular tiles that are less organised in shape and placement are common in western mountain towns, but can also be found towards the center of the country.

title: Nepal - Roofs Made From (Plonkit)
description: Roofs made from sheets of corrugated metal are most common between Birgunj and Janakpur.

title: Nepal - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Roofs that have a railing along the sides of the roofs, usually made of dark concrete, are found in some parts of western Nepal. They are most common in the Tulsipur valley, where the railings sometimes have a stair shape. The easternmost region where they’re found is the plains by Kawasoti. The westernmost regions often have lower quality “railings”, sometimes consisting of a few sticks.

title: Nepal - Kawasoti Features (Plonkit)
description: Gable ends decorated by carvings of gods, goddesses, and other religious symbols, usually painted in a golden colour, are mostly around Kawasoti, west of Bharatpur.

title: Nepal - Fences Varying Build (Plonkit)
description: Fences of varying build quality, made of mainly sticks, are most commonly found in the eastern plains of Nepal.

title: Nepal - Far East (Plonkit)
description: In the far east, you will mainly see roofs made of sheet metal with a triangular "window" just below the ridge of the roof, and an outwards sloping section below it.

title: Nepal - Biratnagar Hills (Plonkit)
description: Large hip roofs made of sheet metal with a small protrusion just below the ridge are found around Biratnagar in the east.

title: Nepal - Biratnagar Hills (Plonkit)
description: Similar to the above hint, hip roofs made of sheet metal with an even smaller protruding piece of metal at the ridge are mainly found west of and around Biratnagar.

title: Nepal - Mosques Concentrated Few (Plonkit)
description:
Mosques are concentrated in a few Muslim majority spots in southern Nepal.
- In the east, just around Janakpur.
- In the east, just around Birgunj.
- In the west, just around Nepalgunj.
- In the east, around Biratnagar and west of the Koshi river.

title: Nepal - Birgunj Features (Plonkit)
description: Small round clay huts with thatched roofs are mainly found around Birgunj.

title: Nepal - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles with a cross attached near the top are common in the east.

title: Nepal - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: In Kathmandu, you’ll find poles with an asymmetrical crossbar, which has a triangular attachment on top of it, as well as a support bar below it.

title: Nepal - Nepal Features (Plonkit)
description: While the most common water tank colours in Nepal are green and black, which are found everywhere, yellow ones are mainly found in the east.

title: Nepal - Orange Google Car (Plonkit)
description:
An orange google car can be found around:
- Nepalgunj in the west
- Madi, south of Bharatpur in the central south
- Biratnagar in the east
- Birtamod in the far east.

title: Nepal - Biratnagar Features (Plonkit)
description: An orange car with a blue ribbon on the front is found around Biratnagar.

title: Nepal - Blue Car Found (Plonkit)
description:
A blue car is found around:
- Pokhara, under the Nepal label
- Birgunj, southwest of Kathmandu
- Malangawa, near the Indian border southeast of Kathmandu.

title: Nepal - Pokhara Features (Plonkit)
description: If the blue car has an antenna, you will be around Pokhara.

title: Nepal - White Car Be (Plonkit)
description:
A white car can be found in the following areas:
- Around Butwal, southwest of the Nepal label
- On the H10 going to Pokhara
- On the H04 east to Kathmandu
- On some roads near Kathmandu
- Northeast of Birgunj, southwest of Kathmandu
- From Janakpur to Lahan, southeast of Kathmandu
- Around Itahari, in the east.

title: Nepal - Janakpur Features (Plonkit)
description: A car with a black spoiler is found just around Janakpur, southeast of Kathmandu.

title: Nepal - Kathmandu Features (Plonkit)
description: A regular grey car can be found around Kathmandu, and to the southeast, around Lahan.

title: Nepal - Blocky Grey Truck (Plonkit)
description: A blocky grey truck can be found east of Birgunj and just south of Kathmandu.

title: Nepal - Grey Car With (Plonkit)
description:
A grey car with a visible backlight can be found in the following areas:
- Around Pokhara, under the Nepal label
- Around Kathmandu
- North of Malangawa, near the Indian border southeast of Kathmandu
- East of Itahari, in the east.

title: Nepal - Kathmandu Features (Plonkit)
description: A red car, that usually has a long antenna, can be found in Kathmandu, and north of Janakpur, which is southeast of Kathmandu.

title: Nepal - Regional Buses (Plonkit)
description: Some roads north of Siddhicharan, in eastern Nepal are unique due to the high elevation hills with dark green rhododendron bushes growing in abundance. The bushes have red flowers which can be hard to see.

title: Nepal - Foggy And Gloomy (Plonkit)
description: This foggy and gloomy road hosts the only natural forest dominated by east himalayan fir. You can recognise it from all the tall dark trees present around the road. It is located just northwest of Bhimeshwor Municipality, east of Kathmandu.

title: Nepal - Sketchy Yelloworange Dirt (Plonkit)
description: This sketchy yellow/orange dirt road can be recognised from the high elevation landscape with the high elevation oaks. It can be found northeast of Phungling in far northeastern Nepal.

title: Nepal - Snow-Capped Mountains (Plonkit)
description: This dirt track in a northwestbound valley can be recognised by the snowcapped mountains to the northwest. You can find it north of the Khaptad national park in western Nepal.

title: Nepal - Limited Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Trekker coverage in Nepal is limited to the northeast of the country, in the general area southwest of Mount Everest.

title: Nepal - Green Forests And (Plonkit)
description: Green forests and trees are found in the southern parts of the Nepalese trekker coverage.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Barren mountain trails are found in the northern parts of the coverage.

title: Nepal - Snow-Capped Mountains (Plonkit)
description: A lot of the coverage in the vicinity of Namche Bazar can be summarised as being sunny, with the trails going close to the treeline, meaning you will be either near the top of or just above a forest for most of this coverage. You will generally see barren or snowy mountains in some direction.

title: Nepal - Bazar Features (Plonkit)
description: Namche Bazar is by far the largest and most densely populated settlement with trekker coverage. There is also some coverage looking down on the town.

title: Nepal - City Features (Plonkit)
description: The southernmost trekker coverage is situated in the town of Lukla, which can be recognised by the narrow street with relatively large buildings, combined with the extremely dark coverage.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description:
Khumjung village, situated just north of Namche Bazar, can be recognised by the jagged mountain towering above the village. Almost every house in the village has a green roof.
Beware that there is a label for Khumjung further north, which is not close to the village.

title: Nepal - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Pangboche is a fairly large settlement with fairly bright coverage. The surrounding landscape mainly consists of forested mountains nearby and some taller mountains in the distance.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Phorste is a fairly scarcely built settlement with a massive recognizable mountain close by. There are a lot of dead-looking trees surrounding the village.

title: Nepal - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Around the southern tip of the Nepalese trekker coverage, you will get this dark, overcast coverage inside a forested valley.

title: Nepal - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: North of Phakding you will get more overcast coverage in the same forest valley, however here the coverage is far brighter.

title: Nepal - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The coverage from Monjo up to Namche Bazar is also within the same valley, however here the coverage is mostly sunny and bright.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The valley by Thamu can be recognised by the generally forested mountainsides, combined with the angle of the valley, going northwest to southeast.

title: Nepal - Snow-Capped Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Next to the village of Thame you can see this snowy, and shining bright mountain range.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Northeast of Namche Bazar, you can find this semi-green river valley with clouds covering all mountains surrounding it.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: On a section north of Phorste, you get a view of the mountain Tobuche, covered in a blanket of clouds.

title: Nepal - Further North Cloud (Plonkit)
description: Further north, the cloud blanket is replaced by small, spotty clouds somewhat resembling smoke coming out of chimneys.

title: Nepal - Even Further North (Plonkit)
description: Even further north, the clouds disappear completely, and you get a clear view of the Tobuche peak.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Leaving Tobuche behind, you will find this small, ice-covered lake, right by Gokyo, with jagged mountains as a backdrop.

title: Nepal - Lake Views (Plonkit)
description: North of the icy lake, you reach a barren landscape, with a trail going to the north-north-west.

title: Nepal - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: East of Gokyo, you reach this dried out glacial valley, with bright grey rocks as far as you can see.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: East of the glacial valley, you get to a somewhat red-coloured, rugged mountainside right next to the trail.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Leaving the red mountainside behind, you enter a somewhat U-shaped valley, going firmly upwards.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Above the U-shaped valley, you get a view of this spiky mountain range. While there are some clouds around the peaks, they are mostly clearly visible.

title: Nepal - Snow-Capped Mountains (Plonkit)
description: As you lose sight of the spiky mountains, you cross over a glacier, which is the largest patch of snow covered ground with coverage in the country.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The area east of the glacier can be recognised by the many irregular clouds spread across the sky and covering various mountain peaks.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Further along the trail, you get this stunning view over Tobuche from the eastern side. The mountains get increasingly covered in clouds to the west.

title: Nepal - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Closing in on the final trek toward Everest, you get a view of this wide, high-altitude river valley.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Slightly east of Namche Bazar, you can find this very overcast trail following the mountainside. There are still some trees around, and the trail is noticeably higher above the valley than other overcast sections with trees.

title: Nepal - East Poi Called (Plonkit)
description: East of the POI called ‘Deboche’, you get this very overcast forest coverage. The dirt here is very bright and sandy, which can help differentiate it from the southern trail.

title: Nepal - Hazy Mountains (Plonkit)
description: You can recognise the trail between Pangboche and Dingboche by the massive mountains, combined with the sun looking somewhat hazy.

title: Nepal - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: North of Dingboche, you reach a high-altitude valley with very low clouds covering the sky and most of the surrounding mountains.

title: Nepal - Closing Everest Get (Plonkit)
description: Closing in on Everest, you get this completely barren landscape, with the trail going to the north-north-east.

title: Nepal - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Reaching the endpoint of the coverage, you finally get a stunning view of the world's tallest mountain, Mount Everest.

title: Pakistan - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Coverage in Pakistan was mainly taken with a Generation 3 trekker camera.

title: Pakistan - Urdu Language (Plonkit)
description:
While many languages are spoken in Pakistan, Urdu is considered the National language and most commonly found on signage. It is written in the Urdu alphabet, which is closely related to the Arabic alphabet and may appear almost indistinguishable, however Urdu often uses softer and curvier fonts.
Notably, English is also an official language in Pakistan and is fairly common on signage.

title: Pakistan - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Pakistan uses short licence plates and each region has its unique design. However, as all of the coverage was taken in Punjab, most plates will have the Punjab design, with a green strip on the left side. Fully green plates are also fairly common.

title: Pakistan - Historic Fortress (Plonkit)
description: A significant portion of the Pakistani coverage was taken in large, well ordered gardens, often surrounded by stone walls and in combination with old temples or fortresses. This type of garden is typically referred to as a Mughal garden.

title: Pakistan - Pakistan Features (Plonkit)
description: Typically brightly coloured, baggy pants are very common in Pakistan.

title: Pakistan - Limited Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Coverage in Pakistan is extremely limited, only being found in Punjab around major temples and tourist attractions.
Due to the number of distinct coverage spots, this section will only focus on the parts that are considered pinpointable.

title: Pakistan - Lahore (Grey Car) (Plonkit)
description: You may find this grey car, with a visible right side, driving around Lahore Fort in the north of Lahore.

title: Pakistan - Lahore (Urban Trekker) (Plonkit)
description: Just south of Lahore Fort you can find a trekker walking around some narrow urban streets that are typically very busy.

title: Pakistan - Historic Fortress (Plonkit)
description: Lahore Fort is a large fortress in Lahore, with the Alamgiri Gate being one of the most iconic monuments in Pakistan.

title: Pakistan - Inside Lahore Fort (Plonkit)
description: Inside Lahore Fort you may find this road completely surrounded by tall red brick walls on both sides.

title: Pakistan - University Campus (Plonkit)
description: The Government College University of Lahore can be recognised by its gothic architecture.

title: Pakistan - King Edward Medical University (Patiala Block) (Plonkit)
description: The Patiala Block of King Edward Medical University in Lahore is a large white colonial building with large white domes having black lines going around them.

title: Pakistan - Kinnaird College (Plonkit)
description: Kinnaird College for Women University is mainly made up of traditional Pakistani red brick buildings, often combined with red brick paths.

title: Pakistan - Jallo Features (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in Jallo, an eastern suburb of Lahore, can be recognised by the semi-urban coverage in a fairly poor-looking neighbourhood, with a very thick haze.

title: Pakistan - Bahria Grand Hotel (Plonkit)
description: Bahria Grand Hotel, in the southwestern suburbs of Lahore, can be recognised by the minigolf course in front of the hotel. There is also a statue of a cow by the entrance to the hotel grounds.

title: Pakistan - Harappa Museum Path (Plonkit)
description: West of Sahiwal, just northwest of Harappa, you can find a trekker starting in the south at Harappa Museum. This trekker can be recognised by most of the coverage being taken on a very narrow path made of concrete.

title: Pakistan - Lake Views (Plonkit)
description: Hiran Minar is a small temple, completely surrounded by a small lake with a single bridge connecting it to land, can be found just northwest of the city of Sheikhupura.

title: Pakistan - Kasur (Shrine of Hazrat Baba Bulleh Shah) (Plonkit)
description: The coverage around the shrine of Hazrat Baba Bulleh Shah, in western Kasur, can typically be recognised by the mosque with a large green dome, and two smaller green domes on top of the minarets. While the mosque itself isn’t visible from all of the coverage, the minarets can be seen from most spots.

title: Pakistan - Pākpattan (Market Street Rug Roof) (Plonkit)
description: In Pākpattan you can find a busy market street with a roof made of rugs.

title: Pakistan - Pākpattan (Busy Urban Street) (Plonkit)
description: Just west of the market street in Pākpattan you can find a very busy-looking urban street.

title: Pakistan - Pākpattan (Narrow Alleyway) (Plonkit)
description: You can also find this narrow alleyway in Pākpattan, just north of the market street.

title: Pakistan - Historic Fortress (Plonkit)
description: Rohtas Fort, west of Jhelum, can typically be recognised by the almost black fortress walls. While the walls aren’t always nearby, they can usually be seen in the distance.

title: Pakistan - Katas Raj Temples (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in Katas, north of Sargodha, can be recognised by the hazy sky combined with the hilliness.

title: Pakistan - Patriata Pine Forests (Plonkit)
description: Patriata, northeast of Islamabad can be recognised by the hilly forests, mainly consisting of tall pine trees. Interestingly, parts of the coverage were taken from an aerial lift.

title: Pakistan - Changa Features (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in Changa Manga Forest Park can be recognised by the path angle being northeastern, and the narrow channel closely following the path, either on the northern or southern side.

title: Philippines - Concrete Roads (Plonkit)
description: Concrete roads are extremely common in the Philippines.

title: Philippines - Driving Side (Plonkit)
description: The Philippines drives on the right.

title: Philippines - Black-White Plates (Plonkit)
description: Standard white licence plates with black text are used for passenger vehicles. You can also find many older plates from the 2002 series, which are recognisable due to their green tint.

title: Philippines - Octagonal Poles (Plonkit)
description: Octagonal metal poles are quite common in the Philippines.

title: Philippines - Pole Insulator (Plonkit)
description: You will often see a single insulator at the top of a vertical bar which is attached to the side of a utility pole.

title: Philippines - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description:
Middle road lines in the Philippines can be either yellow or white. In particular, you will often see combined yellow and white middle lines, which is not common in any other East Asian country.
Yellow road lines commonly have a distinct orange tint.

title: Philippines - Yellow Kilometre Stones (Plonkit)
description: These tall, square yellow road stones are unique to the Philippines.

title: Philippines - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Chevrons are typically red on white.

title: Philippines - Sign Posts (Plonkit)
description: Sign posts are often painted red, orange or yellow.

title: Philippines - Tuk-tuks (Plonkit)
description: Tuk-tuks, also referred to as tricycles, are extremely common in the Philippines, in many areas they are more common than typical cars.

title: Philippines - English Language (Plonkit)
description: Although Filipino is the official language of the Philippines, English is extremely common to find on signs. It is the only major Southeast Asian country where you’re likely to come across English.

title: Philippines - Gen 3 Car (Plonkit)
description:
In Generation 3 you can come across a white Street View car with the black roof clearly visible.
You may also come across a silvery grey car, which is also found in Bhutan.

title: Philippines - Drying Grains (Plonkit)
description: It is somewhat common to see grains being spread out on roads to dry.

title: Philippines - Pole Boxes (Plonkit)
description:
These black or white boxes are commonly seen on utility poles. Most of the time they feature a three letter abbreviation of the municipality you are in. The abbreviations will either have all three letters stand for the municipality, or the first two letters will abbreviate the municipality while the third letter indicates the province.
In the first image the "GMI" and "GMU" stands for the town of Gamu in the province of Isabela while the second image the "BGE" stands for the town of Bangued.

title: Philippines - Tuk-tuk Map (Plonkit)
description:
The Philippines have several different tuk-tuk and tricycle designs, roughly distributed as shown in this infographic.
This image was provided by AeroGelo. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Philippines - Province Names (Plonkit)
description:
Province names are very common to find on signs and can thus be very useful. However, they do not appear on the map, meaning they’re necessary to memorise in order to use them.
It is worth mentioning that Davao de Oro changed its name from Compostela Valley in 2019.

title: Philippines - Phone Codes (Plonkit)
description: Landlines will start with a 0 followed by the area code. Mobile phone numbers start with 09.

title: Philippines - Motorcycle Plates (Plonkit)
description: Motorcycles in the Philippines have regional colour-coded plates as seen on this map. Notably, the northern half of the country has the coloured strip at the top, while the southern half has it on the bottom of the plate.

title: Philippines - Northern Luzon Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The forested mountain range in Northern Luzon is characterised by somewhat dry mountainsides and an abundance of pine trees. You may rarely come across a similar landscape on high-altitude roads in Mindanao.

title: Philippines - Corn (Plonkit)
description: While corn can be found in most of the country, it is most common on northern Luzon and on Mindanao.

title: Philippines - Oil Palms (Plonkit)
description: The vast majority of Oil palm plantations are found on Mindanao.

title: Philippines - Sugarcane (Plonkit)
description: The majority of sugarcane in the Philippines can be found on the islands of Negros and Panay.

title: Philippines - Pineapples (Plonkit)
description: Pineapple plantations are mostly found on Mindanao.

title: Philippines - Bananas (Plonkit)
description: Banana plantations are almost exclusively found in central and southern Mindanao.

title: Philippines - Mindanao Trees (Plonkit)
description: Moluccan albizia are trees with light coloured trunks and pinnate leaves near the top of the tree. They are mainly found on Mindanao and are especially common in the eastern and central regions of the island.

title: Philippines - Diamond Pattern Houses (Plonkit)
description: Houses built with amakan walls, a traditionally woven bamboo mat, with a diamond pattern are almost exclusively found in the southern half of the country.

title: Philippines - Palawan Pattern Houses (Plonkit)
description: Houses built with amakan walls (referred to as Sawali in the north) with a diagonally woven pattern are mostly found on the island of Palawan, but can also be found throughout the northern half of the country.

title: Philippines - CAR Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: In the Cordillera Administrative Region you can find yellow and black striped concrete guardrails.

title: Philippines - Bicol Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: White guardrails with three recurring black stripes are unique to the region of Bicol in southern Luzon.

title: Philippines - Chile-style Poles (Plonkit)
description: Square concrete poles with an indent on both side, similar to the poles found in Chile, are mainly found north of Manila and in and around the city of Bacolod on the island of Negros.

title: Philippines - Manila Poletop (Plonkit)
description: A poletop made up of two tall vertical metal bars having an L-shaped cross-section which are connected via several thin wires, making it resemble a ladder, is unique to Manila and the surrounding area.

title: Philippines - Zamboanga Poles (Plonkit)
description: Square metal mesh poles are found on Mindanao, mainly on the Zamboanga peninsula.

title: Philippines - Muslim Region (Plonkit)
description: While most of the Philippines is strongly Christian, a region of western Mindanao is majority Muslim.

title: Philippines - Mountain Dew Decorations (Plonkit)
description: Decorations made of neon-green Mountain Dew bottles are commonly found in the north, particularly on northern Luzon.

title: Philippines - Kuliglig (Plonkit)
description: This type of tractor, called a kuliglig, is mostly found on the plains around Cauayan on northern Luzon.

title: Philippines - Chocolate Hills (Plonkit)
description: On central Bohol you can find these distinct round grassy hills. The hills generally have dark brown soil beneath the grass, earning them the name of Chocolate Hills.

title: Philippines - Arayat Volcano (Plonkit)
description: The Arayat Volcano can be recognised by being completely surrounded by flat agricultural fields.

title: Philippines - Mayon Volcano (Plonkit)
description: The Mayon Volcano is one of the tallest mountains in the Philippines and can be recognised by its almost perfect smooth cone shape. Beware that it will very often be covered in clouds.

title: Philippines - Marawi Ruins (Plonkit)
description: In and around the city of Marawi, Mindanao you can find many destroyed houses and ruins from the Marawi siege in 2017.

title: Philippines - Bataan Death March Markers (Plonkit)
description: These large decorated white waystones, commemorating the Bataan Death March, can be seen along roads going from Mariveles and Bagac in the south to San Fernando in the north.

title: Philippines - Puerto Princesa Highway (Plonkit)
description:
The highway going south from Puerto Princesa on Palawan can be characterised by being very wide, often featuring six lanes, while simultaneously having very little traffic.
Along the road you will usually see this double electrical wire, which can help confirm your guess.

title: Philippines - Siquijor Lamp Posts (Plonkit)
description: Lamp posts on Siquijor are typically painted yellow, with black stripes at the bottom.

title: Philippines - Marinduque Statues (Plonkit)
description: Images and statues of ancient Roman soldiers can be found on the island of Marinduque.

title: Philippines - General Santos Car (Plonkit)
description: You may find this black Street View car with a visible roof rack in and around the city of General Santos.

title: Philippines - Bohol Car (Plonkit)
description: In northwestern Bohol you can find this Street View car with tape on the back.

title: Philippines - Corregidor Car (Plonkit)
description: An orange Street View car with visible side mirrors can be found on Corregidor Island.

title: Philippines - Mayon Car (Plonkit)
description: This vehicle with several thick black bars can be found just south of the Mayon Volcano.

title: Philippines - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Standard white licence plates with black text are used for passenger vehicles. You can also find many that are privately issued, which are recognizable due to their green tint.

title: Qatar - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Regular cars in Qatar have long, white licence plates with a maroon strip on the left. Trucks have square, black licence plates and police plates are blue.

title: Qatar - Qatar Car (Plonkit)
description:
The Google car will usually be blurred, with only the antenna on the left and a sliver of the car visible. Sometimes the entire white pickup truck can be visible. Rusty clips can be seen on the crossbar.
See the region guessing section for more information.

title: Qatar - Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Qatar's landscape is predominantly desert, with arid, and mostly flat expanses of sand as far as the eye can see. You will often not see a lot of trees or other greenery.

title: Qatar - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Qatar typically uses solid outer white lines with either white or yellow in the middle. More rarely, you can also find outer yellow lines too.

title: Qatar - Qatar Poles (Plonkit)
description: Qatar uses round poles with 3 insulators on the pole top, with the middle one being slightly higher. The crossbar also has 2 diagonal bars connecting it to the pole.

title: Qatar - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Qatar uses white on red and white on blue chevrons.

title: Qatar - World Cup Banners (Plonkit)
description: Since some coverage was taken before the 2022 World Cup took place, many banners can be seen mentioning the event.

title: Qatar - Crossing Signs (Plonkit)
description: Qatari crossing signs feature a man in a thobe.

title: Qatar - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Qatar is pretty well covered, with almost every main road and some side roads having coverage. Only the south and west lack coverage at the moment.

title: Qatar - Municipalities (Plonkit)
description: Qatar is divided into municipalities, further divided into numbered zones, which can be seen on street signs. This infographic shows which number corresponds to each zone.

title: Qatar - Northern Antenna (Plonkit)
description: This very short antenna is found in northern Qatar.

title: Qatar - Doha Antenna (Plonkit)
description: This fairly long antenna is found in and around Doha.

title: Qatar - Southwestern Antenna (Plonkit)
description: And this long antenna is mostly found in southwestern Qatar.

title: Qatar - Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
Bollards in Qatar are only found on a few roads, and you can easily tell them apart.
- The horizontal road just west of Qatar map label uses black and yellow centre lines.
- The horizontal road south of Madinat al Kaban has a lot more greenery and, the coverage is also very overcast.
- The coastal road south of Fuwayrit has coastal shrubs all around, and you can often see the coast.
- If the road doesn’t fit the above descriptions, guess on the long vertical road west of Qatar map label.

title: Qatar - Al Bayt Stadium (Plonkit)
description: Al Bayt Stadium can be recognized by the black and white horizontal stripes on the stadium along with the tent-like roof.

title: Qatar - Lusail Stadium (Plonkit)
description: Lusail Stadium, in Lusail, can be recognized by its golden bowl-like shape.

title: Qatar - Lusail Towers (Plonkit)
description: Four towers, resembling a screw thread, can be seen from almost every point in Lusail.

title: Qatar - Ahmed bin Ali Stadium (Plonkit)
description: A structure resembling a gahfiya can be seen around the Ahmed bin Ali Stadium, in Rawdat Al Jahhaniya district.

title: Qatar - Mall of Qatar (Plonkit)
description: The Mall of Qatar in Rawdat Al Jahhaniya can be recognized by the boxy appearance with many ads on the side of the building. Large car parks are also seen next to the mall.

title: Qatar - Education City Stadium (Plonkit)
description: Education City Stadium can be recognized by the large, grey cladding with a diamond pattern.

title: Qatar - Education City Roads (Plonkit)
description: Education City features distinct black-tiled roads.

title: Qatar - Education City Signs (Plonkit)
description: Brown street signs, often fixed to the ground, are seen in Education City.

title: Qatar - Khalifa International Stadium (Plonkit)
description: Khalifa International Stadium can be recognized by the dual arches shaped like a wide open mouth.

title: Qatar - The Torch Tower (Plonkit)
description: The Torch Tower can be seen from almost every point in the Baaya District, and can be recognized by its hyperboloid structure, along with it being the tallest building in Qatar.

title: Qatar - Bed Box (Lusail) (Plonkit)
description: This cardboard box in the right side of the bed is seen in Lusail. The rusty clips will also be visible.

title: Qatar - Bed Box (Left - Ar-Rayyan) (Plonkit)
description: This black box on the left side of the bed is seen southeast of Ar-Rayyan, around the green area.

title: Qatar - Bed Box (Right - Al Khor) (Plonkit)
description: The black box on the right side of the bed is seen in Al Khor, and in the green area around The Torch Tower and Khalifa International Stadium.

title: Qatar - Airport Tripod (Plonkit)
description: A tripod was used to capture the interior of the Hamad International Airport. A unique tripod that captured the inside of a plane can also be seen here.

title: Singapore - Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
Singapore is a highly developed city-state, characterised by an overall cleanliness and orderliness.
Main roads are often divided, and commonly feature black-and-white curbs and double yellow outside lines. You will often see tall apartment blocks nearby.

title: Singapore - Street Name Signs (Plonkit)
description: All street name signs in Singapore follow this unique format. They are green, with rounded edges and a distinct white font.

title: Singapore - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Most Singaporean licence plates are black, with white text. Occasionally, you will be able to see the British style white-and-yellow plates and very rarely red plates.

title: Singapore - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Directional signs are also green, with white letters and English writing.

title: Singapore - Square Road Signs (Plonkit)
description: Road signs in Singapore are unique in that they are always set on a square white background.

title: Singapore - Rain Trees (Plonkit)
description: Rain trees are seen all around Singapore, and are often planted along main roads.

title: Singapore - Road Warnings (Plonkit)
description: Warnings are often written on the road in large letters, such as the famous “HUMP AHEAD”.

title: Singapore - Buses (Plonkit)
description: Singaporean buses are mostly lime-green, making them easily recognisable. Other designs can also be found, for example the white-and-purple SBS Transit variants.

title: Singapore - Bus Stop Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Moreover, all bus stops are protected by concrete bollards with unique black-and-yellow warning bands.

title: Singapore - Bus Leaving Box (Plonkit)
description: In addition to the concrete bollards on bus stops, Singapore sometimes has a unique and yellow bus-leaving box with an arrow on the street.

title: Singapore - Traffic Lights (Plonkit)
description: Almost all Singaporean traffic lights follow this design and are supported by a curved sheet of metal containing several holes.

title: Singapore - Neighbourhood Signs (Plonkit)
description: Many streets are named after the neighbourhood they are in, especially in the suburbs.

title: Singapore - Tuas Industrial Area (Plonkit)
description: The Tuas planning area is an industrial area that is characterised by straight roads, industrial complexes, cranes and shipping containers, making it recognisable.

title: Singapore - Sentosa Island (Plonkit)
description: You can easily recognise the island of Sentosa thanks to the green signposts, winding roads and general resort feel. Occasionally you might see a green lane like this as well.

title: Singapore - Pulau Ubin Trekker (Plonkit)
description: The Generation 3 trekker on Pulau Ubin can be identified by the unusually rural forest coverage and the camouflage-type hat sometimes visible when looking down.

title: Singapore - St John & Lazarus Islands (Plonkit)
description: You can recognise St John and Lazarus Islands thanks to the Generation 3 trekker, the smooth asphalt roads and the sea almost always nearby.

title: Singapore - Kusu Island (Plonkit)
description: The miniscule Kusu Island is easily identifiable because of the red paving stones used for the entire pathway.

title: South Korea - License Plates (Plonkit)
description:
South Korea uses a variety of different licence plates.
- Pre-2006 plates are short and green. These will still show up in the street view coverage.
- Post-2006 plates are white for private vehicles, and yellow for commercial vehicles. These can be long and short.

title: South Korea - Gen 3 Car (Plonkit)
description:
Almost all road coverage in South Korea is made with a Generation 3 camera.
In most, but not all, of the coverage, the back of the Google car is visible. You can see three colours: black, white and silver. The car never has an antenna.

title: South Korea - Season (Plonkit)
description:
A considerable amount of the coverage was made during autumn and winter.
Note that more pleasant-looking spring and summer coverage is also not uncommon.

title: South Korea - Hangul Script (Plonkit)
description: The Korean writing system (Hangul) is very unique and recognizable. One of its standout features is the presence of circles in many of its letters. This sets it apart from most other East Asian writing systems.

title: South Korea - Pole Markings (Plonkit)
description:
Utility poles almost always have these pole markings near the bottom, consisting of black and yellow diagonal stripes.
These markings look similar to the ones found in Taiwan. There are however two main differences:
- In South Korea, the stripes do not reach all the way to the bottom, whereas in Taiwan they do.
- In South Korea, the stripes are more yellow. In Taiwan, they have more of an orange tint.

title: South Korea - Pole Spike (Plonkit)
description: Most poles have a tapered “spike” on top.

title: South Korea - Driving Side (Plonkit)
description: South Korea drives on the right.

title: South Korea - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Roads generally have yellow middle lines and white outer lines.

title: South Korea - Red Block Markings (Plonkit)
description: You can sometimes see red block markings on the road.

title: South Korea - Warning Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Triangular warning signs have a yellow background.
Note that circular prohibition signs, such as speed signs, have a white background. Yield signs also have a white background.

title: South Korea - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs will be blue, arrow-shaped and commonly hanging from a metal bar mounted to utility poles.

title: South Korea - Direction Signs (Plonkit)
description: Direction signs in South Korea have white text on a green background.

title: South Korea - Speed Bumps (Plonkit)
description: Speed bumps are often painted yellow and white.

title: South Korea - Crossing Signs (Plonkit)
description: South Korean pedestrian crossing signs can be easily recognised from the distinct pentagonal shape combined with the blue background.

title: South Korea - House Numbers (Plonkit)
description:
Korean buildings have very distinctive house numbers. They are blue and usually are shaped quite literally like a house. The full address of the building is written on them, in both Hangul and Latin script.
Some places have unique house numbers, which you can use to region-guess. More information about this can be found in the spotlight section.

title: South Korea - Wedge Bollards (Plonkit)
description: You will sometimes see these black and white wedge-shaped bollards. They have a round yellow reflector on the front, and a grey one on the back.

title: South Korea - Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The South Korean landscape is predominantly mountainous. It is very rare to not see at least some hills or mountains in the distance. Even in the flat areas, you can almost always see elevation on the horizon.

title: South Korea - Red Bricks (Plonkit)
description: Red brick is a very common building material in South Korea.

title: South Korea - Tiled Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Many buildings have traditional tiled roofs like these. These often have decorative elements on the corners, and tend to have sides that curve slightly upwards. Blue roofs are quite common.

title: South Korea - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: South Korea has fairly limited and very spotty coverage. Other than large highways, most of the coverage is concentrated in and around major cities.

title: South Korea - Phone Codes (Plonkit)
description: Area codes in South Korea increase to the south, from 02 in the north, to 064 on Jeju. It is also notable that Seoul has the only two-digit area code in the country.

title: South Korea - Gen 2 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Generation 2 coverage is almost exclusively found in Seoul and Busan. It can also be found on a couple of highways outside the cities, however almost all of that coverage has been overwritten.

title: South Korea - Rear Camera Car (Plonkit)
description: A small camera can be seen mounted above the brake light on the Street View car on coverage northeast of Seoul and around Pohang.

title: South Korea - Jeju Soil (Plonkit)
description: Jeju is a volcanic island with a lot of dark volcanic dirt, where you can also often see volcanoes in the distance.

title: South Korea - Jeju Rock Walls (Plonkit)
description: Jeju also has a lot of rock walls, made of dark volcanic rocks.

title: South Korea - Gimje Plains (Plonkit)
description: The area around Gimje can be recognised by being one of the only completely flat areas of South Korea, combined with the open, yellow-green fields along almost every road in the area.

title: South Korea - Hampyeong House Numbers (Plonkit)
description: House numbers in the Hampyeong region can be recognised from the large white section at the top of the sign.

title: Sri Lanka - Sri Features (Plonkit)
description: Vehicles in Sri Lanka have long white front plates and short yellow rear plates.

title: Sri Lanka - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: In most Generation 3 coverage, you will be able to see the front of the Google car partially through the blur: it is visible as blue-white-red patches, reminiscent of the French flag. The red patch is usually most visually distinct.

title: Sri Lanka - Gen 4 Low-Cam Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
All Generation 4 coverage is low-cam. This means that the camera on the Google car is intentionally set up lower than in most other countries. This can be recognized in two ways:
- The car blur is significantly bigger. Generally, the bigger car blur is the most consistent way to recognize low-cam.
- Roads look wider and objects around you are seen from a lower angle.
Note that Sri Lanka’s Generation 3 coverage is made with a normal height camera!

title: Sri Lanka - Sri Lanka See (Plonkit)
description:
In Sri Lanka, you will see two scripts: Sinhala and Tamil. You will also sometimes see English, written in Latin script.
Sinhala is most common, and can be found throughout the entire country. It has a very curvy, ‘rounded’ look.
Tamil is more regionally limited. It has straighter lines. For an exact distribution, see the region-guessing section.

title: Sri Lanka - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Sri Lanka typically uses concrete utility poles. Two pole types are common and distinctive:
- Square poles with small pinholes in the sides. These pinholes are limited to the top part of the pole.
- Poles with large see-through holes in the lower half of the pole (“holey poles“). These poles are unique to Sri Lanka.

title: Sri Lanka - Stone Bollards (Plonkit)
description: These short, wide stone bollards are unique to Sri Lanka. They have a tapered shape, with a black base and a white top.

title: Sri Lanka - Waystones (Plonkit)
description: Tall, white concrete waystones with an indented section near the bottom containing a yellow road number, are unique to Sri Lanka.

title: Sri Lanka - Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Sri Lanka commonly uses black and white striped signposts.

title: Sri Lanka - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Rural roads often have outside lines, but no middle lines. In the absence of other clues, this can sometimes be a way to decide a tough 50-50.

title: Sri Lanka - Vegetation (Plonkit)
description: Sri Lanka is a tropical country. It usually has very lush, green vegetation. It is densely populated and many parts are covered in a patchwork of agricultural fields.

title: Sri Lanka - Red Soil (Plonkit)
description:
Many parts of Sri Lanka have reddish soil.
Less commonly, you may encounter white, sandy soil.

title: Sri Lanka - Palm Trees (Plonkit)
description: Palm trees are very common in Sri Lanka, more so than many other Asian countries.

title: Sri Lanka - Tiled Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Houses often have orange or red tiled roofs. Due to wear and tear, these tiles often have an almost brown tint to them.

title: Sri Lanka - Buddhism (Plonkit)
description: The country is majority Buddhist: 70% of the population practise this religion. Throughout the country, you will often see signs of the religion, including temples, Buddha statues, stupas and the Buddhist flag.

title: Sri Lanka - Other Religions (Plonkit)
description: A substantial minority of the population adhere to other religions: Hinduism (13%), Islam (10%) and Christianity (7%). These religions have strong regional distribution patterns; see the region-guessing section for more information.

title: Sri Lanka - Tuktuk (Plonkit)
description: This style of tuktuk is common in Sri Lanka: it has a bulky shape and a black roof. They are usually coloured green, yellow or red, though other colours appear as well.

title: Sri Lanka - Low-Quality Camera (Plonkit)
description: Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Sri Lanka. This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”). It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours. A good map will not usually include this coverage, but it is good to be aware of its existence, in order to not be caught off-guard by it.

title: Sri Lanka - Phone Codes (Plonkit)
description:
Sri Lankan telephone numbers have 10 digits.
The first three digits of landline phone numbers are the area code. The first digit of that area code is always a 0, while the remaining two digits are shown on the map.
Mobile phone numbers always start with 07 and are not associated with any particular region.
You can click on the image to enlarge it. Image credit: Maccem.

title: Sri Lanka - Religion Map (Plonkit)
description:
These maps shows the distribution of each of Sri Lanka’s four main religions. This can help with region-guessing when you spot a house of worship or other symbol associated with one of the religions.
- Buddhism is found in most of the country but is mostly absent from the north and some parts of the east coast.
- Hinduism is predominantly found in the north and parts of the east, as well as around the town of Nuwara Eliya in the central mountains.
- Islam is strongest on the east coast, but not a majority in any district.
- Christianity is mostly confined to the northwest, and is strongest around the town of Mannar.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Sri Lanka - Tamil Script (Plonkit)
description:
The presence of the Tamil script is strongly correlated with the distribution of Hinduism (though not all Tamils are Hindu and vice versa).
There are two groups that use the Tamil script:
- Native Sri Lankan Tamils, who predominantly live in the north and the east.
- Indian Tamils, who mostly live in and around the central Nuwara Eliya district.
Note that it is not uncommon to find bilingual Sinhala and Tamil signs far outside the area where Tamil is the predominant language. However, Tamil-only signage can be a strong indicator for one of the Tamil-majority areas.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Sri Lanka - Topography (Plonkit)
description:
This map shows Sri Lanka’s topography. Hills and mountains are strongly concentrated in the central-southern part of the country.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Sri Lanka - Wet Climate (Plonkit)
description: The southwest of Sri Lanka has a more wet climate that is characterised by lush, dense vegetation. Deep green tones dominate the landscape.

title: Sri Lanka - Dry Climate (Plonkit)
description:
Conversely, the rest of the country has a slightly more dry climate. The vegetation is often lower and more open. The landscape usually has a mix of brown and green tones.
Note that the difference is not extreme, as the landscape in Sri Lanka never truly gets downright arid. However, with some practise, you can often learn to tell the difference. Your mileage may also vary depending on the season, local forest cover, or coverage type (Generation 3 often tends to make the landscape look more arid than it really is).

title: Sri Lanka - Tea Plantations (Plonkit)
description:
Tea plantations are found in the central and southwestern parts of the country. They are most common in the area just west of Nuwara Eliya.
Tea plants look like small, compact shrubs with bright green leaves. They are usually planted in organised rows or clusters on hillsides.

title: Sri Lanka - Horton Plains NP (Plonkit)
description: Horton Plains National Park has a very distinct and bait landscape, consisting of hilly plains covered in long grass. In the distance, you can see forests, but most of the park’s roads meander through a wide open landscape.

title: Taiwan - Taiwan Uses Traditional (Plonkit)
description:
Taiwan uses Traditional Chinese. It is one of the most complex scripts visible on street view, with intricate characters that consist of many strokes.
!!Japanese uses some Chinese characters (kanji), meaning the script can look somewhat similar. However, Japanese will also have a considerable amount of more simplified looking characters (katakana and hiragana).

title: Taiwan - Pole Markings (Plonkit)
description: Poles almost always feature these black and yellow diagonal-striped markings that run all the way to the bottom.

title: Taiwan - Driving Side (Plonkit)
description: Taiwan drives on the right side of the road.

title: Taiwan - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Roads in Taiwan generally feature double yellow middle lines with single white outer lines. Thinner roads sometimes use single dashed yellow lines instead.

title: Taiwan - Outside Lines (Plonkit)
description: Roads with outside white road lines and no middle lines at all are common. In the absence of better clues, this type of road line can be a very good way to identify Taiwan.

title: Taiwan - Red Outer Lines (Plonkit)
description: Red outer lines that indicate no parking are common in Taiwan, especially in cities. This is essentially unique to the country.

title: Taiwan - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Taiwan uses black on yellow chevrons.

title: Taiwan - Mirrors (Plonkit)
description: These mirrors with orange hoods are frequently featured in intersections and bends.

title: Taiwan - Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
Taiwan uses these bollards with either two or three circular reflectors on a black rectangle.
You can also find these lollipop looking reflectors on guardrails, similar to the designs found in Japan.

title: Taiwan - Drainage Ditches (Plonkit)
description: Concrete drainage ditches are commonly found on the side of roads.

title: Taiwan - Transformers (Plonkit)
description: These distribution transformers that look like boxes are frequently found in Taiwan, especially in urban areas.They are mostly painted in dark green or grey.

title: Taiwan - Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Architecture in Taiwan varies in designs, ranging from cramped, multiple-story housing to flat, single-story houses with backyards. Many residential buildings have a very boxy look. A lot of walls are covered in tiles, usually white. Sheds made out of tin are also featured, commonly painted in a light green colour.

title: Taiwan - Gen 3 Black Car (Plonkit)
description: In Generation 3 coverage, you can find this black car with a long antenna and a red brake light in the middle, similar to the one you can see in Russia.

title: Taiwan - Gen 3 Wide Blur (Plonkit)
description:
You can also find this Generation 3 car with a very large blur that covers the entire car and almost looks like low-cam.
Note that this is not the same as low-cam: the camera is still at a normal height, meaning you see the world around you from a normal vantage point.

title: Taiwan - Counties Map (Plonkit)
description:
This is a map of the counties of Taiwan. Importantly, Taiwan has a couple of smaller islands and island groups with coverage that are fairly far away from the main island. It is important to be aware of these, as they often catch beginning players off-guard. These include:
- Kinmen close to the coast of mainland China.
- Lienchiang (Matsu Islands), also close to the coast of mainland China.
- Penghu in the middle of the Taiwan Strait.
- Green Island and Orchid Island, southeast of the main island. These two islands belong to Taitung County.

title: Taiwan - Area Code Map (Plonkit)
description:
Taiwan telephone numbers are 10 digits, with the first two digits indicating the area code. Area codes range from 02 to 08, increasing as you go south.
This image was provided by DrizzleMayFiddle.

title: Taiwan - Freeway System (Plonkit)
description:
Taiwan’s National Freeway system is organised so that odd numbers represent north-south roads and even numbers represent east-west. Generally, numbers also increase moving west to east and north to south. The 1 and the 3 are by far the longest, running across the west coast.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Taiwan - Township Roads (Plonkit)
description:
These signs indicate Township roads, with the character written before or above the road number indicating the county.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Taiwan - Pole Plaques (Plonkit)
description:
Many poles in Taiwan feature these blue plaques with strings of letters and numbers that act as precise coordinates.
For an example of how to read the plaques in-game, the only thing that is useful here is the string “E3264”. “BE08” can further narrow down the position but is not practical in-game.
“E” refers to the 50x80km rectangle from this map.
“3264” means that within the rectangle, we are 32% eastward and 64% northward.
This article explains how the string “BE08” can be further used to narrow down the exact coordinates of the telephone pole.

title: Taiwan - Western Plains (Plonkit)
description: The central western plain of Taiwan mainly consists of flat to low rolling plains. It is common to find crops and other farmland in this area.

title: Taiwan - Central Mountains (Plonkit)
description:
The central-eastern region that covers two-thirds of Taiwan consists of forested mountains.
The central mountain range that runs all the way to the south of the island is made up of tall mountains and rugged valleys. At high elevations, the vegetation can look less tropical and feature temperate or even coniferous trees.

title: Taiwan - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description:
The Hualien-Taitung Valley is a thin and long valley located on the east coast of the island passing from Hualien City at the north to Taitung City at the south. It is very recognizable as it consists of flat gentle plains surrounded by densely-forested mountains to the east and west.
There are also other valleys in central Taiwan that can look similar.

title: Taiwan - Yilan Plain (Plonkit)
description: The Yilan Plain is easily identifiable by the mountain ranges that are seen in the north, west, and south. Rice paddies are also extremely common as well as houses built right next to these fields.

title: Taiwan - Kinmen (Plonkit)
description: The island of Kinmen can be recognized by these trees with fuzzy leaves lining the road and red-tinged soil.

title: Taiwan - Miaoli and Hsinchu (Plonkit)
description: Miaoli and Hsinchu share a landscape of low rolling hills and winding roads as well as sparse farmland with vegetation that can look messy and unkempt.

title: Taiwan - Taichung (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, Taichung features these open plains surrounded by low mountains that are often in the distance.

title: Taiwan - Areca Palms (Plonkit)
description:
Areca catechu, also known as areca palms or betel nut palms, are extensively found in central and southern Taiwan.
Areca palms are most common in the mountainous regions of Taiwan, you can still see dense areca palm patches in northern counties but they are few and far between.

title: Taiwan - Coconut Palms (Plonkit)
description: Coconut palms (Cocos nucifera) are primarily found in the southern-half of the island, toward the coast.

title: Taiwan - Norfolk Island Pines (Plonkit)
description: Norfolk island pines (Araucaria heterophylla) are extremely common in the county of Penghu, especially in tightly-packed rows next to roads.

title: Taiwan - Leafless Trees (Plonkit)
description: These leafless trees are most frequently seen in Penghu.

title: Taiwan - Fish Farms (Plonkit)
description: Cultivated fish farms are mostly found right next to the coast in the western counties.They are generally seen in the southern-half of the island, anywhere from Changhua to Pingtung, but predominantly found in the counties of Yunlin, Chiayi, Tainan, and Kaohsiung.

title: Taiwan - Tea Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Tea plantations are generally seen in mountainous areas all over Taiwan. You can find them commonly in Chiayi, Nantou, Hsinchu, and Miaoli.

title: Taiwan - Pingtung Plantations (Plonkit)
description: These areca palm plantations are mostly found in the county of Pingtung.

title: Taiwan - Disorganised Housing (Plonkit)
description: Old and disorganised housing units as well as tall dingy-looking apartment blocks are frequently seen in the urban areas of northern Taiwan.

title: Taiwan - Taoyuan Apartments (Plonkit)
description: Taoyuan features these red brick and sometimes red tile apartment buildings.

title: Taiwan - Yilan Villas (Plonkit)
description: In Yilan, you can find these rich multiple-story villas.They come in all types of designs and are often gated.

title: Taiwan - Penghu Houses (Plonkit)
description: White-tinged cream coloured houses are frequently seen in Penghu.

title: Taiwan - Kinmen Houses (Plonkit)
description: You can find these small, traditional-looking houses in Kinmen.

title: Taiwan - Lamp Stickers (Plonkit)
description:
Similar to the blue plaques found on utility poles, Taiwan also features stickers to ID the locations of lamps. These can be found on both lampposts and utility poles with lamps attached to them.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Taiwan - White Speckles (Plonkit)
description: Pavement with white speckles is commonly found along the east coast.

title: Taiwan - Kinmen Lampposts (Plonkit)
description: Kinmen often features lampposts with red and white diagonal stripes.

title: Taiwan - Kaohsiung Lampposts (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, lampposts with red and white diagonal stripes on a trapezoidal base are frequently found in Kaohsiung City.

title: Taiwan - Yunlin Poles (Plonkit)
description: In Yunlin, you can find poles with a thicker support below the pole top.

title: Taiwan - Changhua Features (Plonkit)
description: Many traffic control boxes in Changhua County are marked with large yellow stickers. You will find these boxes at intersections.

title: Taiwan - Chiayi Green Squares (Plonkit)
description: These green square stickers are typically seen on every pole in Chiayi City.

title: Taiwan - Bent Sign Holders (Plonkit)
description: These bent sign and chevron holders with two black and yellow-striped stickers are only found in Pingtung, Kaohsiung, and Taitung.

title: Taiwan - Raised Transformers (Plonkit)
description: Distribution transformers raised by a dark green holder are mostly found in New Taipei City and Keelung City.

title: Taiwan - Blue Outer Lines (Plonkit)
description: Blue outer lines are almost entirely exclusive to Penghu.

title: Taiwan - Orchid and Green Island (Plonkit)
description: The islands east of Taitung, Green Island and Orchid Island, are distinct due to the more tropical climate, abundance of coconut palms, and lush cliffs. Additionally, it is common to find run-down, concrete pavement.

title: Taiwan - Matsu Islands (Plonkit)
description: Lienchiang County, also referred to as the Matsu Islands, is recognizable from the hilly landscape and frequent use of concrete roads. The coverage is overcast and this pavement can also commonly be found.

title: Taiwan - Provincial Highway 8 (Plonkit)
description:
The Provincial Highway 8 that runs from Taichung to Hualien is very recognizable, specifically in the Hualien part, due to the yellow guardrail that can be found all throughout the western half of the road in the county.
The eastern half of the road features these tall exposed-rock cliffs that tower over the road.

title: Taiwan - Provincial Highway 20 (Plonkit)
description: The Provincial Highway 20, specifically the part that runs through Yushan National Park, features tall mountains covered with coniferous trees. The road also utilises these tube-like double guardrails.

title: Taiwan - Taipingshan Road (Plonkit)
description: The road that leads up to Taipingshan National Forest in Yilan is distinct due to it often being very foggy when covered. Other features of this road include the coniferous trees and a guardrail with red legs.

title: Taiwan - Hualien Plains (Plonkit)
description: This open landscape with forests of short trees surrounding a narrow grassy road can be found in Hualien in the flat parts of Guangfu and Fenglin. This area can be distinguished due to it being commonly covered in Generation 2; however, you can find similar landscapes in Generation 3 and 4.

title: Taiwan - Green Train Car (Plonkit)
description: A green train car can be found in east Chiayi around Alishan National Forest.

title: Taiwan - Blue Truck (Plonkit)
description: A blue pickup truck can be seen in a few of the riverside parks in Taipei City.

title: Taiwan - Traditional Chinese (Plonkit)
description: Taiwan uses Traditional Chinese. It is one of the most complex scripts visible on street view, with intricate characters that consist of many strokes.

title: Taiwan - Phone Codes (Plonkit)
description: Taiwan telephone numbers are 10 digits, with the first two digits indicating the area code. Area codes range from 02 to 08, increasing as you go south.

title: Taiwan - Hualien-Taitung Valley (Plonkit)
description: The Hualien-Taitung Valley is a thin and long valley located on the east coast of the island passing from Hualien City at the north to Taitung City at the south. It is very recognizable as it consists of flat gentle plains surrounded by densely-forested mountains to the east and west.

title: Thailand - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Thailand uses large, white licence plates on passenger vehicles, and yellow ones on commercial vehicles.

title: Thailand - Driving Side (Plonkit)
description: Thailand drives on the left hand side of the road.

title: Thailand - Bollards (Plonkit)
description: The Thai bollard is square shaped with a pointed top, and has black-and-white stripes.

title: Thailand - Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Signposts in Thailand are square and bulky in shape, usually white, and often have the bottom painted black.

title: Thailand - Concrete Roads (Plonkit)
description: Concrete roads are common in Thailand. They often have a large square shaped pattern.

title: Thailand - Square Poles (Plonkit)
description: Thai poles are square and have small holes running vertically up the pole.

title: Thailand - Thai Script (Plonkit)
description: Thai script is compact and in many fonts has tiny circles within most letters.

title: Thailand - Middle Lines (Plonkit)
description: Thailand has yellow middle lines. These middle lines are either solid or dashed lines.

title: Thailand - Lamp Post Stripes (Plonkit)
description: Street light poles have red-and-black or black-and-white stripes on the bottom.

title: Thailand - Lamp Posts (Plonkit)
description: Thailand has very distinct long, thin lamp posts that hang over the side of the road.

title: Thailand - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Directional signs on smaller roads are white, and are composed of two signs: one with an arrow at the bottom, and one with the information at the top. These can have place names. When they do not, you will see them as just the road number with a Garuda. Moreover, highway signs are green, and frequently feature the place names in Latin script below the Thai name.

title: Thailand - Stop Signs (Plonkit)
description: Stop signs in Thailand feature the Thai script, instead of Latin.

title: Thailand - Two Road Markers (Plonkit)
description:
These two road markers are generally found in Thailand. They will either have a white or a black Garuda on them.
On the map, national roads are white-and-black, while provincial roads are blue-and-yellow.

title: Thailand - Flags (Plonkit)
description: Thailand often has many flags lining the side of its streets. Aside from the national flag, you can often see royal flags, which are usually yellow.

title: Thailand - Green Village Signs (Plonkit)
description: These distinctive green signs can be found all around Thailand, often in small villages.

title: Thailand - Gen 3 No Car (Plonkit)
description: Most Generation 3 coverage has no visible Street View car.

title: Thailand - Phone Codes (Plonkit)
description: Thai landline phone numbers have 9 digits. The first digits of phone numbers are the area code. The Bangkok area code is 02, the other area codes have three digits. The area codes are grouped, so even just learning the first digit is useful.

title: Thailand - National Roads (Plonkit)
description: National roads are grouped into four regions based on their first digit. Roads beginning with 1 can be found in the north, 2 in the northeast, 3 in the centre and 4 in the south of the country.

title: Thailand - Province Abbreviations (Plonkit)
description:
Waystones and road signs on provincial roads will often provide a two-letter abbreviation of the province in Thai script. They will not appear on waystones or road signs for national roads.
You can use this site to view and practice all province abbreviations.

title: Thailand - Black Boxes (Plonkit)
description:
These black boxes will often provide a three-letter abbreviation of the province. Two formats are used:
- Starting with the abbreviation followed by 4 numbers
- Starting with TCC-L2, or rarely TCC-L1, followed by the abbreviation
Shown in the picture is the abbreviation “NTB” for Nonthaburi. The abbreviations may vary slightly in each province depending on the format.

title: Thailand - Islamic Influence (Plonkit)
description: The majority of Muslims in Thailand live in the very south of the country. In these areas, you will often see Islamic religious attire, Jawi script, based on the Arabic script, on signs and mosques.

title: Thailand - Flat and Dry Regions (Plonkit)
description: Thailand has two regions that are relatively flat and dry compared to other areas. One north of Bangkok, the other more east.

title: Thailand - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Tall mountains are most often seen in northwestern Thailand.

title: Thailand - Low Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Low, smooth and forested mountains can be found in the centre-north of the country.

title: Thailand - Exposed Rock Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Steep mountains with a lot of exposed rock are most commonly found in the west and on the peninsula.

title: Thailand - Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: Red soil is most common in the northeast of Thailand, but can be seen throughout the entire country.

title: Thailand - Gravel Roads (Plonkit)
description: Gravel roads can be found all throughout Thailand, but are most common in the darkly highlighted areas.

title: Thailand - Rubber Wood Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Rubber wood plantations are typically seen in Thailand. Most of them are located in the south. You can recognize them by the small, black taps on the bottom of the tree's trunk.

title: Thailand - Rice Cultivation Area (Plonkit)
description: A majority of Thailand’s rice cultivation occurs within the highlighted area.

title: Thailand - Dry Season Rice (Plonkit)
description: Rice cultivated during the dry season is most common in the central plains. The dry season in Thailand can typically be recognized by a haze in the sky due to wildfires.

title: Thailand - Wet Season Rice (Plonkit)
description: During the wet season, the majority of rice cultivation occurs in the eastern plains.

title: Thailand - Palm Oil Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Over 90% of the palm oil in Thailand is produced in the south. This means that palm plantations are most often seen in southern Thailand.

title: Thailand - Short Coconut Leaves (Plonkit)
description: Dense plantations of short or medium sized coconut palms are most commonly found west of Bangkok.

title: Thailand - Tall Coconut Palms (Plonkit)
description: Slightly less dense plantations of tall coconut palms are most common in Prachuap Khiri Khan.

title: Thailand - Palmyra Palms (Plonkit)
description: Large numbers of palmyra palms are typically found near the eastern coast of the peninsula, specifically just south of Bangkok as well as in the far south.

title: Thailand - Areca Palms (Plonkit)
description: Areca palms are mainly found across the peninsula, but are especially common around Ranong.

title: Thailand - Sugar Cane (Plonkit)
description: Sugar cane is mostly grown in central and eastern Thailand.

title: Thailand - Cassava (Plonkit)
description: Cassava is a bush-like plant with digitate leaves. It can be found throughout most of Thailand, but is considerably more common in the central and northeastern plains.

title: Thailand - Corn (Plonkit)
description: Corn is most commonly found in the north and central regions of Thailand.

title: Thailand - Fruit Plantations (Plonkit)
description: The most extensive fruit plantations can be found in the valley between Chiang Mai and Lamphun as well as eastern Sa Kaeo and Chanthaburi.

title: Thailand - Durian Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Durian plantations are most common around Chanthaburi, but can be found around the peninsula and other areas. When they are young, they can be identified by their cone-shaped appearance. When fully grown, durian trees can be identified by their dark bark, branches that nearly reach the ground, and oblong leaves with pointed tips.

title: Thailand - Pineapple Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Pineapple plantations are most commonly found southeast and southwest of Bangkok.

title: Thailand - Eucalyptus Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Eucalyptus plantations are most common around Sa Kaeo.

title: Thailand - Teak Trees (Plonkit)
description: Tectona grandis, also known as teak, is most commonly found in high densities in the north. It can be recognized by its large leaves and yellow flowers.

title: Thailand - Pine Trees (Plonkit)
description: Pine trees, specifically Pinus latteri, or Tenasserim pines, are more or less exclusive to the north and northwest of the country.

title: Thailand - Garden Croton (Plonkit)
description: Codiaeum variegatum, also known as garden croton, is a decorative plant recognised by its yellow, orange and red leaves. It is most common around Ranong and other coastal provinces.

title: Thailand - Corrugated Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Gray corrugated metal roofs are most commonly found in the north and south of the country, but can occasionally be found throughout the country.

title: Thailand - Indented Poles (Plonkit)
description: Regular poles with a Chilean style indent are found around Bangkok.

title: Thailand - Wind Turbines (Plonkit)
description: Wind turbines are most often found on the western side of Chaiyaphum and Nakhon Ratchasima as well as the eastern coast of Songkhla and Nakhon Si Thammarat.

title: Thailand - Chiang Mai Bollard (Plonkit)
description: This black bollard with three large white reflectors is most frequently seen in Chiang Mai and Mae Hong Son.

title: Thailand - 7 Ridge Insulator (Plonkit)
description: Insulators with 7 or more ridges are found in the southern half of the peninsula, as well as highways in Chiang Rai and Phayao.

title: Thailand - One Insulator (Plonkit)
description: Poles with only one insulator on the crossbar can be found from south on the peninsula to Ranong and Chumphon.

title: Thailand - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Conversely, poles with two insulators on the crossbar can be found in the rest of the country.

title: Thailand - Phuket (Plonkit)
description: The island of Phuket is very touristy and wealthy. You will often see modern buildings, resorts, and heavy traffic among hills.

title: Thailand - Gulf Islands (Plonkit)
description: Koh Samui and Koh Pha-Ngan are touristy islands with narrow, crowded roads and a tropical feel.

title: Thailand - Bangkok Taxis (Plonkit)
description: Bangkok uses pink and yellow on green taxis.

title: Thailand - Red Songthaews (Plonkit)
description: These red trucks, known as songthaews, are transport vehicles found most commonly in Chiang Mai.

title: Thailand - Bangkok Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs with a smaller green section underneath a blue section are found in Bangkok and Nonthaburi.

title: Thailand - Pattaya Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs shaped like a helm are exclusive to Pattaya City.

title: Thailand - Chiang Rai Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Red street signs with golden decorated borders can be found in Mueang Chiang Rai.

title: Thailand - Phrao Valley (Plonkit)
description: The Phrao District in Chiang Mai is a fairly flat valley surrounded by mountains in all directions. The valley will commonly grow rice and fruit.

title: Thailand - Doi Luang Chiang Dao (Plonkit)
description: Doi Luang Chiang Dao is the 3rd tallest mountain in Thailand. It along with other distinctly shaped mountains can be seen clearly from the Chiang Dao district of Chiang Mai.

title: Thailand - Phayao Mountains (Plonkit)
description: A large and slightly jagged north-south mountain ridge runs through the middle of Phayao. It can be seen to the east from afar.

title: Thailand - Western Tak (Plonkit)
description: Rolling hills of corn or sugar cane fields can be found in the west of the Tak province. In this area, paved roads are often very brown.

title: Thailand - Phetchabun Valley (Plonkit)
description: Large north-south mountains can be seen on either side of the Phetchabun valley.

title: Thailand - Kanchanaburi Fields (Plonkit)
description: Deep red fields with cassava and rubber trees can be found in Kanchanaburi.

title: Thailand - Lopburi Mountains (Plonkit)
description: These distinctly shaped mountains can be found in southwestern Lopburi.

title: Thailand - Saraburi Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The northern half of Saraburi consists of large, exposed rock mountains in an east-west orientation.

title: Thailand - Chaiyaphum Ridges (Plonkit)
description: Chaiyaphum features very long and flat mountain ridges that can be seen from nearly anywhere in the province.

title: Thailand - Khao Yai National Park (Plonkit)
description: The area around Khao Yai National Park in southern Nakhon Ratchasima is a large tourist attraction. You will see many advertisements, businesses, restaurants, and resorts along otherwise rural roads. Large rocky hills can be seen closer to the border with Nakhon Nayok and Prachin Buri.

title: Thailand - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: In northern Nakhon Phanom, along the Mekong River, you will sometimes see jagged limestone karst mountains to the northeast. These formations stand on the Lao side and are often visible from long distances.

title: Thailand - Mukdahan Hills (Plonkit)
description: The province of Mukdahan features many long, low hills among fields of rice, sugarcane, cassava and rubber trees.

title: Thailand - Khao Sam Roi Yot (Plonkit)
description: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park in western Prachuap Khiri Khan features large, distinct exposed rock mountain massifs. Notably, the mountains can be seen from the center of the province.

title: Thailand - Khao Sok National Park (Plonkit)
description: Khao Sok National Park in northern Phang-nga and western Surat Thani features some of the tallest and steepest exposed rock mountains in the south of Thailand. The mountains generally run east-west.

title: Thailand - Western Krabi Mountains (Plonkit)
