description: Western Krabi and parts of eastern Phang-nga also feature large exposed rock mountains running north-south.

title: Thailand - Southeastern Nakhon Ratchasima (Plonkit)
description: Brown paved roads among fields of sugarcane, cassava, and corn can be found in southeastern Nakhon Ratchasima.

title: Thailand - Southern Sisaket (Plonkit)
description: Brown paved roads among fields of bananas, durians, rubber, and corn can be found in southern Sisaket.

title: Thailand - Lopburi Grid (Plonkit)
description: Southern Lopburi features a large, slightly north-north-west grid with fields of rice, corn, sugarcane, and cassava. Ridges can often be seen to the north, south and west.

title: Thailand - Pathum Thani Grid (Plonkit)
description: A large, almost perfectly north-south grid can be found in central and eastern Pathum Thani.

title: Thailand - Rayong Grid (Plonkit)
description: Western Rayong province features a northeast-southwest grid filled with modern and industrial buildings among fields of rubber trees, cassava, and pineapple.

title: Thailand - Highway 44 (Plonkit)
description: Highway 44 going through Krabi and Surat Thani is a divided four-lane highway with very large spacing in the middle. Often, you will not be able to see the other side of the highway. Rather, a yellow inner line will imply that the road is divided.

title: Thailand - Southern Thailand Car (Plonkit)
description: This rare Google car with a visible mirror is only found in far southern Thailand.

title: Thailand - Ko Sichang Car (Plonkit)
description: This rare Google car is only found on the island of Ko Sichang. It is recognizable due to the bar(s) protruding out of the blur.

title: Thailand - Khao Yai Smudge (Plonkit)
description: A smudge on the front left of the camera can be seen on the densely forested road going through Khao Yai National Park. This smudge can also be found in nearby areas of Nakhon Nayok and Prachin Buri.

title: Thailand - Road Markers (Plonkit)
description: These two road markers are generally found in Thailand. They will either have a white or a black Garuda on them.

title: Turkey - White-Blue Plates (Plonkit)
description: Turkey uses the same licence plates as most of Europe: they are long and white, with a blue strip on the left.

title: Turkey - Turkish Language (Plonkit)
description:
The Turkish language has a fairly unique look. It uses the following special characters:
- Ç ç and Ş ş with a cedilla (“hook” below the letter).
- Ö ö and Ü ü with an umlaut) (two dots).
- Ğ ğ with a breve.
- Dotless I ı. This letter in particular is noteworthy, as it is essentially unique to Turkish. In case you are confused: this is similar to the letter i, but without a dot when written in lowercase.
- Capital İ with a dot.

title: Turkey - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
Turkish bollards have a simple design: rectangular, plain white, and with a red reflector on the front. They are thin when seen from the side.
There is a rare yellow version, seen in some areas with high snowfall.

title: Turkey - Yellow Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: The colour of Turkish road lines is somewhat inconsistent. Most roads simply have white road lines. However, it is not uncommon to see yellow road lines. These roads can have fully yellow lines, or a combination of yellow and white lines.

title: Turkey - Salt and Pepper Roads (Plonkit)
description: Many roads have pavement with a grainy “salt and pepper” texture.

title: Turkey - Mediterranean Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Divided highways are extremely common, especially compared to other Mediterranean countries.

title: Turkey - Red-White Chevrons (Plonkit)
description:
Turkish chevrons are typically red on white. Beware that there are some other regional variants.
Usually, the tip of the arrow does not touch the edge of the chevron. Some chevrons have a neon yellow border.

title: Turkey - Yellow-Black Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: On intersections, you can often find this distinctive black and yellow chevron, with multiple arrows that point upward.

title: Turkey - Red-White Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Sometimes, you can see these narrow chevrons that have a red and white colour scheme.

title: Turkey - Direction Signs Use (Plonkit)
description: Direction signs use a very distinct font that can often be recognised by the noticeably wide letter spaces.

title: Turkey - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Snow poles usually feature a colour sequence of black-orange-black-white from top to bottom, with small red reflectors.

title: Turkey - Stop Signs Have (Plonkit)
description: Stop signs have the word “DUR” written on them. This is unique to Turkey.

title: Turkey - Mediterranean Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
Turkey uses both main types of guardrails:
- A-type guardrails, which have rounded edges.
- B-type guardrails, which have square edges.
While most Mediterranean countries use the A-type, B-type can help solve some tough 50-50s. Furthermore, seeing both types will exclude all southern European and Middle Eastern countries, other than Montenegro and Israel & the West Bank. For a full overview of which guardrails are found in which European country, see this infographic.

title: Turkey - Metal Poles (Plonkit)
description: Metal poles, either in the shape of a ladder or with a mesh pattern, are extremely common in Turkey.

title: Turkey - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: In the Generation 3 coverage, the Google car never has an antenna.

title: Turkey - Turkey Features (Plonkit)
description: The Generation 4 coverage in Turkey typically features a white Google car. Usually, only a tiny sliver of the back of the car is visible. The car can have a short antenna, or no antenna at all.

title: Turkey - Pickup Truck Meta (Plonkit)
description: A grey pickup truck can be found in some Generation 4 coverage.

title: Turkey - Turkey Also Has (Plonkit)
description: Turkey also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: Turkey - Flat Agricultural Land (Plonkit)
description:
The Turkish landscape ranges from arid in the southeast to a Mediterranean landscape in the southwest. In the north you will often find a more forested and lush landscape. The most typical landscape is semi-arid, either rolling or flat, with vast agricultural fields, containing very limited vegetation other than crops.
Beware that Turkey is a very naturally diverse country with many landscapes that are not mentioned in this tip.

title: Turkey - Turkey Features (Plonkit)
description: Tall and somewhat square apartment blocks are very common in Turkey.

title: Turkey - Turkey Features (Plonkit)
description: Turkey is a Muslim-majority country, and as such mosques can be found in most towns. In particular, tall minarets are extremely common and a good clue for the country.

title: Turkey - Brick Pavement Very (Plonkit)
description: Brick pavement is very common in urban areas, and the bricks will typically have the shape shown in the image.

title: Turkey - Area Code Map (Plonkit)
description: Turkish area codes follow a fairly easy to learn pattern and can be very useful to get the general region. Most notably, the first digit of area codes are ordered from 2 in the west to 4 in the east.

title: Turkey - Turkey Has Three (Plonkit)
description: Turkey has three main types of numbered roads. The largest type are the O-roads, which on kilometre markers feature an O followed by a hyphen and the road number. The second largest type are the D-roads, which omit the “D” on kilometre markers and instead only feature a 3-digit road number, followed by the road section number on the top and the kilometre at the bottom. The section number will generally increase to the southeast.

title: Turkey - Language Features (Plonkit)
description: The third type of roads are provincial roads. While these generally aren’t labelled on the map, they can still be used to regionguess since the kilometre markers feature the provincial code as the first two digits on the sign. These codes generally increase alphabetically from 01 to 76 with some newer regions being unordered. Shown in the image is a road from the Afyon Province (03).

title: Turkey - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
Generation 4 truck coverage is mainly found in the far east of the country and along the southern coast, with smaller pockets in the west and around Kastamonu.
For a more detailed look, see this document.

title: Turkey - Northern Turkey Tends (Plonkit)
description: Northern Turkey tends to be significantly lusher and more forested than the rest of the country.

title: Turkey - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: In the northeast you will find uncultivated grasslands in valleys surrounded by round hills. Trees are very limited in the region. In Generation 3 the area has an extremely distinct look, with deep green grass covering the hills. It is significantly more difficult to recognise in Generation 4, where the grass has a more arid look.

title: Turkey - Mediterranean Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Turkish pines (pinus brutia) are mainly found near the Mediterranean coast.

title: Turkey - Tea Plantations Common (Plonkit)
description: Tea plantations are common in the province of Rize.

title: Turkey - Mediterranean Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Olive trees are mainly found on the Mediterranean coast.

title: Turkey - Sunflowers Mainly Found (Plonkit)
description: Sunflowers are mainly found in northwestern Turkey.

title: Turkey - Turkey Features (Plonkit)
description: A majority of all vineyards in Turkey can be found in a region east of Izmir.

title: Turkey - Cotton Features (Plonkit)
description: Cotton is mainly found in the region surrounding the city of Şanlıurfa.

title: Turkey - Lake Views (Plonkit)
description: Lake Van is by far the biggest lake in Turkey and has a semi-arid landscape, being surrounded by dry grassy hills and occasional trees and agricultural fields near the shore.

title: Turkey - Dark Volcanic Rocks (Plonkit)
description: Dark, volcanic rocks are commonly found between the cities of Şanlıurfa and Diyarbakır.

title: Turkey - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: River valleys surrounded by steep, barren and rocky cliff sides can be found between the cities of Erzurum and Artvin and in the southeast near the city of Hakkâri.

title: Turkey - Tiled Roofs Mostly (Plonkit)
description:
Tiled roofs are mostly found in the western two thirds of the country.
Note that for this and the following roof-related tips to be reliable, the majority of all visible roofs should preferably be of that type.

title: Turkey - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Flat roofs are mostly found in the southeast and to a lesser extent along the south coast.

title: Turkey - Metal Roofs Most (Plonkit)
description: Metal roofs are most common in the east.

title: Turkey - Lake Views (Plonkit)
description: Sheet metal roofs shaped like low pyramids are mainly found far east, particularly in the general area surrounding Lake Van.

title: Turkey - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Many buildings in the Nevşehir Province are built by large, light and unevenly coloured, sandstone bricks.

title: Turkey - Yellow-Black Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Yellow on black chevrons are mainly found in and around the Balıkesir Province in the west and in the Kars Province in the far east. Beware that you may very rarely find them elsewhere.

title: Turkey - Yellow-Black Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Black on yellow chevrons are mainly found north of Izmir.

title: Turkey - Road Markings (Plonkit)
description:
Four-lane divided highways with no divider, other than double middle road lines, are almost exclusively found in the eastern half of the country.
Beware that divided highways with clear dividers, such as guardrails, can still be found in the east.

title: Turkey - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Vertical water tanks can be found in most of Turkey, but are notably uncommon along the south and west coast.

title: Turkey - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Horizontal water tanks placed on top of vertical water tanks are primarily found in a line following the south coast and going up to Elâzığ.

title: Turkey - Square Water Tanks (Plonkit)
description: Square water tanks with angled corners are found in the south, approximately from İskenderun to Sanliurfa.

title: Turkey - White Spherical Water (Plonkit)
description: White spherical water tanks can be found in the southeast, mainly south of Batman.

title: Turkey - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: In the European part of Turkey, except Istanbul, utility poles, and other electrical infrastructure, will have a 6 digit code, which is often seen on a small pole plate under the yellow electricity warning plate.

title: Turkey - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Street signs in the Ankara Province are blue with a small round top. Similar street signs can very rarely be found in Giresun.
Beware that some newer street signs are red.

title: Turkey - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs in the Izmir Province are dark blue, noticeably bulge outwards and very commonly have the emblem of Izmir in white at the top of the sign.

title: Turkey - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: If you find yourself surrounded by greenhouses, you are likely to be along the south coast west of Adana.

title: Turkey - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Around the city of Bodrum you will commonly find this type of whitewashed buildings with flat roofs, often combined with blue details or unpainted stone walls.

title: Turkey - Sandstone Buildings (Plonkit)
description: Göreme, west of Kayseri, can be recognised by the tall sandstone monoliths with ancient dwellings carved into them.

title: Turkey - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Mount Ararat, labelled as Ağrı Dağı on Google Maps, is a dormant volcano in far eastern Turkey and the tallest mountain in the country. It is often seen together with Küçük Ağrı, a smaller volcano to the southeast.

title: Turkey - Banana Plants Found (Plonkit)
description: Banana plants are found around the city of Alanya.

title: Turkey - Flat Agricultural Land (Plonkit)
description: Road E99 south of Şanlıurfa is a divided highway which can be recognised by the slightly hazy Generation 4 sunrise coverage combined with the flat agricultural landscape and general south-north road angle.

title: Turkey - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Road D525 south of Söke is a completely straight road going south-south-west to north-north-east with winter Generation 3 coverage. Along the road you will typically find a large amount of reed.

title: Turkey - Lake Views (Plonkit)
description: Along the western shore of Lake Beyşehir and Lake Eğirdir you can find this small single lane road with jagged, exposed rock and Turkish pines to the west. These two can be differentiated by the road west of Lake Eğirdir having a middle road line.

title: Turkey - Light Blue And (Plonkit)
description: These light blue and grey touristic signs which are either arrow shaped or rectangular with a half circle on the top can be found on the island of Bozcaada.

title: Turkey - White Street Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in several cities. In the bottom right corner, you can find a white arrow and some numbers. If this arrow is pointing in both directions and has a single arrowhead, rather than double, then you are almost certainly in Istanbul.
Beware that simple arrows pointing in only one direction can be found in both Istanbul and in other cities. However, if you see such signs in combination with red house numbers, then you should be in Istanbul.

title: Turkey - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs in Trabzon and Yalvaç are red and oval-shaped. House numbers also feature the same design.

title: Turkey - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs in Bursa are green, and generally have slightly extruded letters, meaning the signs are not completely flat.

title: Turkey - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs in Bolu are also green, but are completely flat and lack any kind of border.

title: Turkey - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Turkish bollards have a simple design: rectangular, plain white, and with a red reflector on the front. They are thin when seen from the side.

title: Turkey - Turkey Features (Plonkit)
description: Turkey is a muslim country, and as such mosques can be found in most towns. In particular, tall minarets are extremely common and a good clue for the country.

title: United Arab Emirates - Flat Desert (Plonkit)
description: The UAE typically features a flat desert landscape.

title: United Arab Emirates - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Outer roadlines are yellow, middle lines either white or yellow.

title: United Arab Emirates - Gen 3 White Car (Plonkit)
description: In almost all Generation 3 coverage, a white car with visible black roof racks was used.

title: United Arab Emirates - Gen 4 White Pickup (Plonkit)
description: In Generation 4 coverage, a white pickup truck with a trekker camera was used for much of the coverage. In a lot of the coverage, the truck is completely blurred out.

title: United Arab Emirates - Gen 4 Black Car (Plonkit)
description: You can also find regular Generation 4 coverage taken with a black car. The brake light is commonly visible.

title: United Arab Emirates - Arabic Script (Plonkit)
description: The official language in the UAE is Arabic. Its script can be identified by its lines and dots.

title: United Arab Emirates - Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Houses in residential areas are typically made of light-coloured stone. Reddish stones are often used for sidewalks.

title: United Arab Emirates - Striped Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Many signposts in the UAE have black-and-white stripes.

title: United Arab Emirates - Striped Curbs (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, almost all curbs are striped. They can be either black-and-white, or black-and-yellow.

title: United Arab Emirates - Roundabouts (Plonkit)
description: Divided roads and roundabouts are both very commonly seen in the UAE.

title: United Arab Emirates - Electricity Poles (Plonkit)
description: Electricity poles in the UAE are mostly made of dark brown wood. The pole tops consist of three insulators, symmetrically attached to a horizontal metal bar.

title: United Arab Emirates - Unpaved Residential Roads (Plonkit)
description: Although the UAE is a wealthy country, it is not uncommon for residential roads to be unpaved.

title: United Arab Emirates - Rifts (Plonkit)
description: Rifts can occasionally be found in the UAE.

title: United Arab Emirates - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Coverage in the UAE is mostly limited to the Northeastern part of the country.

title: United Arab Emirates - Dubai Skyline (Plonkit)
description: The skyline of Dubai is dominated by numerous skyscrapers, including the iconic Burj Khalifa.

title: United Arab Emirates - Eastern Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Mountains are only found in the far east of the country.

title: United Arab Emirates - Ras al Khaimah Mountains (Plonkit)
description: You can easily recognise the Northern part of the emirate of Ras al Khaimah thanks to the light-coloured mountains visible to the east.

title: United Arab Emirates - Gulf of Oman Coast (Plonkit)
description: If you see mountains to the west, and flatness to the east, you are likely near the Gulf of Oman, in the extreme East of the country.

title: United Arab Emirates - Sir Baniyas Island Car (Plonkit)
description: This rare white Google car with visible side mirrors and sparse vegetation is found on Sir Baniyas Island.

title: United Arab Emirates - Dubai Old Town Trekker (Plonkit)
description: In some parts of Dubai, including the old town, a Generation 4 sidewalk trekker was used. Sometimes, the employee’s black hair is visible.

title: United Arab Emirates - Dubai Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: These blue street name signs, with a narrow metal border, are specific to Dubai.

title: United Arab Emirates - Al Ain Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: The city of Al Ain has several trekkers, far away from the area with car coverage: two forts (Qasr Al Muwaiji and Al Jahili) and a zoo.

title: United Arab Emirates - Abu Dhabi Racetrack (Plonkit)
description: This racetrack coverage is found slightly east of Abu Dhabi.

title: United Arab Emirates - Southern Desert Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: Remote trekkers, with sand dunes all around, can be found in the far south of the country, between the towns of Taraq and Alyhyali.

title: Albania - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Albanian licence plates either have blue strips on both sides or a single red strip on the left side.

title: Albania - All Generation 4 (Plonkit)
description: All Generation 4 coverage in Albania was taken using a “smallcam” camera, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: Albania - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: ‘Rifts’ can rarely be seen in Albanian generation 3 coverage, due to poor stitching.

title: Albania - Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Albanian bollards have a black top with a red and grey reflector. The bottom is painted white.

title: Albania - Triangular Poletops (Plonkit)
description: These pole tops, with an upside down triangle shape, are a good clue for Albania.

title: Albania - Horizontal Bar Poletops (Plonkit)
description: Other, more simple Albanian pole tops will often have horizontal bars.

title: Albania - Yellow-Black Chevrons (Plonkit)
description:
Albanian chevrons are white on black.
Montenegro uses two chevrons, both of which are different from the Albanian chevron: black on white and red on yellow.

title: Albania - Black Sign Backs (Plonkit)
description: The backs of road signs are often painted black.

title: Albania - Stop Sign Font (Plonkit)
description: The “S” on Albanian stop signs feature a distinct shape; the ends of the S are quite short and have the same angle as the middle, rather than being vertical. This is also sometimes seen on directional signs.

title: Albania - Speed Sign Font (Plonkit)
description: The numbers on speed signs are written in a bold font.

title: Albania - Guardrail Endings (Plonkit)
description: These flat and wide guardrail endings that bend away from the road can often be found in Albania.

title: Albania - Language (Plonkit)
description:
Albanian is not very closely related to any other European languages, and therefore has a fairly distinct look.
Words often contain the letter Ë, ë, and sometimes Ç ç.

title: Albania - Rruga (Plonkit)
description: The Albanian word for street is rruga.

title: Albania - Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Albania is generally a mountainous country, with a Mediterranean climate and vegetation. In between the hills and mountains, you can sometimes find more flat, agricultural valleys. The mountains are usually quite green, sometimes with patches of exposed rock visible.

title: Albania - Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: Albania has a lot of exposed red soil next to roads.

title: Albania - See Lot (Plonkit)
description:
You will see a lot of cylinder-shaped water tanks on the roofs of buildings.
Some parts of Turkey also have a lot of similar-looking water tanks.

title: Albania - Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Albania has a lot of Italian-style buildings: pastel colours, orange tiled roofs, and blocky shapes with lots of balconies.

title: Albania - Mercedes (Plonkit)
description: Mercedes is the most popular car brand in Albania, by quite a margin. The specific style of sedan pictured here is particularly common.

title: Albania - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
There are two types of car and camera meta in generation 3 Albania:
- Coverage where the Google car has a long antenna and you can see rifts in the sky.
- Coverage where the Google car has a short antenna and there are no rifts visible.
You can click on the image to enlarge it. You can also use this Maps layer to look at the coverage in more detail (credits to icraig1205).

title: Albania - Albania Elevation (Plonkit)
description:
Albania is generally a very mountainous country. This map shows the elevation and relief.
- Low-lying areas are mostly concentrated in the west, around Shkodër, Tirana and Vlorë. This part of the country is characterised by agricultural flatlands and low, undulating hills. Note that the highland plateau around Korçë in the southeast is also very flat.
- The highest mountains can be found in the far north and the far south. In places, these mountains can have an almost alpine look.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Albania - Theth National Park (Plonkit)
description: The road leading into Theth National Park can typically be recognised by the tall, jagged mountains, often with bare mountainsides.

title: Albania - Montenegro Border Valley (Plonkit)
description: The road by the eastern part of the Montenegrin border goes in a valley with tall, fully exposed cliff sides along the road.

title: Albania - Maja e Papingut (Plonkit)
description: Maja e Papingut is a massive mountain in the south of Albania, with an almost completely vertical cliffside near the top. It can be seen from several nearby roads.

title: Albania - Devoll River Valley (Plonkit)
description: A wide, almost dried out river valley going southeast to northwest, can be seen along the SH71 between Pishaj and Kokel.

title: Albania - Bay of Vlorë (Plonkit)
description: The large Bay of Vlorë can be seen on many parts of the SH4 between Vlorë and Orikum. It can be recognized by the large Karaburun peninsula jutting out into the ocean from the south, and the small Sazan island just to its north.

title: Albania - Vlorë Pine Forest (Plonkit)
description: A couple of small roads northwest of Vlorë can be recognised by the very coastal-looking Aleppo pine forest.

title: Albania - SH4 Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: On the SH4 between Levan and Tepelenë and right by the Greek border, you may see double outer road lines with a wide gap between them.

title: Albania - A1 Highway (Plonkit)
description:
Albania only has a few divided highways covered on Street View. All of these and how to differentiate them will be covered in the tips below.
The most easily recognisable divided highway is the A1 between Fushë Milot and Thumanë, which is the only one with a triple guardrail.

title: Albania - Concrete Dividers (Plonkit)
description: The sections of the SH2 between Durrës and Tirana and of the SH4 between Lushnjë and Rrogozhinë are both divided by simple concrete blocks.

title: Albania - Grassy Concrete Dividers (Plonkit)
description: In Tirana, Durrës and on the A3 and SH3 south of Tirana you can find highways which are divided by concrete blocks, with grass and greenery in between.

title: Albania - SH4 Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Most of the SH4 between Durrës and Fier is divided by a basic double guardrail. The road does not go through any mountains.

title: Albania - E851 Guardrail (Plonkit)
description: The E851 is the only divided road with a basic double guardrail that goes directly through mountains.

title: Albania - A2 Highway (Plonkit)
description: The A2 north of Vlorë can be recognised by the fairly flat surroundings combined with the double guardrail with an extra tall fence dividing the highway.

title: Albania - Lezhë (Plonkit)
description: The city of Lezhë can often be recognised by the old castle at the top of a tall hill.

title: Albania - Gjirokaster (Plonkit)
description: Gjirokaster is a city situated on the western hillside of a wide valley.

title: Albania - Rifts (Plonkit)
description: ‘Rifts’ can commonly be seen in Albanian coverage, due to poor stitching.

title: Albania - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Albanian chevrons are white on black.

title: Albania - Water Tanks (Plonkit)
description: You will see a lot of cylinder-shaped water tanks on the roofs of buildings.

title: Albania - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Coverage in Albania is limited. Generally only the larger towns have extensive side-road coverage.

Note that while the coverage is limited, a lot of it still appears to be very rural. It is not just on big main roads or urban areas.

You can click on the image to enlarge it, or use this site to study the official coverage in detail.

title: Albania - Camera Metas (Plonkit)
description:
There are two types of car and camera meta in Albania:

Coverage where the Google car has a long antenna and you can see rifts in the sky.

Coverage where the Google car has a short antenna and there are no rifts visible.

You can click on the image to enlarge it. You can also use this Maps layer to look at the coverage in more detail (credits to icraig1205).

title: Albania - E86 Bollards (Plonkit)
description: On this section of the E86 near the Greek border, you will sometimes see these unique bollards. They have a round shape and a simple red reflector. They look superficially similar to the flatter Turkish bollard.

title: Albania - E86 Yellow Lines (Plonkit)
description: There are three sections of road in Albania with yellow centre lines. The first is on the E86 near lake Ohrid with the lake in the east, making it easily recognisable.

title: Albania - SH97 Yellow Lines (Plonkit)
description: The second is the SH97 which goes through a fairly hilly landscape. It also goes through some smaller valleys.

title: Albania - SH1 Yellow Lines (Plonkit)
description: The final road with a yellow centre line is the SH1 north of Tirana. It goes through a wide valley with fairly tall mountains on either side.

title: Andorra - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Andorran licence plates have an orange dot on the left side and can be regularly found throughout the country.

title: Andorra - Camera Generations (Plonkit)
description:
Andorra only has Generation 2 and Generation 3 coverage. In all Generation 3 coverage, a medium-short antenna is visible on the Google car.
Generation 3 is by far the most common. Almost all of Generation 2 is overwritten and is mostly confined to a couple of smaller off-roads.

title: Andorra - Autumn Colors (Plonkit)
description: All the Generation 3 coverage was taken in October, meaning that many deciduous trees have autumn colours.

title: Andorra - Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Andorra has a lot of these stone buildings. They can be seen almost everywhere in the country.

title: Andorra - Snow Poles (Plonkit)
description: Andorran snow poles are made out of wood and can have a variety of colours on them.

title: Andorra - Language (Plonkit)
description:
Catalan is the main language in Andorra. It is a Romance language that is closely related to Spanish and French.
If you are unfamiliar with Romance languages, it can be hard to distinguish between Catalan and Spanish. If you see i instead of y (“and” in English), it is Catalan. In addition, more Catalan words end with consonants.

title: Andorra - Carrer (Plonkit)
description: The Catalan word for street is “carrer”.

title: Andorra - Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: These kilometre markers with CG and CS road numbers are found in Andorra.

title: Andorra - Guardrail Reflectors (Plonkit)
description: Andorra uses yellow reflectors on its guardrails.

title: Andorra - Bollards (Plonkit)
description: The Andorran bollard has an orange reflector and can be occasionally found on the main highways.

title: Andorra - Traffic Cones (Plonkit)
description: Yellow and turquoise-green traffic cones are used in the whole country.

title: Andorra - Pedestrian Signs Have (Plonkit)
description: Pedestrian signs have 8 stripes.

title: Andorra - Snow Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: Andorra has a lot of Generation 2 snow trekkers, especially on ski resorts.

title: Andorra - Andorra la Vella (Plonkit)
description: Andorra la Vella is a capital city surrounded by high mountains, making it recognisable.

title: Andorra - Caldea Tower (Plonkit)
description: In the capital Andorra la Vella you can often see the Caldea tower and the sky wheel.

title: Andorra - Pas de la Casa (Plonkit)
description: Pas de la Casa, a touristy city in eastern Andorra, can be easily recognized by the plethora of shops and hotels. As it is located at an altitude of 2080 metres, there are no trees visible on the mountains surrounding it.

title: Austria - White-Blue Plates (Plonkit)
description:
Austria has long, white licence plates with the standard blue EU strip on the left.
Swiss plates are long and white, but lack the blue strip.

title: Austria - Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
Austria uses white bollards, with a black top. The colour of the reflector is (dark) red or dark grey.
Many bollards also feature a small nipple-shaped black cap on the top. Bollards sometimes have a snow pole on top.

title: Austria - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description:
Austria uses two colour schemes for chevrons:
- white on red
- red on yellow

title: Austria - Wooden Poles (Plonkit)
description: Round wooden poles are the most common type of pole found in Austria.

title: Austria - Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Most of Austria is mountainous and covered in forests. However, some areas in the east and northeast are much more flat and agricultural.

title: Austria - Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Alpine architecture is common in Austria and other countries in the Alps. Houses commonly have distinct light coloured walls, with wooden elements such as balconies or panelling around the top floor, with dark-coloured wooden roofs that extend outward. The roofs can sometimes be angled downward at the front and back. In addition, houses are also often multi-storeyed.

title: Austria - Language (Plonkit)
description: The official language of Austria is German. The German language uses the special letters Ä, Ö, Ü and ß.

title: Austria - Camera Generations (Plonkit)
description:
You can tell the three German-speaking countries apart by camera meta alone:
- Austria only has Generation 3 and Generation 4 coverage (the only exceptions being Generation 2 on one road in Burgenland, and several ski resort trekkers).
- Germany only has Generation 4 coverage. (the only exceptions being spills and trekkers)
- Switzerland car coverage is always low-cam. This can be recognized by the much bigger car blur.

title: Austria - Smallcam (Plonkit)
description: Austria also has generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: Austria - Direction Signs (Plonkit)
description: Direction signs have a white background, a blue outline, and a unique font.

title: Austria - Town Entrance Signs (Plonkit)
description: Similar white signs with a blue outline and unique font can also be seen at the entrance of towns.

title: Austria - Green Signs (Plonkit)
description: Green signs can commonly be seen, giving directions to different local facilities.

title: Austria - Pedestrian Signs (Plonkit)
description: Pedestrian signs have a unique design: instead of zebra stripes, they have two horizontal dashed lines.

title: Austria - Sign Mounting (Plonkit)
description: Road signs in Austria are sometimes mounted by four metal clips, which is unique within central Europe. However, plenty of Austrian signs are attached in other ways.

title: Austria - Road Markers (Plonkit)
description: Road markers are blue with white numbers. They have one decimal separated by a comma, making them very recognizable.

title: Austria - Bus Stop Signs (Plonkit)
description: Austrian bus stop signs contain a yellow and green circle with the letter H.

title: Austria - One-Way Signs (Plonkit)
description: These one-way traffic signs, with the word ‘EINBAHN’ written on them, are unique to Austria.

title: Austria - No Stopping Signs (Plonkit)
description: “No Stopping” and “No Waiting” signs in Austria will often have the words “Anfang” or “Ende” (meaning “beginning” and “end”) written on, or below, them.

title: Austria - Europe Features (Plonkit)
description:
These simple dead-end signs with a white upside down T are mostly unique to Austria.
Most countries in Europe use this sign.

title: Austria - Gas Poles (Plonkit)
description: These yellow natural gas poles, which resemble snow poles, are unique to Austria.

title: Austria - Elevation Map (Plonkit)
description:
Elevation is very important when region-guessing Austria based on landscape alone.
The central and western parts of Austria are the most mountainous. The flatter areas are found in the east, mostly near the borders. Note that “flat” is a relative concept in Austria: even in the flat areas, rolling hills are still common.

title: Austria - Autobahn Map (Plonkit)
description:
A map of Austrian A-roads can be seen here, following the general trend of increasing in number from east to west.
You can click the image to enlarge it.

title: Austria - B-Roads Map (Plonkit)
description:
Austrian B-roads, indicated by white text inside of a blue rectangle, also follow the general trend of increasing in number from east to west.
An important exception to this are roads 222-230, which are located inside the state of Vienna.
You can click the image to enlarge it.

title: Austria - State Flags (Plonkit)
description:
Each Austrian state has its own unique flag, shown in the image.
You can click the image to enlarge it.

title: Austria - Bus Companies (Plonkit)
description:
Each Austrian state has its own unique bus company, the logo of which can be seen on the side of buses.
You can click the image to enlarge it.

title: Austria - Vorarlberg Bus Stops (Plonkit)
description: Bus stops consisting of neon-yellow poles are found in Vorarlberg.

title: Austria - Vorarlberg Pole Stickers (Plonkit)
description: These yellow and white stripes around poles and signposts are found in Vorarlberg.

title: Austria - Vorarlberg KM Markers (Plonkit)
description: White kilometre markers can be found in Vorarlberg as well as on a road in western Salzburg.

title: Austria - Salzburg Road Squares (Plonkit)
description: A large white painted square in the middle of the road can be found next to kilometre markers in Salzburg.

title: Austria - Burgenland Güterweg Signs (Plonkit)
description: Green “Güterweg” signs are found in Burgenland.

title: Austria - Upper Austria Güterweg Signs (Plonkit)
description: White “Güterweg” signs with a black outline are mainly found in Upper Austria.

title: Austria - Lower Austria Sign Borders (Plonkit)
description: In Lower Austria, you may find signs with yellow and blue sign borders, corresponding to the flag of the region.

title: Austria - Vineyards (Plonkit)
description:
Vineyards are limited to the far eastern part of the country.
You can find a very precise map here. Notably, there are a lot of vineyards close to Vienna and around Lake Neusiedl.

title: Austria - Highest Mountains (Plonkit)
description:
The highest parts of the Alps are found in the west and central parts of the country.
The tallest mountains are found in the panhandle of Austria, on the Italian border. These mountains can be recognized by their generally sharper peak and grander appearance.

title: Austria - Tin Foil Antenna (Plonkit)
description: This unique tin foil antenna can be found in western Austria, mostly near the Swiss border.

title: Austria - Vienna Street Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Vienna street signs are extremely recognizable dark blue plaques with a traditional-looking white serif font. The number at the start will indicate which district you are in (see the map).
You can click the image to enlarge it.

title: Austria - White Street Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Most other major cities in Austria also have their own unique street signs.
- Vienna - District Number
- Salzburg - Unique Font
- Klagenfurt - Irregular White Border
- St Polten - Rounded White Border
You can click the image to enlarge it.

title: Austria - Vienna/Innsbruck Pole Tape (Plonkit)
description: Poles in Vienna and Innsbruck feature these red-and-white pieces of tape that look like the Austrian flag. They can be differentiated by the fact that the tapes in Vienna are thinner, and there are typically two on each pole.

title: Austria - Lake Constance (Plonkit)
description: Lake Constance (known in German as the Bodensee) is a large lake on the western border of Austria. It can be recognized by its vastness, which is not seen in other lakes within the mountainous part of the country.

title: Austria - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Austria has long, white licence plates with the standard blue EU strip on the left.

title: Austria - Dead-End Signs (Plonkit)
description: These simple dead-end signs with a white upside down T are unique to Austria.

title: Austria - City Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Most other major cities in Austria also have their own unique street signs.

title: Azores - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Since the Azores is an autonomous region of Portugal, you will often come across various types of Portuguese infrastructure, such as poles, chevrons and bollards.

title: Azores - Agricultural Area (Plonkit)
description: Most of the Azores visible on Street View consists of open agricultural fields in a rolling landscape, often with taller round hills in the background.

title: Azores - Dry Rock Walls (Plonkit)
description: Dry rock walls made of volcanic rocks are very common on the Azores.

title: Azores - Hydrangeas Commonly Be (Plonkit)
description: Hydrangeas can commonly be seen on the Azores.

title: Azores - Japanese Cedars Cryptomeria (Plonkit)
description: Japanese cedars (cryptomeria japonica) are very common on the Azores.

title: Azores - Houses Azores Typically (Plonkit)
description:
Houses in the Azores are typically one or two stories, with an orange tiled roof. They are painted white or in pastel colours, and dark green shutters on windows are common.
While you can also find yellow or blue highlights like in mainland Portugal, grey highlights are almost exclusive to the Azores.

title: Azores - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs in the Azores are almost exclusively painted ceramic tiles, with blue letters and, typically, a decorative pattern around the edge.

title: Azores - Signposts Azores Often (Plonkit)
description: Signposts on the Azores are often striped.

title: Azores - Black And White (Plonkit)
description: Black and white cows are very common on the Azores.

title: Azores - Only Islands Azores (Plonkit)
description: The only islands in the Azores with car coverage are Ilha de São Miguel, Ilha Terceira and Ilha do Faial.

title: Azores - Only Island With (Plonkit)
description: The only island with Generation 4 coverage is Ilha de São Miguel.

title: Azores - Shitcam Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
Shitcam coverage is found on Ilha de São Miguel and Ilha do Faial.
The car seen on São Miguel has an indentation in the centre, while the one on Faial appears as a smooth surface, sometimes with an antenna visible.

title: Azores - Lake Views (Plonkit)
description: Ilha de São Miguel is the only island in the Azores or Madeira where you can find lakes.

title: Azores - Rock Walls With (Plonkit)
description: Rock walls with a white painted concrete top are somewhat common on Ilha Terceira.

title: Azores - Ilha Do Faial (Plonkit)
description: On Ilha do Faial, you will sometimes find traditional whitewashed rock walls with unevenly sized dark basalt stones.

title: Azores - Trekker Going Along (Plonkit)
description: A trekker going along the edge of a crater can be seen on Ilha do Faial.

title: Belarus - Only Coverage Belarus (Plonkit)
description:
The only coverage in Belarus, apart from spills, is a single walking trekker in the historic centre of Minsk.
Instead of learning a lot of country-specific clues, it is more practical to simply memorise what the trekker looks like.
You can recognise trekkers by the fact that the camera feels a bit lower than the usual Google car. In Belarus’ case, the trekker is also mostly on pedestrian-only roads.
You can find information about the border spill coverage in the Spillover Guide.

title: Belarus - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: The Minsk trekker features a historic part of the city, with well-maintained classical European architecture. Many buildings have white or pastel coloured walls. Most of the roads you see are pedestrian-only.

title: Belarus - Holy Spirit Cathedral (Plonkit)
description: The Holy Spirit Cathedral features prominently in the coverage. Its two towers can often be seen from far away.

title: Belarus - Minsk Features (Plonkit)
description: The pavement which the trekker walks on in Minsk is mostly grey rectangular tiles. On a small part, there are pink-ish tiles in a specific pattern.

title: Belarus - Cyrillic Script (Plonkit)
description: Signs will be in Belarusian or Russian. Both languages use the Cyrillic alphabet.

title: Belarus - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: The Minsk centre street signs are sea-green, and can be seen almost everywhere.

title: Belgium - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Licence plates in Belgium use red text. You can recognise this distinct colour even through the blur.

title: Belgium - Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Belgium uses white bollards with a yellow rectangular reflector on the front and white on the back. A second type of bollard is dark brown with two red stripes at the top. Occasionally, other bollards can be seen.

title: Belgium - Guardrail Reflectors (Plonkit)
description: Belgium uses A-type guardrails with yellow reflectors.

title: Belgium - Poles (Plonkit)
description: Most poles in Belgium are concrete, square shaped, and have tiny holes running up them. They often have small metal wrappings around them. The second most common type of pole has oval-shaped holes. You can find many different types of concrete poles in Belgium.

title: Belgium - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Directional signs in Belgium are most often blue or white.

title: Belgium - Blue Signs (Plonkit)
description: Road signs often have an additional small blue sign. In other European countries, these small signs are usually just white.

title: Belgium - Pedestrian Signs (Plonkit)
description: Belgium uses pedestrian crossing signs without any stripes, but with two horizontal dotted lines. The man on the sign has a square head.

title: Belgium - Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: Kilometre markers in Belgium are often green, but can have red text as well.

title: Belgium - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Belgium uses white chevrons, with a red arrow.

title: Belgium - Concrete Slab Roads (Plonkit)
description: A lot of rural roads in Belgium are made out of concrete slabs, almost like you would see in the Philippines or Thailand.

title: Belgium - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Belgium uses all white road lines. These can be continuous or broken. Roads are often accompanied by bike lanes on both sides.

title: Belgium - Red Brick Architecture (Plonkit)
description: A lot of houses in Belgium are made of distinctive red bricks.

title: Belgium - Stone Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Houses in the South of the country use a lot of stone, have gray tones and generally look more French.

title: Belgium - Orange Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Signposts in Belgium are often orange. The backs of signs are also sometimes orange. This is unique to Belgium.

title: Belgium - Street Name Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street name signs in Belgium are very diverse, and often unique to a city. Most common colours are white and dark blue. They often have the town or city name written on them.

title: Belgium - Town Entry Signs (Plonkit)
description: Town entry signs in Belgium are white with a black border. They also mention the name of the city or municipality in bold, black text.

title: Belgium - Priority Signs (Plonkit)
description: Priority signs in Belgium have an orange diamond and are much smaller than in other countries.

title: Belgium - Bus Stops (Plonkit)
description: Bus stops are always marked by yellow signposts. Bus shelters often have yellow roofs.

title: Belgium - Traffic Lights (Plonkit)
description: Traffic lights are most often supported by black-and-yellow or red-and-white striped poles.

title: Belgium - Water Hydrant Signs (Plonkit)
description: Belgium uses these red water hydrants signs with the letter H on top.

title: Belgium - Gutters (Plonkit)
description: Almost all roads (big or small) in Belgium use gutters on both sides. This is much less common in neighbouring countries.

title: Belgium - Bicycle Path Lines (Plonkit)
description: Belgian bicycle paths have short dashed outer lines.

title: Belgium - Blurred Houses (Plonkit)
description: After Germany, Belgium is the next country in which you can find the most blurred houses.

title: Belgium - Red Car Antenna (Plonkit)
description: Coverage with a red car and a long antenna can rarely be seen in Belgium.

title: Belgium - Smallcam (Plonkit)
description: Belgium also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: Belgium - Flatness (Plonkit)
description: Belgium is generally flat in the northwest of the country, especially near the coast. The further south east you go, the hillier.

title: Belgium - Languages (Plonkit)
description:
Belgium has 3 official languages.
- Dutch (Flemish), spoken in Flanders, the Northern part of Belgium. There is an abundance of letters and combinations like z, w, ee and ij.
- French (Walloon), spoken in Wallonia, the Southern part of Belgium. You can see letters like ç, é, è and à.
- German, spoken in Ostbelgien, a small region in the east of the country. You can see letters like ä, ü, ö and ß.

title: Belgium - Bilingual Brussels (Plonkit)
description: Brussels, the capital of Belgium, is bilingual. You will see both French and Dutch on signs.

title: Belgium - Regional Bus Stops (Plonkit)
description: Bus stop signs in Flanders (and Brussels) have a white rectangle at the top. In Wallonia they will have a yellow top.

title: Belgium - Warning Sign Borders (Plonkit)
description: In Flanders (and Brussels), 95% of warning signs have a thick red outline, without a white border. Contrarily, you will most often find warning signs with a small white outline in Wallonia.

title: Belgium - Traffic Light Poles (Plonkit)
description: Traffic lights held up by yellow-and-black poles are unique to Flanders. In contrast, Wallonia and Brussels frequently use a red-and-white design.

title: Belgium - Area Code Map (Plonkit)
description:
Phone codes in Belgium are very useful to determine the region you are in. They are 9 digits long. The 1 or 2 number(s) after the leading 0 indicate the area code.
0X XXX XX XX (Brussels, Antwerp, Liege, Ghent.)
0XX XX XX XX (Other cities.)
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Belgium - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description:
As mentioned before, municipality names are often mentioned on street signs, usually in smaller font than the street name. The map shows a selection of recognizable street signs in the bigger cities.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Belgium - Ardennes (Plonkit)
description: The Ardennes, located in the southeast part of Belgium, have a very distinct landscape. You can see a lot of steep hills, dense forests, and valleys.

title: Belgium - Polders (Plonkit)
description: The coastal plain is extremely flat and consists of so-called polders, which are man-made fields at or below sea level, surrounded by many waterways. This landscape is situated near the North Sea coast, as well as near the western part of the border with the Netherlands, particularly around Antwerp.

title: Belgium - North Sea Coast (Plonkit)
description:
Many parts of the Belgian North Sea coast are lined by apartment blocks, in a manner that is often derisively referred to as a “wall” of buildings by locals.
Near the coast, you will also sometimes be able to spot a dune landscape, with low bushes, long grass and sandy soil.

title: Belgium - Baarle-Hertog (Plonkit)
description: Baarle-Hertog, located north-east of Antwerp, is composed of several exclaves and enclaves of Belgium and the Netherlands. You can often see the country's borders in this city (indicated by small white crosses). Street name signs tell you whether you are in Belgium or The Netherlands.

title: Belgium - Phone Codes (Plonkit)
description:
Phone codes in Belgium are very useful to determine the region you are in. They are 9 digits long. The 1 or 2 number(s) after the leading 0 indicate the area code.

0X XXX XX XX (Brussels, Antwerp, Liege, Ghent.)

0XX XX XX XX (Other cities.)

title: Belgium - Street Signs Map (Plonkit)
description: As mentioned before, municipality names are often mentioned on street signs, usually in smaller font than the street name. The map shows a selection of recognizable street signs in the bigger cities.

title: Bulgaria - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Bulgarian licence plates have the typical European design, with the blue strip on the left.

title: Bulgaria - Cyrillic Script (Plonkit)
description:
Bulgaria mainly uses the Cyrillic alphabet. However, a lot of signs will also have the Latin alphabet.
The letter “Ъ” is only found in Bulgarian and Russian, although it is fairly uncommon in Russian.

title: Bulgaria - Bulgarian Word Street (Plonkit)
description:
The Bulgarian word for street is улица (ulitsa), sometimes abbreviated ул. (ul.).
Russia also uses улица/ulitsa.

title: Bulgaria - Gen 4 Cars (Plonkit)
description:
There are three types of Generation 4 cars that were used to cover Bulgaria:
- A blue car, which can be found in most European countries.
- A red car, which is also found in Latvia, Lithuania, Russia, Slovakia, and Sweden. Of these, Russia and Slovakia are easiest to confuse with Bulgaria.
- A black car, which is found in many European countries; of which Greece and Croatia are the ones more likely to be confused with Bulgaria.
All cars can be found with or without antenna. Additionally, you can also encounter coverage where the car is completely hidden.

title: Bulgaria - Winter Gen 3 (Plonkit)
description: The majority of Generation 3 coverage in Bulgaria was taken during March and April, resulting in very distinct dead-looking “winter” coverage.

title: Bulgaria - Flag Antenna (Plonkit)
description:
You can commonly see a small piece of grey tape at the top of the car antenna in Generation 3 coverage. The community sometimes refers to it as “flag antenna”.
Not all Gen 3 coverage has this tape.

title: Bulgaria - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Most utility poles in Bulgaria are cylindrical and made of concrete.
There is also a less common concrete ‘ladder pole’ variation. You can also sometimes see simple wooden poles.

title: Bulgaria - Hook Insulators (Plonkit)
description: Most poles have small, alternating hook-shaped insulators.

title: Bulgaria - Three Hook Poletop (Plonkit)
description: This style of pole top, with 3 large, alternating insulators that are shaped like upward facing hooks, is a good clue for Bulgaria. This pole top is probably unique to the country.

title: Bulgaria - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Bulgarian chevrons are typically red on white.

title: Bulgaria - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Bulgarian directional signs are blue, arrow-shaped, and use both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabet. Importantly, even if you are far away and cannot decipher the script, you can still see that the sign has two lines of text instead of one.

title: Bulgaria - Town Entry Signs (Plonkit)
description: Town entry signs have a simple white design and also use both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabet. Like with the directional signs, the two lines of text are obvious, even when seen from far away.

title: Bulgaria - Pedestrian Signs (Plonkit)
description: Bulgarian pedestrian signs have four stripes, and the person is wearing a hat.

title: Bulgaria - Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
Bollards are generally fairly rare in Bulgaria.
When you see them, they almost always have this somewhat generic design, which is relatively similar to the bollards found in Croatia and Hungary. They have a red reflector on the front, and a white one on the back. The design isn’t terribly consistent: sometimes they are thinner, and the shape of the reflector varies.

title: Bulgaria - Thin Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Bulgaria usually has thin roadlines. This is particularly useful to tell Bulgaria apart from Romania, where roadlines are usually much thicker.

title: Bulgaria - Road Quality (Plonkit)
description: Bulgaria generally has fairly poor-quality roads, with many small cracks and occasionally potholes.

title: Bulgaria - Roofs (Plonkit)
description:
Most houses in Bulgaria have orange tiled roofs, with distinct patches of mortar) along the corner tiles.
Famously, Bulgarian roofs often seem poorly constructed: the roof tiles and mortar tend to be uneven, especially when compared to other European countries.

title: Bulgaria - Metallic Bins (Plonkit)
description: Metallic trash bins with this shape are very common in Bulgaria.

title: Bulgaria - Topography (Plonkit)
description:
The Balkan mountains cut across Bulgaria and divide the country in two distinct halves. North of them, you will find a mostly flat area that goes all the way to the border with Romania.
The Rhodope Mountains start close to Sofia and run South-East into Greece. In them you will find the highest peaks of Bulgaria.
Between both mountain ranges you will find the second biggest flat area of Bulgaria.
The westernmost part of the country usually features many small valleys surrounded by hills and small mountains.

title: Bulgaria - Area Codes (Plonkit)
description:
Area codes in Bulgaria are one of the best clues to regionguess urban rounds. Conveniently, they are ordered by first digit, so just learning the first digit can yield high results with little effort.
Numbers between parentheses in the map are area codes from a neighbouring province that frequently spill into that one.
Codes next to a small dot represent area codes unique to the province capital.

title: Bulgaria - National Parks (Plonkit)
description: The towering mountains of Pirin and Rila National Parks can be recognised by the tall pyramid-shaped peaks, and can be seen from a few different vantage points in Blagoevgrad, Kyustendil and Sofia Provinces.

title: Bulgaria - Wind Turbines (Plonkit)
description: Wind turbines are most common in Dobrich Province, and usually towards the coast.

title: Bulgaria - Smolyan Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Buildings with features similar to Alpine architecture, such as white walls with brown wooden details are commonly found in and around the Smoljan region in the south.

title: Bulgaria - Invisible Gen 4 Car (Plonkit)
description: Locations with an invisible Generation 4 Street View car can be found along the North and West borders of Bulgaria, as well as the northern half of the coast.

title: Bulgaria - Red Gen 4 Car (Plonkit)
description:
A red Generation 4 Street View car is mostly found in central and southeastern Bulgaria.
This car can be found with and without an antenna.

title: Bulgaria - Tape Antenna (Plonkit)
description: Generation 3 coverage with a piece of tape on a short antenna can be commonly found in the eastern part of Bulgaria.

title: Bulgaria - Long Antenna Tape (Plonkit)
description: Generation 3 locations with a taped long antenna and visible white car can be found in Stara Zagora, and rarely a few small roads in Plovdiv and Burgas.

title: Bulgaria - Varna Antenna (Plonkit)
description: This antenna with unpeeled tape at the top, resulting in a bulkier antenna tip, can be found in the Varna Province. Coverage with this antenna is exclusively in March, resulting in a dead winter look.

title: Bulgaria - Vratsa Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The mountains overlooking Vratsa from the southwest have a very distinct “bumpy” shape, and can be seen from afar in the province.

title: Bulgaria - Old Towns (Plonkit)
description: The old town of Nessebar, and to a lesser extent Sozopol, can be recognised by the well-preserved old buildings made of a combination of unpainted stone, white stone walls and brown wood. Most of the streets are paved with cobblestone.

title: Bulgaria - Sofia Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: White street signs with two red strips; one covering the bottom and one covering part of the top, can be found in Sofia.

title: Bulgaria - Stara Zagora Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Brown street signs with bright yellow text can be found in Stara Zagora.

title: Bulgaria - Ulitsa (Plonkit)
description: The Bulgarian word for street is улица (ulitsa), sometimes abbreviated ул. (ul.).

title: Bulgaria - Suburbs (Plonkit)
description: Suburbs in Bulgaria are generally among the poorest areas in Europe, with small, densely built houses and generally an almost ghetto-like look.

title: Croatia - White-Blue Plates (Plonkit)
description: Croatia has long, white licence plates. Some plates have a blue strip on the left, some are fully white. Most cars seen in Generation 3 will not feature a blue strip on their licence plates. In addition, there is a mix of cars with or without blue strips in Generation 4, with blue strips more common on newer cars.

title: Croatia - Angled Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Croatian bollards are white with a black rectangle and red or white reflector. From the top, it is shaped like a triangle.

title: Croatia - Language Features (Plonkit)
description: Croatian is a Slavic language. It is always written in the Latin alphabet. ‘IJE’ is common in Croatian whereas Serbian uses only ‘E’ instead.

title: Croatia - Red-White Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Croatia features chevrons with a red arrow on a yellow or white background.

title: Croatia - Road Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Croatia has square (B-type) guardrails.

title: Croatia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Generation 3 coverage often has a non-standard car blur where the side mirrors of the car are partially visible. This is not unique to Croatia, but by far most common there.

title: Croatia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
Another quirk of Generation 3 coverage is that the majority of it was made in autumn. This means that the vegetation in this coverage will often have distinct yellowish or orange fall colours.
Take note that this seasonal meta is not found in Generation 4 coverage.

title: Croatia - Croatia Features (Plonkit)
description: A black generation 4 car that will never have an antenna can be found in Croatia.

title: Croatia - Croatia Features (Plonkit)
description: A white generation 4 car that will never have an antenna can be found in Croatia.

title: Croatia - Stickers With Letters (Plonkit)
description: Stickers with the letters HR can be found on Croatian cars. HR stands for Hrvatska, the Croatian name for Croatia.

title: Croatia - Croatia Has Direction (Plonkit)
description: Croatia has direction signs with a yellow background and a black outline. They often have a pencil-shaped tip.

title: Croatia - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Croatian utility poles are cylindrical and made of concrete or wood, often with alternating hooks on the wooden poles (somewhat similar to Latvian poles).

title: Croatia - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Buildings in Croatia sometimes feature exposed red brick walls. This architecture is more common in inland areas.

title: Croatia - Generation Features (Plonkit)
description: Croatia features blue fire hydrants with two diagonal protrusions on either side. Newer fire hydrants seen in Generation 4 have a smaller top but are still recognisable due to the blue paint.

title: Croatia - Croatias Pedestrian Sign (Plonkit)
description: Croatia’s pedestrian sign features a pedestrian with a belt and a zebra path with 5 stripes.

title: Croatia - Karlovačko And Ožujsko (Plonkit)
description:
Karlovačko and Ožujsko are common Croatian beer companies, with advertisements seen around the country.
Konzum and Plodine are common supermarket chains, mostly found in big cities. Plodine is exclusive to Croatia, while Konzum also operates stores in Bosnia.

title: Croatia - Gen 2 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Croatia does not have Generation 2 car coverage. However, in some historic downtown areas, a Generation 2 trekker camera was used.

title: Croatia - Area Code Map (Plonkit)
description: Croatian landlines typically start with a zero followed by the area code.

title: Croatia - Flat Agricultural Land (Plonkit)
description: The north-eastern region of Croatia is mostly flat and features a lot of agriculture. It is similar in terms of landscape to Hungary and north-western Serbia.

title: Croatia - Hilly Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The region north and west of Zagreb is hilly and agricultural.

title: Croatia - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The Adriatic coast features rocky mountains similar to those seen in Montenegro or Albania. Shrubs are more common instead of trees along the coast, especially in the south. This coastal region has a lot of islands and peninsulas.

title: Croatia - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Houses and walls made of beige brick are common on the Adriatic coast. They often feature green shutters.

title: Croatia - North-western Region Istria (Plonkit)
description: The north-western region of Istria, south of the Italian city of Trieste, sometimes has distinct red soil.

title: Croatia - Istria Features (Plonkit)
description: Bilingual street name signs with Croatian and Italian are typically found in Istria, especially in the western cities.

title: Croatia - Town Names Ending (Plonkit)
description: Town names ending with “-ec” are common to see in the northern parts of central Croatia.

title: Croatia - Hilly Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Croatia’s capital Zagreb has a distinct big city feel. Apartment blocks can be seen throughout the city. The northern part of the city is hilly. Furthermore, Zagreb has blue electric trams.

title: Croatia - Croatia Features (Plonkit)
description: Zagreb and Osijek are the only two cities in Croatia with trams.

title: Croatia - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The region northeast of Zadar is recognizable as it is flat with a mountain ridge visible in the distance north.

title: Croatia - There Lot Vineyards (Plonkit)
description: There are a lot of vineyards around the town of Ilok, near the Serbian border, west of Novi Sad. You can find vineyards in other parts of Croatia as well, but they are most common in this area. If you see lots of vineyards in a northeastern Croatian landscape, you are more often than not near Ilok.

title: Croatia - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Traffic lights in Rijeka are held up by long blue poles that extend out over the road. These are exclusive to the city.

title: Croatia - Town Petrinja Severely (Plonkit)
description: The town of Petrinja was severely damaged by an earthquake in 2020. As a result, many buildings can be seen ruined and undergoing repair.

title: Croatia - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: The city of Dubrovnik in the far south of coastal Croatia is famous for its beautifully preserved medieval city walls, which can be seen from many points in and around the Old Town.

title: Croatia - Tall Cypress Trees (Plonkit)
description: These tall cypress trees are commonly found near the southern tip of Croatia.

title: Czechia - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Bollards in Czechia have orange double reflectors on the front and a single white reflector on the back. There are also rarer blue and red variants.

title: Czechia - Road Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Czechia and Slovakia both use a special kind of type B guardrail, which is wider than the normal type. No other European countries use the same kind.

title: Czechia - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Czechia and Slovakia most commonly use wide, round concrete poles, which are quite often attached in pairs.

title: Czechia - Metal Poles (Plonkit)
description: Czech and Slovak pole tops typically feature short metal bars that hold the insulators.

title: Czechia - Metal Poles (Plonkit)
description: Two support bars holding up the metal bar on pole tops, resembling an upside down triangle, can sometimes be found in Czechia and Slovakia.

title: Czechia - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: You may also see concrete poles with trident poletops, with two arms angled upwards. The number of insulators and other details will vary, however the general shape will be the same. Out of the pole tops listed, these are the least common, but unique to the two countries.

title: Czechia - Street Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Lamp posts with a thick base mounted by opposing pairs of bolts are common in both countries. The exact shape of the base may vary.

title: Czechia - Striped Sign Posts (Plonkit)
description: It is common in both Czechia and Slovakia to see temporary square sign posts coated in red and white stripes.

title: Czechia - Red-White Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Czech and Slovak chevrons are white with red arrows. Less commonly, you may find red on yellow chevrons.

title: Czechia - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Stripy gas and water poles reminiscent of snow poles can often be found next to the road.

title: Czechia - Czechia Features (Plonkit)
description: Hiking markers, made up of one colourful strip between two white ones, are commonly found in Czechia and Slovakia. They sometimes form an arrow.

title: Czechia - Like All Former (Plonkit)
description: Like all of the former Eastern bloc, prefabricated panel apartment buildings are a common sight in urban areas. What distinguishes Czechia and Slovakia is the relatively good maintenance often combined with vibrant colours and patterns. Some smaller buildings also adhere to this style.

title: Czechia - Roofs With Diamond (Plonkit)
description: Roofs with diamond shaped tiles are common in both Czechia and Slovakia.

title: Czechia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: A car antenna with a grey piece of tape stuck to the top can be seen on much of the Generation 3 coverage in Czechia and Slovakia.

title: Czechia - Red Generation 4 (Plonkit)
description: A red generation 4 Google car can be found in both Czechia and Slovakia.

title: Czechia - Black Generation 4 (Plonkit)
description: A black generation 4 Google car can also be found in both Czechia and Slovakia.

title: Czechia - end of Bridge (Plonkit)
description: These black signs can often be found by the end of bridges in Generation 4 coverage. The road number is displayed on the left.

title: Czechia - Czech And Slovak (Plonkit)
Czechia - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The Czech landscape is fairly rolling, with a lot of hills and altitude changes, but not a lot of tall mountains. Generally speaking, Slovakia has more mountains, but also more completely flat areas.

title: Czechia - Czechia Often Has (Plonkit)
description: Czechia often has solid outer roadlines, with no centre line.

title: Czechia - Czechia Uses Arrow-shaped (Plonkit)
description: Czechia uses arrow-shaped directional signs with a filled in tip. Due to the shape, they are recognizable from behind.

title: Czechia - Borders Czech Road (Plonkit)
description: The borders of Czech road signs are almost always separated from the edge by a strip in the same colour as the sign background.

title: Czechia - Czech Highway Signs (Plonkit)
description: Czech highway signs can be either blue or green, and have a thin white border, which is separated from the edge by a second coloured border.

title: Czechia - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description:
The most common type of street sign in Czechia are bright red signs, which can either be wide and stuck on walls, or thin and attached to signs posts. Note that other street signs do occur in some areas, most notably in Brno. Similarly designed blue signs are also fairly common.
Furthermore, the Czech word for street is “ulice”, unlike most Slavic languages which use “ulica”. This word is usually omitted, but finding “ulice” on street signs is still possible.

title: Czechia - Czechia Features (Plonkit)
description: House numbers in Czechia are generally written on blue or red signs with thin white borders.

title: Czechia - Czech Sign Posts (Plonkit)
description: Czech sign posts typically have thick, black caps.

title: Czechia - Czech Pedestrian Signs (Plonkit)
description: Czech pedestrian signs have five stripes.

title: Czechia - Czech Road Signs (Plonkit)
description: Czech road signs have a fairly thin font.

title: Czechia - Czech Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: Czech kilometre markers have a yellow outline outside the black frame and do not have a black horizontal middle line.

title: Czechia - Czechia Features (Plonkit)
description: Bicycle signs in Czechia are yellow. You may also find markings similar to hiking markers, but with yellow stripes instead of white.

title: Czechia - Czechia Features (Plonkit)
description: Suburban houses in Czechia are commonly connected in pairs.

title: Czechia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Much of Czech Generation 3 coverage was taken during winter, resulting in very grey, and occasionally snowy, coverage.

title: Czechia - Czechia Features (Plonkit)
description: A white Google car is present in Czechia but not Slovakia.

title: Czechia - Czech Railway Crossing (Plonkit)
description: Czech railway crossing signs do not have a background.

title: Czechia - Gen 2 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: While rare, it is possible to find Generation 2 in Czechia.

title: Czechia - First Digit Road (Plonkit)
description:
The first digit of road numbers can be anything between 1-6. Though, roads starting with 6 are scattered across most of the country. There are three exceptions, being roads 7, 8 and 9, which all start in Prague and go to the north and northwest.
Roads starting with 1-5 are mostly distributed as the map shows, with some overlap and exceptions mainly due to longer, two-digit roads.

title: Czechia - Four-digit Bike Paths (Plonkit)
description: Four-digit bike paths follow a geographical pattern, increasing clockwise, starting in Southern Bohemia. They do not show up on Google Maps, and as such remembering the general pattern is necessary to make them useful. Single- and two-digit bike paths are shown on this map, however they are far less useful to know.

title: Czechia - Area Code Map (Plonkit)
description: Czech phone numbers are typically made up of 9 digits, of which the first 1-3 digits are the area code. Note that if the first digit is 6 or higher, it does not indicate a specific area. They’re not very common.

title: Czechia - Czechia Wine (Plonkit)
description: Around 95% of all wine produced in Czechia comes from the Moravian wine region.

title: Czechia - Much Northern Bohemian (Plonkit)
description: Much of the northern Bohemian landscape can be characterised by a rolling landscape combined with steep solitary hills.

title: Czechia - Czechia Features (Plonkit)
description: Timber framed houses in Czechia are mostly found along the northern parts of the German border.

title: Czechia - Wooden Poles (Plonkit)
description: Houses with thick, dark wooden poles supporting the upper floors are common in the northernmost parts of the country.

title: Czechia - Dark Wooden Houses (Plonkit)
description: Dark wooden houses, with white stripes shining through the wood, are common in most of northern Czechia.

title: Czechia - Town Houses Moravia (Plonkit)
description:
Town houses in Moravia typically have two distinctive features:
- Houses have the long side parallel to the road and are often connected in large groups.
- Front doors are abnormally large, similar in size and shape to barn doors.

title: Czechia - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: A variant of baroque architecture called Selské Baroko (folk baroque) can be found in the region surrounding České Budějovice. The style is characterised by highly decorated walls, with the setting being small villages rather than towns and cities.

title: Czechia - It Features (Plonkit)
description: It is more common to see houses with single pane windows in the northwestern parts of the country.

title: Czechia - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: While possible to find in most of the country, blue street signs are more common in the east of the country, with Ostrava being the only major city to mainly use them.

title: Czechia - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: If you see a white street sign with blue text and a red border, the same as is typical for Slovakia, then you should be near the Slovak border.

title: Czechia - White Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: White street signs with red text are most commonly found in the eastern parts of the country. They can also be found in the southernmost parts.

title: Czechia - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: White street signs with blue text are most common in the eastern parts of the country, but can also be seen in the central northern parts.

title: Czechia - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: White street signs with black text are most commonly found in the southeastern parts of the country. Note that these can look very similar to the ones with blue text.

title: Czechia - Streets Downtown Prague (Plonkit)
description: Streets in downtown Prague are commonly paved with grey and white marble stones, which is also typical for Portugal. They’re often arranged in intricate square mosaics, but some sections are far more plain. NOTE: Similar pavement can be found in much lower volume in other towns too. Consider the apparent size of the city before guessing Prague.

title: Czechia - Cube Shaped Functionalist (Plonkit)
description: Cube shaped, functionalist red brick houses are found in Zlín, as a remainder of the shoemaking company Baťa’s houses for their workers. In the city centre, high rise buildings are constructed in similar style.

title: Czechia - Brno Features (Plonkit)
description: Pairs of black and white house numbers are found in Brno.

title: Czechia - Pilsen House Numbers (Plonkit)
description: Pilsen house numbers typically consist of two red and white octagonal plates with inverse colour schemes.

title: Czechia - House Numbers České (Plonkit)
description: House numbers in České Budějovice have one red and one white plate with underlined numbers.

title: Czechia - Red House Numbers (Plonkit)
description:
Red house numbers with a dividing line and a Roman numeral are unique to Liberec.
The dividing line is an important identifying factor, as Roman numerals can be found on house numbers in other cities.

title: Czechia - Písek Uses Yellow (Plonkit)
description: Písek uses yellow house numbers with a black outline.

title: Czechia - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Polish bilingual street signs are found in Český Těšín, and very rarely in other nearby towns.
