description: Pine forests can be found in the north and a small area north of Nikšić, but most commonly in the east.

title: Montenegro - Durmitor National Park (Plonkit)
description:
Durmitor National Park can be recognized by a distinct landscape consisting of grassy, treeless mountains with a high-altitude feel.
The town of Žabljak is situated in this national park, and can be recognized by the landscape but also by the unique architecture.

title: Montenegro - Podgorica (Plonkit)
description: Podgorica is the capital and largest city in Montenegro, and can be recognized by the modern buildings, wide roads and modern infrastructure.

title: Montenegro - Cemi River Valley (Plonkit)
description: These distinct staircase-like mountainsides can be seen in the Cemi River Valley.

title: Montenegro - Slansko Lake Islands (Plonkit)
description: Many small islands can be seen within Slansko Lake.

title: Montenegro - Pljevlja Coal Mine (Plonkit)
description: The Pljevlja Coal Mine can be recognized by the wide, artificial wall of gravel. The mine can often be seen from afar.

title: Montenegro - Skadar Lake Bridge (Plonkit)
description: The Skadar Lake Bridge can be recognized by the railway and stone bollards next to the road.

title: Montenegro - Sky Rifts (Plonkit)
description: ‘Rifts’ can commonly be seen in Montenegrin coverage, due to poor stitching.

title: Montenegro - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Coverage in Montenegro is limited to main roads, with very few minor roads covered. The only main road not covered is the A1, south of Kolasin.

title: Montenegro - Rift Map (Inland vs Coast) (Plonkit)
description: This map shows the distribution of where rifts are found. Although rifts are common in Montenegro, coastal rounds will almost never have them. By the coast, there will be a short antenna with no rifts. There will be a long antenna with rifts inland.

title: Montenegro - P15 Police Car (Plonkit)
description: The Google Car can be seen chasing this police car on the P15, between Lovcen National Park and Čevo.

title: Montenegro - E80 Yellow Lines (Plonkit)
description: The southern part of the E80, between Orahovo and Đurmani, can be recognized by the yellow outer lines.

title: Netherlands - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: The Netherlands has long, yellow licence plates with the standard European blue strip on the left. Dutch taxis have blue plates.

title: Netherlands - Dutch Language (Plonkit)
description: Dutch is a Germanic language. It features a lot of double vowels. Typical letter clusters are ij, ieuw and oe. “IJ“ written as one capitalised letter is also unique to the language.

title: Netherlands - White Bollards (Red Reflector) (Plonkit)
description: The Netherlands has a simple, white bollard with a red reflector.

title: Netherlands - Lack of Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: The Netherlands usually does not have any utility poles. You might see larger power lines like the ones shown in the image, but essentially never any street-level smaller utility poles.

title: Netherlands - Flat Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The Netherlands is extraordinarily flat. In most of the country, you will get no more than a few metres of elevation. Large swathes of the country are reclaimed land that is at or even below sea level.

title: Netherlands - Water Management (Dikes/Canals) (Plonkit)
description: In addition, the Netherlands is a very water-rich country. The country has innumerous waterways. Canals and ditches next to the road are common. Water management is an important facet of Dutch infrastructure, so you will often see dikes (low earthen walls to protect against water), dams and bridges.

title: Netherlands - Tree-Lined Roads (Plonkit)
description: Many rural roads are lined by rows of trees.

title: Netherlands - Urban Planning & Row Houses (Plonkit)
description: The Netherlands has a high amount of urban planning, and as a result tends to have a very organised look. Road infrastructure is well-maintained. Suburbs are usually master-planned and typically feature row houses.

title: Netherlands - Road Markings (Plonkit)
description: Like most of Europe, the Netherlands has all-white road lines. Many roads have dashed outside lines. Sometimes, you can find unique green middle lines.

title: Netherlands - Bicycle Paths (Plonkit)
description:
Many Dutch roads are flanked by bicycle paths. Different designs exist, but a very common one is a reddish-pink lane.
Cycling is one of the most common modes of transportation in the Netherlands. You will see cyclists and bicycles everywhere.

title: Netherlands - Brick Roads (Plonkit)
description: Brick roads are common in the Netherlands, both in rural and urban areas. The brick pattern shown in the image is especially common.

title: Netherlands - Sidewalk Tiles (Plonkit)
description: Most Dutch sidewalks use the same type of square grey tiles and offset tiling pattern. In some historic areas, you might find smaller brick sidewalks.

title: Netherlands - Speed Bumps (Plonkit)
description: The Netherlands has very recognizable speed bumps. They usually have white warning stripes that alternate between long and short. The example image is on a brick road, but they also occur on asphalt roads.

title: Netherlands - Brick Rumble Strips (Plonkit)
description: Many rural roads feature a sort of brick rumble strip on the sides. This is fairly unique to the Netherlands and a good way to identify the country in very rural rounds.

title: Netherlands - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Street signs are almost always blue with white lettering. Very rarely, you can find yellow, white or green street signs.
The Dutch word for street is straat. Other common road name endings are -weg, -laan, -pad, and -plein. However, if you see a blue sign with the word ‘fietspad’, do not search for it; it simply means ‘bicycle path’.

title: Netherlands - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Dutch direction signs are blue with white lettering. Signs for bicyclists are white with a red border.

title: Netherlands - Town Entry Signs (Plonkit)
description: Dutch town entry signs are blue. The signs sometimes have very elaborate designs, often with frames and additional signs.

title: Netherlands - Green Hectometer Markers (Plonkit)
description:
Dutch road markers are green. Many list the road number in a small yellow or red box.
Highways have a red box and start with the letter A. Regional roads have a yellow box and start with the letter N.

title: Netherlands - Sign Edges (Folded) (Plonkit)
description: Edges of Dutch road signs will extend to the back, creating a border visible from behind, sometimes retaining the colour of the sign. This is both consistent and unique to the country.

title: Netherlands - Striped Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Many Dutch signposts feature striped markings with a black-and-white or blue-and-white colour scheme.

title: Netherlands - Yellow Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Road signs on traffic islands often have these bulky yellow signposts.

title: Netherlands - Striped Road Barriers (Plonkit)
description: On some roads, especially in rural areas, you might find these distinctive striped barriers.

title: Netherlands - Brick Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Brick architecture is very common in the Netherlands. Many buildings feature red-brownish-coloured bricks. Roofs often have orange or dark grey tiles.

title: Netherlands - Row Houses (Plonkit)
description: As mentioned before, row houses are very common in the Netherlands. Almost half of the Dutch housing stock are row houses, significantly more than almost all other European countries.

title: Netherlands - Windmills (Plonkit)
description: Windmills, both traditional water or grain mills, and modern wind power turbines, are common in the Netherlands.

title: Netherlands - Gen 4 Black Car Glitch (Plonkit)
description: Some Generation 4 coverage has a car blur glitch where the black back of the Google car is visible.

title: Netherlands - Smallcam Coverage (Plonkit)
description: The Netherlands also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: Netherlands - Area Code Map (Plonkit)
description:
Dutch landline phone numbers start with a three- or four-digit area code. These are geographically grouped, except for the ones that start with 07, and two of the 02 codes.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Netherlands - Province-Specific Bollards/Markers (Plonkit)
description:
Some road markers (“hectometre markers”) have province-specific designs. This only applies to markers for regional N-roads, which have road numbers in yellow boxes.
Not all N-road markers have province-specific designs: some just have a generic design that can be found nationwide.
The A-roads all have the same signs and are recognizable because the road number is in a red box.
Bollards sometimes feature kilometre stickers, which are also limited to specific regions.
You can click on the image to enlarge it. Image provided by Timzkii.

title: Netherlands - Provincial Flags (Plonkit)
description:
All Dutch provinces have their own flag. However, most of these are very rarely seen in the wild. The major exceptions to this are the flags of Friesland and Noord-Brabant.
In addition, you can sometimes see the unofficial but very popular flag of the Achterhoek cultural region in the east of Gelderland.
For a full list of all provincial flags, you can view this Wikipedia page.

title: Netherlands - Frisian Language (Plonkit)
description:
In the province of Friesland, the Frisian language is commonly spoken. While Dutch language is still most prevalent on signs, a lot of town entry signs will feature bilingual town names.
Some street names in Friesland uniquely end in -wei or -strjitte.

title: Netherlands - Limburg Pole Stickers (Plonkit)
description: This long, vertically arranged white sticker with three to four digits is found on street lights in Limburg.

title: Netherlands - North Brabant Pole Stickers (Plonkit)
description: Similarly to Limburg, North Brabant also has white stickers on their street lights, however it is horizontally arranged and only has one or two digits.

title: Netherlands - Polder Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Most of the west and north is at or below sea-level. As a result, most of this region’s countryside has a distinct “polder” landscape: the landscape is marshy, often with a large amount of small waterways.

title: Netherlands - Eastern/Southern Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Conversely, the south and the east tends to have a more typical flat European farmland look. Waterways are still common, but the landscape can look less marshy.

title: Netherlands - Limburg Hills (Plonkit)
description: While most of the Netherlands is very flat, Southern Limburg has some low hills.

title: Netherlands - Veluwe Forest (Plonkit)
description:
The Veluwe area is unusually forested for Dutch standards. Some parts feature a very slight amount of elevation.
Some parts of the Veluwe feature old-growth forest, heath or sandy soil. This area can look odd and unlike the rest of the Netherlands if you have never seen it before.

title: Netherlands - Flevoland Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Almost all of the land belonging to the province of Flevoland was reclaimed from the sea in the mid-20th century. As a result, the province has a distinct, man-made look: extremely straight roads and large crop fields dominate the landscape. Wind turbines are common. In urban areas, there are no historical buildings.

title: Netherlands - Coastal Dunes (Plonkit)
description: Most of the Dutch North Sea coast is lined by dunes.

title: Netherlands - Wadden Islands (Plonkit)
description: The islands in the northwest are called the Wadden Islands. They are very popular local tourism destinations, which is sometimes evident in the street view coverage. Their northwestern coastlines feature a lot of sand dunes.

title: Netherlands - Northern Farm Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Farms in the north of the Netherlands often have very large roofs.

title: Netherlands - Rolling Shutters (Plonkit)
description: Rolling shutters on house windows are more common in the southern half of the Netherlands.

title: Netherlands - Curaçao (Plonkit)
description:
Curaçao is a constituent country in the Kingdom of the Netherlands, located north of western Venezuela in the Caribbean Sea. As such, for country streaks purposes, it is counted as the Netherlands.
Plonk It has a more in-depth guide to Curaçao here.

title: Netherlands - Amsterdam Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Amsterdam street signs feature the city district in a smaller font size below the actual street name.

title: Netherlands - Oegstgeest Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: The municipality of Oegstgeest, just northwest of Leiden, uses uniquely illegible street signs with yellow text on a red background.

title: Netherlands - Zaanstreek Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Buildings in the Zaanstreek region just north of Amsterdam often feature wooden architectural elements, usually painted green or black; with white trims. They sometimes have tall roof spires, usually painted white.

title: Netherlands - Afsluitdijk (Plonkit)
description: The Afsluitdijk is a very recognizable man-made causeway between Noord-Holland and Friesland. It is a divided highway that runs in a very straight southwest to northeast direction. You can see water to your southeast, and a dike to your northwest.

title: Netherlands - Westland Greenhouses (Plonkit)
description: In the Westland municipality, just southwest of The Hague, greenhouses are extremely common. They cover most of the municipality’s land surface.

title: Netherlands - Hoge Veluwe Trekker (Plonkit)
description: In the southern part of the Veluwe, in National Park De Hoge Veluwe, you can find a trekker that is recognizable because the Google employee’s brown hair is visible.

title: Netherlands - Rotterdam Harbour (Plonkit)
description: The harbour of Rotterdam is one of the largest in the world. It extends all the way from downtown Rotterdam to the North Sea coast. If you see a lot of industrial activity, often in combination with large, round fuel storage tanks, there is a good chance that you are in this harbour area.

title: Netherlands - Lelystad Street Names (Plonkit)
description: Many streets in Lelystad follow a fairly distinct naming scheme: instead of having unique names, they are named after the neighbourhood they are in, followed by a number. Some of these neighbourhood names show up on the Google map.

title: Netherlands - Baarle-Nassau/Hertog (Plonkit)
description: Baarle is a town in the south of the Netherlands which contains a number of Belgian enclaves. Throughout the town, you can sometimes see signs of this, such as markings on the pavement and Dutch and Belgian flags being flown together.

title: Netherlands - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description: Dutch landline phone numbers start with a three- or four-digit area code. These are geographically grouped, except for the ones that start with 07, and two of the 02 codes.

title: North Macedonia - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: North Macedonian licence plates are white and sometimes have the standard European blue strip on the left. They also have a noticeable red block near the left side of the licence plate.

title: North Macedonia - All Generation 4 (Plonkit)
description: All Generation 4 coverage in North Macedonia was taken using a “smallcam” camera, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: North Macedonia - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: North Macedonia uses two types of bollards. One is rounded and very thin, while the other one is wedge-shaped. They both are white and have red or white reflectors, typically on a black surface.

title: North Macedonia - Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: North Macedonia uses A-Profile guardrails, like most of Europe. The guardrails have red reflectors.

title: North Macedonia - Bilingual Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Direction signs in North Macedonia are typically yellow with biscriptal text: town names are written in both Latin and Cyrillic script.

title: North Macedonia - Language & Alphabet (Plonkit)
description:
Macedonian is a Slavic language which uses the Cyrillic script. Road signs have Latin on them too, although most other signs are fully in Cyrillic.
The letters ‘Ѓ’ and ‘Ќ’ are unique to Macedonian. ‘Љ’, ‘Њ’, and ‘Џ’ are only in Serbian and Macedonian.

title: North Macedonia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
There will never be an antenna on the Google car.
Every other country in Europe will have an antenna sometimes in Generation 3 coverage. For clarity’s sake: this means that cars with no antenna can be found outside North Macedonia.

title: North Macedonia - Dry Grassland Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The general landscape of North Macedonia consists of relatively dry grasslands, and small hills and scattered trees.

title: North Macedonia - Greek-Style Lamps (Plonkit)
description: These ‘Greek Lamps’ on utility poles can be found in North Macedonia. They can also be found in various other countries, such as (unsurprisingly) Greece or Serbia.

title: North Macedonia - Yellow Warning Signs (Plonkit)
description: North Macedonia normally uses yellow-filled in warning signs. Most of Europe uses white ones.

title: North Macedonia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
Generation 3 Coverage is sparse, only including some highways and some cities in the country.
The cities of Skopje, Bitola, Kumanovo, Prilep, Tetovo, Veles, Ohrid, and Strumica are the only ones with significant coverage inside the city.
You can view the official coverage in more detail on this site.

title: North Macedonia - Skopje (Plonkit)
description: Skopje is the capital and by far the largest city. If you see any large apartments or buildings, you are almost guaranteed to be in Skopje.

title: North Macedonia - Obituary Posters (Plonkit)
description:
Each city has its own city-specific posters with public obituaries. They are commonly found on utility poles.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: North Macedonia - Kumanovo Obituaries (Plonkit)
description: Obituaries in Kumanovo are the most distinct. They are the only obituaries to have a thick light blue border.

title: North Macedonia - Bitola Obituaries (Plonkit)
description: Obituaries in Bitola are horizontal and can be either light or dark blue. The cross is in-between the border, leaving a gap in the rectangle.

title: North Macedonia - Ohrid Obituaries (Plonkit)
description: Obituaries in Ohrid are horizontal and either red or blue. The cross is underneath the border, which is unique to Ohrid when the obituary is red.

title: North Macedonia - Strumica Obituaries (Plonkit)
description: Obituaries in Strumica are vertical and blue. They are the only obituaries to have an intricate pattern in the corner of the poster.

title: North Macedonia - Veles Obituaries (Plonkit)
description: Obituaries in Veles are vertical and blue. Veles has the largest variety of obituaries, but will never have the pattern in the corner like the ones seen in Strumica. They are also the only city that will have the cross above the border when blue.

title: North Macedonia - Prilep Obituaries (Plonkit)
description: Obituaries in Prilep are vertical and black. The border does not go completely around the poster, which makes it easy to distinguish.

title: North Macedonia - Tetovo Obituaries (Plonkit)
description: Obituaries in Tetovo are vertical and black. There are 2 main types found in the city, one with the cross above the border and one with a thick cross in-between the border.

title: North Macedonia - Strumica Kerbs (Plonkit)
description:
If you see black and yellow striped kerbs, you are most likely to be in Strumica.
They are rarely found in Skopje and if you see them around roundabouts, you will most likely be in Tetovo.

title: North Macedonia - Ohrid Lake (Plonkit)
description: Ohrid is the only large city located next to a lake.

title: North Macedonia - Prilep Street Lamps (Plonkit)
description: These long rectangular lamps are only found in the city of Prilep.

title: North Macedonia - Prilep Rocky Hills (Plonkit)
description: These two extremely rocky hills are visible in some parts of the city of Prilep.

title: North Macedonia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: In GENERATION 3 coverage A green truck is visible behind the Google Car for a portion of the E-65. The truck is visible from Kichevo to Arbinovo.

title: North Macedonia - Gen 3 No Antenna (Plonkit)
description:
All coverage in North Macedonia is Generation 3. There will never be an antenna on the Google car.

Every other country in Europe will sometimes or always have an antenna in Generation 3 coverage. For clarity’s sake: this means that cars with no antenna can be found outside North Macedonia.

title: North Macedonia - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Rural coverage in North Macedonia will normally mostly be on highways. This is because of the limited coverage outside urban areas in the country.

title: North Macedonia - Urban Coverage List (Plonkit)
description:
Coverage is sparse, only including some highways and some cities in the country.

The cities of Skopje, Bitola, Kumanovo, Prilep, Tetovo, Veles, Ohrid, and Strumica are the only ones with significant coverage inside the city.

You can view the official coverage in more detail on this site.

title: North Macedonia - Winter Coverage Cities (Plonkit)
description: Winter to late fall coverage is found in the cities of Skopje, Tetovo, Prilep, Bitola, and Ohrid.

title: North Macedonia - Green Truck Glitch (Plonkit)
description: A green truck is visible behind the Google Car for a portion of the E-65. The truck is visible from Kichevo to Arbinovo.

title: North Macedonia - E75 Triple Yellow Lines (Plonkit)
description:
For some of the E-75 north of Veles, there are triple yellow lines with a dashed centre line. In the northern part of the road, there is a yellow-truck following the Google car.

The rest of the road is either under construction or newly paved. This road is very similar to the A3 east of Veles, although that one is much flatter and has an arid landscape surrounding it.

title: North Macedonia - A3 Triple Yellow Lines (Plonkit)
description: A section of the A3 east of Veles also has triple yellow lines, which in Europe is extremely uncommon. The rest of the road has a very arid landscape and is noticeably under construction.

title: North Macedonia - Single Camera Smudge (Plonkit)
description: You can sometimes see some smudges on the camera. If you see one black smudge on the camera, you will most likely be on the A3 between Bitola and Prilep, or the R1302 in the far east. Keep in mind smudges can be randomly seen throughout the country.

title: North Macedonia - Triple Camera Smudge (Plonkit)
description: If you see three smudges, you will always be on the R1304. The only large city on this road is Kočani, although it has extremely limited coverage.

title: North Macedonia - Brown Camera Smudge (Plonkit)
description: If you see a brown smudge, you will be in the far southeast of the country.

title: North Macedonia - R1205 Fly Glitch (Plonkit)
description: A fly can be seen on the southern portion of the R1205. This is found nowhere else in the country.

title: North Macedonia - Divided Highways Map (Plonkit)
description:
Some roads in North Macedonia are divided. The map shown here gives an overview of where you can find such roads.

You can learn more about these roads below.

title: North Macedonia - E65 Concrete Median (Plonkit)
description: The E-65 just south of Tetovo has one concrete median separating each lane instead of a normal guardrail. This is the only highway in the country to have this.

title: North Macedonia - E65 Trees in Median (Plonkit)
description:
The E-65 between Tetovo and Skopje will sometimes have trees in between the guardrails.

This is the only highway to have them, besides a small part of the E-75/A1 road south of Veles (see the next tip).

title: North Macedonia - A1 Trees in Median (Plonkit)
description:
A small part of the E75 and the A1 also have planted trees in the median.

As mentioned, trees can also be seen on E-65 between Tetovo and Skopje. To distinguish between these roads, the E-65 is much more mountainous than the A1.

title: North Macedonia - E75 Sloped Hill Median (Plonkit)
description: For a section of the E-75 between Skopje and Kumanovo, there is a large sloped hill in between the lanes.

title: North Macedonia - E75 Single Guardrail Median (Plonkit)
description: Most of the E-75 next to the Greek Border has only one guardrail separating each lane. Some parts have a guardrail on one side and concrete median on the other. These are both only found on this highway.

title: Norway - Mountainous Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Norway is a very mountainous country, with many fjords along most of the coast.

title: Norway - Wooden Houses (Plonkit)
description: The vast majority of Norwegian houses are made of wood. Many houses are painted red, which is also typical for Sweden and Finland. Black painted houses are also quite common, more so than in Sweden or Finland.

title: Norway - License Plates (Green Commercial) (Plonkit)
description:
Norway has long white licence plates with the standard European strip on the left.
Commercial plates are green. These are often seen on vans.

title: Norway - Road Lines (Long Dashes) (Plonkit)
description: Smaller Norwegian roads typically have long dashed white outer lines, while larger roads have solid outer lines and yellow middle lines. The yellow lines have a distinct tinge of orange.

title: Norway - Dotted Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Road lines will often be made up of small dots of paint.

title: Norway - Norwegian Language Contains (Plonkit)
description:
The Norwegian language contains the special letters Æ, Ø and Å.
- Danish uses Æ, Ø and Å.
- Swedish uses Å, but not Æ or Ø. Norwegian also uses more E’s than Swedish, while Swedish uses more A’s instead. Norwegian uses “kk” where Swedish uses “ck”.
- Icelandic uses Æ, but not Ø or Å.
- Finnish uses Å, although it is viewed as a Swedish letter.

title: Norway - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Norway uses thin, curved rectangular bollards with the reflector inside of a black parallelogram.

title: Norway - Orange Snow Poles (Plonkit)
description: Norwegian snow poles are typically orange, with a fairly thin white reflector. The reflector is normally toward the middle of the pole.

title: Norway - Painted Wooden Snow Poles (Plonkit)
description: It is also fairly common to find thin wooden snow poles with painted reflectors.

title: Norway - Wooden Guardrail Posts (Plonkit)
description: Guardrails often have wooden posts.

title: Norway - Pedestrian Sign (Plonkit)
description: Norwegian pedestrian signs typically have four stripes and a very simply drawn person. Note however, that there is a version with five stripes and a version where the person is more detailed and wearing a hat.

title: Norway - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Norwegian directional signs are yellow with a black border. You will commonly see the road number displayed, either in a green box for European highways and major roads, or in a white box, for smaller roads.

title: Norway - Meeting Point Sign (M) (Plonkit)
description: On smaller roads, it is common to see these blue signs with a large white M.

title: Norway - Bus Stop Sign (Plonkit)
description: Norwegian bus stops usually have this small, blue sign with a white bus.

title: Norway - Zone Signs (Sone) (Plonkit)
description: White signs with the text “Sone”, generally featuring a speed limit, are common in urban areas.

title: Norway - Street Name Suffixes (Plonkit)
description: The most common street name suffixes in Norway are vei and gate. While attached to the name, they take the forms -veien and -gata or -gate.

title: Norway - Street Sign Position (Plonkit)
description: Street signs will generally be centred on top of sign posts.

title: Norway - Red Outline Traffic Signs (Plonkit)
description: Norwegian traffic signs have a red outline and a white background.

title: Norway - Yellow Construction Signs (Plonkit)
description: You can also find these road construction signs, with a bright yellow background.

title: Norway - Sign Bolt Pattern (Plonkit)
description: Most smaller road signs will be attached with four visible sign bolts in the shape of a tall rectangle. Beware that you may occasionally find framed signs instead, particularly in urban settings.

title: Norway - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Norway uses yellow on black chevrons.

title: Norway - Road Number/Distance Sign (Plonkit)
description:
Small white square signs, displaying the road number on top, and the distance to the closest town, are common to see along medium sized roads.
The road number will be preceded either by an R or an F. F roads show up as Fv on the map and are generally difficult to locate, while R roads lack any letters on the map and are generally more findable.

title: Norway - Wooden Poles with Metal Cap (Plonkit)
description: Norwegian poles are normally wooden and often have a small black metal cap on the top.

title: Norway - Street Lamp Bolting (Plonkit)
description: Lamps attached to wooden poles in Norway are normally mounted to the pole with a thick single bolting.

title: Norway - Grass Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Traditional houses in Norway commonly have grass covered roofs.

title: Norway - Smallcam Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Norway has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: Norway - Road Number Zones (Plonkit)
description:
The first digit of Norwegian road numbers are region dependent. Note that there are some exceptions among single and two-digit roads.
There are also a small number of roads beginning with a 9: Road 9, going north of Kristiansand, and a couple of two-digit roads in the far north.

title: Norway - Bilingual Sami Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Bilingual signs with Sámi can be found in several northern areas in Norway. While the Sámi languages are very different from Norwegian, the best way to recognize them are the letters Á, Đ and the use of several vowels in a row, something which is uncommon in Norwegian.
Note that not all signs in these areas will be bilingual.

title: Norway - Species Fern Pteridium (Plonkit)
description: This species of fern (Pteridium aquilinum, also known as bracken) which typically has a fairly tall stem and many wide leaves branching out, is mostly found in the south of Norway. Beware that other species of ferns can be found further north.

title: Norway - Spruce Forests (Plonkit)
description: Spruces are mainly found in the southern half of the country, particularly in the southeast and around Trondheim.

title: Norway - Pine Forests (Plonkit)
description: Pines are most common in coastal and far inland areas in the southern half of the country.

title: Norway - Oak Trees (Plonkit)
description: Oaks are mainly found in the far south of Norway.

title: Norway - Maple Trees (Plonkit)
description: Maples are mainly found in the south, particularly by the farmlands around Oslo.

title: Norway - Coloured Moss (Plonkit)
description: Brightly coloured moss is common to find in the area between Lillehammer and Oppdal.

title: Norway - Farmlands Overview (Plonkit)
description:
Large farmlands are mainly found in three areas, the southeast, the area surrounding Trondheim, and south of Stavanger.
The following clues will explain how to differentiate between the three.

title: Norway - Oslo Farmlands (Plonkit)
description: The largest concentration of farmland is found in the southeast, in the general vicinity of Oslo. The area is much flatter than most of the country, and it is common to get a rolling landscape with smooth, round forested hills in the distance. The area southeast of Oslo is particularly flat.

title: Norway - Trondheim Farmlands (Plonkit)
description: The farmlands surrounding Trondheim are generally very hilly, and the hills are typically both steeper and more uneven than in the southeast.

title: Norway - Jaeren Farmlands (Plonkit)
description: Similarly to the southeast, the farmland south of Stavanger is flatter than most of the country. However, the fields look more vast and open, and it is very common to see rock walls made of large, round rocks. Furthermore, rather than crops, most fields will only contain grass.

title: Norway - Western Fjords (Plonkit)
description: While fjords can be found along most of the Norwegian coast, deep fjords surrounded by tall mountains are most common between Bergen and Trondheim.

title: Norway - Lofoten Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Distinct, sharp, rocky mountains with few trees can be seen on the Lofoten Archipelago.

title: Norway - Northern Birch Vegetation (Plonkit)
description: The northeast of Norway can typically be recognized by a somewhat rolling landscape, rather than tall mountains, and vegetation mainly consisting of very small birches combined with patched grass.

title: Norway - Southwestern Highlands (Plonkit)
description: Barren highlands, with no trees or bushes, and often with rocky mountains along the road, are mostly found in the southwest.

title: Norway - Rocky Coast (Plonkit)
description: Exposed rock, often spotted with small coastal pines and bushes, are mainly found on the south coast.

title: Norway - Northern Coastal Grasslands (Plonkit)
description: Coastal grasslands with little to no other vegetation and only somewhat low, distant mountains can be found by coastal roads in the far north.

title: Norway - Southern White Houses (Plonkit)
description: While completely white wooden houses can be found in the entire country, they’re especially common on the southern coast, where you’ll commonly see entire villages made up of them.

title: Norway - Black Snow Poles (Plonkit)
description: Black snow poles are most commonly found between Bergen and Trondheim.

title: Norway - Southeastern Pole Plates (Small) (Plonkit)
description: Small, wide black pole plates, with a single line of letters and digits, can be found in southeastern Norway.

title: Norway - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Rusty guardrails are almost exclusively found in coastal regions, and particularly on the southern half of the west coast.

title: Norway - Svalbard (Plonkit)
description:
Svalbard is an unincorporated archipelago within the Norwegian Kingdom.
A separate Plonk It guide to Svalbard can be found here.

title: Norway - Oslo Pole Plates (Large) (Plonkit)
description: Fairly large black or red pole plates can be found in Oslo.

title: Norway - Stavanger Lamp Stripes (Plonkit)
description: Two red stripes going around lamp posts are commonly found in Stavanger.

title: Norway - Bergen Fire Hydrants (Plonkit)
description: You can find this specific design of green fire hydrants in Bergen.

title: Norway - Russian Border Road (Plonkit)
description: Along the Russian border you can see this noticeably humid and green-looking road, with very overcast and occasionally foggy coverage. The trees are somewhat low and mainly consist of thin birches and pines.

title: Norway - Russian Signs (Plonkit)
description: Russian can sometimes be seen alongside Norwegian on signs near the Russian border. It is mostly found on roads E6 and E105 near Kirkenes.

title: Norway - Røros Wooden Architecture (Plonkit)
description: The old mining town of Røros can be recognised by the densely built traditional wooden architecture.

title: Norway - Language Characters (Plonkit)
description: The Norwegian language contains the special letters Æ, Ø and Å.

title: Norway - Bracken Ferns (Plonkit)
description: This species of fern (Pteridium aquilinum, also known as bracken) which typically has a fairly tall stem and many wide leafs branching out, is mostly found in the south of Norway. Beware that other species of ferns can be found further north.

title: Norway - Rusty Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Almost exclusively found in coastal regions, and particularly on the southern half of the west coast.

title: Poland - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Poland has long white plates with the standard European blue strip on the left.

title: Poland - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
Polish bollards have a red strip that wraps all the way around the bollard. This strip has a red reflector on the front (sometimes hard to see), and a white reflector on the back. Bollards sometimes have numbers on them.
There is also a thinner, curved version of the bollard.

title: Poland - Holey Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Poland usually has thin concrete utility poles with see-through holes. They are commonly known as “holey poles”. The holes often do not extend all the way to the bottom of the pole.
Sometimes, two poles are joined together, or put in an A-frame shape. You can also find round concrete poles.

title: Poland - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Poland has all-white road lines. Double middle lines are very common and usually a good clue for Poland.

title: Poland - Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Poland has square (normal B-type) guardrails, with circular red reflectors.

title: Poland - Warning Signs (Plonkit)
description: Warning signs are triangular and have a yellow background and a distinct thin red border.

title: Poland - Prohibitory Signs (Plonkit)
description: However, prohibitory signs are round and have a white background with a thicker red border.

title: Poland - Pedestrian Sign (Plonkit)
description: Poland has a unique pedestrian sign. Instead of the usual zebra stripes, it just has a single horizontal line.

title: Poland - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Regular Polish direction signs have a green background. These signs use a distinct font, which is a good clue for Poland.

title: Poland - Town Entry Signs (Plonkit)
description: Poland has two town entry signs: a green one with the locality’s name, and a white-and-black one with a stylized urban area.

title: Poland - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Polish chevrons are white with red arrows.

title: Poland - Language Characters (Plonkit)
description:
Polish is a Slavic language. In contrast to other slavic languages, the Polish alphabet includes:
- Ł with a stroke through it (unique to Polish)
- Ą and Ę with a small hook (also found in Lithuanian)
- Ć, Ń, Ó, Ś, Ź with an acute accent. Of these, Ń is unique to Polish. In addition, the only other language with Ś and Ź is Montenegrin.
- Ż with a small dot (unique to Polish)
Polish is very consonant-heavy, with lots of consonant clusters. Polish does not use V. Instead, it uses W a lot, the only Slavic language to do so. Other unusually common consonants are the Z, K, and C.

title: Poland - Landscape Overview (Plonkit)
description: Poland is generally a flat country, with occasional rolling hills. The country is very green, with a lot of agriculture, and some amount of forest cover.

title: Poland - Tree-Lined Roads (Plonkit)
description: Many roads in Poland are lined by rows of trees.

title: Poland - Tiled Sidewalks (Plonkit)
description: Neatly tiled sidewalks are very common in Poland. Tiles are often grey or light red. Occasionally, even roads have tiled pavement. Many different types of tile patterns occur, including larger square tiles.

title: Poland - Architecture Overview (Plonkit)
description:
Polish architecture is fairly similar to other Central European countries. Buildings usually have plain stone walls covered in light or pastel stucco. Frequent roofing colours are orange or red, black, and brown. Roof tiles and panes often have a tidy, almost plastic-like look. Some rural houses have corrugated sheet roofs similar to those often found in the Baltics.
Detached single family homes are common throughout Poland. They sometimes have a blocky look.
In bigger towns, apartment buildings are common. Many date from communist times, and some of them still have a somewhat austere look. However, many have been renovated and look nice and well-kept.
Downtown areas are usually dense and often have historic buildings.

title: Poland - Catholic Shrines (Plonkit)
description: Poland is one of the most Catholic countries in Europe. You can often find Christian shrines on the side of roads. Blue-white and yellow-white Polish Catholic flags also sometimes appear.

title: Poland - Gen 4 Black Car (Rare) (Plonkit)
description: A black generation 4 Google car can rarely be found in Poland.

title: Poland - Gen 4 White Car (Rare) (Plonkit)
description: A white generation 4 Google car can also rarely be found in Poland.

title: Poland - 3-Digit Road Numbers (Plonkit)
description:
Regional roads have 3-digit road numbers. These numbers often appear in yellow boxes on direction signs. The first digit is usually region-specific, as there is a high level of geographic clustering of these road numbers.
There is some overlap between numbers near the margins of the regions. Some exceptions also exist.

title: Poland - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description: Polish landline phone numbers have 9 digits. The first 2 digits are the area code. These area codes are distributed in a sensible manner across the country. Even just learning the first digit of the area codes can greatly narrow down the region. You can click on the infographic to enlarge it.

title: Poland - Place Name Suffixes (Plonkit)
description: When it comes to Polish place names, the -owo ending is mostly limited to the northern half of the country, and the -ów ending mostly to the southern half. You may also encounter -ino or -yno, mainly in the northwest, and -ew near the centre of the country.

title: Poland - Minority Languages (Plonkit)
description:
While rare, bilingual signs can be found in the highlighted regions.
- Kashubian, found in the north, is another West Slavic Language, featuring a lot of umlauts and accents.
Wszëtczi lëdze rodzą sã wòlny ë równy w swòji czëstnoce ë swòjich prawach. Mają òni dostóne rozëm ë sëmienié ë nôlégô jima pòstãpòwac wobec drëdzich w dëchù bracënotë.
- German is mostly found in the Opole Voivodeship.
- Lithuanian can be found around Puńsk, near the Lithuanian border.
- Belarusian is found near the Belarusian border.
- Lemko, another Cyrillic language, can be found in the southeast.

title: Poland - Southern Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Even though most of Poland is flat, the southern border area is very hilly. Some parts even have mountains.

title: Poland - Eastern Wooden Houses (Plonkit)
description: Traditional wooden houses are commonly found in the east, mainly in Podlaskie Voivodeship.

title: Poland - Orchards Mostly Concentrated (Plonkit)
description: Orchards are mostly concentrated around the towns of Grójec and Sandomierz in southeastern Poland.

title: Poland - Yellow Pole Markings (Plonkit)
description:
Electricity poles with yellow markings are predominantly found in western and southern Poland.
For more detailed information on Polish utility poles, including the markings and lamps discussed here, see this document.

title: Poland - Black Pole Markings (Plonkit)
description: Black pole markings are most commonly seen in the southeast of the country, as well as some areas in the north.

title: Poland - White Pole Markings (Plonkit)
description: Markings with a white background are most commonly found in Podlaskie voivodeship, and can occasionally be seen in Łódź voivodeship and elsewhere.

title: Poland - Top-Mounted Street Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Street lamps mounted on top of the pole become more common towards the northeast of the country, with some pockets in the far south.

title: Poland - Side-Mounted Street Lamps (Plonkit)
description: In contrast, lamps attached to the side of the pole are rarely found in the northeast.

title: Poland - Tatra Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The Tatra Mountains are the highest mountains in Poland. They can be found near Zakopane, on the border with Slovakia.

title: Poland - Gdańsk Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Gdańsk is a large city in northwestern Poland. Its historic downtown features unique buildings that were inspired by Dutch Golden Age architecture. These buildings look somewhat similar to Amsterdam.

title: Poland - Hel Peninsula Road (Plonkit)
description: The main road on the Hel peninsula is very recognizable: it is a coastal forest road with a railway track running parallel to it.

title: Poland - Białystok Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Białystok uses turquoise street signs, with the district marked on the bottom.

title: Poland - Szczecin Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Szczecin uses colourful green and blue signs. The city district is marked on the bottom.

title: Poland - Poznań Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs in Poznań are mainly black, with the district being marked on the blue section at the bottom.

title: Poland - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Polish bollards have a red strip that wraps all the way around the bollard. This strip has a red reflector on the front (sometimes hard to see), and a white reflector on the back. Bollards sometimes have numbers on them.

title: Portugal - License Plates (Plonkit)
description:
Portuguese plates are long and white, with a blue strip on the left. Most plates have a yellow strip on the right, which is unique to Portugal.
The yellow strip was discontinued in 2020, so in Generation 4 coverage you may sometimes see plates with just the blue strip.

title: Portugal - Language Characters (Plonkit)
description: Portuguese is a Romance language that is closely related to Spanish. Unlike Spanish, Portuguese includes the letters Ç, Ã, Õ, Â, and Ê, while it does not include the letter Ñ, which is very common in Spanish.

title: Portugal - Eucalyptus Trees (Plonkit)
description: Eucalyptus trees are very common in Portugal. The only other part of Europe where you’ll commonly see eucalyptus is northern Spain.

title: Portugal - Rua (Road) (Plonkit)
description: The Portuguese word for road is ‘Rua’.

title: Portugal - Ladder Poles (Plonkit)
description: Concrete ladder poles, with very tall ladder steps, are common in Portugal. Each step often has a small see-through hole.

title: Portugal - Hunting Signs (Plonkit)
description: Hunting signs with a red and white colour scheme are a common sight in rural areas. They are either diamond shaped or rectangular.

title: Portugal - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Portuguese bollards are either wedge-shaped with a noticeably thin white top, or flat with a wide reflector. While most reflectors will be white, you may also find orange reflectors. These are noticeably darker than the yellow reflectors in Spain.

title: Portugal - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Directional signs are generally white, with black arrows that are not touching the borders of the sign.

title: Portugal - Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: Most kilometre markers are wide rectangles with a coloured section on the left side divided diagonally from the white part. Every kilometre you will find a larger square sign with a coloured top half featuring the road number.

title: Portugal - Waystones (Plonkit)
description: Black and white waystones can commonly be found in Portugal.

title: Portugal - Stop Signs (Large Font) (Plonkit)
description: Stop signs in Portugal feature a fairly large font.

title: Portugal - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Portuguese chevrons are black with yellow arrows.

title: Portugal - Pedestrian Sign (Plonkit)
description: Pedestrian signs have five stripes, and the person is wearing a belt, which is noticeably high.

title: Portugal - Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Portugal uses A-type guardrails with red reflectors.

title: Portugal - White Bordered Signs (Plonkit)
description: Portuguese road signs are typically encased by a white border.

title: Portugal - Cobblestone Roads (Plonkit)
description: Cobblestone roads are very common in Portugal. These will typically be made of square cobblestones arranged diagonally compared to the road direction.

title: Portugal - Cobblestone Sidewalks (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, cobblestone sidewalks made of distinctly bright stones are very common.

title: Portugal - White Stone Houses (Plonkit)
description: White painted stone houses with orange tiled roofs are extremely common in Portugal.

title: Portugal - House Trim Colours (Plonkit)
description: You’ll commonly see blue or yellow lines painted around windows and doors, as well as around the edges of walls.

title: Portugal - Tiled House Facades (Plonkit)
description: Houses made of decorative mosaic tiles are somewhat common in Portugal.

title: Portugal - Smallcam Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Portugal has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: Portugal - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description:
The first three digits of Portuguese landlines make up the area codes, which are distributed as seen on the map. Phone codes not starting with a 2 are not regional, and codes starting with 29 will either be the Azores or Madeira.
For a complete list of the third digits, see this page.

title: Portugal - Decorative Chimneys (Plonkit)
description: In the Faro district in the south of Portugal you will very commonly come across decorative chimneys, which will either be round or square shaped with small spire-shaped tops. The round chimneys are a particularly strong clue.

title: Portugal - Concrete Block Houses (Plonkit)
description: Houses in northern Portugal are often made of square concrete blocks, which are commonly put together with white mortar.

title: Portugal - Oak Fields (Plonkit)
description: Open fields sparsely populated with holm oaks (Quercus ilex) and cork oaks (Quercus suber) are very common in the southeast. These species of oaks tend to be on the smaller side, and have a Mediterranean look. While these fields will look quite dry during summer and fall, they will look much lusher during spring.

title: Portugal - Olive Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Olive plantations are generally more common in the eastern half of the country, particularly in the far northeast and slight southeast.

title: Portugal - Eucalyptus Forests (Plonkit)
description: Dense eucalyptus forests are mostly found in the northwest.

title: Portugal - Maritime Pine Forests (Plonkit)
description: Forests, or plantations of Maritime pines (Pinus Pinaster) are very common in the northern half of Portugal. You can recognize the tree by its grey bark with red undertones, and fluffy branches that point upwards. Older trees often don’t have any branches in the bottom half of the tree.

title: Portugal - Terraced Vineyards (Plonkit)
description: In the Douro wine region, straight east of Porto, you will commonly find steep terraced vineyards.

title: Portugal - Citrus Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Citrus plantations are mostly found along the south coast.

title: Portugal - Islands Overview (Plonkit)
description:
The islands of Madeira and the Azores are found southwest and west of mainland Portugal respectively. For country streak purposes they are both counted as Portugal.
Plonk It has more in-depth guides to Madeira here and a guide to the Azores here.

title: Portugal - Serra da Estrela (Plonkit)
description: The Serra da Estrela natural park can be recognised by the rocky mountainous highland landscape, often combined with yellow and black striped snow poles.

title: Portugal - Sandy Pine Forests (Plonkit)
description: Pine forests with extremely sandy white soil can be found near the coast between the cities of Setúbal and Sines.

title: Portugal - Southwest Landscape (Plonkit)
description: In the far southwest of the country you can find a flat uncultivated landscape with very limited vegetation, which typically appears quite dry. There are almost no trees nearby, and only very low bushes and grass.

title: Portugal - Porto Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Lime green street signs can be found in Porto.

title: Romania - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Romania uses standard long, white European plates with a single blue strip on the left.

title: Romania - Language Characters (Plonkit)
description:
Romanian is a Romance language similar to Italian, containing the following special letters:
- Ă ă
- Ș ș
- Ț ț
These letters are also found in some other European languages:
- Â â, used in French, Portuguese and Turkish
- Î î, used in French, Turkish and Italian

title: Romania - Holey Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: The most common types of utility poles in Romania are holey poles with the holes going all the way to the bottom. The holes are typically either quite wide or quite tall.

title: Romania - Round Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Round concrete poles are also quite common.

title: Romania - White-Painted Trunks (Plonkit)
description: Trees and poles will often have white painted bottoms.

title: Romania - Yellow Pole Stickers (Plonkit)
description:
This type of extremely large yellow pole sticker is specific to Romania.
Beware that smaller stickers are also common and that both Bulgaria and Hungary can have similar ones.

title: Romania - Triangle Pole Top (Plonkit)
description: Two support bars holding up the metal bar on pole tops, resembling an upside down triangle, can sometimes be found in Romania.

title: Romania - Waystones (Plonkit)
description: It is very common to see waystones in Romania. They are typically fairly large, with red or blue framing with the road number on the side, or made of actual stone and somewhat rugged-looking. There is also a very small variant which is all white.

title: Romania - Road Lines (Short Dashes) (Plonkit)
description: While there are many types of roadlines in Romania, these outer lines, consisting of short dashes with narrow spaces, can be a good clue for the country.

title: Romania - Thick Middle Lines (Plonkit)
description: Middle lines are often noticeably thicker than average. This is especially useful to tell Romania apart from Bulgaria, which generally has thinner road lines.

title: Romania - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Romanian directional signs are blue, arrow shaped, and have a white border. They will very often display the road number, which can be either red or blue.

title: Romania - Town Entry Signs (Plonkit)
description: The most common type of town entry sign in Romania is a yellow sign displaying a speed limit and a city skyline, with a white sign displaying the town name below.

title: Romania - Black Sign Backs (Plonkit)
description: Romanian sign backs are often black.

title: Romania - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Romanian chevrons are red on white, often with a yellow frame.

title: Romania - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Romanian bollards are thin and white, with a red vertical strip near the top. It is worth noting that bollards in Romania are somewhat rare.

title: Romania - Thick Border Yield Sign (Plonkit)
description: This yield sign, with an extremely thick red border, with a thin white outline, is unique to Romania. Beware that different yield signs also exist in Romania.

title: Romania - Architecture Overview (Plonkit)
description: Romanian architecture primarily consists of single-family houses made of stone, typically painted in different pastel colours and with roofs ranging from orange tiles to grey metal. It is also somewhat common to see houses with walls made of painted square tiles in different patterns.

title: Romania - Landscape Overview (Plonkit)
description: The Romanian landscape ranges from tall forested mountains and hills in the centre to flat or rolling agricultural landscapes in the south, west and east.

title: Romania - Haystacks (Plonkit)
description: This type of haystack, typically featuring a stick going straight through, is very common in Romania.

title: Romania - Dacia Cars (Plonkit)
description: Dacia is the most common car brand in Romania, making up more than a quarter of all vehicles in the country.

title: Romania - Elevation Map (Plonkit)
description: This is an elevation map of Romania. The tallest mountains are found in the middle and north of the country, while the south and west are particularly flat.

title: Romania - Southern/Western Plains (Plonkit)
description: Completely flat agricultural landscapes can be found in the south and west.

title: Romania - Western Tiled Roofs (Plonkit)
description: If you see several houses and almost all of them have orange tiled roofs, you are likely to be in the western half of the country.

title: Romania - Eastern Metal Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, if you see several houses and almost all of them have metal or plastic fake tiled roofs, you will probably be in the eastern half of the country.

title: Romania - Hungarian Border Villages (Plonkit)
description: Villages near the Hungarian border will often be built in the same style as villages in Hungary. This style can be summarised as having long, straight streets with single-storey houses being evenly spaced along the road, typically having the short side of the house facing the road. The vast majority of roofs will have orange tiles.

title: Romania - Moldovan Border Valleys (Plonkit)
description: South of Iași, near the border to Moldova, you can find rolling agricultural valleys with a very specific north-north-west to south-south-east angle.

title: Romania - Bilingual Hungarian Signs (Plonkit)
description: Bilingual signs with Hungarian are mostly found in the central regions of Covasna, Harghita and Mureş, but also less commonly near the Hungarian border.

title: Romania - Maramureș Wooden Gates (Plonkit)
description: Elaborately decorated wooden gates are commonly found in the region of Maramureș.

title: Romania - Sunflower Fields (Plonkit)
description: Sunflowers are primarily found in the far east of the country, and secondly in the far west.

title: Romania - City Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Several Romanian cities and towns have unique street signs. This infographic covers all with a population above 100 000.

title: Romania - Road 67C (Plonkit)
description: The 67C is a mountain road with all yellow road lines.

title: Romania - Road 7C (Plonkit)
description: The 7C is recognisable as going through some of the most dramatic mountains in Romania. The highest point on the road is right by the border between Sibiu and Argeș.

title: Romania - Sibiu Eye Windows (Plonkit)
description: This type of window, shaped like a squinting eye, is most commonly found in the city of Sibiu.

title: Romania - Brașov Gen 2 Hills (Plonkit)
description: If you see a mountainous landscape in Generation 2, you are likely close to Brașov.

title: Romania - Bucharest Gen 2 Flats (Plonkit)
description: Flat landscapes in Generation 2 are mostly found near Bucharest.

title: Romania - Danube Delta Boat (Plonkit)
description: A boat trekker, with a green boat, can be found in the far east of the country. It mostly goes through small, overgrown canals in a flat landscape.

title: Russia - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Russian licence plates are fully white with black text.

title: Russia - Language Characters (Plonkit)
description:
The Russian language uses the Cyrillic script, and contains the special letters Ы, Э, Ё and Ъ.
Ё is also used in Mongolian and Ъ is used in Bulgarian.

title: Russia - Ulitsa (Street) (Plonkit)
description: The Russian word for street is улица (ulitsa), sometimes abbreviated ул. (ul.).

title: Russia - Gorod (City) (Plonkit)
description: The Russian word for city is город (gorod), abbreviated г. (g.).

title: Russia - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Russia has three main types of bollards: a very thin type being attached to a stick, one with a black top section and a red vertical reflector below and a German-style bollard.

title: Russia - Intersection Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Near intersections in Russia you will commonly see a very large number of bollards.

title: Russia - Wide Intersections (Plonkit)
description: Along with containing a large number of bollards, many intersections are unusually wide compared to other countries.

title: Russia - Black Painted Pole Base (Plonkit)
description: Signposts in Russia often have black painted bottoms.

title: Russia - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Russia mainly uses square concrete poles.

title: Russia - Pole Support Blocks (Plonkit)
description: You can often see concrete support blocks at the bottom of utility poles, with wooden poles often being raised above ground by the support.

title: Russia - Gen 3 Antenna Cars (Plonkit)
description: Three Generation 3 Street View cars are commonly found in Russia. The two most useful ones for recognising Russia are a black and a white car, both with a long antenna. You may also see a short antenna without a visible car.

title: Russia - Pedestrian Sign (Plonkit)
description: Russian pedestrian signs have a simply drawn person and three stripes. Signs will commonly have a bright yellow border.

title: Russia - Zebra Crossings (Plonkit)
description: Russian pedestrian crossings contain alternating white and yellow stripes.

title: Russia - Striped Barriers (Plonkit)
description: Black and white striped guardrails, kerbs and bridge barriers are common in russia.

title: Russia - Urban Apartments (Plonkit)
description: The vast majority of urban housing in Russia are large rectangular apartment buildings made of simple concrete. Newer buildings in wealthier areas appear more modern.

title: Russia - Rural Wooden Houses (Plonkit)
description: Rural housing in Russia consists mostly of a basic wooden structure with metal roofs.

title: Russia - Decorated Window Frames (Plonkit)
description: This style of richly decorated window frames is commonly found on traditional Russian homes, especially on log cabins. They are often painted blue.

title: Russia - Urban Areas Sometimes (Plonkit)
description: In urban areas, you can sometimes see pipes which are exposed above the ground and are held up by other vertical pipes.

title: Russia - Pole Shields (Plonkit)
description: Black & white-striped pole shields are common along highways, especially in European Russia.

title: Russia - Birch Trees (Plonkit)
description: Birch trees, identified by their white peeling bark, have a wide range in Russia. Notably they are almost never found far south or far north in the western part of the country.

title: Russia - Eastern Birch Forests (Plonkit)
description: Birches very close together, as well as forests consisting of only birches, are indicative of areas east of the Urals, most commonly between Chelyabinsk Oblast and Novosibirsk Oblast.

title: Russia - Siberian Larches (Plonkit)
description: Siberian larches are one of the dominant tree species in much of eastern Russia, recognized by their unique needle-like leaves. Generally speaking, they become more prevalent the further east you go in the country, as well as at high elevations.

title: Russia - Spruce Forests (Plonkit)
description:
Spruce trees are an evergreen tree that can be identified by their dense and droopy or parallel branches, and generally are darker in color than most trees.
A similar evergreen tree, a caucasian fir, exists in the Caucasus Mountains. It has much more well organized and straighter branches.

title: Russia - Sakhalin Butterbur (Plonkit)
description: Giant butterbur (commonly referred to as Sakhalin cabbage) is very common in Sakhalin Oblast, particularly in the southern half. Related plants can very rarely be found in Adygea.

title: Russia - Hogweed (Plonkit)
description: This type of white flower (heracleum sosnowskyi) is most commonly found around Moscow, Komi Republic, and Perm Krai.

title: Russia - Fireweed (Plonkit)
description: Large amounts of the pink or red flower fireweed (Chamaenerion angustifolium) typically indicates a northern region of Russia. Similarly, most places north of Moscow commonly have fireweed.

title: Russia - Sunflower Fields (Plonkit)
description: Sunflowers are common along the border with Ukraine as well as more eastern oblasts like Ulyanovsk, Samara, and northern Orenburg.

title: Russia - Blue-pod Lupines (Plonkit)
description: Blue-pod lupines appear very commonly in northern Vladimir Oblast, eastern Ivanovo Oblast, and southwestern Kostroma Oblast. It can also be found less commonly elsewhere in Kirov Oblast and towards the Baltics.

title: Russia - Black Poplar (Plonkit)
description: The black poplar is commonly found south, near the border with Ukraine, as well as toward the western border with Kazakhstan.

title: Russia - Russian Olive (Plonkit)
description: The Russian olive is typically found along the Kazakhstan border.

title: Russia - Kaliningrad Trunks (Plonkit)
description: Lined oak trees, often with a single white stripe around the trunk, are extremely common in Kaliningrad.

title: Russia - Tatarstan Larches (Plonkit)
description: Sparsely planted larches along the road with open rolling fields is common in Tatarstan and adjacent federal subjects.

title: Russia - Sandy Roadsides (Plonkit)
description: Sandy roadsides are common in Khanty-Mansi and Yamalo-Nenets and adjacent subjects, as well as areas around Nizhny Novgorod on the Volga river. Other notable areas are Karelia, Murmansk, and western Sakha. Beware, however, that sandy roadsides can less commonly be found near rivers in other regions.

title: Russia - Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: Red soil is common in the highlighted areas, notably around Izhevsk and Perm, much of Arkhangelsk Oblast, Leningrad Oblast, and Pskov Oblast, and near Volgograd and Astrakhan. Note that this map is by no means exhaustive; red soil can be found almost anywhere in the country near water or iron mines.

title: Russia - Kamchatka Soil (Plonkit)
description: The Kamchatka peninsula has unique grey gravelly soil, as well as the largest number of volcanoes of any region in Russia. They are frequently seen across the peninsula, and in some places can appear quite close such as in Klyuchi.

title: Russia - Yakutsk Gravel Soil (Plonkit)
description: Extremely gravelly and sometimes dark soil appears as you approach the mountains east of Yakutsk, starting around Keskil.

title: Russia - Vladivostok Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Lush and diverse forests in a hilly landscape characterises the noticeably warmer region around Vladivostok. Most of the coverage is overcast and has a white car with a long antenna. Further south, near the tri-border, you will find a more open rolling hill landscape.

title: Russia - Magadan Road (Plonkit)
description: The eastern half of the Kolyma Highway going to Magadan features a lot of tall hills and mountains, usually shrouded in a haze. Most of the roads are unpaved and feature dark gravelly soil. The haze is not present in the western half.

title: Russia - South Yakutsk Road (Plonkit)
description: A presence of Siberian larches and large mountains on a mostly paved, but sometimes wide-gravel road indicates the main road south of Yakutsk, with Generation 4 white car appearing north of Berkakit.

title: Russia - Sakha Haze (Plonkit)
description: Very hazy coverage is found east and south of Mirny, especially along the Vilyuy river. The colour of the haze varies, but it is often orange or white.

title: Russia - Buryatia Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The landscape in Buryatia is very unique, containing open grassy landscape with shrubs and mountains. It is lusher near Baikal, but the mountains persist.

title: Russia - Buryatia Haze (Plonkit)
description: This forest fire haze is found near Lake Gusinoye, southwest of Ulan-Ude in Buryatia. While similar to the haze found near Mirny, the Buryatia haze coverage can typically be recognised by the open rolling landscape, which is not found near Mirny.

title: Russia - Altai Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The main road of Altai Republic has a black car long antenna driving north through the Altai Mountains, often with foggy or rainy coverage.

title: Russia - Tuva/Altai Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Dry steppe mountains with a long antenna will usually indicate the Tuva Republic. The south part of the main road in the Altai Republic and Tuva can appear similarly dry, so things such as driving direction and cloudiness can be used to distinguish them.

title: Russia - Tundra Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The landscape in the far north can be recognised by the relatively flat landscape, with very low vegetation.

title: Russia - Omsk Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
The coverage in Omsk Oblast is some of the most recognizable in Russia. It is typically summer Generation 4 and has a distinct landscape consisting of green agricultural fields, which are interrupted by isolated patches of (primarily) birch forest.
Note that in Generation 3, this landscape can be seen in a much larger area of Russia.

title: Russia - Caspian Steppe (Plonkit)
description: The area west of the Caspian Sea can often be recognised by its extremely dry and flat landscape, especially in Kalmykia, Astrakhan Oblast, and Dagestan.

title: Russia - Dagestan Spring (Plonkit)
description: Grassy fields, with bushy vegetation, in early spring Generation 4 coverage is typical for Dagestan. The landscape can either be completely flat or mountainous. These flowers are also quite common in the Generation 4 Dagestan coverage.

title: Russia - Caucasus Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The Caucasus mountain range is one of the largest mountain ranges in Russia. The tallest mountain in Russia, Mount Elbrus, can be found on the border of the Kabardino-Balkarian Republic and Karachay-Cherkessia.

title: Russia - Roadside Rocks (Plonkit)
description: Rocks along the road are extremely common throughout most of Karelia and Murmansk Oblast. They can also be found in Perm Krai and Buryatia but are less common and smaller in size.

title: Russia - Murmansk Landscape (Plonkit)
description: An open, hilly landscape with low shrubbery and fireweed usually indicates Murmansk. The lower the shrubbery, the more north it generally is.

title: Russia - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description: This is a map of Russian area codes. Notably, area codes starting with 8 are in the west, codes starting with 3 are fairly central and codes starting with 4 are either east or around Moscow.

title: Russia - License Plate Codes (Plonkit)
description: In Generation 3 coverage you will somewhat commonly find unblurred licence plates, featuring a regional code on the right side. The codes are generally ordered alphabetically within each type of federal subject, starting at republics and ending with autonomous okrugs. Therefore, the Republic of Adygea will be represented by 01, and the Amur Oblast by 28, both being the first alphabetical subjects of republics and oblasts respectively. If you encounter a three digit code, the second and third digit will form the regional code, in this case 123 becomes 23, for Krasnodar Krai. You may also find the codes written out on the back of trucks and vans.

title: Russia - Bus Stops (Plonkit)
description: These are the bus stops unique to specific federal subjects in Russia. Notably common and memorable ones include Krasnoyarsk Krai, Chuvashia, Tatarstan, and Mari El Republic.

title: Russia - RHD Cars (Plonkit)
description: Japanese-made cars with the steering wheel on the right become more common the further east you go, generally starting around Novosibirsk.

title: Russia - Thin Stick Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Russian bollards that appear very thin and attached to a stick are usually found in the eastern part of the country, starting around Omsk. Note that ordinary Russian bollards are still plentiful in this part of the country.

title: Russia - Black Sign Backs (South) (Plonkit)
description: This black traffic sign bottom is primarily found in Stavropol and Chechnya, as well as western Dagestan. Rarely, exceptions can be found in other southern federal subjects such as Kabardino Balkaria, but these will typically be uncolored.

title: Russia - Signpost Clips (Plonkit)
description: Clips on edges of signposts are found in Leningrad and St. Petersburg, and very rarely in Pskov, Novgorod or elsewhere.

title: Russia - Kursk Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Outer dashed road lines are usually found throughout Kursk Oblast. An exception can be found in Tuva Republic. Rarer exceptions include the Republic of Karelia, Primorsky Krai and Khabarovsk Krai.

title: Russia - Concrete Slab Roads (Plonkit)
description: As you go further north in Russia, some roads are made out of several concrete blocks. It is notably common in the Komi Republic, Nenets, and Yamalo-Nenets.

title: Russia - Bilingual Signs (Plonkit)
description: Some republics of Russia with minority languages use bilingual town entry and directional signs, such as in Bashkortostan and Tatarstan displaying Bashkir and Tatar respectively.

title: Russia - Latin Script Town Names (Plonkit)
description: Town names written in both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabets are common near the Baltic border and around Moscow, and to a lesser extent in federal subjects on the Finnish border.

title: Russia - Brown Tourist Signs (Plonkit)
description: These brown signs, pointing to typical tourist attractions, are common in Moscow Oblast and the oblasts bordering it. However, they can also less commonly be seen in city centres or near tourist attractions of other regions.

title: Russia - Limestone Brick Buildings (Plonkit)
description: Buildings made of white limestone brick are indicative of Dagestan, as well as adjacent regions.

title: Russia - Red Brick Buildings (Plonkit)
description: Buildings built almost entirely of red brick are mostly found south, but other notable exceptions include Magnitogorsk, Orsk, and Omsk.

title: Russia - Mosques (Plonkit)
description: While mosques can be found everywhere in Russia, they are by far most common in areas with a Muslim majority, mainly in much of south Russia as well as Tatarstan and Bashkortostan.

title: Russia - Mari El Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Historical buildings in Mari El often have a unique architecture style. You will frequently see design patterns that include green roofs, red brick sprinkled with white stone details. Local churches commonly feature a similar style.

title: Russia - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
This is the full coverage map of Russia. It can be helpful to know areas where there isn’t any coverage. The coverage is notably very sparse in the east and north.
You can check out the extent of the official coverage on this website.

title: Russia - White Car (Snow) (Plonkit)
description: White car long antenna is found in many places, most commonly in southern Chelyabinsk, on snow coverage around Novosibirsk, and in the Far East beginning in Amur Oblast.

title: Russia - A-Type Short Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The A-type short antenna has its highest ridge on the right. Notable areas for this antenna are around Kaluga, Orenburg, and Krasnodar.

title: Russia - B-Type Short Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The B-type short antenna has its highest ridge on the left. This antenna is wide-ranging, but it is most notably found near Nizhny Novgorod, Elista, and Yekaterinburg and Tyumen.

title: Russia - B-Type Pronounced Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The B-type pronounced antenna is the same as the B-type antenna but the ridge is more “rectangular”. This antenna is fairly limited, only being found commonly in Moscow Oblast, Kurgan Oblast, near Krasnoyarsk, and southwest Krasnodar.

title: Russia - C-Type Short Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The C-type short antenna can be thought of as a low A-type or a “twisting antenna” with the ridges being further from the top. It is found north and east of Moscow, with the furthest south being Rostov Oblast.

title: Russia - Blurred Short Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The blurred short antenna is visibly blurrier than any of the other short antennas. It is mainly found in two major clusters around Ufa and from Stavropol to Makhachkala.

title: Russia - A-Type Long Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The A-type long antenna has its highest ridge on the right side. Notable areas include Leningrad Oblast, Republic of Karelia, and Vologda Oblast. Almost all the white car long antenna coverage is A-type, so checking for A-type can also help confirm car colour.

title: Russia - B-Type Long Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The B-type long antenna has its highest ridge on the left side. Notable areas include Yaroslav to Vladimir, Tula Oblast, and much of the coverage near Tuva and Irkutsk.

title: Russia - Blurred Long Antenna (Plonkit)
description: Blurred long antenna is visibly blurrier than other long antenna cars, and is a strong clue for Sakhalin and various roads in the east, as well as much of Khanty-Mansi. On the other end there exists a blurred antenna in far western Bryansk Oblast and some of Tula Oblast.

title: Russia - Tilted Short Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The tilted short antenna is visibly tilted to the left and can be found primarily on a diagonal from St. Petersburg down to Volgograd, with exceptions in Stavropol and Ufa. Since the ridge is on the same side, it can sometimes appear as the A-type short antenna.

title: Russia - Large Red Brake Light (Plonkit)
description: A large, red brake light is common in Kaliningrad, however it can also be found in some older coverage in western Russia.

title: Russia - Autumn Gen 3 (Plonkit)
description: Autumn Generation 3 coverage is common in Kaliningrad, Bryansk, Tula, and Belgorod in western Russia, but Kaliningrad only has autumn coverage.

title: Russia - Snow Coverage (Plonkit)
description: In Generation 4 coverage, significant snow on the ground is most commonly seen in Saratov Oblast and Eastern Voronezh Oblast.

title: Russia - Gen 4 Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Generation 4 coverage is quite extensive and is found in most federal subjects in the country. Notably, areas like the Altai mountains and most of the Far East lack Generation 4 completely. Knowing where Generation 4 can be found isn’t the most helpful at the beginner level; other clues like season and car are more important. The dark red signifies areas where all of the coverage is Generation 4.

title: Russia - Winter Gen 4 (Plonkit)
description: Winter Generation 4 is most common in the south of Russia, ranging from Ryazan all the way down to Kabardino-Balkaria and Dagestan. Winter can appear differently depending on the month (and even time of month the coverage was taken) which can be used to further regionguess.

title: Russia - Spring Gen 4 (Plonkit)
description: Spring Generation 4 is common in several distinct places, such as around Kemerovo and Krasnoyarsk, Orenburg and Kamyshin, around Lipetsk, and in Moscow city. Differentiating these places typically comes down to landscape, as they tend to be fairly distinct.
