title: Russia - Summer Gen 4 (Plonkit)
description: Summer Generation 4 is the most common coverage in generation 4. It is pretty much everywhere except in the south and some of the east, but can be further subdivided by car colour.

title: Russia - Autumn Gen 4 (Plonkit)
description: Autumn Generation 4 is quite rare and only found around Kazan and a few roads in Murmansk, as well as some of Ulan-Ude.

title: Russia - Gen 4 Red Car (Plonkit)
description: Generation 4 red car is the most common generation 4 car meta, found primarily east around Khanty-Mansi, as well as along the main highways down to Irkutsk and Ulan-Ude. There is also a sizable patch near Penza and Tatarstan, as well as Rostov-on-Don.

title: Russia - Gen 4 White Car (Plonkit)
description: Generation 4 white car is found in the May coverage near Lipetsk, in Moscow city, and most notably across all the coverage north of Berkatit in the Sakha Republic and Magadan.

title: Russia - Gen 4 Black Car (Plonkit)
description: Generation 4 black car is found mostly near Moscow, Tver, and Voronezh, with some also existing in Tatarstan and less commonly in the south.

title: Russia - Vorkuta Winter (Plonkit)
description: Vorkuta in far northern Komi Republic has dead-looking winter coverage, sometimes with reddish soil. The apartment blocks will typically have large northern apartment block foundations.

title: Russia - Vanino Winter (Plonkit)
description: Sovetskaya Gavan and Vanino in eastern Khabarovsk have winter coverage, somewhat similar to Vorkuta.

title: Russia - Okha Road (Plonkit)
description: The road to Okha in northern Sakhalin is unpaved, revealing its very sandy soil. The road is surrounded by short, stunted bushes and trees.

title: Russia - Khabarovsk-Vanino Road (Plonkit)
description: The Khabarovsk-Vanino road has a mountainous landscape with very sunny coverage. It also drives west with a black car with a blurred, long antenna, which helps to confirm.

title: Russia - JAO Foggy Road (Plonkit)
description: The Jewish Autonomous Oblast effectively has one road of coverage, outside of Birobidzhan. The west side has highly rainy and foggy coverage.

title: Russia - JAO Wet Road (Plonkit)
description: On the east side of the Jewish Autonomous Oblast, the coverage turns from rainy to wet after the rain.

title: Russia - P-297 Sunset (Plonkit)
description: Sunset coverage, with the sun very close to the horizon, with an eastern-looking landscape will be the P-297 in Amur Oblast, roughly between the towns of Never and Sivaki.

title: Russia - Olkhon Island (Plonkit)
description: Olkhon Island on Lake Baikal has a single road, driving on rolling sandy hills during sunset. You can often see Lake Baikal directly with a mountain ridge across the bay.

title: Russia - Tunkinsky National Park (Plonkit)
description: Tunkinsky National Park in western Buryatia is a very green river basin with tall, jagged mountains to the north. In comparison to most of Buryatia, it is much greener.

title: Russia - Caspian Desert Gen 4 (Plonkit)
description: In the desert-like region west of the Caspian Sea, this completely flat and rural Generation 4 coverage on small poorly-tracked dirt roads can only be found in northern Dagestan and southwestern Astrakhan Oblast.

title: Russia - Black Sea Palms (Plonkit)
description: Tropical plants in Russia such as palm trees are only found on the Black Sea, most commonly around Sochi.

title: Russia - Kamchatka Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: Kamchatka trekkers encompass a majority of the trekkers present in Russia. They can be recognized using the same clues to recognize Kamchatka normally.

title: Russia - Moscow Blue Signs (Plonkit)
description: These blue signs are only found in Moscow and usually feature English translations of important tourist points.

title: Russia - St. Petersburg Signs (Plonkit)
description: St. Petersburg street signs include a transliteration of the street name on a black background. They are primarily found downtown.

title: Russia - Saransk Signs (Plonkit)
description: Saransk has an exclusive circular street sign design with the street name being written in up to 4 different languages.

title: Russia - Tatar Street Suffix (Plonkit)
description: Tatar bilingual signs use “урамы” (ур., abbreviated) for street instead of “улица” and are unsurprisingly found in Tatarstan.

title: Russia - Bashkir Street Suffix (Plonkit)
description: Bashkir bilingual signs are found in Bashkortostan and use “урамы” for street, the same as Tatar, but are often not abbreviated.

title: Russia - Chuvash Street Suffix (Plonkit)
description: Chuvash bilingual signs, found in Chuvashia, use “урамӗ” for street.

title: Russia - Mari Street Suffix (Plonkit)
description: Mari bilingual signs, found in Mari El, use “урем” for street.

title: Russia - Komi Street Suffix (Plonkit)
description: Komi bilingual signs, found in the Komi Republic, use “улича” for street.

title: Russia - Ulyanovsk Red-White Poles (Plonkit)
description: These alternating red and white poles are mainly found in Ulyanovsk city, but also less commonly in the greater Nizhny Novgorod area as well as somewhat randomly elsewhere in the country.

title: Russia - Saransk Striped Poles (Plonkit)
description: These striped red and white poles are found mostly in Saransk, but also in a few other cities in Mordovia.

title: Russia - Tatarstan Pole Plates (Plonkit)
description: Yellow pole plates attached by a metal band are commonly found in Tatarstan. They are found on the majority of poles, but not all.

title: Russia - Murmansk Pole Bands (Plonkit)
description: On the main road of Murmansk in generation 4, as well as some roads in Karelia covered in 2018, the vast majority of signposts will have two yellow bands wrapped around them.

title: Russia - Kaliningrad Cobble (Plonkit)
description: Cobblestone pavement is notably common in Kaliningrad, Nizhny Tagil in Sverdlovsk, and Kizel in Perm Krai.

title: Russia - Extended Insulator Bars (Plonkit)
description: Extended insulator bars on poles are notably found in southern Chelyabinsk Oblast and eastern Orenburg Oblast, as well as southern Kemerovo Oblast.

title: Russia - Mesh Poles (Plonkit)
description: Utility poles with a mesh framework are usually found in Petrozavodsk, but can much less commonly be found in cities like Tolyatti.

title: Russia - Murom Red Poles (Plonkit)
description: These red painted poles are only found in Murom.

title: Russia - Chita Angled Insulator (Plonkit)
description: An angled extended insulator bar on the pole as shown is found in Chita.

title: Russia - Kostroma Bollard (Plonkit)
description: This unique bollard, with a grey rectangle and double red reflectors, is specific to the P100 in Kostroma Oblast.

title: Russia - Chelyabinsk Sign Hooks (Plonkit)
description: Pedestrian signs with a U-shaped hook attached to a pole are unique to Chelyabinsk.

title: Russia - Pskov Pedestrian Signs (Plonkit)
description: This distinct decorative design of pedestrian sign holders is specific to Pskov Oblast.

title: Russia - Nizhnevartovsk Hanging Signs (Plonkit)
description: The city of Nizhnevartovsk has these unique hanging pedestrian signs.

title: Russia - Chelyabinsk Fences (Plonkit)
description: Rounded rectangular fences with a line through the middle are unique to Chelyabinsk Oblast and eastern Orenburg Oblast.

title: Russia - Syzran/Samara Fences (Plonkit)
description: This fence with a thin rounded rectangular design at the top is found in the cities of Syzran, Tolyatti, and Samara. In Tolyatti it will commonly be painted yellow.

title: Russia - Irkutsk Orange Fences (Plonkit)
description: Decoratively designed fences usually with a bright orange colour are unique to Irkutsk.

title: San Marino - Monte Titano (Plonkit)
description: The 739m-tall Monte Titano dominates the surrounding landscape and is visible from almost every point in the Republic.

title: San Marino - Landscape Overview (Plonkit)
description: The landscape of San Marino largely consists of smooth agricultural hills, with many small winding roads. The vegetation is distinctly Mediterranean, and normally appears quite lush.

title: San Marino - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Sammarinese licence plates are short, white and have blue lettering on them.

title: San Marino - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Road signs and bollards are generally identical to the ones used in Italy.

title: San Marino - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Just like Italy, most utility poles in San Marino are round and made of concrete. Wooden poles are also found in the country.

title: San Marino - Yellow Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: San Marino is the only country in the world to use yellow chevrons with burgundy red arrows.

title: San Marino - Blue-White Crosswalks (Plonkit)
description: These elaborate pedestrian crossings, with painted blue crosswalks and hanging signs, are specific to San Marino.

title: San Marino - Green/Black Bins (Plonkit)
description: Lime-green bins are particularly common in San Marino. In Generation 4 coverage some of them have been replaced by black bins.

title: San Marino - Superstrada Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: The Superstrada di San Marino runs from the border village of Dogana to the City of San Marino. It is the only divided road in the country, and the lanes are separated by a metal guardrail.

title: San Marino - Historic Centre Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: The historic centre is covered by a Generation 3 trekker camera.

title: Serbia - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Serbia has a few bollard designs, however most of them will have an off-centred reflector. The bollards are usually flat, with no depth to them.

title: Serbia - B-Profile Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Serbia uses B-Profile guardrails exclusively.

title: Serbia - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Serbia uses chevrons with a black arrow on a white background.

title: Serbia - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Serbian licence plates are white with a blue strip on the left. Agricultural plates, on vehicles such as tractors, are green.

title: Serbia - Cyrillic & Latin Script (Plonkit)
description:
Serbian is a Slavic language which uses both the Cyrillic and Latin script. These letters are unique to Serbian:
- Ђ ђ
- Ћ ћ
These letters are found in Serbian and Macedonian:
- Љ љ
- Њ њ
- Џ џ

title: Serbia - Latin Special Characters (Plonkit)
description: When written in the Latin script, Serbian uses the special letters Č, Ć, Đ, Š and Ž. Note that all of these letters may also be found in Croatian and Montenegrin.

title: Serbia - Serbia Has 4 (Plonkit)
description: Serbia has 4 different truck colours that were used in different areas.

title: Serbia - Serbia Also Has (Plonkit)
description: Serbia also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot. And a short antenna or black blur can be seen on the backside.

title: Serbia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Most of the generation 3 coverage in Serbia was taken by a Google car with no antenna.

title: Serbia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: This is a generation 3 coverage map of Serbia. Most of the coverage is in the north in Vojvodina, around Belgrade and in the southeast around Niš. Kosovo does not have any coverage.

title: Serbia - Landscape Overview (Plonkit)
description:
In the north of Serbia in the Vojvodina region, from the Hungarian border to Belgrade, the landscape is extremely flat, with no hills whatsoever. A slight ridge however can be seen at Fruška Gora National Park.
A more hilly landscape can be seen in the central-southern region. The most mountainous regions of Serbia are found in the southwest and southeast, where the Dinaric Alps, Carpathian and Balkan mountains run through Serbia.

title: Serbia - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description: Serbia uses 2 digit area codes, with the first digit between 1 and 3. Area codes starting with 2 are found in the north, area codes starting with 1 are found in central and eastern Serbia. Area codes starting with 3 are found in the south-west.

title: Serbia - Vojvodina Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Vojvodina, the northern region between the Hungarian border and Belgrade, can be recognized by the flat, agricultural landscape. The landscape will be completely flat with no hills whatsoever.

title: Serbia - Fruška Gora Ridge (Plonkit)
description: This slight ridge in an otherwise flat landscape can be seen in Fruška Gora National Park, southwest of Novi Sad.

title: Serbia - Central Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description: Central-northern Serbia can be recognized by the slight rolling hills.

title: Serbia - Southern Morava Basin (Plonkit)
description: A similarly rolling landscape can be seen in the southern Morava River basin, however larger hills and mountains can be seen.

title: Serbia - Southern Mountains (Plonkit)
description: A lush, green, mountainous landscape can be seen in the south and southeast, along the Bulgarian and Kosovo border.

title: Serbia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Generation 3 Fall coverage can be seen in this region south of Čačak, and a small area around Valjevo.

title: Serbia - White Car Short Antenna (Plonkit)
description: A white Google Car with a short antenna can be seen in Novi Sad, Kovilj, in and around Belgrade, Niš, and the E75 connecting them.

title: Serbia - Vršac Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The distinct Vršac Mountains can be seen east of Vršac near the Romanian border. The mountains protrude out from a flat landscape and vineyards can commonly be seen to the south of the mountains. The Vršac Castle can also be seen atop the mountain.

title: Serbia - Bilingual Hungarian Signs (Plonkit)
description: Bilingual signs with Serbian alongside Hungarian can be seen in northern Vojvodina, where there is a Hungarian majority.

title: Serbia - No Antenna Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Most of the coverage in Serbia was taken by a Google car with no antenna.

title: Serbia - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: This is a coverage map of Serbia. Most of the coverage is in the north in Vojvodina, around Belgrade and in the southeast around Niš. Kosovo does not have any coverage.

title: Serbia - Autumn Coverage (Valjevo) (Plonkit)
description: Fall coverage can be seen in this region south of Čačak, and a small area around Valjevo.

title: Serbia - Divided Highways Map (Plonkit)
description:
There are 3 main divided highways in Serbia:

The A1, or E-75 from the Hungarian border to south of Leskovac, running through Novi Sad, Belgrade and Niš.

The A3, or E-70 from the Croatian border to Belgrade

The A4 which branches off of the A1 north of Niš, to just before Sicevo Canyon Nature Park.

title: Serbia - Tadpole Smudge (Plonkit)
description: This tadpole-shaped smudge can be seen east of Belgrade, from just west of Bavanište to the Romanian border.

title: Serbia - E-80 Yellow Lines (Plonkit)
description: A small section of the E-80 north of Pirot has yellow centre lines.

title: Slovakia - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Bollards in Slovakia have orange double reflectors on the front and a single white reflector on the back. There are also rarer blue and red variants.

title: Slovakia - Wide B-Profile Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Slovakia and Czechia both use a special kind of type B guardrail, which is wider than the normal type. No other European countries use the same kind.

title: Slovakia - Double Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Slovakia and Czechia most commonly use wide, round concrete poles, which are quite often attached in pairs.

title: Slovakia - Metal Bar Poletops (Plonkit)
description: Slovak and Czech poletops typically feature short metal bars that hold the insulators.

title: Slovakia - Triangle Support Poletops (Plonkit)
description: Two support bars holding up the metal bar on pole tops, resembling an upside down triangle, can sometimes be found in Slovakia and Czechia.

title: Slovakia - Trident Poletops (Plonkit)
description: You may also see concrete poles with trident poletops, with two arms angled upwards. Some features, such as the number of insulators, will vary, however the general shape will be the same. Out of the pole tops listed, these are the least common, but unique to the two countries.

title: Slovakia - Bolted Lamp Base (Plonkit)
description: Lamp posts with a thick base mounted by opposing pairs of bolts are common in both countries. The exact shape of the base may vary.

title: Slovakia - Striped Sign Posts (Plonkit)
description: It is common in both Slovakia and Czechia to see temporary square sign posts coated in red and white stripes.

title: Slovakia - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Slovak and Czech chevrons are white with red arrows. Less commonly, you may find red on yellow chevrons.

title: Slovakia - Gas/Water Poles (Plonkit)
description: Stripy gas and water poles reminiscent of snow poles can often be found next to the road.

title: Slovakia - Hiking Markers (Plonkit)
description: Hiking markers, made up of one colourful strip between two white ones, are commonly found in Slovakia and Czechia. They sometimes form an arrow.

title: Slovakia - Panel Apartment Buildings (Plonkit)
description: Like all of the former Eastern bloc, prefabricated panel apartment buildings are a common sight in urban areas. What distinguishes Slovakia and Czechia is the relatively good maintenance often combined with vibrant colours and patterns. Some smaller buildings also adhere to this style.

title: Slovakia - Diamond Roof Tiles (Plonkit)
description: Roofs with diamond shaped tiles are common in both Slovakia and Czechia.

title: Slovakia - Gen 3 Antenna Tape (Plonkit)
description: A car antenna with a grey piece of tape stuck to the top can be seen on much of the Generation 3 coverage.

title: Slovakia - Gen 4 Black Car (Plonkit)
description: A black generation 4 Google car can also be found in both Slovakia and Czechia.

title: Slovakia - Gen 4 Red Car (Plonkit)
description: A red generation 4 Google car can be found in both Slovakia and Czechia.

title: Slovakia - Bridge Markers (Plonkit)
description: These black signs can often be found by the end of bridges in Generation 4 coverage. The road number is displayed on the left.

title: Slovakia - Language Characters (Plonkit)
Slovakia - Landscape Overview (Plonkit)
description: The Slovak landscape varies between very mountainous and completely flat. Generally speaking, Czechia is hillier, but less mountainous.

title: Slovakia - Blue Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Slovakia uses blue directional signs, with small white arrows.

title: Slovakia - Borderless Road Signs (Plonkit)
description: Slovak road signs commonly have the painted sign border right at the edge of the sign.

title: Slovakia - Borderless Highway Signs (Plonkit)
description: Slovak highway signs can be either blue or green, and have a white border right at the edge of the sign.

title: Slovakia - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: White street signs with blue text and a thin red border are by far the most common in Slovakia.

title: Slovakia - Slovakia Features (Plonkit)
description: House numbers in Slovakia are typically written on white signs with a thin red or black border.

title: Slovakia - Top Slovak Sign (Plonkit)
description: The top of Slovak sign posts are typically either open, have a grey metal cap or a thin black cap.

title: Slovakia - Slovakia Uses Two (Plonkit)
description: Slovakia uses two major pedestrian signs, both having five stripes. The first has a simply drawn person with a belt, and the second has the stripes very close together.

title: Slovakia - Slovak Road Signs (Plonkit)
description: Slovak road signs normally feature a very bold font.

title: Slovakia - Slovak Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: Slovak kilometre markers typically have two sections divided with a black horizontal line. The top section contains the road number.

title: Slovakia - Slovak Cycling Signs (Plonkit)
description: Slovak cycling signs use the letter C as their symbol, unique to the country. They’re visually analogous to the Czechoslovak hiking markers mentioned in step 1.1, including the yellow post on directional signs.

title: Slovakia - Slovakia Features (Plonkit)
description: Window shutters are considerably more common in Slovakia than in Czechia.

title: Slovakia - Many Slovak Houses (Plonkit)
description: Many Slovak houses have the short side facing the road with the roof ending in a hip end.

title: Slovakia - Grey Metal Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Grey metal roofs are very common, particularly in the eastern parts of Slovakia.

title: Slovakia - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: While Czechia has a lot of Generation 3 winter coverage, Slovakia has a lot of Generation 3 spring coverage.

title: Slovakia - Slovak Railway Crossing (Plonkit)
description: The Slovak railway crossing sign has a white rectangular background.

title: Slovakia - Slovakia Features (Plonkit)
description: It is fairly common to see small signs with double sign posts in Slovakia.

title: Slovakia - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Slovakia recently changed its standard bollard to a design very similar to the one found in Hungary: a standard European wedge-shaped bollard with a red front reflector. Note that for the time being, this bollard is still very rare.

title: Slovakia - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description:
It is somewhat more common to see wooden poles, and in turn, white concrete supports in Slovakia rather than in Czechia.
Note that because there are many variables, it may sometimes be inconsistent. Therefore, this information should preferably be used to help decide between a difficult fifty-fifty.

title: Slovakia - Area Code Map (Plonkit)
description: Slovak phone numbers typically consist of 10 digits, of which the first 2-3 digits are the area code.

title: Slovakia - Apart From Major (Plonkit)
description:
Apart from the major highways, for which the numbers do not follow any clear pattern, there are two types of numbered roads in Slovakia: 3-digit and 4-digit roads. While many 3-digit roads do not follow any pattern, the ones between 500-560 are generally ordered from west to east. Similarly, the 4-digit road numbers also increase to the east.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Slovakia - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The tallest mountains in Slovakia are found in the central and northern parts of the country, while the flattest areas are found mainly in the southwest and in the southeast.

title: Slovakia - Flat Agricultural Land (Plonkit)
description: The western lowlands in Slovakia are characterised by completely flat agricultural fields, which are rare to find anywhere else in the country.

title: Slovakia - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The eastern lowlands can typically be recognized by wide, flat fields, surrounded by hills or mountains in the far distance.

title: Slovakia - Several Areas Southern (Plonkit)
description: Several areas in southern Slovakia have a Hungarian majority, with bilingual street and information signs.

title: Slovakia - Painted Poles (Plonkit)
description: Concrete poles in Nitra and Trnava regions commonly have yellow circles painted on them, usually containing a number. They are also occasionally found in adjacent regions.

title: Slovakia - Street Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Yellow lamp posts with a blue base are mainly found in the east, with a notable exception being the city of Zvolen.

title: Slovakia - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Two wide valleys surrounded by tall, often sharp mountains can be found in the northern parts of the country. Due to the directions of the valleys, figuring out the direction to the closest mountain is typically enough to differentiate the two.

title: Slovakia - Pine Forests (Plonkit)
description: Pine forests are common in the westernmost part of the country.

title: Slovakia - Cyrillic Script (Plonkit)
description: In the northeastern parts of the Prešov region, you may find bilingual town entry signs in Rusyn, a Cyrillic based language closely related to Ukrainian.

title: Slovakia - Not Only Bratislava (Plonkit)
description: Not only is Bratislava by far the largest city in the country, it is also the only major city with a large river running through it.

title: Slovakia - Bratislava And Košice (Plonkit)
description: Bratislava and Košice are the only two cities with trams, using a red and a yellow-blue-white colour scheme respectively.

title: Slovakia - Painted Poles (Plonkit)
description: Trolleybuses in Žilina use a green-yellow-white colour scheme. The trolley supporting electricity poles, often doubling as lamps, are painted with matching yellow and green colours.

title: Slovakia - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Skalica, in the northwestern corner of the country, has red street signs, similar to the ones commonly found in Czechia. However, the somewhat stylized font distinguishes it from the Czech signs.

title: Slovakia - Čičmany Westernmost Parts (Plonkit)
description: Čičmany, in the westernmost parts of the Žilina Region, is easily recognized by the dark brown wooden houses, whose walls are filled with art consisting of white lines.

title: Slovenia - Landscape Overview (Plonkit)
description:
The Slovenian landscape is generally very hilly and forested, with occasional agriculture.
For exceptions to this, see the region guessing section.

title: Slovenia - Forest Roads (Plonkit)
description: A very significant portion of the coverage in Slovenia was taken on small roads deep inside forest.

title: Slovenia - Alpine Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Slovenian architecture takes much inspiration from alpine architecture, with light coloured walls, dark wooden details and semi-steep roofs. The most common roof shape is half-hipped roofs.

title: Slovenia - Language Characters (Plonkit)
description: Slovene is a Slavic language featuring the special letters Č, Š, and Ž. It is closely related to Croatian, Serbian and Montenegrin.

title: Slovenia - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Slovenian bollards are white with a black top. The front reflector will typically be bright red, while the back reflector will be white.

title: Slovenia - Yellow Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Slovenian directional signs are yellow with a black border.

title: Slovenia - Kilometer Markers (Plonkit)
description: Slovenian kilometre markers have a very distinct design. At the top left the road number is shown in a yellow rectangle, and a second number is to the right of it. A horizontal black line divides the top and bottom, and the distance is shown below.

title: Slovenia - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description:
Slovenian chevrons usually have red arrows on a white background.
You can also find a less common version with a black arrow on a white background.

title: Slovenia - Pedestrian Signs (Plonkit)
description: Slovenian pedestrian signs have five stripes and a simply drawn person without a belt.

title: Slovenia - Long Outer Dashes (Plonkit)
description: Slovenian roads commonly feature long outer dashes.

title: Slovenia - White Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Slovenian street signs are most commonly white with a metal border attached to signposts, or red and attached to house walls.

title: Slovenia - Red House Numbers (Plonkit)
description: Slovenian house numbers are typically red with white text.

title: Slovenia - A-Type Guardrails (Plonkit)
description:
Slovenia uses a regular A-type guardrail, like most European countries. This guardrail type has rounded edges.
This is mostly useful for 50-50s with Croatia, which uses B-type guardrails. This type has square edges.

title: Slovenia - Kozolec Hayracks (Plonkit)
description: This type of shed, called a kozolec, made of thin wooden beams with noticeable gaps in between, is very typical for Slovenia.

title: Slovenia - Gen 4 Black Car (Plonkit)
description: A black generation 4 car can be found in Slovenia.

title: Slovenia - Gen 4 White Car (Plonkit)
description: A white generation 4 Google car can also rarely be found in Slovenia.

title: Slovenia - Alpine Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The tallest mountains in the country can be found in the northwestern alpine region.

title: Slovenia - Eastern Plains (Plonkit)
description: Flat, or rolling, agricultural fields with no mountains or tall hills in view can be seen in the east of the country.

title: Slovenia - Coastal Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Near the coast you get a landscape similar to the rest of the Adriatic coast; white cliffs with bushy vegetation, vineyards and Mediterranean architecture.

title: Slovenia - Southeast Valley (Plonkit)
description: A wide valley going east to west, with mountains to the north and south can be found in the southeast.

title: Slovenia - Bilingual Italian Signs (Plonkit)
description: Italian bilingual signs can be found in the westernmost region.

title: Slovenia - Green House Numbers (Plonkit)
description: Instead of the normal red house numbers, Ljubljana will typically feature green house numbers.

title: Slovenia - Celje Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs in Celje feature the emblem of the city, a blue shield with three yellow stars.

title: Slovenia - Trbovlje Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Similar to Celje, Trbovlje also features the city’s coat of arms, which is a blue and green shield with a black crest.

title: Spain - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Spain uses standard long, white European plates with a single blue strip on the left.

title: Spain - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: The standard Spanish bollards have a yellow-orange reflector on the front and two white dots on the back (though the back can also be blank). They are typically hollow.

title: Spain - Concrete Ladder Poles (Plonkit)
description:
In Spain, you can find a variety of electricity poles and pole tops. In small towns and sparsely populated rural areas concrete ladder poles and wooden poles are the most common.
“Ladder” poles have indents that resemble a ladder, hence the name.

title: Spain - French Poletops (Plonkit)
description: “French style” poletops are common in Spain. They are shaped like an upside down triangle, with a horizontal top bar that is curved slightly upwards. They are usually found on top of tall ladder poles or medium sized steel poles.

title: Spain - Mediterranean Landscape (Plonkit)
description: High voltage electricity lines supported by pylons are very common in Spain, especially compared to other Mediterranean countries.

title: Spain - Road Markers (Plonkit)
description: Spain has distinct road markers with a variety of colourful borders. The code on top is the number of the road.

title: Spain - Hunting Signs (Plonkit)
description: In rural areas you will often find hunting signs. There are two versions, both of which are unique to Spain. One is a simple white sign with a text starting with “coto” and ending in “caza”. The other one has a diagonally divided black and white background.

title: Spain - A-Type Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Spain has yellow reflectors on rounded A-type guardrails.

title: Spain - 8-Stripe Crosswalks (Plonkit)
description: Spanish pedestrian crossing signs have 8 stripes. This is the highest number of stripes in Europe, and almost unique to Spain.

title: Spain - Small Stop Sign Font (Plonkit)
description: Spanish stop signs have a distinct small font.

title: Spain - Borderless Red Signs (Plonkit)
description: Red borders on road signs extend all the way to the edge of the sign. There is no small white border separating the red part from the edge.

title: Spain - Flat Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Almost all traffic signs, kilometre markers, chevrons and some direction signs in Spain have a flat signpost.

title: Spain - Yellow-Black Chevrons (Plonkit)
description:
Spain has two chevrons: black with white arrows, and blue with white arrows. Chevrons with a single arrow are rare.
- In Southern Europe, black with white chevrons can be found in Italy, Greece and Albania.
- France is the only other European country that has blue with white chevrons.
- Portugal has black with yellow chevrons.

title: Spain - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Spanish direction signs have a white background. They often feature colourful boxes with road numbers, making them recognizable. These road number boxes can be many different colours.
Highway signs have a blue background.

title: Spain - Dashed Outer Lines (Plonkit)
description:
Rural roads sometimes have dashed outer lines. This can help tell Spain apart from Portugal and Italy, where such road lines are (almost) non-existent.
Note that the reverse is not true: like Italy and Portugal, many Spanish roads do have solid outer lines.

title: Spain - Language Differences (Plonkit)
description:
Spanish is the main language in most of the country. It is a Romance language that is closely related to Portuguese.
Spanish and Portuguese can look very similar. Some key differences between the two:
- Ñ is unique to Spanish.
- Ç and lh are unique to Portuguese (Ç is also present in Catalan).
- Portuguese uses the -ao word ending, and -nh- instead of ñ.
- Spanish uses de and del, while these are often contracted to da, do, das and dos in Portuguese.

title: Spain - Word for Street (Calle) (Plonkit)
description: The Spanish word for street is calle.

title: Spain - No Parking Signs (Vado) (Plonkit)
description:
You will often find no parking signs in front of garage doors and gates. They will usually read “Vado permanente”.
These signs will very often have the name of the municipality after “Ayuntamiento de”.

title: Spain - Landscape Variety (Plonkit)
description: Spain has highly diverse landscapes, ranging from lush Atlantic forests to bone-dry semideserts. Elevation is also varied: highland plateaus interspersed with rolling hills are common, but you might also encounter jagged mountain ranges and very flat lowland areas.

title: Spain - Mediterranean Landscape (Plonkit)
description: While there is not one single definitive Spanish landscape, most of the country has a somewhat dry, Mediterranean climate, with matching vegetation and agriculture.

title: Spain - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Generation 3 cars can have long, short or no antennas. The back of the car is usually not visible, but when it is, it can be either black or white.

title: Spain - Gen 4 Cars (Plonkit)
description: Generation 4 cars are blue or less commonly black. The car can be completely hidden.

title: Spain - Gen 4 Smallcam (Plonkit)
description: Spain also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: Spain - Ari / Shitcam (Plonkit)
description: Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Spain. This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”). It has a wide circular car blur, and can be distinguished from Generation 2 by its lack of a sky halo and often somewhat brownish colours. A good map will not usually include this coverage, but it is good to be aware of its existence, in order to not be caught off-guard by it.

title: Spain - Spanish Regional Road (Plonkit)
description:
Spanish regional road numbers feature region-specific codes. These are found on road markers, and sometimes on direction signs.
For example, the SG code on road markers refers to a road in Segovia province.
The infographic shows almost all the regional codes, except for some very rare codes. Click on the image to enlarge it.
- National roads use the following codes: E, AP, A, R, N. These can be found anywhere in the country.
- Be careful: A is also used for community roads in Andalusia and Aragon.
- Some autonomous communities do not have community roads, only provincial roads. These have been indicated with grey on the map.
- Asturias uniquely has a large variety of local road codes.
- Ceuta only has N-roads. Melilla uses the code ML.

title: Spain - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description:
Area codes in Spain are very useful, as you only need two digits to get a very accurate guess. Every landline number starts with “9”, followed by the regional numbers.
Mobile numbers start with “6”, and are not relevant in region guessing.

title: Spain - Regional Languages (Plonkit)
description:
Spain has several regional languages. The ones that are most useful to GeoGuessr are Catalan, Basque and Galician.
Some other regions, such as Asturias, also have their own regional languages. But there, non-Spanish signage is much more rare.

title: Spain - Catalan Language (Plonkit)
description:
Catalan is a Romance language that is closely related to both Spanish and French.
It is spoken in Catalonia, the Valencian Community, and the Balearic Islands. In Catalonia and the Balearic Islands, it is (much) more common than Spanish on signage. The Valencian Community is more bilingual.
If you are unfamiliar with Romance languages, it can be hard to distinguish between Catalan and Spanish.
- The Catalan word for “and” is i, compared to Spanish y.
- The grave accent (à, è, ò), is exclusive to Catalan within Spain and very common to see in words, especially on à.
- The c with cedilla (ç) is also exclusive to Catalan within Spain.

title: Spain - Catalan Street (Carrer) (Plonkit)
description: The Catalan word for street is “carrer”.

title: Spain - Catalan No Parking (Plonkit)
description: No parking signs in Catalan speaking areas will read “Gual permanent”. Most municipalities use “gual” in Catalonia and the Balearic Islands, while it’s more common to find a mix of Spanish and Catalan signs in Valencia.

title: Spain - Basque Language (Plonkit)
description:
Basque is a language isolate that is spoken in the Basque Country and northern Navarre. In these regions, you will find a mix of Spanish and Basque signs (often bilingual).
Basque is not related to any other language, so it has a unique look. Z and K are common letters.

title: Spain - Basque Street (Kalea) (Plonkit)
description: Streets in Basque-speaking areas are sometimes called “kalea”. However, Spanish “calle” is also still common.

title: Spain - Basque Road Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Road signs in the Basque Country and Navarre often have these distinctive bilingual sub-signs with a thick black border.
Generally you will find Basque on top in the Basque Country, while it is more common to find Spanish on top in Navarre.

title: Spain - Galician Language (Plonkit)
description:
Galician is a Romance language that is closely related to Portuguese. It is (unsurprisingly) spoken in Galicia. Compared to Catalan, it is less dominant, meaning you will still find a lot of Spanish-only signs in this region.
Galician can look very similar to Portuguese. Some ways to tell them apart is the use of ñ and the lack of ç in Galician.

title: Spain - Galician Street (Rúa) (Plonkit)
description: Streets are commonly called Rúa in Galicia, whereas in Portugal they are called Rua (without an accent). However, you can sometimes find signs without the accent in Galicia.

title: Spain - Galician Town Names (Plonkit)
description: Many Galician town names start with A, O, As or Os articles (examples: “A Pena”, “O Burgo”, “As Cruces”). This is both very common and unique to this region, and rarely over the border in western Asturias.

title: Spain - Regional Flags (Plonkit)
description: The regional flags of the autonomous communities are reasonably common, so it is worth learning them.

title: Spain - Catalan Independence Flag (Plonkit)
description: The Catalan Independence flag is not official, but is commonly found in Catalan-speaking areas. It uses the red-and-yellow striped Senyera pattern that is also used in four of the autonomous community flags.

title: Spain - Mountain Ranges (Plonkit)
description:
Spain is a very mountainous country.
The highest mountain ranges are the Pyrenees in the northeast, and the Baetic System (which includes Sierra Nevada) in the southeast.
The Meseta Central is a high altitude, mostly flat area in the centre of the country. It is surrounded by several smaller mountain ranges: the Cantabrian Range in the north, the Iberian System in the east, and Sierra Morena in the south.
Within the Meseta Central there are two more mountain ranges: the Sistema Central (going from the Portuguese border to the northeast of Madrid) and Montes de Toledo.
There are four big river basins in Spain. The Tajo and Guadiana cross Extremadura and go into Portugal, the Guadalquivir covers most of the southwest of Andalusia and the Ebro river basin starts in Navarra and flows into the mediterranean in the south of Catalonia.

title: Spain - Northern Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The landscape in the far north is much more green and lush than the rest of Spain. The landscape is generally quite hilly. Hedges and green meadows are common. In some places, this region’s landscape bears a vague resemblance to Ireland, France and the UK.

title: Spain - Pyrenees Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The Pyrenees is a large mountain range on the border between Spain and France. Its mountains are some of the highest in all of Spain. It can be recognized by its light grey rock and abundance of pine trees. Local architecture features many rock walls.

title: Spain - Basque/Navarra Pines (Plonkit)
description: Thick forests of tall pines can be found all throughout the Pyrenees. When encountered in smaller mountains in between grazing fields or agricultural land, it will most likely be in the Basque Country or Navarra.

title: Spain - Castilla y León Plains (Plonkit)
description: The centre of Castilla y León features a mostly flat agricultural landscape, with only slight changes in elevation. Most of the fields will have cereal crops like wheat and barley, and it is fairly common to find sunflower plantations.

title: Spain - La Rioja Vineyards (Plonkit)
description: Vineyards can be found in several places in Spain. However, if you see vineyards in between mountain ranges to the north and south, you are most likely in La Rioja.

title: Spain - Ebro Semi-Desert (Plonkit)
description: Starting in Navarra and cutting across the middle of Aragón, there is a strip of semi-desert landscape on both sides of the Ebro river basin. Light sandy soil and small shrubs growing on small hills are common in this area.

title: Spain - Teruel Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
Very arid looking and mostly flat areas are common in central and south Aragón.
The soil is very white and rocky in the northern part. Red soil is more common in Teruel.

title: Spain - Castilla-La Mancha Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
Castilla la Mancha can have completely flat landscapes, which are not that common in Castilla y León. Half of Spain’s wine is produced in this region, so vineyards are fairly common.
In the western provinces of Ciudad Real and Toledo, it is very common to see olive tree plantations, generally in flatter ground than those found in Andalusia.

title: Spain - Dehesa Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
Open fields sparsely populated with holm oaks (Quercus ilex) and cork oaks (Quercus suber) are very common in Extremadura and neighbouring regions. These species of oaks tend to be on the smaller side, and have a Mediterranean look. Be careful not to confuse them with olive trees, as they can look superficially similar to the untrained eye.
North of Cáceres the vegetation is more lush and winter and spring coverage is more common.

title: Spain - Murcia Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
In the southeast of Spain, especially in Murcia, you can find a rather arid landscape, with very sandy soil and medium sized mountains surrounding.
Small shrubs and small plantations of fruit trees and olive trees are a common sight around rural roads.

title: Spain - Murcia/Alicante Haze (Plonkit)
description:
Mountains in this area, especially Murcia and the south of Alicante have a very distinct look.
They are quite rugged, usually lacking in vegetation. This region commonly features a hazy look, making mountains in the distance look like they are behind a sort of mist.

title: Spain - Sierra Nevada (Plonkit)
description: The mountain range of Sierra Nevada features snowy peaks through the months of November and May. Sierra Nevada is the only mountain range in south Spain with snow during most of the year.

title: Spain - Málaga White Villages (Plonkit)
description: Towns built on a mountain face, consisting entirely of white houses, are very common on the south coast of Spain, around Málaga.

title: Spain - Olive Trees (Plonkit)
description: Olive trees are one of the main crops planted in Spain, they can be commonly seen in more than half of the country.

title: Spain - Andalusia Olives (Plonkit)
description:
Around Córdoba and Jaén, you can find massive olive tree plantations growing over rolling hills and going as far as the eye can see.
The bigger and more remote plantations are usually only covered in Generation 2.

title: Spain - Castilla-La Mancha Olives (Plonkit)
description: South of Madrid, olive tree plantations are usually in small or medium sized fields, in mostly flat terrain and commonly accompanied by red soil.

title: Spain - East Coast Olives (Plonkit)
description: Olive plantations on the east coast are commonly fenced or behind rock walls and you will almost always see mountains in some direction.

title: Spain - Eucalyptus Plantations (Plonkit)
description: All throughout the north coast of Spain you will find eucalyptus plantations looking like this. Galicia has more plantations than the rest of the north combined.

title: Spain - South Eucalyptus (Plonkit)
description: When you encounter eucalyptus trees in a dry environment, you will most likely be in the province of Huelva. You can find them more rarely in Extremadura in the north and up until Córdoba in the east.

title: Spain - East Coast Oranges (Plonkit)
description: On the east coast of Spain, you can find many orange tree plantations. They are usually in small valleys, and if they are in flat land you can usually see mountains to the west, north or south.

title: Spain - Andalusia Oranges (Plonkit)
description:
In the Guadalquivir river basin you can also find many orange plantations, usually in much more open and flat terrain than those of the east coast.
There are some extensive plantations in the mountains, but coverage is sparse there.

title: Spain - Corn Fields (Plonkit)
description: Corn is most commonly grown in big river basins in Spain. It is also grown on the north coast, especially Galicia, and in an area in the north west of Castilla y León.

title: Spain - Stone Pines (Plonkit)
description:
Stone pines (Pinus pinea) can be recognized by their fluffy leaves, and compact bulbous crown that is wider than it is tall.
Forests of exclusively stone pines in a flat area are very common around Valladolid and Huelva. It is common to see them in the mountains close to Barcelona in residential areas.

title: Spain - Aleppo Pines (Plonkit)
description:
Aleppo pines (Pinus halepensis) also have fluffy leaves, but their crown is less compact, more disorganised looking, and often taller, compared to stone pines.
This is the most common pine on the east coast of Spain and the Balearic Islands.

title: Spain - Baltic Pines (Plonkit)
description:
Baltic pines (Pinus sylvestris) are tall and thin, with a dark bark that sheds at the top, revealing the orange-red wood underneath. They usually do not have branches on the bottom half of the trunk, especially when fully grown.
Baltic pines can be found in mainly three mountain ranges: the Pyrinees, Sierra de Guadarrama and the Iberian System.

title: Spain - Maritime Pines (Plonkit)
description: Maritime pines (Pinus Pinaster) has two variants in Spain, near the Atlantic coast, it has grey bark with red undertones, and fluffy branches that point upwards. Older trees often don’t have any branches in the bottom half of the tree.

title: Spain - Mediterranean Pines (Plonkit)
description:
In the rest of Spain you can find the Mediterranean variant of the tree. It still has a grey bark with red tones, and it is usually very fissured.
You can find the tree in most of the mountain ranges in central and southern Spain. Extensive plantations in flat ground can be found North of Segovia.

title: Spain - Road Lines (Plonkit)
description:
On small roads, particularly those without a middle line, roadlines can be a very good clue to determine where in the country a location can be.
- In places where straight outer lines are prevalent you will very rarely find dashed outer lines.
- In places where dashed outer lines are the main style, finding straight outer lines is rare, but less so than for the reverse.
Some provinces have their own style of roadline, such as Araba where simple long dashed middle lines are the most common style, or Gipuzkoa, where you can see long outside dashes in roads with a middle line.
Catalonia also frequently features atypical roadlines but there is not one prevalent design.

title: Spain - Square KM Markers (Plonkit)
description:
Most kilometre markers in Spain are either rectangular or square in shape. This can be a good clue to exclude half the country if you can see one in the distance.
There are also some unique designs.
- Andalusian markers are especially tall, featuring an extra stripe with the name of the governing body responsible for the road.
- Madrid markers are square and feature the regional flag at the top.
- Markers in Biscay are bigger than usual and feature a semi-circle shape at the top.

title: Spain - KM Markers Colors (Plonkit)
description:
Kilometre markers in Spain feature a coloured border. The standard colours, going from bigger to smaller roads, are orange, green, and yellow.
Some autonomous communities and provinces use different colours, or even unique designs altogether.
You can read more about the unique designs in this document.

title: Spain - Galician Town Signs (Plonkit)
description: Galician towns frequently use signs with a green or blue strip at the top featuring the name of the municipality.

title: Spain - Asturias Bus Stops (Plonkit)
description: Most bus stops in Asturias have a red post with the CTA logo at the top.

title: Spain - Asturias Trash Bins (Plonkit)
description: Trash containers in Asturias frequently have the logo of COGERSA, the logo’s shape is distinct and can be recognized from afar.

title: Spain - Asturias Snow Poles (Plonkit)
description: Yellow snow poles with one or two reflectors are unique to Asturias. They are usually found in the south of the region.

title: Spain - Aragon Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
In Aragón, it is common to see this bollard design on regional roads.
It has a simple design, consisting of a short flat rectangular white stick with a grey reflector on both sides.

title: Spain - Corrugated Signposts (Plonkit)
description:
Many signs in Catalonia have round, corrugated signposts. This is especially common for direction signs. A similar design is also common in the Basque Country and the Balearic Islands.
Note that municipalities may use signposts like this anywhere in the country, and that regular traffic signs retain the standard flat Spanish design.

title: Spain - Catalan Hunting Signs (Plonkit)
description: In Catalonia and sometimes the Balearic Islands you will find huntings signs in Catalan, usually reading “Àrea privada de Caça”.

title: Spain - Catalan/Canary Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
Within mainland Spain, this bollard is almost exclusive to the provinces of Lleida and Tarragona in Catalonia.
It features a more square and orange reflector on the front, compared to the standard Spanish bollard design. There is a white reflector on the back, instead of the two dots of standard bollards.
Some toll highways like the AP-6 also use this design.

title: Spain - Catalan Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Big square chevrons with a single arrow are commonly found in Catalonia.

title: Spain - Murcia Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Small square chevrons with a red arrow on a white background are exclusive to Murcia.

title: Spain - Madrid Bus Stops (Plonkit)
description:
The surrounding region of Madrid has round topped red bus stops, and green buses. Some bus stops are just a red post.
In the city centre, you can find urban blue buses.

title: Spain - Extremadura Bollards (Plonkit)
description: In the region of Extremadura, it is common to see the normal Spanish bollards with green tops. This bollard variant is exclusive to this region.

title: Spain - Castilla-La Mancha Markers (Plonkit)
description: In Castilla la Mancha you can find stone markers with the region’s coat of arms lining up fields. It can be recognized from afar by the blue coloured left side and the unpainted right side.

title: Spain - Rectangular Mesh Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles with a steel mesh structure making rectangular shapes instead of the typical triangles can be found in the southern half of Spain, and are particularly common in Murcia and southern Alicante.

title: Spain - Andalusian Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Signs from the local government of Andalusia are very recognizable because of the green stripe on the left side.
It is also very common to see small versions of these signs around nature reserves with green signposts.

title: Spain - Andalusian Snow Poles (Plonkit)
description: Blue and yellow snow poles are unique to Andalusia.

title: Spain - Slate Roofs (Plonkit)
description:
There is a large part of north-west Spain where you will find almost exclusively slate roofs (recognisable by their almost black colour). This type of roofing can be seen sparingly all the way to the west coast of Galicia, but ends rather abruptly on the east.
Slate roofs can also be found in the Pyrenees near Andorra, and in the mountain ranges north east of Madrid.

title: Spain - Concrete Block Houses (Plonkit)
description:
Many houses in Galicia are built with big concrete blocks, sometimes textured to resemble natural stone.
Plain concrete blocks are also an extremely common material for walls and miscellaneous buildings like garages.

title: Spain - Galician Granaries (Plonkit)
description: In Galicia, these unique granaries called “horreos gallegos”, or “cabazos”, are very common. Note that they can be made from various materials, but the shape remains the same.

title: Spain - Asturias Hórreos Bigger (Plonkit)
description:
In Asturias, “hórreos” are bigger, generally with a square design, and are built above four pillars, with or without walls. You will sometimes find a rectangular variation, usually built on top of six or eight pillars called “panera”.
If you find an “horreo” with a slate roof, you will be in western Asturias.

title: Spain - Basque/Cantabrian Houses (Plonkit)
description: Large white houses with wooden frames are common in the Basque Country, the Basque part of Navarra, and Cantabria.

title: Spain - Masías (Farmhouses) (Plonkit)
description:
Traditional farm houses called “masías” are common in Catalonia, eastern Aragón and parts of the Valencian Community.
They are usually made of stone and stand isolated or as part of a small complex.

title: Spain - White Towns (Plonkit)
description:
Within the centre and south of Spain, towns made completely out of white painted houses are very common in Andalucía and Extremadura.
You can still see a fair amount of white painted houses in Castilla la Mancha but streets where every house is white will not be common.

title: Spain - Asturias Black Car (Plonkit)
description: In Asturias you can find a black car with no antenna and a visible brake light.

title: Spain - White Tip Antenna (Plonkit)
description:
You can sometimes find a special Generation 3 antenna with a distinctive white top, similar to the one found in Gibraltar.
This antenna is found in the eastern half of Andalusia and in the provinces of Huesca and Lleida in the northeast of the country.

title: Spain - Balearic Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The Balearic islands have a recognizable, coastal Mediterranean look. Somewhat dry looking forests of Aleppo pines cover most of the hills, and small patches of agricultural land, mainly with fruit trees and olive trees, cover the flatter areas between towns.

title: Spain - Balearic Rock Walls (Plonkit)
description: Low rock walls are extremely common on the Balearic Islands.

title: Spain - Balearic Architecture (Plonkit)
description: The stereotypical Balearic house is painted completely white. You can find flat roofs, but tiled roofs with a small incline are the most common.

title: Spain - Menorca Grazing (Plonkit)
description: Within the Balearic Islands, grazing fields are almost exclusive to the island of Menorca.

title: Spain - Formentera Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The small island of Formentera frequently features low coastal shrubs. It is common to be able to see the mountains of Ibiza from Formentera’s north coast.

title: Spain - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The north-west of Mallorca has a tall mountain range that can be seen from many places on the island. It is the only island in the Balearics with mountains this big.

title: Spain - Canary Islands Location (Plonkit)
description: The Canary Islands (or Canaries for short) are a Spanish archipelago off the west coast of Africa. Because they are so far away from mainland Spain, being able to consistently recognize them is important for your scores.

title: Spain - Canary Landscapes (Plonkit)
description: The Canaries have extremely diverse landscapes, including steep mountains, pine forests, volcanic soil, and extreme aridity. You can also encounter more normal landscapes that can look more like mainland Spain.

title: Spain - Lanzarote Soil (Plonkit)
description: In some parts of the island of Lanzarote on the Canary Islands, a very dark, exposed volcanic soil can be seen. In places, this landscape superficially resembles the surface of the moon.

title: Spain - Fuerteventura Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The island of Fuerteventura in the Canary Islands is characterised by a very arid landscape with little to no vegetation. Orange soil is very common, and within the Canary Islands archipelago essentially unique to this island.

title: Spain - Las Palmas Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
This unique bollard design is extremely common in the province of Las Palmas (which includes the islands of Gran Canaria, Fuerteventura and Lanzarote).
It features a more square and orange reflector on the front, compared to the standard Spanish bollard design. There is a white reflector on the back, instead of the two dots of standard bollards.
This bollard can also be found on mainland Spain, in the provinces of Lleida and Tarragona.

title: Spain - Lanzarote Vineyards (Plonkit)
description: You can find these unique wine plantations with volcanic soil and rocks in the shape of a semicircle on the island of Lanzarote.

title: Spain - La Graciosa (Plonkit)
description: Off the north coast of Lanzarote, you will find the small island of La Graciosa. The island’s landscape is completely barren, and the entire coverage features overcast weather. There are two towns on the south coast of the island, with white flat-roofed houses like the east Canaries.

title: Spain - Ceuta & Melilla (Plonkit)
description: The two Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla in North Africa, which are partially surrounded by Morocco, both have coverage. They often catch beginning players off-guard, so it is good to be aware of them and their location.

title: Spain - Ceuta Architecture (Plonkit)
description:
Ceuta features north African architecture, consisting of mainly flat roofed houses in warm colours, ranging from pale yellow to red.
Almost all of the Generation 4 coverage in Ceuta features a bright blue sky in sunny weather with occasional clouds.

title: Spain - Ceuta Landscape (Plonkit)
description: You will find a mountainous, mediterranean landscape in Ceuta, featuring a mix of eucalyptus trees and pines.

title: Spain - Ceuta Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Within Spain, black and white guardrails are unique to Ceuta.

title: Spain - Melilla Architecture (Plonkit)
description:
Melilla also features similar North African architecture. The coverage in Melilla has a hazy look, with a significantly less saturated sky than Ceuta. Most of the coverage is cloudy or overcast.
Melilla has little rural coverage, mainly by the Morocco-Spain border.

title: Spain - Camino De Santiago (Plonkit)
description:
The Camino de Santiago (the Way of St. James in English), is a network of pilgrim's ways across Europe leading to the shrine of apostle James (Santiago in Spanish) in Santiago de Compostela.
These paths are frequently marked with a yellow scallop on a blue background. Markers can be found both in traffic signs and in waystones.
It is common to see pilgrims hiking or biking along these routes, particularly during the summer.

title: Spain - Castilla-La Mancha Gen 3 (Plonkit)
description:
Coverage during early spring on dirt roads between green grassy fields, and leafless vineyards with red soil, is very common in the central-north part of Castilla la Mancha.
This type of coverage is particularly extensive in the northern part and exclusively in generation 3. Towards the south you will also find very similar looking coverage in generation 4.

title: Spain - Navarra AP-15 Features (Plonkit)
description: The AP-15 in Navarra features unique bollards with a simple flat design and a square red reflector. Guardrails also have red reflectors unlike the rest of Spain.

title: Spain - Barcelona Taxis (Plonkit)
description: Taxis in Barcelona are black with yellow doors, including the trunk door.

title: Spain - Ebro Delta (Plonkit)
description:
The Ebro delta (Deltebre in catalan) features an extremely flat landscape, where rice fields and water canals are very common.
There are significant mountains to the South, West, and North, and some of them can be seen from almost every location in the delta.

title: Spain - Greenhouses (El Ejido) (Plonkit)
description: Between Almeria and Motril you can find many greenhouses with white roofs, in the lowland area close to the sea. They are especially common in El Ejido.

title: Spain - Bilbao Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: The city of Bilbao uses this unique street sign, with a very elaborately decorated frame. It is not found anywhere else in Spain.

title: Spain - Doñana National Park Car (Plonkit)
description: In Doñana National Park, southwest of Seville, you will find this rare and unique car meta.

title: Spain - Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Spain has two chevrons: black with white arrows, and blue with white arrows. Chevrons with a single arrow are rare.

title: Spain - Regional Road Codes (Plonkit)
description:
Spanish regional road numbers feature region-specific codes. These are found on road markers, and sometimes on direction signs.

For example, the SG code on road markers refers to a road in Segovia province.

The infographic shows almost all the regional codes, except for some very rare codes. Click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Spain - Mallorca Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The north-west of Palma has a tall mountain range that can be seen from many places on the island. It is the only island in the Balearics with mountains this big.

title: Svalbard - Svalbard Location (Plonkit)
description: Svalbard is an archipelago in the Arctic Ocean, of which Norway has sovereignty over. As such, Svalbard is counted as Norway for country streaks purposes.

title: Svalbard - Yellow on Black Plates (Plonkit)
description: Licence plates in Svalbard are generally black with yellow text.

title: Svalbard - Treeless Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The general landscape consists of barren, treeless mountains. Trees and greenery are a very rare sight, with the majority of vegetation consisting of moss and grasses. The sky is also often overcast, with a gloomy look to the coverage.

title: Svalbard - Russian Signs (Plonkit)
description: Russian can sometimes be found on signs.

title: Svalbard - Longyearbyen Features (Plonkit)
description: Longyearbyen is the largest settlement on Svalbard, with many boxy, minimalistic buildings around the town.

title: Svalbard - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Pyramiden feels more abandoned compared to Longyearbyen. Multi-storey soviet-style apartment blocks can be seen, however, with a lack of human-activity. As the name suggests, many pyramidal mountains can be seen in the distance.

title: Svalbard - Coverage Hills (Plonkit)
description: Of the three towns, Barentsburg feels the most desolate. Distinct, multi-coloured apartment blocks can be seen near the top of the hill. Coverage is also more overcast and gloomy than Longyearbyen or Pyramiden.

title: Svalbard - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: This road going south-east of Longyearbyen can be recognized by the barren, treeless mountains on both sides of the road, with lakes leading up to the mountains. A small black mirror can sometimes be seen on the left.

title: Svalbard - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: A trekker can be seen holding on to a red car heading up a winding road, south of the Svalbard Airport. If the car is not present, this distinct line of mountains to the northeast is a good indicator that you are there.

title: Svalbard - Northwest Spitsbergen Park (Plonkit)
description: This large ship can be seen around the Northwest Spitsbergen National Park. The coverage gets increasingly late toward the east, where it eventually becomes dark.

title: Svalbard - Boat With Wooden (Plonkit)
description: This boat with a wooden deck can be seen in these places.

title: Svalbard - Small Red Boat (Plonkit)
description: This small red boat with men in red jackets on board can be seen in the northwest.

title: Svalbard - Isfjorden Features (Plonkit)
description: This boat with a black deck can be seen in Isfjorden, between Barentsburg and Grumant.

title: Svalbard - Boat Be Seen (Plonkit)
description: This boat can be seen east of Pyramiden, and can be identified by the slanted front of the wheelhouse.

title: Sweden - Swedish Plates (Plonkit)
description: Swedish licence plates are long, white, and have the standard blue EU strip on the left side. Licence plates on taxis have a yellow background instead of white.

title: Sweden - Language Features (Plonkit)
description:
Swedish is a North Germanic language that is closely related to Danish and Norwegian. The Swedish alphabet contains the special letters Å, Ä and Ö.
- Danish uses Å, but not Ä or Ö.
- Norwegian uses Å, but not Ä or Ö.
- Icelandic uses Ö, but not Å or Ä.
Finnish uses Ä and Ö. Å is also used, but is treated as Swedish. Finnish words are typically longer and often use double vowels, which are very rare in Swedish.

title: Sweden - Small Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: On smaller roads, the outer road lines are white and dashed. They are distinctly shorter than the Norwegian dashed lines. In contrast to Norway and Finland, all road lines are white.

title: Sweden - Highway Lines (Plonkit)
description: The outer road lines on highways look solid from a distance, but are typically divided into small sections with a unique pattern, which is different from the solid lines in Finland and Norway. Road lines in Denmark can have a similar pattern, however the individual sections should be rectangular.

title: Sweden - Swedish Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Swedish bollards are black-and-white, typically with a grey reflector. Reflectors by intersections are commonly orange instead. They can be either wedge-shaped, round, or thin and curved.

title: Sweden - Swedish Snow Poles (Plonkit)
description: Snow poles are typically orange, with a tall white reflector slightly above the middle of the pole. Some poles have a second, thinner reflector above the normal one.

title: Sweden - Poletop Caps (Plonkit)
description: Swedish utility poles are usually wooden and can have a variety of poletops. There is commonly a small black metal cap on the very top, which is only found in Nordic countries.

title: Sweden - Double Bolted Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Lamps attached to wooden poles in Sweden are normally mounted slightly below the top of the pole with a double bolting.

title: Sweden - Electricity Markers (Plonkit)
description: These wooden electricity markers, with a blue and a white stripe at the top, are often found near utility poles and pylons, and are not found in any other Nordic country.

title: Sweden - Pedestrian Sign Stripes (Plonkit)
description: Swedish pedestrian signs have four stripes. There is notably a version featuring a female silhouette.

title: Sweden - Blue vs Yellow Signs (Plonkit)
description:
Most directional signs are blue with a white font and border. A thin arrow shows the direction.
Yellow signs with a black font and red border are also common. Places showcased on yellow signs are typically very small and thus hard to find on a map.

title: Sweden - Yellow Background Signs (Plonkit)
description: Swedish road signs have a red border and a yellow background.

title: Sweden - Yellow-Blue Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Sweden is the only country in Europe whose chevrons have yellow arrows on a blue background.

title: Sweden - Meeting Place (M) (Plonkit)
description: On smaller roads, it is common to see these blue signs with a large white M.

title: Sweden - Striped Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Signposts will often have striped markings. Blue and white, and red and yellow are the two most common, but you can also find other colours such as blue and red or white and red.

title: Sweden - Red-Yellow Infrastructure (Plonkit)
description: On top of having red and yellow road signs and signpost markings, Sweden often has a lot of road infrastructure, such as road work signs and road blocks, painted red and yellow. You can even come across red and yellow chevrons.

title: Sweden - Street Name Suffixes (Plonkit)
description: Swedish street names most commonly use the suffixes “vägen” and “gatan”. They are often shortened into “v” and “g” respectively on street signs. Street names can also use “väg” or “gata” as a separate word in a street name. Additionally, the suffix “gränd” can be found near city centres.

title: Sweden - Red Wooden Houses (Plonkit)
description:
Houses in the Swedish countryside are most commonly wooden and often painted with a distinct dark red paint, which is almost exclusively found in Sweden, Norway and Finland.
Urban architecture is usually modern and made of concrete and bricks, while suburban buildings are commonly freestanding single family houses built of either wood or brick.

title: Sweden - Landscape Variety (Plonkit)
description: Sweden has a varied landscape, with a lot of boreal forests, small to medium-sized farmlands and many lakes. The northern and western parts of the country are quite mountainous, with long, narrow lakes and rivers, while the southern and eastern parts are generally flatter.

title: Sweden - Traditional Fences (Plonkit)
description: This type of traditional wooden fence, made out of thin spaced out vertical tree trunks and slightly diagonal trunks stacked on top of each other, is commonly found in Sweden.

title: Sweden - Volvo Cars (Plonkit)
description: The most common car brand in Sweden is Volvo, which makes up almost 30% of all passenger cars.

title: Sweden - Church Flag (Plonkit)
description: The Swedish church flag has a red cross on a yellow background with a crown in the middle, and is often found near churches throughout the country.

title: Sweden - Gen 3 Antenna (Plonkit)
description: A white street view car with a long antenna is featured on a lot of Generation 3 coverage.

title: Sweden - Gen 4 Cars (Plonkit)
description: Generation 4 coverage in Sweden features three Street View cars: a red, a white, and a blue car. Each of the cars can be seen with or without a visible antenna.

title: Sweden - Gen 4 Smallcam (Plonkit)
description: Sweden has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: Sweden - Birch Distribution (Plonkit)
description: Broad leafed trees, other than birches, only grow naturally in the southern half of the country, and become increasingly common the further south you get.

title: Sweden - Fern Distribution (Plonkit)
description: Ferns are mostly found in southern and central Sweden. It can occasionally be found further north in the east.

title: Sweden - Treeless Mountains (Plonkit)
description: While it is possible to see forested mountains in several regions in the country, mountains with no trees at the top can only be found in the northwestern parts of the country.

title: Sweden - Northern Vegetation (Plonkit)
description: This type of vegetation, consisting of thin, weak-looking boreal trees and somewhat sandy soil can be found in the far north of Sweden.

title: Sweden - Beech Forests Which (Plonkit)
description: Beech forests, which can generally be recognised by the barren ground covered in brown leaves, are mainly found in the far south.

title: Sweden - Rock Walls (Plonkit)
description:
Rock walls are mainly found in the south, with the largest concentration being in several coastal areas, on Öland, and on the southern and northern tips of Gotland.
Beware that rock walls around churches and cemeteries are common further north.

title: Sweden - West Coast Rocks (Plonkit)
description: It is very common to see exposed, often somewhat round, rocks on the Swedish west coast. They will often have lower vegetation, such as small bushes, growing on them.

title: Sweden - Skåne Agriculture (Plonkit)
description: In Skåne you will find the most open agricultural landscape in Sweden. It is the only region where, rather than a dense forest in the distance, you can get only a few small patches of trees strewn across the fields. On top of that, crops are often more diverse than the cereal crops, which are typical for the rest of Sweden.

title: Sweden - Lake Mälaren Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The area surrounding lake Mälaren can often be recognized by the fairly flat ground with medium sized agricultural fields, forests beyond them, and small “islands” of bushes and trees in the middle of the fields.

title: Sweden - Västergötland Plains (Plonkit)
description: The agricultural landscape of Västergötland and Östergötland is mostly flat, similarly to the landscape around lake Mälaren. The two most consistent differences is that this landscape is more open and has lots of wind turbines. While you can almost always see a forest in the distance, it will typically be much further away than around Mälaren.

title: Sweden - Halland Landscape (Plonkit)
description: On the west coast, and particularly in Halland, you will see a lot of flat agricultural fields with small, round, forested hills in the distance. Generally, the hills get larger and the fields get smaller further north. The area also has more precipitation than most of the country, and as such it typically looks very lush.

title: Sweden - North Coast Landscape (Plonkit)
description: If you see flat, medium-sized to small agricultural fields, and you suspect that you are in the northern half of the country, you are likely somewhat close to the coast between Umeå and Luleå.

title: Sweden - Jämtland Farms (Plonkit)
description: In most of Jämtland County, particularly around lake Storsjön, you can find large farmlands, commonly situated in the middle of wide, often somewhat steep hills, which is uncommon in the rest of the country, where most farmlands will be either on flat ground or in valleys. The fields are generally not cultivated and will mostly consist of ordinary grass.

title: Sweden - High Coast Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The landscape around the High Coast in Västernorrland can be recognised by the many forested, rocky mountains surrounding agricultural valleys. The valleys are rarely straight and the mountains are of varying heights and shapes.

title: Sweden - Södermanland Valleys (Plonkit)
description: Agricultural fields in and around Södermanland very often go through small valleys, with forests up on the sides of the valleys. The fields are typically medium to small sized.

title: Sweden - Gotland White Sand (Plonkit)
description: White sand can often be seen next to roads on Gotland. It is typically more noticeable in the northern half of the island and on Fårö.

title: Sweden - Gotland Fences (Plonkit)
description: Traditional Swedish fences are typically made of thin round tree trunks and branches. However, on Gotland these fences are typically made of larger trunks that have been cut into sharp-looking wedges.

title: Sweden - Red Dirt Roads (Plonkit)
description: Red dirt roads are mainly found in Dalarna, but can also be found in and around Kalmar county, the border between inland Norrbotten and Västerbotten, and rarely between lakes Vänern and Vättern.

title: Sweden - Jämtland Dirt Roads (Plonkit)
description: Dirt roads which have a deep grey colour and are aligned with low, green grassy vegetation on either side are commonly found in the northern half of Jämtland. This is mostly found in Generation 4 summer and Generation 3 fall coverage.

title: Sweden - Öland Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Öland is an extremely flat island with a somewhat barren south half with many small bushes, while the north is typically slightly lusher with fewer, but larger bushes and some trees. The island also contains a very large number of small rock walls.

title: Sweden - North Coast Birches (Plonkit)
description: It is very common to see long, neat rows of moderately thin birches in urban areas along the north coast.

title: Sweden - Metal Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Grey metal roofs on residential buildings generally get more common the further north in the country you get. Note that metal roofs on barns and sheds can be found significantly further south.

title: Sweden - Houses Skåne Commonly (Plonkit)
description: Houses in Skåne commonly have either a white stone, or a red brick wall with a coloured wooden triangle beneath the roof on the sides. Similar houses with other materials (such as grey brick) for the walls can be found elsewhere in the southern half of the country.

title: Sweden - Half-Timbered Houses (Plonkit)
description: Half-timbered houses can be found mainly in the southern half of Skåne, but also in the northern half and southern Halland. It can also be found in Visby on rare occasions.

title: Sweden - Skåne Red Brick (Plonkit)
description: A lot of single family houses in Skåne are built out of red brick. They typically look slightly older than red brick houses in other parts of the country.

title: Sweden - Mossy Metal Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Corrugated square metal roof panels with moss growing on them are typically found in southern Sweden, particularly in Skåne and Blekinge. It is mainly found on large barns, and the roofs are often very steep.

title: Sweden - Diamond-Tiled Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Grey diamond-tiled roofs are mainly found in Skåne, Blekinge, Öland, and occasionally on Gotland.

title: Sweden - West Coast Houses (Plonkit)
