title: Canada - Provincial Flags Appear (Plonkit)
description:
Provincial flags appear decently often. The Fleurdelisé of Québec in particular is very common.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Canada - Painted Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Acadia is a French-speaking cultural region in the Canadian Maritimes without clearly defined borders. It is usually understood to at least include north and east New Brunswick, with some isolated communities in Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island.
It has its own flag, which is a French-style tricolour with a yellow star in the blue band. It can be seen either flown or painted on poles in this region.

title: Canada - New Brunswick Bollard (Plonkit)
description: These flat, yellow bollards can be found on the Trans-Canada highway in New Brunswick.

title: Canada - Dempster Highway (Plonkit)
description:
The Dempster Highway (road numbers 5 and 8) connects the Klondike Highway (road number 2) in Yukon with the remote town of Inuvik in the Northwest Territories.
It is very recognizable: it is an unpaved road with Generation 2 coverage, dark brown soil, and a tundra landscape with short trees. It is mostly hilly and mountainous, but the section between Fort McPherson and Inuvik is flat. Closer to Inuvik, the weather gets cloudy.

title: Canada - Top of the World Highway (Plonkit)
description: The Top of the World Highway west of Dawson City in Yukon has overcast Generation 2 coverage and is located mostly high up in the mountains, making it recognizable.

title: Canada - Yukon Motorcyclists (Plonkit)
description: A group of motorcyclists can be seen in front of the Google car on this stretch of Highway 1 near Beaver Creek in Yukon.

title: Canada - Banff/Jasper AB-93 (Plonkit)
description: The AB-93 highway through Banff and Jasper National Park features distinct, gradual, and steep mountains with a sharp peak on either side of the road. Tall, somewhat thin trees can also be seen.

title: Canada - Drumheller Canyons (Plonkit)
description: The area near Drumheller, Alberta has distinct canyon-like treeless rock formations that comprise the landscape.

title: Canada - Pine Forests (Plonkit)
description: The Trans-Labrador Highway (road numbers 500 and 510) is a recognizable road, covered by Generation 4, mostly during sunny weather conditions. Thin pine trees line the side of the road, and it has a remote, cold, and northern feel. On many parts of the road, the sun is low in the sky. In addition, when the car drives past the city of Happy Valley-Goose Bay, it is common to see snow on the ground.

title: Canada - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: QC-167 and QC-113 are covered in Gen 3 and identifiable for their overcast autumn coverage, often with snow on the ground. In addition, a smudge can be seen on this road.

title: Canada - Gaspe Peninsula (Plonkit)
description: The inland roads of the Gaspé Peninsula feature densely forested mountainous terrain. It is particularly common to encounter overcast coverage in this region.

title: Canada - Cape Breton Highlands (Plonkit)
description: The Cape Breton Highlands in northeastern Nova Scotia have an unusual amount of elevation for Eastern Canadian standards. It is very forested, with a mix of broad-leaf trees and pine trees.

title: Canada - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Route 430 on Newfoundland runs in a roughly south-southwest to north-northeast direction, with the road lines slightly washed out. It is located in a remote and sparsely populated part of the island. On many sections of the road, the coast is visible to your west. To your east, you will usually see low balsam fir forests, and occasionally an imposing wall of mountains in the far distance.

title: Canada - Iqaluit Signs (Plonkit)
description: Iqaluit is the capital of Nunavut, meaning it is more urban, and built up compared to other Nunavut settlements. The city features bilingual turquoise street signs. Speed limit signs are also uniquely bilingual. And on the outskirts of the city, these unique road markers can be seen.

title: Canada - Churchill Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The remote town of Churchill in northern Manitoba features a trekker with a distinct thin antenna visible on the front right side of the car. The town also has unique street signs.

title: Canada - Tulita Car (Plonkit)
description: This unique Google car and dark-coloured soil is found in Tulita, NWT. The car will most often look like this, but can also be fully blurred with just the antenna visible, or with the hood of the car visible.

title: Canada - Sanikiluaq Snowmobile (Plonkit)
description: Sanikiluaq is a remote town situated in Hudson Bay. This snowy town was covered by a snowmobile whose driver wore a dark brown coat.

title: Canada - Inukjuak Snowmobile (Plonkit)
description: Inukjuak is a town in northern Québec. This town can be recognized by the snowmobile that is visible through the blur.

title: Canada - Grise Fiord (Plonkit)
description: Grise Fiord is the northernmost covered town in Canada. It can easily be recognized by these unique mountains and the ice floes on the coast.

title: Canada - Resolute Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The northern town of Resolute can be recognized by the barren landscape with visible patches of snow.

title: Canada - Cambridge Bay Gen 2 (Plonkit)
description: Cambridge Bay is the only Nunavut settlement to have Generation 2 trekker coverage.

title: Canada - Qikiqtarjuaq Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The town of Qikiqtarjuaq features distinct mountains, and red tinted soil.

title: Canada - Kangiqsualujjuaq Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Kangiqsualujjuaq is a town in northern Québec, surrounded by green rocky hills, with trees visible in the distance.

title: Canada - Nain Coast (Plonkit)
description: Nain is a small town on the Northeastern coast of Labrador. The town features colourful wooden houses, and trees in and around the town. To the north, a big hill is usually visible. And to the south, rocky cliffs can be seen on the other side of the bay. Additionally, kids can sometimes be seen walking beside the trekker.

title: Canada - Red Bay (Plonkit)
description: Red Bay is a town on the southern coast of Labrador, and as such, the coast is always visible. It features slightly red soil, and most of the houses are painted white.

title: Canada - Ellesmere Island (Plonkit)
description: The northernmost Google Street View coverage in the world is a trekker on Ellesmere Island in northern Nunavut. It shows a glacier in a rocky, desolate landscape that is devoid of any vegetation.

title: Canada - Smallcam Generation (Plonkit)
description: Canada also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot. When the car isn’t blurred properly, you will usually see a mirror sticking out on the right side.

title: Canada - Diamond T-Junctions (Plonkit)
description:
Canada uses unique diamond-shaped T-Intersection signs.

Some provinces use different designs. You can learn more about those in the region guessing section.

title: Canada - Province Plates (Plonkit)
description: Each province has its own unique licence plates, some recognizable from afar even when blurred. Multiple provinces do not require front plates, which can be useful when deciding between provinces.

title: Canada - Yukon Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Yukon has a very northern, boreal landscape that is mostly hilly, sometimes with large mountains in the distance. Coniferous trees line the roads and the further north you go, the thinner and shorter the trees get. While this region recently got a lot of new Generation 4, older Generation 2 coverage is still very common.

title: Canada - Manitoba Aspen (Plonkit)
description: Aspen trees are common in the forested parts of Manitoba. They are recognizable by their white, birch-like trunks. In most seasons, they have regular green leaves, but in fall coverage, they turn a characteristic bright yellow colour.

title: Canada - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description: Canadian phone numbers start with a three-digit area code. Both landlines and mobile phones use the same area codes.

title: Canada - Provincial Flags (Plonkit)
description:
Provincial flags appear decently often, so it is worth learning them. The Fleurdelisé of Québec in particular is very common.

You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Canada - Acadian Cultural Region (Plonkit)
description: Acadia is a French-speaking cultural region in the Canadian Maritimes. It does not have clearly defined borders, but is usually understood to at least include north and east New Brunswick. It has its own flag, which is very commonly seen in this region. The flag is a French-style tricolour with a yellow star in the blue band.

title: Canada - Trans-Labrador Highway (Plonkit)
description: The Trans-Labrador Highway (road numbers 500 and 510) is a recognizable road, covered by Generation 4, mostly during sunny weather conditions. Thin pine trees line the side of the road, and it has a remote, cold, and northern feel. On many parts of the road, the sun is low in the sky.

title: Canada - Newfoundland Route 430 (Plonkit)
description: Route 430 on Newfoundland runs in a roughly south-southwest to north-northeast direction, with the road lines slightly washed out. It is located in a remote and sparsely populated part of the island. On many sections of the road, the coast is visible to your west. To your east, you will usually see low pine tree forests, and occasionally an imposing wall of mountains in the far distance.

title: Costa Rica - White Pickup Meta (Plonkit)
description: Costa Rica’s Generation 4 imagery was captured using a large white pickup truck. In many locations, it is either fully or partially visible, but can occasionally be entirely blurred out. There is an antenna attached to the front of the car.

title: Costa Rica - White-Blue Plates (Plonkit)
description: Costa Rican licence plates are typically short and white with blue text, giving them a light blue tint through the blur.

title: Costa Rica - Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description: Costa Rica is a mostly lush tropical country, with rolling hills, agricultural lowlands, peaky volcanoes running through the centre of the country, as well as dense rainforests dotted around.

title: Costa Rica - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Costa Rican architecture is less colonial than that of Panama. Few houses have proper tiled roofs, with dark red sheet metal or dark red plastic tiles being more common. Buildings typically have pastel-coloured concrete walls and are usually either a low single-family house or boxy two-storey structure. They are often heavily guarded with fences and barred windows, to the point that it can be hard to even see a building on many streets.

title: Costa Rica - Spanish Language (Plonkit)
description: Like in most of Latin America, Spanish is the official language of Costa Rica.

title: Costa Rica - Mexico Features (Plonkit)
description: Like in Mexico, Panama and Guatemala, Costa Rican stop signs display the word “ALTO”.

title: Costa Rica - Costa Features (Plonkit)
description: Red taxis are the standard in Costa Rica.

title: Costa Rica - Costa Rica Uses (Plonkit)
description: Costa Rica uses long silver insulators.

title: Costa Rica - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: One of the most common pole tops is an even crossbar with uneven insulators, meaning there is one on one side and two on the other. Additionally, the crossbar is further down on the pole than usual.

title: Costa Rica - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles that have a single insulator attached to the side at the top of the pole are commonly found in Costa Rica.

title: Costa Rica - Street Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Utility poles in Costa Rica feature a lamp with a blue dot on the top, similarly to other Latin American countries like Panama, Colombia and Brazil.

title: Costa Rica - Also Common Thin (Plonkit)
description: Also common is this thin metal crossbar that is bent 90 degrees to form an L-shape.

title: Costa Rica - Many Road Signs (Plonkit)
description: Many road signs have a distinct cross on the back. This is most common on diamond-shaped warning signs, while others are mostly attached regularly.

title: Costa Rica - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: The equivalent of a bollard in Costa Rica would be these vertical orange boards with 3 black circles on them.

title: Costa Rica - Costa Features (Plonkit)
description: Electricity counters in Costa Rica are circular and often have a big metal box alongside them.

title: Costa Rica - Costa Features (Plonkit)
description: Imperial beer ads with its black eagle mascot are a common sight in Costa Rica.

title: Costa Rica - Provinces Sometimes Written (Plonkit)
description: The provinces are sometimes written on signs, so they are useful to know. We will also refer to them in the clues below.

title: Costa Rica - Each Province Has (Plonkit)
description: Each province has their own provincial flag.

title: Costa Rica - Area Code Map (Plonkit)
description: Area codes are moderately useful to learn for Costa Rica.

title: Costa Rica - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Poles are sometimes marked with large black or white stickers, containing multiple lines of text. The first digit of the topmost number is province-specific.
For more specific information, please see this research document created by L’Heureux Traité.

title: Costa Rica - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Asymmetrical pole tops with one insulator on one side of the pole and two on the other are found in and around San José.

title: Costa Rica - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Pole attachments consisting of numbers made out of wires are found in central Alajuela and over the border in Heredia province.

title: Costa Rica - Metal Poles (Plonkit)
description: White pole plates with black lettering are specific to the Greater Metropolitan Area. They are usually attached to the pole using metal bands, although these may sometimes be missing.

title: Costa Rica - Usually Blue Lettering (Plonkit)
description: Usually blue lettering forming a P-XXXXX code with or without the accompanying white background can be found in western Cartago province.

title: Costa Rica - QR Code Signs (Plonkit)
description: Small black stickers with a QR code on the bottom can be seen around Corralillo, south of San José.

title: Costa Rica - Painted Poles (Plonkit)
description: Yellow pole paint that is tall and has 3 sections with numbers is mainly found in Puntarenas and southern Alajuela provinces.

title: Costa Rica - Painted Poles (Plonkit)
description: Yellow pole paint that is shorter and contains all the numbers without dividing lines is mainly found in Guanacaste and northwestern Alajuela provinces.

title: Costa Rica - Painted Poles (Plonkit)
description: Yellow pole paint divided into 2 sections with horizontal characters at the bottom are almost unique to southern Alajuela province.

title: Costa Rica - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: These black pole stickers with yellow lettering, located near the bottom of the pole, are limited to western Guanacaste province and the Nicoya peninsula.

title: Costa Rica - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: North of the mountains lie the largely flat Caribbean Lowlands, characterised by extensive agriculture, grey dirt and a good number of straight roads. Although overcast coverage is common in this area, some locations can be rather sunny.

title: Costa Rica - Seasonal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: A lot of the coverage in western Costa Rica was captured during the dry season.

title: Costa Rica - Lim Features (Plonkit)
description: Most of the banana plantations are found in Limón province.

title: Costa Rica - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: The majority of oil palm plantations are found along the coast in Puntarenas province. A few smaller plantations are located in Limón province.

title: Costa Rica - Puntarenas Features (Plonkit)
description: Pineapple plantations can be seen in western Limón province, northern Alajuela province as well as around the town of Buenos Aires in Puntarenas province.

title: Costa Rica - Sugarcane Plantations Be (Plonkit)
description: Sugarcane plantations can be found in multiple areas across the country, but the major areas are usually distinguishable based on landscape. In the southern area around San Isidro de El General and Buenos Aires you can find sugarcane plantations in bloom with silvery tufts of strands at the top of the plants.

title: Costa Rica - Rice City (Plonkit)
description: Rice fields are mostly found south of the town of Bagaces in Guanacaste province. Some fields are harvested or just recently planted but can be recognized by the raised edges around the paddies.

title: Costa Rica - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The majority of coffee plantations are located throughout the central valley.

title: Costa Rica - Cassava Plantations Most (Plonkit)
description: Cassava plantations are most commonly found in western Limón province.

title: Costa Rica - Guanacaste Features (Plonkit)
description: Teak is recognisable for their tall straight trunks and round glossy, yellow-green leaves and is most common in Guanacaste.

title: Costa Rica - Guanacaste Trees Be (Plonkit)
description: Guanacaste trees can be recognised by their thick trunk and characteristically large, umbrella-shaped crown. They are mostly seen in the eponymous Guanacaste province.

title: Costa Rica - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Mainly growing along the southern coast, Attalea palms can be recognised by the upwards facing leaves that droop slightly.

title: Costa Rica - Macaw Palms Common (Plonkit)
description: Macaw palms are common in western Costa Rica and can be recognised by the long and disheveled looking broods that form an almost round crown. They also usually have a spiky trunk as well.

title: Costa Rica - Dark Volcanic Rocks (Plonkit)
description: Dark volcanic rocks can be found in most of central Costa Rica, but are more common around Guapiles, Limón Province and around the Miravalles Volcano on the border of Alajuela and Guanacaste provinces.

title: Costa Rica - Costa Features (Plonkit)
description: Taxis in Costa Rica are red, featuring yellow triangles on the sides and top containing the city/town name as well as a letter code denoting the province.

title: Costa Rica - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: San José is the capital and by far the largest urban area in Costa Rica. Situated in a valley between multiple mountains, the roads have a noticeable incline. You will see many suburban neighbourhoods and taller buildings than anywhere else in the country.

title: Costa Rica - Simple Fences Made (Plonkit)
description: Simple fences made of irregular wooden branches or logs are found all over Costa Rica but much more prevalent in the west, compared to the planted tree rows or spiked concrete variants more common elsewhere.

title: Costa Rica - Guanacaste Features (Plonkit)
description: Larger irrigation canals exist in the area south of Bagaces and Cañas in Guanacaste province.

title: Costa Rica - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Houses on stilts are mostly found on the northeastern coast.

title: Costa Rica - Antenna Occasionally Be (Plonkit)
description: The antenna can occasionally be seen folded down, predominantly in the north and northeast of the country.

title: Costa Rica - White Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: The entire municipality of San José consistently uses these green street signs with a white rectangle containing an emblem. Calle/Avenida streets are numerically ordered, increasing from downtown outwards.

title: Costa Rica - There Only Few (Plonkit)
description: There are only a few train tracks in Costa Rica. A few lines exist in the Greater Metropolitan Area, from which they go to Puntarenas in the west, and through Turrialba to Siquirres in the east, where it further continues southeast to Limón and to Patio San Cristobal to the northwest.

title: Costa Rica - Only Concrete Highways (Plonkit)
description: The only concrete highways are the eastern stretch of Ruta Nacional 18, and the divided Pan-American Highway (RN 1) from Liberia to the intersection with RN 18.

title: Costa Rica - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Another major divided highway is the RN 32 from the intersection with RN 4 to Limón on the Caribbean coast. The road passes through lush forests in the generally flat Northern lowlands.

title: Costa Rica - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: From the “Route 32 Toll” close to the San José and Heredia border until where it intersects RN 4 west of Guapiles, the road uses yellow bollards placed between the centre road lines.

title: Costa Rica - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: A yellow follow car with two front windows can be seen trailing the Google truck on RN 2 east of Palmar Norte and halfway up to Buenos Aires. The river valley also makes this section of road unique.

title: Costa Rica - Wind Turbines Found (Plonkit)
description: Wind turbines are found in a few clusters, mainly in Guanacaste province, but also southwest of Cartago, over the province border in San José province. In Guanacaste, you’ll find them around La Fortuna, south and northwest of Tilarán, around Santa Cruz, and quite far north of Liberia around road 917.

title: Costa Rica - Bright White Soil (Plonkit)
description: Bright white soil roads likely place you just north of the city of Liberia, Guanacaste province.

title: Costa Rica - Late Evening Into (Plonkit)
description: Late evening into night coverage can be found in the town of San Vito.

title: Costa Rica - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Tuk-Tuks can be seen around Puerto Viejo de Talamanca on the northeast coast, and less often around Nosara on the west coast.

title: Costa Rica - Spot Rainbolt Himself (Plonkit)
description: You can spot Rainbolt himself, or the filming crew atop a black Toyota around the town of La Fortuna, Alajuela Province.

title: Costa Rica - Southwest La Fortuna (Plonkit)
description:
Southwest of La Fortuna, near the Fortuna Waterfall, you’ll find a Generation 4 trekker taken by Rainbolt on a downhill trail with many stair segments. It concludes at a waterfall. You can recognise it from his brown hair or the camera crew following him.
West of La Fortuna, in the Puentes Colgantes Arenal, Mistico Park, there is another trekker on a tropical trail, taken by a black-haired individual.

title: Costa Rica - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Generation 3 coverage in Costa Rica is very limited, consisting of numerous trekkers in and around San José and by the northern west coast. There is also coverage on Cocos Island, located 500 kilometres southwest of the coast, as well as a boat trekker around Caño Island by the southern west coast.

title: Costa Rica - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Beach trekkers are mostly found on the northern west coast, but can also be found west of San José and on Cocos Island.

title: Costa Rica - Rural Forest (Plonkit)
description: Most rural forest trekkers are found in central Costa Rica. Cocos Island also mainly consists of dense tropical forests.

title: Costa Rica - Urban Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Urban coverage is mainly found in and around San José and Cartago, but also exists in Liberia and Filadelfia de Guanacaste.

title: Costa Rica - Children's Museum (Plonkit)
description: The Children’s Museum in northern San José can be recognised by its grand castle-like exterior.

title: Costa Rica - National Museum (Plonkit)
description: Around the National Museum, you can find several wealthy-looking homes, as well as a small tower built in a style resembling towers on medieval European fortresses.

title: Costa Rica - Orange Pedestrian Bridge (Plonkit)
description:
An orange pedestrian bridge can be found going over a major highway at Parque de la Paz in southeastern San José.
While there is coverage throughout most of the park, you’re not likely to encounter anything but the bridge in a pinpointable map.

title: Costa Rica - La Sabana Park (Plonkit)
description: La Sabana Park has several sports facilities, including the National Stadium of Costa Rica, located in the western part of the park.

title: Costa Rica - University of Costa Rica (Plonkit)
description: The University of Costa Rica, in eastern San José, is fairly busy, with a lot of greenery and various medium-sized buildings strewn across the campus.

title: Costa Rica - Palacio de los Deportes (Plonkit)
description: Palacio de los Deportes is a stadium in Heredia, northwest of San José, which can be recognised by its boxy look combined with the red, blue and white colour scheme.

title: Costa Rica - San Jose Airport (Plonkit)
description: At the Juan Santamaría International Airport you can find the trekker walking in the middle of a major four-lane road. There is also coverage just outside the airport terminal.

title: Costa Rica - Bosque de la Hoja (Plonkit)
description: In Centro Recreativo Bosque de la Hoja, just east of San José de la Montaña, you can see the trekker being followed by three dogs through a pine forest.

title: Costa Rica - Los Manantiales (Plonkit)
description: In Recreational Park Los Manantiales, just southwest of Poás, you can find a road lined with sugarcane plantations and cornstalk dracaena plants.

title: Costa Rica - Laguna de Fraijanes (Plonkit)
description: At the entrance to Laguna de Fraijanes Recreational Park you can find a large orange wooden gate separating the road from a parking lot. As the name suggests, the park itself is situated around a small lagoon.

title: Costa Rica - Cartago Municipal Museum (Plonkit)
description: The Cartago Municipal Museum can be recognised by its palace-like facade with a neatly planted garden in front, as well as the railway in the middle of the street in front of the museum.

title: Costa Rica - Historical Site (Plonkit)
description: The Ruins of Cartago is the remains of a large Catholic church near the centre of the city. The POI is one of the first things to show up when you zoom into the city.

title: Costa Rica - José Rafael Fello (Plonkit)
description: José Rafael “Fello” Meza Ivankovich Stadium in southern Cartago can be recognised by the dark blue walls surrounding it.

title: Costa Rica - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Costa Rica Institute of Technology can usually be recognised by the mountain range which can be seen to the south and east.

title: Costa Rica - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description:
By the entrance of Jardín Botanico Lankester, located southeast of Cartago, you can find a poorly maintained dirt road, surrounded by mountains in the distance, as well as a sign with the name of the garden.
Within the garden itself you will find a plethora of different plants, with the walkways having many soft curves, and almost never being straight.

title: Costa Rica - Turkey Features (Plonkit)
description: The Punta Leona Resort, which can be found by the “Playa Mantas” POI, can be recognised by the red brick pavement, with the bricks having the same shape as you’ll commonly find in Turkey.

title: Costa Rica - Liberia Features (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in Liberia can be recognised by a white building with rounded windows having brown wooden window frames. This building can be seen on all coverage in the town.

title: Costa Rica - Filadelfia Features (Plonkit)
description: Most of the coverage in Filadelfia de Guanacaste was taken on the edge of a park, with a distinct red brick pavement where the bricks are placed in the shape of an “L”.

title: Costa Rica - Gen 3 Trekker (Plonkit)
description:
The vast majority of coverage in Costa Rica was taken with a Generation 3 trekker camera. It can typically be recognised by being closer to the ground than cameras mounted to cars. On urban rounds it can also often be recognised by the trekker being on sidewalks, rather than in the middle of the roads.

There are also some official tripods inside buildings.

title: Costa Rica - Costa Rica Plates (Plonkit)
description: Costa Rican licence plates are typically short and white, with blue text, giving it a light blue tint through the blur.

title: Costa Rica - Round Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Utility poles are typically round and made of concrete.

title: Costa Rica - Alto Stop Sign (Plonkit)
description: Like Mexico and Guatemala, Costa Rican stop signs feature the word “ALTO”.

title: Costa Rica - Limited Coverage (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in Costa Rica is very limited, mainly being found in and around San José and by the northern west coast. There is also coverage on Cocos Island, located 500 kilometres southwest of the coast, as well as a boat trekker around Caño Island by the southern west coast.

title: Costa Rica - Beach Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: Beach trekkers are mostly found on the northern east coast, but can also be found west of San José and on Cocos Island.

title: Dominican Republic - Unique Car Used (Plonkit)
description:
This unique car was used for all street view coverage in the Dominican Republic. It can be recognized by the two metal bars, the thick black stripes on them, as well as the white hood visible at the front.
Within the Americas, you will also see metal bars in Guatemala and Curaçao. However, they will not have thick black stripes.

title: Dominican Republic - Square Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Most electricity poles are square and concrete, with a reverse “L” shape at the top. Less commonly, round or octagonal poles are used.

title: Dominican Republic - Yellow Top Plates (Plonkit)
description: DR licence plates are somewhat reminiscent of New Jersey plates, being pale yellow at the top and white at the bottom.

title: Dominican Republic - Dark Asphalt (Plonkit)
description: Roads in the Dominican Republic are often made of this smooth asphalt, which has a noticeably darker colour than in other countries.

title: Dominican Republic - Pare Stop Signs (Plonkit)
description: Despite being located in Central America, stop signs in DR contain the South American “PARE”. Moreover, many signs are attached to yellow signposts.

title: Dominican Republic - Limited Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Street View coverage in the Dominican Republic is very limited. Only the capital Santo Domingo and the Northern city of Santiago de los Caballeros are covered.

title: Dominican Republic - Northern Mountains (Plonkit)
description: If you have mountains to the North, you will always be in Santiago de los Caballeros.

title: Dominican Republic - Yellow Traffic Poles (Plonkit)
description: Yellow traffic light poles are typically found in the city of Santiago de los Caballeros.

title: Dominican Republic - Santo Domingo Downtown (Plonkit)
description: As the capital and largest city, Santo Domingo has a more developed downtown area, with tall buildings and wide avenues.

title: Dominican Republic - ADN Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street name signs in Santo Domingo often contain the letters “ADN”, a reference to the Distrito Nacional, which the city is located in.

title: Dominican Republic - Purple Pole Markings (Plonkit)
description: These black-and-purple pole markings are only found on poles in the Santo Domingo area.

title: Dominican Republic - Santo Domingo Outskirts (Plonkit)
description: This type of landscape is found on the outskirts of Santo Domingo. It is characterised by narrow dirt tracks, whitish dirt, dried green shrubbery and debris next to the road.

title: Dominican Republic - Santo Domingo Evening (Plonkit)
description: A small portion of the coverage in Santo Domingo was taken late in the evening. Similar imagery does not exist in Santiago de los Caballeros.

title: Dominican Republic - Dominican Republic Car (Plonkit)
description: This unique car was used for all street view coverage in the Dominican Republic. It can be recognized by the two metal bars, the thick black stripes on them, as well as the white hood visible at the front.

title: Greenland - Disjointed Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
The coverage in Greenland is divided into well over fifty small disjoint parts, with different weather conditions, seasons, landmarks and so on. Although the largest concentration is found on the southern half of the west coast, coverage can be found scattered along a lot of the coast. Since differentiating between some of them requires a lot of technical information, such as the position of the sun or clouds, this guide will only cover the parts with clear distinctive features, such as a unique Street View vehicle or an easily recognizable mountain.
Because of the limited coverage, this guide will be structured differently than most other guides. It will be divided into two main sections: one for land coverage and one for boat coverage. These two sections will each be divided into step 2, for larger towns and boats found in multiple locations, and step 3, for smaller settlements and boats found only in one place.

title: Greenland - Gen 3 Trekker (Plonkit)
description: All coverage in Greenland was taken with a Generation 3 trekker camera, which was often attached to a variety of vehicles.

title: Greenland - Greenland Vehicles (Plonkit)
description: Most locations with coverage will have their own odd and unique Street View vehicles, ranging from a red tractor to a snowmobile with a large box at the front.

title: Greenland - Colourful Wooden Houses (Plonkit)
description: Greenlandic architecture mainly consists of small, colourful, simple looking wooden houses, which even in cities are typically placed quite sparsely. The major cities have some larger buildings, which normally look fairly minimalistic.

title: Greenland - Barren Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The Greenlandic landscape is very barren, with no trees or taller vegetation and often featuring snow. Mountains and hills are common, with very limited flat areas. On top of that, almost all coverage was taken in coastal areas, so fjords and visible coastlines are very common.

title: Greenland - Boat Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: Boat trekkers are very common in Greenland, featuring a variety of different boats.

title: Greenland - Nuuk Grey Car (Plonkit)
description: While Nuuk is most easily recognized by the grey Street View car, it can also be recognized by being the largest city by far.

title: Greenland - Sisimiut Black Snowmobile (Plonkit)
description: The city of Sisimiut can be easily recognized by the black snowmobile with side mirrors pointing straight up. The coverage is generally very overcast and grey.

title: Greenland - Ilulissat Green ATV (Plonkit)
description: Most coverage in Ilulissat can be recognized by the green ATV with black bars and the driver wearing a beige hat. Note however that there are some small sections where the driver does not wear it. The coverage is fairly sunny and bright.

title: Greenland - Qaqortoq Red Car (Plonkit)
description: Qaqortoq can be recognized by the red rectangular car. The coverage is extremely sunny and the area is greener and less barren than most of the country.

title: Greenland - Aasiaat Thawing Snow (Plonkit)
description: The most noticeable feature of the coverage in Aasiaat is the windshield with a shiny red, white and black reflection. The large, round side mirrors can also be used to identify the town. The coverage is very sunny and has thick, thawing snow along most of the roads.

title: Greenland - Tasiilaq Grey Handguards (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in Tasiilaq can be recognized by the ATV with large grey handguards on either side. The coverage has a lot of very thin clouds and the area is somewhat green.

title: Greenland - Uummannaq Mountain (Plonkit)
description: Uummannaq has two distinctive features: a sharp mountain to the north and a green snowmobile with large black side mirrors. Neither of the two can be seen on all coverage but at least one can be seen on most.

title: Greenland - Narsaq Antenna (Plonkit)
description: Narsaq can be identified by the thin antenna seen on the right side of the car. The coverage is very sunny and fairly green.

title: Greenland - Maniitsoq Tractor (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in Maniitsoq was taken by a tractor, making it very recognizable. The coverage is overcast and fairly snowy.

title: Greenland - Narsarsuaq Black Hoodie (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in Narsarsuaq can be recognized by the driver wearing a black hoodie. The coverage was taken close to sunset on a very sunny day. There is also a fair amount of small bushes along the road, which is somewhat unusual in Greenland.

title: Greenland - Brattahlid ATV (Plonkit)
description: On the other side of the fjord from Narsarsuaq, a black ATV with an orange and purple bag in the front can be seen. The coverage has a lot of tall green grass and the dirt is unusually red for Greenland.

title: Greenland - Qeqertarsuaq Blue ATV (Plonkit)
description: Qeqertarsuaq is most easily recognized by the blue ATV with wide side mirrors. The coverage is fairly overcast and with a lot of yellow grass along the roads.

title: Greenland - Ittoqqortoormiit Wooden Box (Plonkit)
description: Most coverage in Ittoqqortoormiit can be recognized by the brown wooden box at the front of the ATV and the driver wearing a purple beanie. The ground is mostly grey and stony and the coverage is very sunny.

title: Greenland - Igaliku Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The coverage in and around Igaliku is most easily recognized by the wide, snow-covered mountain range to the northeast which looks very bright due to the setting sun. The green ATV, while not entirely unique on its own, can also be a useful hint.

title: Greenland - Paamiut Grey Car (Plonkit)
description: Paamiut can typically be recognized by the round, grey car which is often only barely visible. The coverage has a lot of thin clouds, but is still quite bright and the foliage consists of a mixture of yellow and green grass, and reddish moss.

title: Greenland - Kangerlussuaq Arid (Plonkit)
description: Kangerlussuaq can typically be recognized by the many streaky clouds in the sky, combined with the significant dryness. The roads near Kangerlussuaq can also be recognized by its unconventional look, with many small bushes, sandy soil with an almost arid climate.

title: Greenland - Kangerlussuaq White Truck (Plonkit)
description: The road east of Kangerlussuaq is easily recognized by the large white truck.

title: Greenland - Sisimiut-Kangerlussuaq Road (Plonkit)
description: The coverage connecting Sisimiut and Kangerlussuaq is easily recognized by the thick layer of snow on and around the road. The sun sets along the road, making the western parts very bright and the eastern parts very dark.

title: Greenland - Saattut Mountains (Plonkit)
description: To the north of Saattut you can see a wide mountain range shrouded in clouds, on the other side of a fjord. The paths covered are mostly dark, muddy dirt roads, and the foliage is mainly yellow grass tufts.

title: Greenland - Kulusuk Island (Plonkit)
description: The coverage on Kulusuk island has a round, red ATV, with a pyramid shaped mountain often seen to the northeast. The footage was taken right after sunset on a clear day, making it fairly dark.

title: Greenland - Kangaatsiaq Thawing Snow (Plonkit)
description: Kangaatsiaq has a large amount of thawing snow on the side of the roads. The sun is setting and there is a large body of water to the west.

title: Greenland - Ikerasak Monolith (Plonkit)
description: Ikerasak is most easily recognized by the large monolithic mountain to the west.

title: Greenland - Ukkusissat Cliff (Plonkit)
description: Ukkusissat is located below a tall cliffside to the east with mountains towering above it.

title: Greenland - Kuummiit Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Kuummiit can be recognized by two distinct mountains, a sharp one to the east and a rounder one to the north. The coverage is slightly dark due to clouds and the sun setting.

title: Greenland - Tiilerilaaq Grey Houses (Plonkit)
description: Unlike most houses in Greenland, the houses in Tiilerilaaq are commonly grey rather than colourful. The village can also be recognized by the ground, which is almost entirely made up of smooth, light grey rocks.

title: Greenland - Niaqornat Rocks (Plonkit)
description: Large, dark grey rocks towering over Niaqornat can be used to recognize the village.

title: Greenland - Siorapaluk Sand (Plonkit)
description: Siorapaluk can be recognized by the sandy, pyramid-shaped mountains to the north, combined with the wide sand beach below the village.

title: Greenland - Qaanaaq Icebergs (Plonkit)
description: To the southwest of Qaanaaq, you can see icebergs in a large body of water, and a wide mountain range on the other side, where the snow is bright white as it reflects the sunlight through the thick clouds.

title: Greenland - Kapisillit ATV (Plonkit)
description: A red and black ATV can be found in and around the village of Kapisillit, northeast of Nuuk. Many mountains in the distance are covered in a layer of snow.

title: Greenland - Kangerluk Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Kangerluk can be recognized by the evenly tall mountains with a particular shape on the other side of the fjord.

title: Greenland - Nuuk East Mountains (Plonkit)
description: On a small bit of coverage east of Nuuk you can see a large number of sharp mountains, powdered in snow. The coverage is somewhat dark due to the thick clouds and the sun being hidden behind the mountains.

title: Greenland - Narsarsuaq Ice Blocks (Plonkit)
description: About 20 km northeast of Narsarsuaq, you can find a small piece of coverage with large ice blocks in every direction.

title: Greenland - Upernavik Runway (Plonkit)
description: In Upernavik, the airport runway is covered on Street View, making it by far the widest paved road found on Street View in Greenland.

title: Greenland - Aasiaat Boat (Plonkit)
description: This boat, with a white cabin and a red roof, can be found by a multitude of towns and villages on the west coast. However, most of the coverage is in the general area around the city of Aasiaat.

title: Greenland - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Similar to the previous boat, this one with a red square cabin can be found at multiple locations on the west coast, most significantly by and around Akunnaaq.

title: Greenland - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: A boat with a black box near the front, and a chequered pattern on the bow can be found fairly north on the east coast. While the western part of the coverage is very foggy and somewhat overcast, the eastern parts of the coverage is slightly less foggy and very sunny. A man wearing a black coat can also be seen captaining the boat.

title: Greenland - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: This bright red boat can be found on the east coast near the towns of Tiilerillaq and Kuummiit respectively. While the coverage near Tiilerillaq does not have a cloud in sight, the coverage near Kuummiit is somewhat overcast.

title: Greenland - Black And White (Plonkit)
description: A black and white boat, with a blue roof, is found between the towns of Kuummiit and Tasiilaq.

title: Greenland - Small White Boat (Plonkit)
description: This small white boat, with a brown wooden top and lights and monitoring devices, can be seen between Tiilerilaaq and Tasiilaq.

title: Greenland - Small Rounded Red (Plonkit)
description: A small, rounded red bow can be found on a boat going south of Tasiilaq.

title: Greenland - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: This small, red and black boat, with multiple people sitting in it, can be found in a fjord far north on the east coast.

title: Greenland - Wooden Fishing Boat (Plonkit)
description: This wooden fishing boat is found outside Ilulissat.

title: Greenland - Small White Boat (Plonkit)
description: This small, white boat with a silver handrail on the bow can be found west of Narsaq and east of Qaqortoq. While the sun is in the west on the coverage near Narsaq, it is in the east on the coverage near Qaqortoq.

title: Greenland - Large All White (Plonkit)
description: This large, all white boat can be seen in between Narsarsuaq with the opposing shore.

title: Greenland - Grey Boat Found (Plonkit)
description: A grey boat is found east of Nuuk.

title: Greenland - Mostly White Boat (Plonkit)
description: A mostly white boat, with extremely tall antennas on the rear can be found going into the fjord east of Nuuk.

title: Guatemala - Blue Tinge Plates (Plonkit)
description: Guatemala has short licence plates, which when blurred will typically have either a blue tinge, or a hint of green on the left side.

title: Guatemala - Guatemala Car (Plonkit)
description: This grey Street View car with a visible roof rack and side mirrors can be seen on all car coverage in Guatemala.

title: Guatemala - Tropical Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Guatemala is a tropical country, and is mainly covered by rainforests.

title: Guatemala - Pastel Stone Houses (Plonkit)
description: Guatemalan architecture mainly consists of pastel painted stone houses, commonly with rusted sheet metal roofs. It is also somewhat common for buildings to be made out of exposed white brick.

title: Guatemala - Thin Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Similarly to Mexico, Guatemalan roads generally have solid white outer lines with a single yellow middle line. Road lines in Guatemala are generally significantly thinner than in Mexico.

title: Guatemala - Like Mexico Panama (Plonkit)
description: Like Mexico, Panama and Costa Rica, Guatemala uses the word “ALTO” on stop signs.

title: Guatemala - Pink/Green Poles (Plonkit)
description: In Guatemala you will very commonly see poles painted with either pink, green or a combination of the two.

title: Guatemala - Limited Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Guatemala has a fairly low amount of coverage, particularly in the north. Here you can see which roads are covered.

title: Guatemala - Topography Map (Plonkit)
description: This is a topographic map of Guatemala. Generally speaking, the middle of the country is mountainous, while the south and north are fairly flat.

title: Guatemala - Southern Flats (Plonkit)
description: The southern regions of Guatemala mainly consist of completely flat agricultural land. It is generally more built up than flat areas in the north.

title: Guatemala - Central Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The central regions of Guatemala are generally mountainous.

title: Guatemala - Northern Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description: The northern regions of Guatemala are typically fairly flat. You will however usually see some hills or a slightly rolling landscape, rather than the complete flatness of the south.

title: Guatemala - Oil Palm Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Oil palm plantations are primarily found in two general areas: in the southwest and just north of the central mountain range.

title: Guatemala - Green Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Completely green utility poles are primarily found in the southeast of the country, but also on a road in the further north in the east and on a small stretch of road around Melchor de Mencos, near the end of the coverage in the far northeast.
These poles also feature small pole plates, which can further narrow down the road. This will be further explained in the next tip.

title: Guatemala - Pole Plate Codes (Plonkit)
description: Most green utility poles contain a white pole plate, for which the top two characters will determine which road you are on. These roads and their corresponding characters are shown in this infographic.

title: Guatemala - Roof Rack Forward (Plonkit)
description: In most of the Guatemala coverage, the top right bar will be facing forward. This means that you can see this line on the side facing forward.

title: Guatemala - Roof Rack Backward (Plonkit)
description: The opposite is true in southeastern Guatemala, where the line is facing backwards.

title: Guatemala - Blue Rope Car (Plonkit)
description: In these regions, you can often see a blue rope on the bottom right bar.

title: Guatemala - Missing Cap Car (Plonkit)
description: These regions in the south and northeast also have the backwards facing bar. The difference here is that the bottom right bar is missing the thin black cap, which is present in the other regions.

title: Guatemala - Phone Code 2 (Plonkit)
description: Phone numbers starting with a 2 are unique to Guatemala City.

title: Guatemala - Phone Code 6 (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, phone numbers starting with a 6 are unique to the Guatemala Department.

title: Guatemala - Lake Atitlan (Plonkit)
description: Lago de Atitlán is by far the largest lake in the mountainous regions of Guatemala. It is surrounded by mountains, and some volcanoes.

title: Guatemala - Tikal Jungle Road (Plonkit)
description: A small dirt road in the middle of a dense jungle can be found north of Tikal, in the far north of the country.

title: Guatemala - Quetzaltenango Bollards (Plonkit)
description: These small white bollards with two black stripes can be found on road 1 northeast of Quetzaltenango.

title: Guatemala - PET-11 Alignment (Plonkit)
description: The PET-11, south of Las Pozas can be recognised by the slightly rolling landscape combined with its completely north-to-south road angle.

title: Guatemala - CA9 Highway (Plonkit)
description: The CA9, going between Escuintla and the coast, can be recognised by being a divided highway with concrete pavement.

title: Guatemala - Tikal Temples (Plonkit)
description:
A trekker featuring several Mayan temples can be found just west of the town of Tikal.
It is worth mentioning that while there are other Guatemalan trekkers featuring Mayan ruins, this is by far the most prominent and contains the largest and most intact temple structures.

title: Guatemala - Electricista Stickers (Plonkit)
description: These white rectangular stickers that have the word ‘electricista’ written on them are unique to Guatemala City.

title: Guatemala - Alto Stop Sign (Plonkit)
description: Like Mexico and Panama, Guatemala uses the word “ALTO” on stop signs.

title: Hawaii - Rainbow Plates (Plonkit)
description: The most common Hawaii licence plate is white with an arcing rainbow across the centre of the plate. When blurred, you can sometimes see the outline of the rainbow. Front plates are required in Hawaii.

title: Hawaii - Hawaiian Language (Plonkit)
description:
Hawaii is the only state to use its own language, though English is still predominantly used. Most place names are in Hawaiian, so you can spot it on street signs, and other road markers.
- Hawaiian is a vowel-oriented language that only uses eight consonants: H, K, L, M, N, P, W, and (ʻ), called an ʻOkina.
- Every Hawaiian word ends in one of 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, or U.
- Each vowel can also have a macron) over it: Ā, Ē, Ī, Ō, and Ū.
These vowels are often combined to make Diphthongs. I.e. UI, AI, AE, etc...

title: Hawaii - Smallcam Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Hawaii has a large amount of Generation 4 "smallcam" coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front, with parts of the car being visible. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

title: Hawaii - Tropical Vegetation (Plonkit)
description:
Hawaii is known for its lush and tropical vegetation, with a variety of plants and trees. However, being a volcanic island chain, Hawaii has a wide range of landscapes, and as such vegetation as well.
You will often see plenty of ferns, tall grass, or other flowers on the sides of the roads.

title: Hawaii - Volcanic Topography (Plonkit)
description: Topography on Hawaii is characterised by many sloping volcanoes, rugged cliffs, hills, valleys and craters. Such distinct topography combined with tropical vegetation is a good way to identify Hawaii.

title: Hawaii - Hawaiian Homes (Plonkit)
description: Contemporary Hawaiian homes are typically 1 or 2 storey wooden structures, commonly lighter in colour. Many homes feature retaining walls made of volcanic rock.

title: Hawaii - Yellow Pole Bands (Plonkit)
description: Thick yellow bands can sometimes be seen on poles in Hawaii.

title: Hawaii - Guitar Pick Shield (Plonkit)
description: Hawaii uses highway shields that resemble a guitar pick, with the numbers on the bottom of the shield. Most highway signs also use yellow signposts.

title: Hawaii - Gen 3 Antenna (Plonkit)
description: A stubby antenna can be seen in most Generation 3 coverage on Hawaii.

title: Hawaii - Gen 2 Blur (Plonkit)
description: Hawaii has a fair amount of Generation 2 coverage, compared to other US states. Especially on more rural roads.

title: Hawaii - Reflector Pattern (Plonkit)
description: Raised pavement markers in Hawaii will commonly be placed in a specific pattern: a single reflector, followed by four reflectors put close together and then a single reflector, repeating the pattern.

title: Hawaii - Highway Numbering (Plonkit)
description:
State highways are grouped by their first digit, with 1 and 2 found on Hawaiʻi, 3 on Maui, 4 on Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi, 5 on Kauaʻi and 6 to 9 on Oʻahu.
Moreover, all four of the so-called interstate highways are located on Oʻahu.

title: Hawaii - Black Car Islands (Plonkit)
description: On the three largest islands, namely Hawaiʻi, Maui and Oʻahu, smallcam coverage was taken with a black Google car.

title: Hawaii - White Car Islands (Plonkit)
description: Smallcam imagery on the islands of Kauaʻi, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi was captured by a white car. Just like with the black car, you will often be able to see the unblurred hood and mirrors.

title: Hawaii - Gen 2 Islands (Plonkit)
description: Generation 2 and non-smallcam Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the islands of Hawaiʻi, Maui and Oʻahu. The other islands only have Generation 3 or smallcam coverage.

title: Hawaii - Kauai Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: The Island of Kauaʻi is the furthest west island in Hawaii with official Google coverage. This island has deep red soil and has large rugged hills with lush, jungle-like vegetation.

title: Hawaii - Oahu Hills (Plonkit)
description: The Island of Oʻahu lies southeast of Kauaʻi. It is known for being home to the Honolulu urban area. It also is home to steep, lush hills, which can be commonly seen from all around the island, especially in Honolulu’s suburbs.

title: Hawaii - Honolulu Skyline (Plonkit)
description: Honolulu, located on southern Oʻahu, is by far the largest city and urban area in Hawaii. If you are in a dense urban area and can see tall buildings, you will always be in or near Honolulu.

title: Hawaii - Molokai Dryness (Plonkit)
description: The Island of Molokaʻi is just southeast of Oʻahu. It features deep red soil and a prominent volcano on the eastern end of the island. Especially in the older Generation 3 coverage, the vegetation appears very dry. Molokaʻi is also very sparsely populated.

title: Hawaii - Lanai Cook Pines (Plonkit)
description: The Island of Lānaʻi is a small, yet distinct island that lies just south of Moloka’i. A volcano is found just east of the centre of the island, adjacent to the town of Lānaʻi. In this area, tall Cook pines are abundant. In addition, some main roads near the centre of the island are lined with younger Cook pines.

title: Hawaii - Lanai Coastal Hills (Plonkit)
description: Towards the coasts of the island of Lānaʻi, hills dotted with dry grass and shrubby vegetation are commonly seen. These areas are very rural with few buildings.

title: Hawaii - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The Island of Maui sits southeast of Molokaʻi. In the centre of the island, you will find dry and somewhat flat grasslands with one or both of the mountain ranges on the island visible.

title: Hawaii - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Coastal areas of Maui are noticeably more lush and green. Banana plants, palm trees, and views of the mountains are all common.

title: Hawaii - Grassy Plains (Plonkit)
description: The Island of Hawai’i (also referred to as The Big Island) is both the largest and farthest southeast island with Street View coverage in the state. The interior areas feature rolling, grassy plains and volcanic rocks. You can typically see one or more of the island’s volcanoes from the road.

title: Hawaii - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: The coastal areas of the island of Hawai’i are where most of the towns and built-up areas on the island are located. These areas are typically more lush and have more trees and fern plants than the interior.

title: Hawaii - Rural Roads Going (Plonkit)
description: Rural roads going through forests within a flat landscape are commonly found south of the city of Hilo, on the island of Hawaiʻi.

title: Hawaii - Hawaii Features (Plonkit)
description: Within Hawaii, a distinct green blur can only be seen on the island of Oʻahu.

title: Hawaii - Infamous Hawaiian Lattice (Plonkit)
description: The infamous “Hawaiian lattice” can be recognized by the volcanic soil and rocks that are abundant in the region. Volcanic vegetation can also be seen lining the roads. Note that the angle of the roads is a big clue for the area, and that this lattice was built on the slope of Mauna Loa.

title: Hawaii - Kaunakakai Features (Plonkit)
description: The town of Kaunakakai is the largest settlement on the Island of Molokaʻi. It is the only area on the island with an ‘urban’ vibe. As it is on Molokaʻi, the soil is somewhat red.

title: Hawaii - Red Hill Easily (Plonkit)
description: The Red Hill can easily be recognised by this unique barren, red rocky landscape. Due to the high altitude, clouds are usually visible below you.

title: Hawaii - Eastern Side (Plonkit)
description: On the eastern side of the island of Molokaʻi lies the Kamakou volcano, leading to a significantly hillier and slightly more vegetated landscape than the western parts of the island.

title: Hawaii - Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description: Kahoʻolawe is a small island that lies just to the southwest of Maui. It only has trekker coverage on small gravel roads and dirt trails, and is characterised by dry, shrubby vegetation, rolling hills, and dark red soil. On the western end of this coverage, several buildings can be seen.

title: Martinique - Gen 3 Trekkers (Plonkit)
description:
Martinique, officially the Department of Martinique, is an overseas department and region of France, in the Caribbean between Dominica and St Lucia. As such, for country streaks purposes, it is counted as France.
Coverage is very limited: there are just three Generation 3 trekkers. Instead of learning metas to identify the territory, it is more useful to just memorise what the trekkers look like.

title: Martinique - Rum Distillery (Plonkit)
description:
Habitation Clément is a rum distillery covered by a trekker. Due to it being pinpointable, some locations are on maps such as ACW. There are several landscapes in and around the distillery, including:
- A warehouse with a truck and a forklift.
- A view of the outside with hills in the background and machinery on display.
- A rural dirt track outside with red soil and palm trees.
- The inside of the distillery with the structure made of H-beam steel.

title: Martinique - Southern Trekker (Plonkit)
description:
The coastal southern trekker can be recognized by a few unique things:
- In the north, the trekker starts off walking on a slightly hilly path, with other people.
- Several houses with orange roofs can be seen.
- A flatter and more open path can be seen, with the ocean slightly visible through the trees.
- The coverage ends in the south with a car park and some stalls.

title: Martinique - Tropical Garden (Plonkit)
description: The Jardin de Balata trekker is the most tropical and humid feeling on Martinique. The trekker can be recognized by dark and damp feeling, the trees with buttress roots, ferns and bamboo. This man wearing a black shirt and grey cap can sometimes be seen with the trekker.

title: Mexico - Octagonal Poles (Plonkit)
description: Most utility poles in Mexico are made of concrete and have an octagonal shape. There will often be engravings on the side.

title: Mexico - Short Plates (Plonkit)
description: Mexico uses short licence plates with a large variety of designs. Front plates are required.

title: Mexico - Yellow Center Line (Plonkit)
description: The most typical Mexican road lines are white solid outer lines with a single unbroken yellow middle line.

title: Mexico - Mexican Bollard (Plonkit)
description: These small, cylindrical white bollards with a black base are unique to Mexico. A yellow reflector can sometimes be seen, as well as a flat version.

title: Mexico - Road Shields (Plonkit)
description: Mexico has two general road shields; one for national highways with “MEXICO” written at the top and a slightly curvy design, and one for state roads which have straight borders, and typically has the state initials written at the top.

title: Mexico - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: Mexican directional signs have a distinctly large, all-caps white font.

title: Mexico - Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: Mexican kilometre markers are white, with black font and outline.

title: Mexico - Cacti Varieties (Plonkit)
description: Cacti, of many different species, are extremely common in Mexico.

title: Mexico - Alto Stop Sign (Plonkit)
description: Mexico uses the word “ALTO” on stop signs.

title: Mexico - Thick Arrow Signs (Plonkit)
description: Arrows on signs are noticeably very thick.

title: Mexico - Yellow Kerbs (Plonkit)
description: Yellow accents on kerbs and bridge barriers are quite common.

title: Mexico - Rooftop Water Tanks (Plonkit)
description: You will commonly see wide cylindrical, black or white water tanks on rooftops.

title: Mexico - Gas Stations (Plonkit)
description: OXXO and Pemex are two of the most popular gas station brands in Mexico.

title: Mexico - Nahuatl Place Names (Plonkit)
description: Many place names in Mexico are of Nahuatl origin, featuring a lot of ‘x’ and ‘tl’ as well as ‘-ec’ and ‘-tlan’ suffixes.

title: Mexico - Circular Meters (Plonkit)
description: Mexico uses circular electricity counters.

title: Mexico - Pickup Trucks (Plonkit)
description: United States car brands are popular in Mexico. In particular, you will see a lot of pickup trucks.

title: Mexico - Gen 2 Availability (Plonkit)
description: Mexico is one of very few Latin American countries that has Generation 2 coverage.

title: Mexico - Gen 3 White Car (Plonkit)
description:
The Generation 3 coverage in Mexico mainly feature two cars:
- A white car with a stubby antenna. There is a diagonal coil wrapped around the antenna.
- A white car with a more visible back and a long red brake light instead of an antenna.
It is possible to find a white car without a stubby antenna, but with a tiny sliver visible where the antenna should be.

title: Mexico - Gen 4 Car (Plonkit)
description:
The Generation 4 cars in Mexico commonly have a visible front and can feature various different colour patterns. The three most common ones are:
- Blue
- White with a blue stripe
- Black

title: Mexico - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description: The first digit of Mexican area codes are regional and can be seen on this map.

title: Mexico - Postal Codes (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, Mexican postal codes can be seen on this map. They will commonly appear at the bottom of street signs, and are ordered alphabetically based on state names.

title: Mexico - State Plates (Plonkit)
description: Every state in Mexico has one or several unique licence plate designs. In this infographic you can find the most common and helpful ones.

title: Mexico - Prickly Pear Cacti (Plonkit)
description: Prickly pear cacti are distinct with their flat oval-shaped pads. They are noticeably more common centrally and are rarely seen in southern and coastal states.

title: Mexico - Pulque Agave (Plonkit)
description: Agave salmiana, also known as pulque agaves, have wide, smooth, curling leaves, and a crown-like appearance. They are common in the central Mexican valley and further north around the city of San Luis Potosi.

title: Mexico - Blue Agave (Plonkit)
description: Vast fields of blue agave (Agave tequilana), used to produce tequila, are mostly found in Jalisco and Nayarit.

title: Mexico - Tree Yucca (Plonkit)
description: Yucca filifera, also known as tree yucca, as well as yucca decipiens are most commonly seen in San Luis Potosi and Zacatecas as well as some of the bordering northern states. They can be recognised by their oblong rosettes of sharp green leaves branching from a single trunk, similar to a tree.

title: Mexico - Giant Cardon (Plonkit)
description: The Mexican Giant Cardon is an extremely common cacti in the Baja California peninsula. It can be identified through its large sprawling arms stemming from a singular trunk and ribbed exterior.

title: Mexico - Saguaro Cacti (Plonkit)
description: The Saguaro Cacti can be spotted in the western half of Sonora, featuring short curving arms that stem from a main trunk.

title: Mexico - Organ Pipe Cacti (Plonkit)
description: Organ Pipe Cacti have long thin stems that often come out from a stem that is around ground level. They are most commonly found in Sonora and occasionally in Baja California Sur.

title: Mexico - Blue Myrtle Cacti (Plonkit)
description: The Blue Myrtle Cacti have short arms that uniformly curve and point upwards. It is abundantly found in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo.

title: Mexico - Sugar Cane (Plonkit)
description: Sugar cane can be found all over the country, but by far most common in Veracruz.

title: Mexico - Coconut Palms (Plonkit)
description: Coconut palms can be found all across the coast, but are often found in large groups in Guerrero and Colima.

title: Mexico - Sabal Palms (Plonkit)
description: Sabal palms are most commonly observed in the east coast of Mexico, the Yucatan peninsula, as well as the state of Nayarit. They feature a spiky, sun-shaped crown, giving the tree a lollipop-like appearance.

title: Mexico - Umbrella Palm (Plonkit)
description: The Attalea rostrata is a huge palm recognizable from its upright leaves, almost resembling an umbrella. It is mostly exclusive to Veracruz and Tabasco, and can be rarely found in Chiapas.

title: Mexico - Oil Palm Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.

title: Mexico - Boojum Trees (Plonkit)
description: Boojum trees can be recognized by their alien, tentacle-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.

title: Mexico - Brittlebush (Plonkit)
description: Brittlebush are small shrubs with bright silver-grey leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.

title: Mexico - White Bark Trees (Plonkit)
description: These thin, white-barked trees can be found in the Yucatan peninsula, but are most prevalent in Quintana Roo.

title: Mexico - Coahuila Gold Tufts (Plonkit)
description: These gold tufts of grass in a line right next to the road are most commonly found in Coahuila.

title: Mexico - Teardrop Grass (Plonkit)
description: These clumps of grass in almost a teardrop shape are common in the region around Tlaxcala.

title: Mexico - Red Fields (Plonkit)
description: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.

title: Mexico - Monterrey Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The Monterrey metropolitan area features tall stunning mountain ranges that surround the city.

title: Mexico - Northern Pine Forests (Plonkit)
description: The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with pine forests. In general, these pines are shorter and more stunted in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.

title: Mexico - Dark Fields (Plonkit)
description: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.

title: Mexico - Baja Hills (Plonkit)
description: These reddish brown-tinged hills, often accompanied by large boulders, are a common sight for the northern half of Baja California.

title: Mexico - White Soil Yucatan (Plonkit)
description: Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.

title: Mexico - Campeche Agriculture (Plonkit)
description: These red agricultural fields surrounded by dense forests of tropical trees are most common in northern Campeche.

title: Mexico - Red Brick West (Plonkit)
description: Red brick buildings are mostly concentrated in the states west of Mexico City, specifically Jalisco, Michoacan, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes.

title: Mexico - White Block East (Plonkit)
description: White concrete block buildings are highly concentrated in the states surrounding Mexico city, and are generally more common to the east. They can however still be found all over the country.

title: Mexico - Mud Brick Buildings (Plonkit)
description: Mud brick buildings are most abundant in Durango, especially full houses constructed with mud brick. However, they can essentially be found in almost all of the dry desert states.

title: Mexico - Northern Bungalows (Plonkit)
description: Architecture in northern Mexico often features design elements from American style bungalows. Many houses are coloured with light or pastel colours, gated and commonly have front yards. Orange tiles inspired by Spanish colonial architecture are also typical.

title: Mexico - Thatched Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Thatched roofs are most common in the Yucatan peninsula and eastern San Luis Potosi. They can also be found elsewhere, mainly in the southeast.

title: Mexico - Yucatan Rock Walls (Plonkit)
description: These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.

title: Mexico - Sign Back Cross (Plonkit)
description: A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.

title: Mexico - Nayarit Bollard (Plonkit)
description: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

title: Mexico - Jalisco Bollard (Plonkit)
description: Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text ‘Jalisco’ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.

title: Mexico - Acorn Insulators (Plonkit)
description: White insulators that are shaped like acorns can be found along the coastal states of Mexico, but are by far most common in Michoacan, Colima, and Veracruz.

title: Mexico - Asymmetric Crossbar (Plonkit)
description: Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.

title: Mexico - Sinaloa Wooden Poles (Plonkit)
description: Wooden poles with a lowered crossbar are mostly found in Sinaloa and Sonora.

title: Mexico - Hanging Insulators (Plonkit)
description: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.

title: Mexico - Baja Hanging Poles (Plonkit)
description: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.

title: Mexico - Durango Mono-Brace (Plonkit)
description: Poles with a lowered crossbar and a single support beam that extend from one end of the crossbar to the pole itself can be found in Durango.

title: Mexico - Mesh Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles with a mesh body are most commonly found in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.

title: Mexico - White Middle Lines (Plonkit)
description: White middle roadlines are most commonly found in Tabasco.

title: Mexico - Red Tree Fences (Plonkit)
description: These fences made out of trees with red-coloured bark are commonly found in Veracruz.

title: Mexico - Black Tar Lines (Plonkit)
description: Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line can be seen in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero.

title: Mexico - Blue Grainy Pavement (Plonkit)
description: Grainy pavement with a blue-ish grey tinge is a common sight for the states of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.

title: Mexico - Irregular Cobblestone (Plonkit)
description: This style of cobblestone pavement, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.

title: Mexico - Hexagonal Pavers (Plonkit)
description: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.

title: Mexico - Three Line Cobble (Plonkit)
description: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is mainly found in Oaxaca.

title: Mexico - CDMX Taxis (Plonkit)
description: Taxis in and around Mexico City have a white lower half with a pink upper half.

title: Mexico - Mexicali Farmland (Plonkit)
description: The area around Mexicali features flat farmland with a ridge to the west. Washingtonia palms are very common and these poles made out of brown wood can be found.

title: Mexico - Poza Rica Citrus (Plonkit)
description: The area around Poza Rica in Veracruz features a lot of citrus tree plantations. It is common to see large amounts of these trees grown right on top of the hills.

title: Mexico - Obregon Canals (Plonkit)
description: The area around Ciudad Obregon is distinct due to the pinkish-tan soil and canals found around the city’s agricultural areas.

title: Mexico - Twin Volcanoes (Plonkit)
description: The twin volcanoes of Iztaccíhuatl and Popocatépetl are found on the border between the State of Mexico and Puebla. Keep in mind that they are usually much less visible than depicted in the image, which is just for reference.

title: Mexico - Cerro del Bernal (Plonkit)
description: Cerro del Bernal is a distinct extinct volcano that is found in southern Tamaulipas. It can be found heading directly northwest of Tampico or west of Morón.

title: Mexico - Sierra del Abra (Plonkit)
description: This extremely long and flat ridge is found in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve in eastern San Luis Potosi.

title: Mexico - Maderas del Carmen (Plonkit)
description: This tall, flat ridge, with very prominent ridgelines, belongs to the Maderas del Carmen Biosphere Reserve in Northern Coahuila near the US border.

title: Mexico - Juarez Outskirts (Plonkit)
description: The outskirts of Ciudad Juárez features a lot of dirt roads with a distinct shade of orange soil and low shrubs.

title: Mexico - Oaxaca Soil Change (Plonkit)
description: The area around San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca and south of it in Oaxaca often feature rolling hills with really distinct orange and beige-tinged soil, passing from one colour to the other with each hill. The beige-tinged soil can be seen more prominent in some locations.

title: Mexico - Guaymas Hills (Plonkit)
description: The town of Guaymas has a lot of jagged cliffs and mountains that make the area very distinct. The soil is also distinctly pinkish and organ-pipe cacti can be seen scattered on the hills and next to the road.

title: Mexico - Pink Lakes (Plonkit)
description: The town of Los Coloradas is famously known for the pink lakes around the area.

title: Mexico - Highway 54 Yuccas (Plonkit)
description: The 54 is a divided highway that runs through northeastern Zacatecas which features yucca trees spammed on both sides of the road. Additionally, the streetview car is often exposed and appears almost white due to the sunlight.

title: Mexico - Highway 40D (Plonkit)
description: The 40D that crosses the Sinaloa-Durango state line is recognizable by the stunning lush cliffs and mountains along the road. The highway commonly passes through tunnels and the road itself features double yellow middle roadlines.

title: Mexico - Highway 95D Divider (Plonkit)
description: This road divider with a yellow top and bottom edge is found all along the 95D from Mexico City to Acapulco.

title: Mexico - Eurus Wind Farm (Plonkit)
description: The Eurus Wind Farm is located in southeast Oaxaca and is the largest wind farm in Mexico. Rows of wind turbines can be found along the 190 around Juchitán de Zaragoza.

title: Mexico - Aguascalientes Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Most lamp posts and lamp arms in Aguascalientes city are yellow.

title: Mexico - Cuernavaca Lamps (Plonkit)
description: This lamp with a black rectangular head is found in Cuernavaca.

title: Mexico - Queretaro Lamps (Plonkit)
description: This lamp with black front and back edges and a white middle section is found in Santiago de Queretaro.

title: Mexico - Cancun Dice Lamps (Plonkit)
description: This lamp with five circular bulbs that looks like a dice is found in Cancun.

title: Mexico - Matamoros Lamps (Plonkit)
description: This lamp with a rectangular head and a ring-shaped light bulb is found in Matamoros.

title: Mexico - Hermosillo Lamps (Plonkit)
description: This lamp with a zig-zag bent pole arm is found in Hermosillo.

title: Mexico - Cuernavaca Pole Paint (Plonkit)
description: The bottom half of poles in Cuernavaca are often painted green.

title: Mexico - Chihuahua Pole Paint (Plonkit)
description: Poles in Chihuahua city occasionally have a strip of white pole paint with the street name written in black or blue text.

title: Mexico - La Malinche Car (Plonkit)
description: This Street View car with a yellow hood can be found by the La Malinche volcano in Tlaxcala.

title: Mexico - Cofre de Perote Car (Plonkit)
description: This white truck with visible rearview mirrors can be seen in the Cofre de Perote national park.

title: Mexico - La Seca Car (Plonkit)
description: This red Street View car with a black roof can be found in the town of La Seca in Sinaloa.

title: Panama - Red Strip Plates (Plonkit)
description:
Panama features short licence plates, most commonly white with a horizontal turquoise strip on the top. Rarely, the strip can have other colours.
Front plates are not required in Panama.

title: Panama - White Pickup Meta (Plonkit)
description: Panama was covered by a large white pickup truck that is usually entirely blurred. An antenna is occasionally visible.

title: Panama - Rolling Hills & Tropical Plants (Plonkit)
description: Panama is a tropical country with a lot of hills. You will find a lot of palms and other tropical plants along with drier rolling hills and fields.

title: Panama - Most Roads Paralleled (Plonkit)
description: Most roads are paralleled by fences that are partly or fully made out of small trees. The rest of the fence posts are also almost always wooden.

title: Panama - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Panamanian architecture often reflects Spanish colonial influences, featuring vibrant colours, and some ornate detailing. The most common type of building has painted concrete or sometimes brick walls with red metal sheets or tiles for a roof. Many windows have bars on them for security.

title: Panama - White Outer Lines (Plonkit)
