description: Panama features a diverse set of road lines, but the most common combination is solid outer white with an inner yellow line. However, those are not unique to Panama. Within Latin America, solid outer white lines with no middle line are almost unique to Panama.

title: Panama - Painted Poles (Plonkit)
description: Panama uses a wide variety of poles, but the most common type is a round concrete pole, with a varying amount of insulators. Poles can also be wooden or metallic. They often have plates attached to them. Blue, white, or red numbers are commonly painted on them as well.

title: Panama - Yellow Plates (Plonkit)
description: Yellow taxis with a chequerboard patterned horizontal stripe are a common sight in Panama. The licence plate will be drawn on the side, containing the city name and a regional code.

title: Panama - Panama Uses Spanish (Plonkit)
description: Panama uses the Spanish word “ALTO” on stop signs.

title: Panama - Eye Stop Sign (Plonkit)
description: Red octagonal signs with an oddly realistic eye are unique to Panama.

title: Panama - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: While Panama is quite well covered, there is barely any coverage on the north coast, or east of Panama City.

title: Panama - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description:
The first digit of phone numbers can be used to regionguess Panama.
The numbers with a smaller font indicate potentially useful regional two-digit codes.

title: Panama - Taxi Plates (Plonkit)
description: The first digit of taxi and bus licence plates can be used to regionguess Panama.

title: Panama - Colon Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Green tropical landscapes with palm trees and very tall grass are common around Colón and Panama City.

title: Panama - David (Volcanic Rocks) (Plonkit)
description: Volcanic rocks that are either scattered on the ground, or built into rock walls, are common north of David.

title: Panama - David Surroundings (Plonkit)
description: The area around David is very flat, with lots of fairly open fields. Usually, mountains will be visible to the north and northeast.

title: Panama - Aguadulce (Brown/Orange Soil) (Plonkit)
description: The region around Aguadulce is relatively flat and features a lot of agricultural fields along with very brown or orange soil.

title: Panama - Eastern Vertical Plates (Plonkit)
description: The eastern provinces often have tall vertical plates that can be yellow or white. They are commonly attached to poles by black zip ties.

title: Panama - Western Horizontal Plates (Plonkit)
description: Many poles in the western provinces will have horizontal plates attached to them. However, if one of these is accompanied by an eastern vertical plate, the eastern plate takes precedence.

title: Panama - Colon Plates (Plonkit)
description: Thin yellow plates, vertical or horizontal, with a visible black border are most common in the Colón Province.

title: Panama - Penonome (Wind Farm) (Plonkit)
description: Wind turbines can be seen south and north of Penonome.

title: Panama - Ngabe-Bugle Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The main covered road in the Ngäbe-Buglé province is very high-altitude and almost above the clouds. The surrounding mountains tend to be quite dry, and the altitude makes for many stunning views.

title: Panama - Changuinola Road (Plonkit)
description: The road going to Changuinola features a lush and green hilly landscape. The weather is cloudy or overcast on the entire road.

title: Panama - Highway 9 (Panama-Colón) (Plonkit)
description: Highway 9 going from Panama City north to Colón is a divided concrete highway. The road is visibly grainy and has a lot of tar lines. The landscape is lush and hilly.

title: Panama - Road 407 (Plonkit)
description: Most of Road 407 features a freshly paved road, with visibly orange soil on the sides of the road. The southern portion is hilly, right before the road quality deteriorates.

title: Panama - Panama City Skyline (Plonkit)
description: Panama City can be recognised by the large number of white high-rise buildings.

title: Panama - Colon Warehouses (Plonkit)
description: Colón features a lot of warehouses and rundown multi-storey buildings.

title: Panama - Changuinola (Banana Plantations) (Plonkit)
description: The region around Changuinola is filled with banana plantations.

title: Panama - South Tonosi Road (Sunset) (Plonkit)
description: Sunset coverage can be found in southern Panama on a small road south of Tonosi.

title: Panama - Volcán (Mountainous/Pines) (Plonkit)
description: A mountainous landscape with pine trees, volcanic rocks, dry grass, and gravel roads can be found northeast of Volcán.

title: Panama - Gatún (Canal Pole Socks) (Plonkit)
description: Yellow pole socks can be found near the Panama Canal, around the town of Gatún.

title: Panama - White Pickup Meta (Plonkit)
description: Panama features a large white pickup truck which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred. There is always a short black antenna attached to the front of the car. Beware that the antenna can sometimes be blurred.

title: Panama - Eastern Road (Car Dirt) (Plonkit)
description: A small cluster of dirt on the car can be found on the eastern road.

title: Panama - Roof Dots (Plonkit)
description: In a lot of central Panama, the Google car will have either one or two black dots visible on the front.

title: Panama - Panama Oeste Red Spot (Plonkit)
description: This small red spot can mostly be found in Panamá Oeste and on the road 2 going from southern Los Santos province to the Verguas province.

title: Panama - Folded Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The antenna can be seen folded down, most commonly in Colón and Panamá provinces, and occasionally in the city of David.

title: Puerto Rico - US Territory (Plonkit)
description: Puerto Rico is a United States overseas territory. As such, it is counted as the US for country streaks purposes.

title: Puerto Rico - Smallcam Antenna (Plonkit)
description: Nearly all of the coverage was captured with smallcam, a variant of Generation 4, which in this case can be recognised by the wide blur and antenna that is often visible. The camera is lower and the front blur more round than pickup truck blurs.

title: Puerto Rico - Gen 3 Antenna (Plonkit)
description: The Generation 3 Street View car found in Puerto Rico has an antenna at the front right. The antenna has a small white dot on the tip.

title: Puerto Rico - Phone Code 787 (Plonkit)
description:
The entirety of Puerto Rico uses (787) as their regional phone code. This number can be seen in front of phone numbers using this format:
(787) XXX-XXXX

title: Puerto Rico - Spanish Signs (Plonkit)
description: Spanish, instead of English, can commonly be seen on signs around Puerto Rico.

title: Puerto Rico - American Chains (Plonkit)
description: American store chains, such as Wal-Mart, are very common in Puerto Rico. This will help distinguish Puerto Rico from other nearby Latin American countries and territories, where American stores are not common.

title: Puerto Rico - No Front Plates (Plonkit)
description: Front plates are not mandatory in Puerto Rico. Therefore, seeing cars with front plates is rare. This helps differentiate from Guam and Northern Mariana Islands.

title: Puerto Rico - Divided Highways (Plonkit)
description: A significant part of the coverage in rural Puerto Rico is taken on large divided highways.

title: Puerto Rico - Highway Shields (Plonkit)
description: Here is an example of what highway shields in Puerto Rico look like. From top left to bottom right they are: primary highway shields, primary urban highway shields, secondary shields, and tertiary shields. These will not be present in any other state or territory of the US.

title: Puerto Rico - Spanish Speed Limit (Plonkit)
description: Speed limit signs in Puerto Rico are identical in shape and size to speed limit signs seen in the mainland US. The major difference is that these signs will always be in Spanish, instead of English.

title: Puerto Rico - Pare Stop Sign (Plonkit)
description: Stop signs in Puerto Rico say ‘PARE’ instead of stop.

title: Puerto Rico - Vertical KM Markers (Plonkit)
description: Puerto Rican kilometre markers are tall, green and with “km” written at the top, followed by a number written vertically in large text.

title: Puerto Rico - Concrete Homes (Plonkit)
description: Most homes in Puerto Rico are made of concrete and have flat rooftops. Metal gates in front of homes are common features as well, especially in urban areas.

title: Puerto Rico - Dry South (Plonkit)
description: Southern Puerto Rico can often look distinctly drier than the rest of the island.

title: Puerto Rico - Coastal Plains (Plonkit)
description: The North and South coasts of Puerto Rico typically feature flat coastal plains or rolling hills.

title: Puerto Rico - Mountain Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Most of the mountainous regions of Puerto Rico are located in the middle section of the country. Most of the coverage in these areas is limited to divided highways.

title: Puerto Rico - Ponce Creole (Plonkit)
description: The Southern city of Ponce features many buildings in the style of Ponce Creole Architecture, which is a combination of Victorian and Spanish Revival styles. Buildings are typically made out of wood and masonry.

title: Puerto Rico - Old San Juan (Plonkit)
description: Old Town San Juan is located at the far Northwest tip of the city of San Juan. This area has very narrow streets, colourful buildings, and a mix of Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque architecture. Also, some streets in this area are made of bricks.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - French Territory (Plonkit)
description: Saint Pierre and Miquelon, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint-Pierre and Miquelon, is an overseas department and region of France, south of Newfoundland in Canada. As such, for country streaks purposes, it is counted as France.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Blue Strip Plates (Plonkit)
description: Licence plates can be either white or yellow and either short or long. They all have a blue EU strip however, and the white plates will also have a blue strip on the right, as is custom in France. Vehicles may or may not have front plates.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Gen 3 Trekker (Plonkit)
description: All coverage was taken with a Generation 3 trekker camera.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Colourful Wooden Houses (Plonkit)
description: Most houses are made of wooden panels with a boxy look and often vivid colours.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Grassy Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The landscape mainly consists of flat or rolling grasslands. The coast will be visible more often than not.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Coverage is fairly limited, being only found in the eastern parts of Saint-Pierre as well as at the northern tip of Miquelon-Langlade.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Miquelon-Langlade (Plonkit)
description: Miquelon-Langlade is a small town in the north of St Pierre. It can be recognized by the houses with timber cladding painted in bold, vivid colours. A shadow of the ATV used to cover this town can also be seen.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Saint-Pierre (Plonkit)
description: Saint-Pierre is the capital and largest town. The coverage in this town is made with a sidewalk trekker. Larger buildings and more cars can be seen, with a more populated feel compared to Miquelon-Langlade.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Ile-aux-Marins (Plonkit)
description: A slightly hilly, grassy landscape with boxy houses spaced apart can be seen on Île-aux-Marins.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Northern Rural Trekker (Plonkit)
description: This rural trekker in the far north can be recognized by the rolling, grassy landscape. The trekker can also be seen walking on a wooden path, with trees on either side.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Saint Pierre Rural (Plonkit)
description: The rural trekker on Saint Pierre island has a more rocky landscape. The trekker also walks on a path with trees on both sides.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon - Boat Trekker (Plonkit)
description: This boat trekker between Saint Pierre Island and Île-aux-Marins can be recognized by this man wearing a grey and black sweater.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Midway Atoll Location (Plonkit)
description:
The US Minor Outlying Islands are a chain of islands that are US overseas territories. As such, it is counted as the US for country streak purposes.
The guide will be somewhat skewed towards the Midway Atoll, as that is the only island with pinpointable coverage.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Gen 2 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: The coverage on the Midway Atoll was made with a Generation 2 camera.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Albatrosses (Plonkit)
description: One of the most distinct features of the Midway atoll is the presence of multiple albatrosses on almost every single location.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Large Part Coverage (Plonkit)
description: A large part of the coverage on the Midway Atoll was taken on two runways, which are the only areas where it can be difficult to spot the albatrosses.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: The islands other than the Midway Atoll can generally be characterised by three things. Firstly, the Generation 3 trekker coverage. Secondly, the low, bushy vegetation, and thirdly, the presence of numerous birds.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Nicely Paved Runway (Plonkit)
description: A nicely paved runway can be seen going west to east on the southern side of the Midway Atoll.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Poorly Paved Runway (Plonkit)
description: A poorly paved runway can be seen going north to south on the Midway Atoll. The pavement gets increasingly poor to the north.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Eastern Side (Plonkit)
description: On the eastern side of the Midway Atoll, you can find a small village.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Lake Views (Plonkit)
description: Southeast Island is arguably the least distinctive island in the chain. It has a small lake near the centre, and a large amount of birds in the sky.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Regional Buses (Plonkit)
description: Lisianski Island only has coverage right by the shore and can typically be recognised by the large bushes going around the entire island.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Island Features (Plonkit)
description: Laysan Island is the only island in the chain where the coverage has almost no clouds.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Shoals Features (Plonkit)
description: The French Frigate Shoals is a fairly long and thin island with a shabby-looking runway. The island has by far the largest number of birds out of all islands in the chain.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: East Island is the smallest island in the chain. There is barely any vegetation and you can see the ocean in all directions.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Western Corner Midway (Plonkit)
description: The western corner of the Midway Atoll runway is arguably the most common location on the official Geoguessr world map and may thus be worth remembering, particularly for a newer player.

title: US Minor Outlying Islands - Eastern Island Situated (Plonkit)
description: Eastern Island, situated right next to the Midway Atoll, has two small areas of low-quality tripod coverage. It does not have any other official coverage.

title: US Virgin Islands - Islands Features (Plonkit)
description: The United States Virgin Islands are a group of islands that are US overseas territories. As such, it is counted as the US for country streaks purposes.

title: US Virgin Islands - Car Coverage Islands (Plonkit)
description: Car coverage on the islands will have a large, visible street view car, which will either be red or white. Details about where to find each car can be found in the region guessing section.

title: US Virgin Islands - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: A unique blend of architecture is found on the United States Virgin Islands. The primary influences are European Renaissance, Spanish Baroque, Rococo and Victorian styles. Facades with large arches are common; as well as central plazas and courtyards.

title: US Virgin Islands - Historical Site (Plonkit)
description: Owing to its former status as a Danish colony, some streets and localities still have Danish names (e.g. gade) or display bilingual signs. This is most common in the historical downtown areas.

title: US Virgin Islands - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Licence plates are short, typically either having a bright blue or a dark blue design.

title: US Virgin Islands - Primary Roads Southern (Plonkit)
description: Primary roads on the Southern US Virgin Island of St. Croix follow a loose grid pattern. Main roads are angled from WSW to ENE, with intersecting roads angled from NNW to SSE. In contrast, the Northern Islands of St. John and St. Thomas have much curvier roads.

title: US Virgin Islands - United States Virgin (Plonkit)
description: The United States Virgin Islands features 3 unique Google cars. The first of which is shown here. This red truck with a red cab can only be seen in the southern island of St Croix. This is the most common car that will be seen as St Croix has the most coverage.

title: US Virgin Islands - White Car Without (Plonkit)
description: A white car without an antenna can also be seen on St Croix, however it will be less common than the red car.

title: US Virgin Islands - White Car With (Plonkit)
description: A white car with an antenna can only be seen in the northern islands of St Thomas and St John. The cab is also noticeably shorter than the other two cars.

title: US Virgin Islands - Hilly Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Two boat trekkers are found on the north coast of St Croix. The boat cannot be seen, however the trekker can be identified by the blue waters and hilly islands. The area near Buck Island National Park also has a distinct pink tint to the camera.

title: United States - Us Uses Phrase (Plonkit)
description:
The US uses the phrase ‘Speed Limit’ on their speed signs.
The numbers on American speed signs are usually lower than on Canadian ones, since they use miles instead of kilometres. In addition, speed limits ending in 5 are more common in the US.

title: United States - Road Signs Us (Plonkit)
description:
Road signs in the US tend to use more words compared to their Canadian counterparts. A good example are railway crossing signs, which feature the literal words ‘railway crossing’ on them. In Canada, these signs are typically blank.
This tendency is also noticeable on yellow diamond warning signs. In Canada, the words will usually be on a rectangular sign below the yellow diamond, which would have a diagram on it instead.

title: United States - height of Bridge (Plonkit)
description:
The US uses American English spelling (e.g. center, color).
In addition, the US primarily uses the imperial system for measurements. For example, speed and distance are measured in miles. You will also often see feet and inches on signs, indicating the height of bridges.

title: United States - Triangular Yellow Signs (Plonkit)
description: Triangular yellow signs with the phrase ‘No Passing Zone’ are exclusive to the US.

title: United States - Rectangular Junction Signs (Plonkit)
description: These rectangular junction signs with a single or double arrow are found in the US.

title: United States - American Yield Signs (Plonkit)
description: American yield signs are shaped like an upside-down triangle with a red border, a white field in the middle and the word ‘YIELD’.

title: United States - American One-way Signs (Plonkit)
description: American one-way signs are usually a horizontal black rectangle with a white arrow inside of it. These signs will also always have the words ‘ONE WAY’ printed on them. In cities, they are a white vertical rectangle with the words ‘ONE WAY’ on them and an arrow underneath.

title: United States - White And Orange (Plonkit)
description: White and orange fibre optic cable markers are almost unique to the US.

title: United States - Road Median (Plonkit)
description:
The US uses yellow middle lines and white outer lines. Double middle lines are the most common.
On divided roads, the outer line closest to the median will be yellow, and the other lines will usually be white.

title: United States - Interstate Highways Us (Plonkit)
description: Interstate highways, US highways, and some state roads have rumble strips on each edge of the road, which are small indentations in the pavement perpendicular to the road. These can be located on the outside edges of the road and in between lanes on multi-lane highways.

title: United States - Small Rectangular Manufactured (Plonkit)
description: Small, rectangular manufactured homes, also known as mobile or ‘trailer’ homes, are popular in rural areas of the US. In general, mobile homes are more common in the Southeast, but they can be seen anywhere in the country.

title: United States - Baptist Churches Very (Plonkit)
description: Baptist churches are very common in the United States. Similar to mobile homes, these are more common in the Southern Plains and Southeast United States, but can be found in all 50 states.

title: United States - Large Highways Us (Plonkit)
description: Large highways in the US use large, rectangular, green metal signs with curved edges and white text to mark highway exits, distances to nearby towns, and the names of upcoming roads (mainly in cities).

title: United States - Leading Up Exits (Plonkit)
description: Leading up to exits on large highways, you commonly see large, blue rectangular signs with white text, highlighting services, such as food, lodging and petrol, that are available at the upcoming highway exit.

title: United States - Gen 2 Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
Generation 2 coverage is rare in the US. If you have a Generation 2 location in a North American setting, you are more likely to be in Canada.
The exception to this is Alaska, and to a lesser extent Hawaii, which have a fair amount of Generation 2. You can also rarely see Generation 2 in rural areas of the Deep South.
Generation 3 coverage is also significantly less common than in Canada.

title: United States - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: In addition to having less Generation 3 coverage than Canada, the side mirrors are also blurred out differently: While they generally appear as two peaks in Canadian Gen 3 coverage, you will mostly see a single peak in the US.

title: United States - Parking Indicator Signs (Plonkit)
description: Parking indicator signs in the US are typically white metal signs with red, green, or black text. They may include specific information about when you can park on said road, and arrows indicating where parking is (or is not) allowed.

title: United States - Example (Plonkit)
description: This is an example of the most common type of orange construction barrel in the United States. They are made out of orange plastic with horizontal white stripes and a black rubber base. They are usually used to block off lanes to traffic during times of road construction.

title: United States - Style Mailbox Resting (Plonkit)
description: This style of mailbox, resting on top of a post and with a small flag on the side, is mostly associated with North America.

title: United States - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description:
North America primarily uses wooden utility poles.
Several European countries also primarily use wooden utility poles. However, a concrete pole in particular is mostly associated with Europe.
In addition, the US and Canada use transformers that are large metallic cylinders. This will never be seen in European countries.

title: United States - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: This style of insulator, which is raised slightly on top of the utility pole, can be a good clue for the US and Canada. It is not typically found in Europe. It is especially apparent on simple poles with a single insulator.

title: United States - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: The United States and Canada will usually have short license plates. Europe usually uses a long license plate which will also have a blue strip on the side.

title: United States - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: In the US and Canada, especially at large intersections, long metal bars with stop lights attached to them hang over the street. These bars also commonly have street signs, highway signs, or other signs attached to them.

title: United States - Thin Metal Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Thin metal signposts are common. They will typically either have several small holes or have a U-profile.

title: United States - North American Semi-trucks (Plonkit)
description: North American semi-trucks have a longer nose, since the engine is in front of the driver’s cab. In contrast, European and Asian semi-trucks are cabovers, meaning the driver sits on top of the engine, giving the truck an L shape.

title: United States - Here Two Common (Plonkit)
description: Here are two common types of water towers seen in towns across the United States and Canada. They are typically very tall, and sometimes have the name of the town and state painted on them, so they can be useful for region guessing.

title: United States - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
Generation 3 coverage in the US and Canada generally has no visible antenna. This can be helpful to distinguish it from Europe in low-info rounds. Some European Generation 3 coverage has no visible antenna, but most of it does.
There is an important exception: in national parks in the US, you can find a Generation 3 car with a stubby antenna with diagonal coils around it. Still, this specific type of antenna is not found in Europe.

title: United States - Both Us And (Plonkit)
description: Both the US and Canada also have Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot. When the car isn’t blurred properly, you will usually see a mirror sticking out on the right side.

title: United States - Shown Here Population (Plonkit)
description:
Shown here is the population density of the United States. In general, areas east of the Missouri river are more densely populated than areas to the west.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - License Plates (Plonkit)
description:
The US, as well as most of the Americas, uses short license plates, in contrast to longer European ones. Around half of the states also do not require front plates, which can also be useful in determining the state.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Each US state has their own unique license plate design. Some of these are recognizable through the blur, and are thus worth learning.

title: United States - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
Interstate Highways are divided highways that often span large areas of the United States. Even-numbered Interstates run west to east, with the lowest numbers along the Gulf Coast and Mexico border. Odd-numbered highways run south to north, with the lowest numbers along the West Coast.
US Highways are also typically long roads that are sometimes (but not always) divided. The numbering system is generally the inverse of Interstate Highways, with low odd-numbered highways located along the East Coast and low even-numbered highways located close to the Canadian border in the north of the country.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - Area Code Map (Plonkit)
description:
US telephone numbers start with a three-digit area code. While these area codes are not clustered by initial digits, they are useful to learn.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - Each 50 States (Plonkit)
description:
Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear sometimes, but many of the more distinct looking flags will appear more often.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description:
Shown here is a topographic map of the US.
Most significant elevation is in the west: here you will find large mountain ranges, but also more flat, high plateaus. Some parts have lower elevation: good examples are the Central Valley) and Imperial Valley in California.
Elevation in the east is generally much lower. The most significant amount of elevation is found in the Appalachians, low mountain ranges running through the eastern and northeastern US. Good examples of hills in otherwise fairly flat regions are the Driftless Area in the Midwest, and The Ozarks in Missouri and Arkansas.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - Forest Density Map (Plonkit)
description:
This is a forest density map of the contiguous United States. Eastern and Northern regions of the country typically have much denser tree cover than Western and Southwestern regions.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - Flat Agricultural Land (Plonkit)
description: The Great Plains are in the middle of the United States and stretch from the Canadian border in the North, to central Texas in the South. This area is primarily flat with few trees. Some areas feature agriculture fields, while others feature dry and barren grassy fields.

title: United States - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The Appalachian mountain range is a low mountain range that runs through the eastern states. The general landscape consists of low, forested mountains, with beech and oak trees being a common sight.

title: United States - Pine Forests (Plonkit)
description: The area stretching from the Canadian border to Northern New Mexico is home to the Rocky Mountains. These jagged, rocky formations often feature many pine trees and visible snow all year round at the highest peaks. Some areas of the Rocky Mountain Range are noticeably dry, with few trees.

title: United States - Snow-Capped Mountains (Plonkit)
description:
The Great Basin, centred around Nevada, can be recognized by the tall, sometimes snow-capped mountains in the background. There are dry, but grassy, and slightly shrubby plains leading up to the mountains.
The tallest mountains are in Nevada, Utah and California. More gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon, and greener mountains can be seen in Idaho and central Utah.
Keep in mind that there are exceptions, so make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

title: United States - Many Parts Deep (Plonkit)
description: Many parts of the Deep South, stretching from Oklahoma to South Carolina, have reddish soil. The exact tint of the soil can range from yellow to deep red.

title: United States - Lake Views (Plonkit)
description: The area spanning from the Montana Border with Saskatchewan to the Western Great Lakes features many ‘prairie potholes.’ These are areas of low-lying wetlands that feature marshy grasses and small, shallow ponds.

title: United States - Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description: The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.

title: United States - Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description: In the Appalachian area stretching from southern New York to southern Virginia, there are a lot of forest-covered rolling hills, with flat valleys dividing them. A majority of the ridges are oriented Southwest to Northeast.

title: United States - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The Lower Mississippi River Valley is a very flat and open landscape with red soil in areas of Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi, and Northeast Louisiana. Corn and other crops are common in this area.

title: United States - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The Ouachita Mountains stretch from Eastern Oklahoma into West-Central Arkansas. Unlike the nearby Ozark Mountains, these mountains are typically more steep in nature and easier to see from a distance.

title: United States - Southwest Centred Around (Plonkit)
description: The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, features many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.

title: United States - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.

title: United States - Agricultural Area (Plonkit)
description: Agricultural golden fields can commonly be seen in eastern Washington.

title: United States - Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description:
Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here.
In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.

title: United States - Just West Metropolitan (Plonkit)
description: Just west of the metropolitan areas of Austin and San Antonio Texas lies a large area of dry, rocky hills featuring many yucca and prickly pear plants. Texas Live Oak trees are the predominant tree type in this area.

title: United States - Flat Agricultural Land (Plonkit)
description: The Rio Grande Valley in South Texas is extremely flat and features shrubby trees and agricultural fields. This area borders the Mexican state of Tamaulipas.

title: United States - Corn Fields Most (Plonkit)
description: Corn fields can most commonly be found in these regions. For a detailed overview, see this map.

title: United States - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Soybeans are short, dark green crops organised in long rows and are found in similar regions where corn is grown. They are most common in the Eastern Plains, Midwest, Lower Mississippi Valley, and areas of the Mid Atlantic.

title: United States - North Features (Plonkit)
description: Along the Canadian border in North Dakota, and rarely Montana, fields filled with short yellow canola flowers (Brassica napus) can commonly be seen from the road.

title: United States - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Cotton is a crop that produces large fields of fluffy white flowers. It is most commonly produced in coastal Southeastern states, the Lower Mississippi River Valley, Western Texas, and parts of California and Arizona. You can click here for a more detailed map.

title: United States - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Rice production only occurs in a few areas of the US, so it is very useful for region guessing. It is typically grown in large, flat fields that resemble low prairies. It is only grown in north-central California and the Lower Mississippi River Valley in Arkansas, Louisiana, Texas, and Mississippi. You can click here for a more detailed map.

title: United States - Regional Buses (Plonkit)
description: The Eastern White Pine (Pinus strobus) has horizontally layered branches that gradually curve upwards at the ends, giving the tree a rather graceful appearance. They are common in New England, the northern Midwest near the Great Lakes, and the Appalachians.

title: United States - Loblolly Pine Pinus (Plonkit)
description: The loblolly pine (Pinus taeda), and longleaf pine (Pinus palustris), commonly referred to as southern pines in the community, are found throughout the southeastern US. They are a great way to recognize this region, as they are abundant, recognizable and mostly limited to this part of the country. They tend to be tall, with fluffy-looking clusters of pine needles.

title: United States - Grass Used Lawns (Plonkit)
description: Grass that is used in lawns in the southern US (colloquially known as Bermuda and St. Augustine grasses) go dormant in the winter months. This causes the lawns to turn beige or light brown in winter; whereas grasses used in more northern areas of the US stay much greener in winter.

title: United States - Regional Buses (Plonkit)
description: Great Basin Sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata) is a short, shrubby blue-green bush that is common in the interior western United States. It is most common in arid areas.

title: United States - Saguaro Cacti Most (Plonkit)
description: Saguaro cacti are most commonly shaped like tall, straight tubes with several branches extending from the main tube. They are most commonly found in southern Arizona, on the Sonoran border.

title: United States - Extremely Tall Conifer (Plonkit)
description:
Extremely tall conifer trees (Douglas firs) with a dark brown bark, and dark green leaves, can most commonly be seen in Cascadia. Notably, they can also be found in northern California, Idaho and as far east as Montana.
Beware that they are also commonly found in British Columbia.

title: United States - Desert Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Palm trees are common in coastal areas of the Southeastern states, as well as the Desert Southwest region. Shown here is the Mexican Fan Palm, which is most common in California and along the Gulf Coast, but other palm tree types have a similar range.

title: United States - Spanish Moss Appearing (Plonkit)
description: Spanish moss, appearing as greyish white drapes, can sometimes be seen on trees in the Deep South.

title: United States - Each State Has (Plonkit)
description: Each state has their own highway shield. Some states have their own unique, recognizable highway shields that can be seen here.

title: United States - Most States Have (Plonkit)
description:
Most states have unique, distinct and learnable Adopt-a-Highway signs, which can be seen on the side of roads. A map of those can be seen here. Keep in mind, some states have slight variations in design.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - Blue And Yellow (Plonkit)
description: Blue and yellow shields are used for county roads, and can be seen in certain states in the US. Keep in mind, unique designs can be found in some counties in certain states. For more information, see here.

title: United States - in US Park (Plonkit)
description:
Guardrails, signs, and signposts are commonly painted a medium brown colour in US National Parks, which are often located in the west. Guardrails that are painted brown can be made out of both wood and metal. Rock walls can also sometimes be seen in place of guardrails.
Here you can find a map showing where all US National Parks are located.

title: United States - Massachusetts Features (Plonkit)
description: These rectangular raised pavement markers are found in the south and west of the US and also in Massachusetts.

title: United States - Snowplowable Raised Pavement (Plonkit)
description: Snowplowable raised pavement markers can only be found on highways in the eastern states shown in the image. They are built into the road and somewhat resemble the letter H.

title: United States - Georgia Features (Plonkit)
description: Rectangular pavement markers each on the side of the double lines are commonly found in Georgia, Florida, Texas, and California. Other rectangular RPM states have the RPM between the double lines.

title: United States - Texas Features (Plonkit)
description: Yellow lines with a noticeably larger gap in between them are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oregon.

title: United States - Texan Roads Often (Plonkit)
description: Texan roads often have a grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface.

title: United States - Some Rural Roads (Plonkit)
description: Some rural roads in the Upper Midwest use a similar road pavement to Texas. They will have a grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface, but will vary in colour. These roads are most common in the state of Illinois.

title: United States - Yellow Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: A black stripe can sometimes be seen in between the two yellow, middle road lines in California.

title: United States - California Features (Plonkit)
description: Some small roads in California and Kentucky lack a middle yellow line; instead only feature solid white lines on each side of the road.

title: United States - Some Roads And (Plonkit)
description: Some roads and highways in the state of Kentucky use uniquely-shaped rumble strips that are thin, relatively long recessed lines on the very outside edges of the road.

title: United States - Yellow Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Some roads in West Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, and Virginia use middle yellow lines that are thicker than traditional yellow road lines.

title: United States - Bridge Features (Plonkit)
description:
Concrete paving on regular roads is much more common in Iowa than in other states.
Do not trust if it is a bridge, a highway, or it is in a city.

title: United States - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Utility poles in most of California have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes. Modoc County and Lassen County in the Northeast of the state are the main exceptions.
This design can also be found in the city of Grants Pass, Oregon.

title: United States - Metal Poles (Plonkit)
description: A rectangular white metal plate, with an orange rectangle and diamond, can be seen on most poles in Wisconsin and the Upper Peninsula of Michigan.

title: United States - Metal Poles (Plonkit)
description: PacificCorp pole markings are thick, yellow, horizontal metal plates with raised lettering or black lettering. They can be found alone or with multiple plates on one pole. They are found in Oregon, eastern Idaho, Utah, and Wyoming, and less commonly in California and Washington.

title: United States - Angled Bollards (Plonkit)
description: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.

title: United States - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
Bollards in Colorado and Wyoming often feature a dark metal post with a white circular reflector, but it is not fully on the top of the post; instead, part of the post goes above the reflector.
The top of the metal pole is sometimes painted white or grey, which is unique to Wyoming.

title: United States - Angled Bollards (Plonkit)
description: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.

title: United States - Angled Bollards (Plonkit)
description: A bollard consisting of a white square reflector on top of a black rectangle reflector is unique to Utah.

title: United States - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a white diamond reflector on top.
Montana tends to have 1 bolt on the reflector, while South Dakota tends to have 2.

title: United States - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: The most common type of bollard in Oregon has a very long rectangular reflector on top.

title: United States - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Black colored bollards with a paddle shaped body are common in Utah and Wyoming, and can also be found in Nebraska.

title: United States - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Bollards with 3 circular reflectors attached to it are common in New Mexico.

title: United States - Striped Bollards (Plonkit)
description: These simple white bollards with black reflectors are unique to Wisconsin.

title: United States - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description:
Bollards where the reflector is shaped like a square are common in Utah, Arizona, and Idaho.
The Utah variant usually has 2 bolts, the Arizona variant usually has one bolt, and Idaho can have both 2 bolts and one bolt.

title: United States - ends of Bridge (Plonkit)
description: Maine, New Hampshire, and Massachusetts use small green and red rectangular signs to mark the ends of bridges and guardrails.

title: United States - placed before Bridge (Plonkit)
description: In Minnesota, these yellow signs with vertical, black triangles are placed before bridges at most major river crossings and at the beginnings and ends of guardrail sections on large highways.

title: United States - Wisconsin And Missouri (Plonkit)
description: Wisconsin and Missouri are the only two states that use a lettering system (A - ZZZ) for their county highways. Wisconsin signs typically have the word ‘county’ above the letter, while Missouri signs typically do not. The borders of the signs also vary slightly.

title: United States - Oregon Features (Plonkit)
description: Speed signs in Oregon often simply have the word ‘Speed’ instead of the standard ‘Speed Limit’.

title: United States - Texas Features (Plonkit)
description: Yellow or red bands can commonly be seen around signposts in Texas.

title: United States - Horizontal Blue Red (Plonkit)
description: A horizontal blue, red, or green sign can commonly be seen at the ends of driveways in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula. The house number is present, in addition to either the town name and or the road name (usually).

title: United States - Michigan Features (Plonkit)
description: Signs attached to two signposts can be seen in Michigan, Ohio, Minnesota, and New York. Not all signs are attached to two signposts.

title: United States - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: West Virginia sometimes features street signs with a symbol that resembles a fraction inside a circle.

title: United States - Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: North Carolina commonly uses a style of street signs showing street numbers and arrows in addition to the street name.

title: United States - Oklahoma Often Find (Plonkit)
description: In Oklahoma, you can often find a green rectangular sign with 3 rows of numbers attached to the back of stop signs at rural intersections.

title: United States - Green Atv Route (Plonkit)
description: These green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.

title: United States - Pennsylvania Features (Plonkit)
description: Rectangular white signs can sometimes be seen attached to signposts at intersections in Pennsylvania. On top, the number of the converging state route is written.

title: United States - Virginia Features (Plonkit)
description: Rectangular white signs can sometimes be seen at intersections in Virginia.

title: United States - North Features (Plonkit)
description: White signs attached to signposts can commonly be seen in North Carolina.

title: United States - White Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Black street signs with white text can commonly be found at intersections in South Carolina.

title: United States - New York And (Plonkit)
description:
New York and Vermont have small rectangular green signs with three rows of horizontal numbers. The top row of numbers correlates to the highway or road number the sign is on. For example, the sign in the image is on road NY-345.
Signs for Vermont will almost always start with 0 on the second row. The second row in New York will start with a number which corresponds to a district of the NYSDOT (link) which will help with narrowing a region.

title: United States - E2 Road Features (Plonkit)
description: In New Hampshire there will often be a white metal sign with the characters ‘E-2’ on it adjacent to the road, typically at either end of bridges.

title: United States - Minnesota Features (Plonkit)
description: On some rural ‘stop’ signposts in Minnesota, a black-and-white marker is attached to the posts horizontally. The shape may vary slightly.

title: United States - White Reflectors Signposts (Plonkit)
description: These white reflectors on signposts are unique to Kansas. They are most commonly seen on ‘stop’ signs in rural areas.

title: United States - Rural Areas Connecticut (Plonkit)
description: In rural areas of Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire, short rock walls are commonly visible adjacent to the road.

title: United States - Oil Pumpjacks Short (Plonkit)
description: Oil pumpjacks are short, industrial-looking metal structures located at the surface of oil fields and are used to pump crude oil from the earth below. They are most common in western states, particularly in Texas, Eastern New Mexico, and North Dakota.

title: United States - Road Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Square guardrails are the most dominant (but not the only) type of guardrail in the states of New York and Wyoming. They have a long bar across the top, with several square legs supporting them.

title: United States - Utah Features (Plonkit)
description: Streets in Utah and Idaho, particularly in urban areas, are often named by using a combination of a number and cardinal direction (i.e. ‘600 South.’)

title: United States - Dark-coloured Wooden Fences (Plonkit)
description: Dark-coloured wooden fences with several horizontal wooden supports are common in farming areas of central and southern Appalachia, stretching from Pennsylvania to Georgia.

title: United States - Michigan Features (Plonkit)
description: Many large intersections in Michigan have stop lights and signs that hang from wires that stretch across the middle of the intersection. These markers are commonly in yellow boxes.

title: United States - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Stilt houses can sometimes be seen on the coast. These are especially common toward the south, and on the Atlantic and Gulf coasts.

title: United States - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Similar in style to aforementioned stilt houses, houses with much shorter stilts are common in the western and central Gulf Coast. These houses typically feature short stilts made of concrete or wood (1-3 feet off the ground) and are primarily found in areas near the coast and any adjacent rivers.

title: United States - Buildings With Very (Plonkit)
description: Buildings with very large, sloped roofs are most common in the states of Oklahoma, Texas, and Louisiana. They can also be seen in neighbouring states to a lesser extent.

title: United States - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
Houses in coastal New England often feature shingle walls, which are layered wood panels overlapping each other.
A similar style of panelling can also be seen, however, having a wider range than the one shown above.

title: United States - New Features (Plonkit)
description: Older three storey wooden houses, also called ‘stacked triplexes),’ are very common in urban areas of the Northeast. They are most prevalent in New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts.

title: United States - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Brownstone buildings are typically row houses or government buildings made out of various types of brick and sandstone. They are most commonly found in dense urban areas of the Northeast US, as well as Chicago.

title: United States - Buildings With Red (Plonkit)
description: Buildings with red metal rooftops are most commonly found in the Mid-South and Southern Appalachia states of Virginia, West Virginia, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas, and North Carolina.

title: United States - New Features (Plonkit)
description: Very narrow, one-storey houses made out of wood are called ‘shotgun houses.’ They are most common in and around New Orleans (LA,) Houston (TX,) Louisville (KY,) and the state of Mississippi.

title: United States - Pueblo Revival Style (Plonkit)
description: Pueblo Revival style houses are commonly seen in New Mexico. They are typically constructed of adobe or brick and concrete. They have rounded edges and flat roofs, and are usually sand-brown in colour.

title: United States - Desert Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Spanish Colonial Revival Architecture can be categorised as buildings with lightly-coloured stucco walls and red clay-tile roofs. They can be found in the desert southwest states of California, Nevada, Arizona, and Texas. You can also find similar types of buildings in Florida and coastal Georgia.

title: United States - Houses And Commercial (Plonkit)
description: Houses and commercial buildings in the interior Western US are often made of lots of dark wooden boards and timbers. Buildings at high elevations also commonly have metal roofs, to avoid snow build-up.

title: United States - Alaska Features (Plonkit)
description:
Alaska is the largest state and the north-, west-, and easternmost state in the US.
A separate Plonk It guide to Alaska can be found here.

title: United States - Hawaii Features (Plonkit)
description:
Hawaii is the youngest state in the US and the only US state outside of North America.
A separate Plonk It guide to Hawaii can be found here.

title: United States - Rico Features (Plonkit)
description:
Puerto Rico is a Caribbean US territory with official Commonwealth status.
A separate Plonk It guide to Puerto Rico can be found here.

title: United States - Samoa Features (Plonkit)
description:
American Samoa is a South Pacific island group and an unorganised US territory.
A separate Plonk It guide to American Samoa can be found here.

title: United States - Micronesia Features (Plonkit)
description:
Guam is an unincorporated territory of the US and the largest island in Micronesia.
A separate Plonk It guide to Guam can be found here.

title: United States - Islands Features (Plonkit)
description:
Northern Mariana Islands is a Northwest Pacific island chain and a Commonwealth US territory.
A separate Plonk It guide to Northern Mariana Islands can be found here.

title: United States - Left-Hand Traffic (Plonkit)
description:
The United States Virgin Islands is a Caribbean US territory and the only area of the US that drives on the left side of the road.
A separate Plonk It guide to the United States Virgin Islands can be found here.

title: United States - Us Minor Outlying (Plonkit)
description:
The US Minor Outlying Islands is a collective name for several small island US territories, with the Midway Atoll being the most relevant in Geoguessr.
A separate Plonk It guide to the US Minor Outlying Islands can be found here.

title: United States - Deep South Florida (Plonkit)
description: Deep South Florida, between the metropolitan areas of Ft. Myers and Miami, features dense, jungle-like forests that have few inhabitants. Roads through these areas are commonly very straight and long.

title: United States - Florida Keys Archipelago (Plonkit)
description:
The Florida Keys are an archipelago of tropical islands west of Miami. The highway connecting the islands can be recognized by green, tropical vegetation on the sides of the usually single lane road. The soil is also sandy white.
Urban locations are also similar, but with many more planted palm trees and mowed grass being a common sight.

title: United States - Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description: The area between the cities of Orlando and Lakeland in Florida sometimes feature low, rolling hills. Lakes and agricultural fields are also common in this area. This is the only main hilly area in central or southern Florida.

title: United States - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Southwestern Oklahoma features a small area of rocky, shrubby peaks. Some of the mountains are also covered in trees, and the rocks can have a pinkish red tint to them.

title: United States - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: Central Colorado is home to a large North-to-South oriented mountain ridge. This divides the Rocky Mountains to the west and the Great Plains to the east.These mountains are adjacent to the major metropolitan areas of Boulder, Denver, and Colorado Springs.

title: United States - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Along the New Mexico and or Texas border there is a ridge of tall, dry peaks known as the Guadalupe Mountains. In adjacent areas of both states, smaller foothills of these mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.

title: United States - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The Black Hills, located in far Western South Dakota and far Eastern Wyoming, are a series of moderately tall mountains with large amounts of conifer trees and rocky outcroppings. The surrounding areas are typically much flatter with lesser tree cover.

title: United States - As Part Promotional (Plonkit)
description:
As part of a promotional campaign, the TransAmerica Trail from Oregon to North Carolina was covered by a Ford Bronco. The car can be recognised by its unblurred black roof and red hood, and is mostly found on unpaved rural roads.
Looking backwards, you will see two other Ford SUVs escorting the camera car.

title: United States - Arizona Features (Plonkit)
description: Interstate 19 in Arizona from Tucson to the Mexico border uses kilometres on the exit and distance signs. This is the only part of the country that uses kilometres instead of miles for highway signs.

title: United States - Many Bridge (Plonkit)
description: Many bridges are used to connect the various neighbourhoods of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. These expansive, steel bridges are commonly painted bright yellow. Additionally, Pittsburgh is easy to identify because of it being flanked by 3 rivers and steep bluffs on all sides.

title: United States - Local Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Row Houses and other buildings in San Francisco are often in the style of Victorian architecture, with many bay windows, turrets, and ornate exterior details. These homes are built close together and can be very colourful.

title: United States - Neighbourhoods All Around (Plonkit)
description:
Neighbourhoods all around the city of New Orleans feature many colourful, historic, shotgun-style houses.
Buildings in central areas of New Orleans often feature colourful facades with second storey wrap-around balconies.

title: United States - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Historical areas of Miami and Miami beach are home to many historical, multi-storey art deco buildings. These buildings are commonly painted in bright colours and are located near the coast.

title: United States - Dry Tortugas Park (Plonkit)
description:
The main island of Dry Tortugas National Park, west of Key West, can be identified by the hexagonal brick structure and the surrounding moat.
The Loggerhead Lighthouse, situated on the Loggerhead Key, has a brown top-half and a white bottom. The path on which the trekker walks on is also made of bright concrete, and many palm trees can be seen around the lighthouse.

title: United States - Desert Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Big Bend National Park is located along the Mexico border in Southwest Texas. It can be identified by its dry, rocky peaks and shrubby foliage. This park is adjacent to the Chihauhan desert, so plants such as yucca and prickly pear cactus are common.

title: United States - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Death Valley National Park can be easily recognized by the dry, sandy, treeless mountains that can be seen from the roads that go through the park. In Generation 3 coverage, the sky can look particularly dusty.

title: United States - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Along the Canadian border in Montana lies Glacier National Park. It is easily recognizable by its extremely tall and steep mountain peaks. Most coverage is also hazy and taken during summer.

title: United States - Badlands Park (Plonkit)
description: Badlands National Park features these distinct, sand-brown, eroded rock formations. The formations may sometimes appear more rounded, and lighter in colour.

title: United States - Fall Colors (Plonkit)
description: Theodore Roosevelt National Park features similar, sand-brown, eroded rock formations to Badlands National Park. The rock formations in this park tend to have more trees on them. Additionally, almost all coverage has fall colours visible.

title: United States - Tall Mountains (Plonkit)
description: In far Northeastern Wyoming lies Devil’s Tower, which is a very tall, standalone butte protruding from the surrounding land. This can sometimes be seen from many miles away because of the lack of nearby mountains.

title: United States - Pictured Here Group (Plonkit)
description: Pictured here is a group of gas stations and convenience store chains that operate in the United States, but not in Canada. This is not a comprehensive list, but some of the most common American-only chains.

title: United States - Pictured Here Group (Plonkit)
description: Pictured here is a group of restaurant chains that operate in the United States, but not in Canada (Chick-fil-A is the only exception with a few locations in the Toronto area). This is not a comprehensive list, but some of the most common American-only chains.

title: United States - Shoprite Regional Supermarket (Plonkit)
description: ‘Shoprite’ is a regional supermarket chain that has locations in 6 states in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic region of the US; Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, and Maryland.

title: United States - Hy-vee Supermarket (Plonkit)
description: ‘Hy-Vee’ is a supermarket that is common primarily in the Upper Midwest states of Iowa, Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Illinois.

title: United States - Supermarket Chain Piggly (Plonkit)
description: The supermarket chain ‘Piggly Wiggly’ is found mostly in the Southeast, as well as the state of Wisconsin.

title: United States - H-e-b Supermarket (Plonkit)
description: ‘H-E-B’ is a supermarket that is only located in the state of Texas. Most H-E-B stores are in large cities.

title: United States - Florida Features (Plonkit)
description: ‘Publix’ is a regional supermarket chain that has locations primarily in Florida and adjacent areas of the Deep South.

title: United States - Restaurant Chain Waffle (Plonkit)
description: The restaurant chain ‘Waffle House’ is a regional chain that is primarily found in the Southern and Southeast US. Some Midwest and Mid-Atlantic states have some locations. Georgia, by far, is the state with the most Waffle House locations.

title: United States - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: ‘Carl’s Jr.’ and ‘Hardee’s’ are fast food restaurants that are operated by the same company and have a similar logo and colour scheme. However, Carl’s Jr. locations are all located on the West Coast and Southwest US, while Hardee’s are found in the central and Eastern areas of the country. Two states, Wyoming and Oklahoma, have both kinds of restaurants present.

title: United States - Zaxbys Fast-food Chicken (Plonkit)
description: ‘Zaxby’s,’ a fast-food chicken chain, is another restaurant that is most common in the Southeast US. There are several pockets outside the Southeast that have locations, such as Utah and Montana. Like Waffle House, Georgia has the highest number of locations.

title: United States - Whataburger Hamburger Restaurant (Plonkit)
description: ‘Whataburger’ is a hamburger restaurant with locations across the South Central US. The State that is home to the most locations, by far, is Texas.

title: United States - Pizza Ranch Restaurant (Plonkit)
description: ‘Pizza Ranch’ is a restaurant chain that is found in the middle of the country. Iowa and Minnesota have the highest number of locations.

title: United States - Tim Hortons Known (Plonkit)
description: ‘Tim Hortons’ is known for being the most popular restaurant chain in Canada. However, there are also many locations in the United States. They are primarily located in states adjacent to the Canadian provinces of Ontario and Québec, with a few locations also in Texas and Georgia.

title: United States - California Features (Plonkit)
description: ‘In-N-Out Burger’ is a regional fast food chain located primarily in the Southwest US. Around two thirds of all locations are located in California.

title: United States - Wawa Regional Gas (Plonkit)
description: ‘WaWa’ is a regional gas station and convenience store chain with locations in the Mid-Atlantic states and Florida. New Jersey and the Philadelphia, Pennsylvania area have the highest density of locations.

title: United States - Another Regional Gas (Plonkit)
description: Another regional gas station and convenience store chain in the Eastern US is called ‘Sheetz’. Most of their locations are in the Mid-Atlantic and Central Appalachian areas of the US. Pennsylvania has the highest number of locations.

title: United States - Kwik Trip Chain (Plonkit)
description: ‘Kwik Trip’ is a chain of gas stations and convenience stores that are located in the Upper Midwest states of Wisconsin and Minnesota. In Iowa, these stores are called ‘Kwik Star’ and have similar branding. Some stores may also have the name ‘Stop-N-Go’.

title: United States - Kum Go Regional (Plonkit)
description: ‘Kum & Go’ is a regional gas station chain based out of the state of Iowa. They also have pockets of locations in the Ozarks, Colorado, Wyoming, and North Dakota.

title: United States - Caseys Popular Gas (Plonkit)
description: ‘Casey’s’ is a popular gas station and convenience store chain that is found in the Midwest, Plains, and parts of the Mid-South. Illinois, Iowa, and Missouri have the highest number of locations.

title: United States - Buc-ees Small Chain (Plonkit)
description: ‘Buc-ee’s’ is a small chain of oversized gas stations located primarily in the state of Texas. These stores feature multiple rows of gas pumps, and a very large convenience store building.

title: United States - Us Uses Phrase (Plonkit)
description:
The US uses the phrase ‘Speed Limit’ on their speed signs.

The numbers on American speed signs are usually lower than that of Canada’s, since they use miles instead of kilometres. In addition, speed limits ending in 5 are more common in the US.

title: United States - American Yield Signs (Plonkit)
description: American yield signs are shaped like an upside down triangle with a red border, with a white field with the word ‘YIELD’.

title: United States - Interstate Highways Us (Plonkit)
description: Interstate highways, US highways, and some state roads have rumble strips in each edge of the road; which are small indentations in the pavement perpendicular to the road. These can be located on the outside edges of the road and in between lanes on multi-lane highways.

title: United States - Pictured Here Group (Plonkit)
description:
Pictured here is a group of gas stations and convenience store chains that operate in the United States, but not in Canada. This is not a comprehensive list, but some of the most common American-only chains. Regional gas station chains are found near the end of the ‘Step 2’ section of this guide.

You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - Pictured Here Group (Plonkit)
description:
Pictured here is a group of restaurant chains that operate in the United States, but not in Canada (Chick Fil A is the only exception with a few locations in the Toronto area.) This is not a comprehensive list, but some of the most common American-only chains. Regional restaurant chains are found at the end of the ‘Step 2’ section of this guide.

You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - Thin Metal Sign (Plonkit)
description: Thin metal sign posts are common. They will typically either have several small holes or have a U-profile.

title: United States - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description:
North America primarily uses wooden utility poles.

Several European countries also primarily use wooden utility poles. However, a concrete pole in particular is mostly associated with Europe.

title: United States - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: This style of insulator, that is raised slightly on top of the utility pole, can be a good clue for the US and Canada. It is not typically found in Europe. It is especially apparent on simple poles with a single insulator.

title: United States - License Plates (Plonkit)
description:
The US, as well as most of the Americas, uses short licence plates, in contrast to longer European ones. Each US state has their own unique licence plate design. Some of these are recognizable through the blur, and are thus worth learning. Around half of the states also do not require front plates, which can also be useful in determining the state.

You can click on the image to enlarge it. Here you can also find a map showing the locations of each plate.

title: United States - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
Interstate Highways are divided highways that often span large areas of the United States. Even-numbered Interstates run west to east, with the lowest numbers along the Gulf Coast and Mexico border. Odd-numbered highways run south to north, with the lowest numbers along the West Coast.

US Highways are also typically long roads that are sometimes (but not always) divided. The numbering system is generally the inverse of Interstate Highways, with low odd-numbered highways located along the East Coast and low even-numbered highways located close to the Canadian border in the north of the country.

title: United States - Each 50 States (Plonkit)
description:
Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: United States - Valley Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Cotton is a crop that produces large fields of fluffy white flowers. It is most commonly produced in coastal Southeast States, the Lower Mississippi River Valley, Western Texas, and parts of California and Arizona. You can click here for a more detailed map.

title: United States - Southwest Centred Around (Plonkit)
description: The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.

title: United States - Maximum Speed Limits (Plonkit)
description:
Maximum speed limits vary by state and territory. The maximum speed limits shown here will generally be seen on interstate highways. Some interstates and highways in their respective states or territories will have lower maximum speed limits than what is shown.

You can click on the image to enlarge it. Here is a map of the maximum speed limits on US territories.

title: United States - Iowa Features (Plonkit)
description: Concrete paving on main highways is much more common in Iowa than in other states.

title: United States - Yellow Lines With (Plonkit)
description: Yellow lines with a noticeably larger gap in between them are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oregon. They can also be found to a lesser extent in Washington, Alabama, and Michigan.

title: United States - Yellow Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Some roads in West Virginia, Virginia, and Maryland use middle yellow lines that are thicker than traditional yellow road lines.

title: United States - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Utility poles in California usually have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes.

title: United States - California Features (Plonkit)
description: Some small roads in California lack a middle yellow line; instead only feature solid white lines on each side of the road.

title: United States - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.

title: United States - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Roadside bollards in Wyoming often feature a dark metal pole with a white circular reflector at the top. The top of the metal pole is sometimes painted white or grey, which is unique to Wyoming.

title: United States - Minnesota Features (Plonkit)
description: On most rural ‘stop’ signposts in Minnesota, a black-and-white marker is attached to the posts horizontally. The shape may vary slightly.

title: United States - Michigan Features (Plonkit)
description: Signs attached to two signposts can be seen in Michigan. Not all signs are attached to two signposts.

title: United States - Properties Rural And (Plonkit)
description: Properties in rural and exurban Ohio, Lower Michigan, and Indiana commonly feature a vertically-oriented metal sign with white numbers, indicating the house number of the adjacent building. These signs are most commonly blue or green, and are commonly attached to mailboxes.

title: United States - Vermont Features Small (Plonkit)
description:
Vermont features small rectangular green signs on stop sign posts with three rows of horizontal numbers. The top row of numbers correlates to the highway or road number that the road with the stop sign intersects with. For example, this image is taken from Vermont State Road 116, looking towards the intersecting road.

The State of New York uses similar style signs. However, these signs can be attached to different types of sign posts (town entry signs, highway signs, etc.)

title: United States - New Features (Plonkit)
description: Older three story wooden houses, also called ‘stacked triplexes,’ are very common in urban areas of the Northeast. They are most prevalent in New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts.

title: United States - In-n-out Burger Regional (Plonkit)
description: ‘In-N-Out Burger’ is a regional fast food chain located primarily in the Southwest US. California has the most locations.

title: United States - As Part Promotional (Plonkit)
description:
As part of a promotional campaign, the TransAmerica Trail from Oregon to North Carolina was covered by a Ford Bronco. The car can recognised by its unblurred black roof and red hood, and is mostly found on unpaved rural roads.

Looking backwards, you will see two other Ford SUVs escorting the camera car.

title: United States - Neighbourhoods All Around (Plonkit)
description:
Neighbourhoods all around the city of New Orleans feature many colourful, historic, shotgun-style houses.

Buildings in central areas of New Orleans often feature colourful facades with second story wrap-around balconies.

title: United States - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Historical areas of Miami and Miami beach are home to many historical, multi-story art deco buildings. These buildings are commonly painted in bright colours and are located near the coast.

title: American Samoa - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: American Samoa is a group of islands east of Fiji, located in the Pacific Ocean. Since it is a US overseas territory, for country streak purposes, it is counted as the US.

title: American Samoa - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The general landscape consists of green, tropical mountains with many palm trees. Small roads are often made of concrete. Most houses are one storey, and have a simple box design. Plain metal sheet roofs are also very common.

title: American Samoa - Slightly Rusted Black (Plonkit)
description:
A slightly rusted black truck bed can be seen on the main island of Tutuila.
This is the most common car that will be seen as it has the most coverage.

title: American Samoa - Bridge Features (Plonkit)
description:
The front of a silver-grey truck with side mirrors can be seen on Manu’a and Olosega, which are connected by a bridge.
See below for more information.

title: American Samoa - Front Similar Truck (Plonkit)
description: The front of a similar truck can be seen on the easternmost covered island of Tau. However, the truck will be glossy black, with side mirrors visible.

title: American Samoa - lane Bridge (Plonkit)
description: The single-lane bridge, connecting the islands of Manu’a and Olosega, can be easily recognized by the thin wire guardrail, with the two islands on either side of the bridge.

title: American Samoa - Airport Features (Plonkit)
description: Ofu Airport is small with a concrete runway. The Google Car covering it has two orange straps on the roof. Many palm trees can also be seen on the other side of the runway.

title: Australia - Eucalyptus Trees (Plonkit)
description: Gum trees (eucalyptus) are by far the most common type of tree in Australia. Their bark is typically light-coloured, with puffy puffy clusters of leaves.

title: Australia - Australian Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Australian bollards are white, with a red reflector on the front, and a grey reflector on the back.

title: Australia - Left-Hand Traffic (Plonkit)
description: Australia drives on the left.

title: Australia - White Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Australia uses almost exclusively white road lines, with a few rare exceptions in alpine regions such as Mount Kosciuszko and Mount Hotham.

title: Australia - White Road Lines (Plonkit)
description:
Outside lines in Australia sometimes feature rumble strips that look like small white stripes perpendicular to the road line.
In addition, you can find similar rumble strips in New Zealand.

title: Australia - Give Way Signs (Plonkit)
description: Give-way signs in Australia have a white border and black text.

title: Australia - Chevron Colors (Plonkit)
description: Australia uses white on black and black on yellow chevrons.

title: Australia - Distance Signs (Plonkit)
description: Green signs with white arrows on either side can be seen at intersections which show nearby towns or cities. A number indicating the number of kilometres away the town can sometimes be seen.

title: Australia - Speed Limit Signs (Plonkit)
description: Australian speed limit signs have black text in a red circle on a large white rectangle.

title: Australia - Gen 3 Antenna (Plonkit)
description: A long antenna can be seen in Generation 3 coverage.

title: Australia - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Different states use different licence plate designs, which can be somewhat visible through the blur.

title: Australia - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description: Australian phone numbers are 8 digits with a 2-digit area code in front. A map of these by state can be seen here. Keep in mind, not all phone numbers will include an area code in front of it.

title: Australia - Bus Stop Designs (Plonkit)
description:
Each state has a unique bus stop design. These are quite common in urban rounds, so are worth learning. Darwin bus stops are usually concrete shelters.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Australia - Nullarbor Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
The area around Warramboo in SA to Madura in WA has a unique landscape. Vegetation is quite dry and is made up of shrubs and wide crowned eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a slight orange tint.
The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has a similar landscape, with the same vegetation but usually with whiter soil.

title: Australia - Lush Green Fields (Plonkit)
description: Lush green or golden fields can be found in this band from the south of the Yorke Peninsula to Echuca. In the SA side, the landscape should be drier than the Victorian side and more wide crowned eucalyptus can be seen. On the Victorian side, the trees generally have more leaves and are taller.

title: Australia - Tropical North Queensland (Plonkit)
description: Coastal northern Queensland is very tropical. Typical vegetation consists of palm trees and dark green vegetation.

title: Australia - Inland NSW Landscape (Plonkit)
