description: The landscape in inland NSW is mostly flat, and the soil gets redder the more inland you go. Vegetation consists of mostly dry pale-green shrubs. Further east and on the Queensland and Victorian borders, the climate gets more temperate but is still quite dry and more eucalyptus trees can be seen, with the soil transitioning into a more sandy colour as well as more hills being visible.

title: Australia - Darwin Vegetation (Plonkit)
description: The vegetation in the area surrounding Darwin is extremely distinct. It features dark red soil, as well as rich green grass and trees. The tree trunks are typically black.

title: Australia - Tasmania Rolling Hills (Plonkit)
description: Tasmania has a cool temperate climate which is uncommon in the rest of Australia and is comparable to central-southern Chile or New Zealand. Typical landscape consists of green rolling hills that can look dry in winter coverage. Eucalyptus trees can be seen on the side of roads and on hills in the distance. Rural Tasmania is also quite hilly with dense eucalyptus forests making up the landscape.

title: Australia - Termite Mounds (Plonkit)
description: Termite mounds can sometimes be seen in the Northern Territory and rarely northern WA and QLD. They appear as brown, spiky formations rising out of the ground.

title: Australia - WA Brush Plants (Plonkit)
description: These brush plants are commonly seen in Western Australia.

title: Australia - Sugarcane Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Sugarcane plantations are very common in Northern Queensland, due to its tropical climate.

title: Australia - Stobie Poles (Plonkit)
description: The iconic Stobie pole, made of steel and concrete, is specific to South Australia. The pole tops (trident or rotated letter “E”) are also unique.

title: Australia - Northern Territory Poles (Plonkit)
description: These rusty metal poles, containing several holes, are unique to the Northern Territory.

title: Australia - Victorian Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: According to a 2006 review, 64% of all concrete poles are located in the state of Victoria.

title: Australia - Painted Poles (Plonkit)
description:
A trident-like pole top can sometimes be seen in Western Australia and Victoria. In Western Australia, the pole will often have red insulators and black paint on the crossbar (shown in the image).
For the meta to work, all 3 insulators must be connected to the crossbar. This link shows a similar looking pole that is incorrect, as the middle insulator is connected to the pole itself rather than to the crossbar.

title: Australia - Queensland Angled Coils (Plonkit)
description: Queensland features these unique pole tops with coils that are angled upwards on the sides.

title: Australia - Victorian Pole Tops (Plonkit)
description: Victorian pole tops feature 3 circular coils; 2 on the sides, and 1 vertical one at the top. At times, other extensions can be seen on these poles.

title: Australia - Tasmanian Pole Tops (Plonkit)
description: Poletops in Tasmania often consist of a thin metal crossbar bent 90 degrees to form an L-shape.

title: Australia - Queensland Blue Stickers (Plonkit)
description: Circular blue stickers can be found on Queensland poles. You may occasionally see the same type of sticker in a different colour, or with the colour almost completely faded.

title: Australia - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: These black markings are specific to electricity poles in the region encompassing the cities of Gold Coast, Brisbane, and Sunshine Coast in Queensland. They are often accompanied by diagonal numbers.

title: Australia - Tasmania Possum Guards (Plonkit)
description: Olive-green possum guards are only found on electricity poles in Tasmania.

title: Australia - WA Painted Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles in Western Australia often have green painted bases, and sometimes a white sticker or a red and white band attached.

title: Australia - Short Reflectors (Plonkit)
description: Reflectors that are shorter in height than the regular ones are most common in Queensland and South Australia.

title: Australia - WA Brown Base Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Bollards with brown paint at the bottom are most commonly found in Western Australia.

title: Australia - Striped Bollards (Plonkit)
description: These black-and-white stripy bollards are unique to Western Australia.

title: Australia - Queensland Black Yellow Bollard (Plonkit)
description: This black-and-yellow bollard is exclusive to Queensland.

title: Australia - WA Yellow Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Yellow signposts are specific to Western Australia.

title: Australia - Flat Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Some signposts in South Australia and Western Australia are flat rather than round.

title: Australia - NT Yellow Stickers (Plonkit)
description: Signposts in the Northern Territory can feature these yellow stickers.

title: Australia - Fluorescent Sign Border (Plonkit)
description: Road signs with a fluorescent border are almost exclusively found in Queensland.

title: Australia - NSW No Stopping (Plonkit)
description: New South Wales is the only state to use red ‘No Stopping’ signs.

title: Australia - ACT Parking Signs (Plonkit)
description: The white ‘No Stopping’ and ‘No Parking’ signs that include text are unique to the Australian Capital Territory.

title: Australia - Tasmania Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: White directional signs can only be found in Tasmania.

title: Australia - C Roads (Plonkit)
description: Roads that start with the letter ‘C’ are only found in Victoria and Tasmania. In addition, South Australia has some C roads near the border with Victoria.

title: Australia - NT Speed Limit (Plonkit)
description: Within Australia, a speed limit of 130 km/h can only be found in the Northern Territory.

title: Australia - Thin Keep Left Sign (Plonkit)
description: Some ‘Keep Left’ signs in New South Wales, Queensland, and the Northern Territory use this thinner version, which does not include an arrow.

title: Australia - Traffic Light Borders (Plonkit)
description: Traffic lights with a white outline around the frame are found in the eastern and western states of WA, QLD, NSW, ACT and Tas. Traffic lights without a border are found in the remaining, central states.

title: Australia - WA Property Markers (Plonkit)
description: You can find these dark green property markers on the sides of roads in Western Australia.

title: Australia - SA Property Markers (Plonkit)
description: You can find these white property markers on the sides of roads in South Australia.

title: Australia - NSW Guardrail Ending (Plonkit)
description: This guardrail ending, featuring a black dash on a yellow background, is almost exclusive to New South Wales and the ACT.

title: Australia - Victorian Hydrant Poles (Plonkit)
description: You can find these white hydrant poles that feature a blue circle and a red section on top of it in Victoria.

title: Australia - Victorian Fire Hydrants (Plonkit)
description: These fire hydrants with red painted tops are unique to Victoria.

title: Australia - No Gen 2 in NT (Plonkit)
description: Generation 2 cannot be found in the Northern Territory.

title: Australia - Capital City Features (Plonkit)
description:
Australia is home to dozens of rare Google cars, which can usually be found in natural reserves.
Most rare Google cars with snorkels are located in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory. The snorkels are dark grey or black extensions to the side of the car, to keep the engine dry when submerged in water.
GeoHints has a complete overview of all rare cars, which can be found on this page.

title: Australia - Island Territories (Plonkit)
description:
For country streak purposes, Christmas Island and Cocos (Keeling) Islands are counted as part of Australia. For example, clicking Australia on Christmas Island counts as a country streak.
These islands have unique cars which makes them easily identifiable.
Plonk It has a more in-depth guide to Christmas Island here.
Plonk It has a more in-depth guide to Cocos (Keeling) Islands here.

title: Australia - Tom Price Gen 2 (Plonkit)
description: The area around Tom Price can be recognized by its red soil, Generation 2 camera and rocky hills.

title: Australia - Alice Springs Rocks (Plonkit)
description: Alice Springs, an isolated town in the southern part of the Northern Territory, features distinct orange rocks that can be seen in the distance or at the end of roads.

title: Australia - Cairns Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The northern QLD city of Cairns is distinct due to its tropical vegetation and big green mountains around the city.

title: Australia - Flat Agricultural Land (Plonkit)
description: The Grampians are isolated hills that are viewable from afar within the otherwise flat western Victorian agricultural landscape.

title: Australia - Mount Gambier Pines (Plonkit)
description: The area around Mount Gambier, SA features white soil and extensive pine tree plantations, making it recognisable.

title: Australia - Kangaroo Island Gen 2 (Plonkit)
description:
Kangaroo Island in South Australia tends to have a distinct look. The vegetation mostly consists of bushes and low, stubby eucalyptus trees with puffy clusters of leaves. The orange soil colour is reminiscent of Western Australia.
In addition, the island only has Generation 2 and Generation 4 coverage.

title: Australia - Mountain Terrain (Plonkit)
description: The Stirling Ranges are a small mountain range in Western Australia that tower over a largely flat plain, such that they can be viewed from a distance.

title: Australia - Nullarbor Highway (Plonkit)
description: The Nullarbor Highway (Latin for “no tree”) can be easily recognized thanks to the flatness, overall grey look and very low vegetation.

title: Australia - Barkly Highway Wire (Plonkit)
description: On most of the Northern Territory section of the Barkly Highway and a small part of the Queensland section, a wire can be seen on the left side of the car.

title: Australia - Dorat Road (Plonkit)
description: Dorat Road (23) in the Northern Territory can be easily recognized thanks to its distinct Darwin area landscape and lack of road lines.

title: Australia - Sturt Highway Lines (Plonkit)
description: The Sturt Highway from Wentworth to Wagga Wagga can have triple broken centre lines.

title: Australia - Stuart Highway Pimba (Plonkit)
description: The Stuart Highway from Alice Springs to around Pimba, SA can be easily recognized by its bright orange dirt, short trees and blue car Generation 4.

title: Australia - Melbourne Pole Stickers (Plonkit)
description: Melbourne poles commonly feature these white, rectangular stickers, with a smaller blue square inside it.

title: Australia - Mount Kosciuszko Yellow Lines (Plonkit)
description:
All-yellow road lines can be seen on roads around Mount Kosciuszko.
In addition, a unique white truck with a snorkel, and cab guard can be found.

title: Australia - Broken Hill Stobie Poles (Plonkit)
description: South Australian style Stobie poles can sometimes be found in the NSW town of Broken Hill.

title: Australia - Brisbane Street Sign (Plonkit)
description: This street sign is unique to Brisbane City Council.

title: Australia - Gold Coast Street Sign (Plonkit)
description: This street sign is unique to Gold Coast City Council.

title: Australia - Sydney Street Sign (Plonkit)
description: This street sign is unique to the City of Sydney.

title: Australia - Rumble Strips (Plonkit)
description: Outside lines in Australia sometimes feature rumble strips that look like small white stripes perpendicular to the road line.

title: Australia - Bus Stop Designs (Plonkit)
description: Each state has a unique bus stop design. These are quite common in urban rounds, so are worth learning. Darwin bus stops are usually concrete shelters.

title: Australia - WA/Vic Trident Poles (Plonkit)
description: A trident-like pole top can sometimes be seen in Western Australia and Victoria.

title: Australia - Queensland Black Markings (Plonkit)
description: These black markings are specific to electricity poles in Queensland. They are often accompanied by diagonal numbers.

title: Australia - SA School Zone (Plonkit)
description: South Australia is the only Australian state that uses a 25 speed limit in school zones.

title: Australia - WA Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: Western Australia, and especially the Perth area, is known for its reddish-orange soil.

title: Australia - Rare Google Cars (Plonkit)
description:
Australia is home to dozens of rare Google cars, which can usually be found in natural reserves.

Most rare Google cars with snorkels are located in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory. The snorkels are dark grey or black extensions to the side of the car, to keep the engine dry when submerged in water.

title: Australia - Perth Sloped Kerbs (Plonkit)
description: You can sometimes see sloped kerbs in Perth, where it gradually declines to the road, whilst in other cities kerbs go straight down at a 90 degree angle.

title: Christmas Island - Location Map (Plonkit)
description: Christmas Island is a small island territory south-southwest of Java. It is an Australian external territory, so for country streaks purposes it is counted as part of Australia.

title: Christmas Island - Silver Pickup Truck (Plonkit)
description:
Christmas Island has two types of coverage: car coverage and a couple of trekkers.
The car coverage was done with a unique Google car: a silver pickup truck, with the bed of the truck visible. Usually, this is all you need to identify Christmas Island.

title: Christmas Island - Dense Tropical Forest (Plonkit)
description: Most of Christmas Island is covered by dense tropical forest. Some unpaved roads feature bright, white sandy soil. A small part of the coverage is in built-up areas. And in some places, palms can be seen.

title: Christmas Island - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Christmas Island uses the standard Australian bollard. It is a simple white bollard with a red reflector on the front, and a grey reflector on the back.

title: Christmas Island - Yellow License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Christmas Island has yellow licence plates.

title: Christmas Island - Rural Trails (Plonkit)
description: While much of the coverage is on regular roads, the Google car also drove on some very rural trails.

title: Christmas Island - Built-up Areas (Plonkit)
description: The built-up areas are in the northeast. The rest of the island is mostly covered by dense forest.

title: Christmas Island - Boat Trekker (Plonkit)
description: There is a boat trekker near the north coast of the island. Some of the boat’s white-coloured deck pokes through the blur. Much of the trekker closely hugs the coast; here you can see the steep, rocky coastline of Christmas Island.

title: Christmas Island - Trail Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: There is an abundance of smaller trail trekkers all over the island. These are mostly surrounded by very dense foliage, but occasionally you can encounter interesting sights like beaches and lookouts.

title: Christmas Island - Jln Pantai Road (Plonkit)
description: An exception to the road coverage mostly having car meta is the coastal Jln Pantai road, where a regular trekker was used. On this road, you will not see the back of the car, just a trekker blur.

title: Christmas Island - Harbour Cranes (Plonkit)
description: The harbour area is recognizable by the large cranes that are visible from many vantage points.

title: Christmas Island - Golf Course Trekker (Plonkit)
description: This golf course trekker is on the northeast coast. In some places, the Google car also drove on this golf course.

title: Christmas Island - Red Crabs (Plonkit)
description: Christmas Island is famous for its red crabs. Near Ethel Beach, you can find a trekker walking among hundreds of these crabs. Another smaller trekker where you can see crabs is near The Dales, on the West Coast. Throughout the island, you can find references on signs to these crabs.

title: Cocos Islands - Location Map (Plonkit)
description: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands consist of two coral atolls. It is an Australian territory, so for country streaks purposes, it is counted as Australia.

title: Cocos Islands - White Sand Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The general landscape consists of bright white sand, many palms and mowed grass. Cocos Islands is significantly less forested or hilly compared to Christmas Island.

title: Cocos Islands - West Island Car (Plonkit)
description: This unique car with a snorkel at the front right and the edges of the bed visible is found on West Island.

title: Cocos Islands - Bantam White Car (Plonkit)
description: This white car with the rear edges visible is found in Bantam.

title: Cocos Islands - Bantam Pavement (Plonkit)
description: Bantam Village can be recognized by the cross-hatched brick pavement.

title: Cocos Islands - Runway (Plonkit)
description: The Cocos Islands runway can be recognized by it being the widest paved road on the island, with mowed grass on both sides of the runway and this follow car.

title: Cocos Islands - Coastal Trekkers (Plonkit)
description: Cocos Islands has many trekkers along the coast. Most of them will be walking on white sand, with the ocean to one side and palms the other.

title: Cocos Islands - Direction Island (Plonkit)
description:
Direction Island can be recognized by the beaches having significantly more litter compared to the other islands. Bricks, styrofoam and dead coral can be seen along some portions of the coast.
In addition, the trekker can be seen walking between many palms inland.

title: Cocos Islands - Horsburgh Island (Plonkit)
description: The inland trekker on Pulau Luar (Horsburgh Island) can be recognized by the dry, yellow grass, and more sparse vegetation.

title: Cocos Islands - Medium Boat (Plonkit)
description: This medium boat with a large seating capacity can be seen from West Island to Bantam.

title: Cocos Islands - North Small Boat (Plonkit)
description: This small boat with black bars at the rear can be seen in the north.

title: Cocos Islands - South Small Boat (Plonkit)
description: This small dark grey boat with a woman sitting at the back can be seen in the south.

title: Guam - Location Map (Plonkit)
description: Guam is a United States overseas territory. As such, it is counted as the US for country streaks purposes.

title: Guam - Antenna Roof Rack (Plonkit)
description: The entire Google car is blurred, however an antenna at the front right and a tiny part of the roof rack can be seen.

title: Guam - Thick Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles on Guam are almost always concrete and commonly very thick.

title: Guam - Green Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Guam uses green street signs, unlike the Northern Mariana Islands, which use blue street signs.

title: Guam - Tropical Vegetation (Plonkit)
description: Guam has a tropical climate with a lot of dense and somewhat low vegetation.

title: Guam - Reflector Spam (Plonkit)
description: Both Guam and Northern Mariana Islands often have a very large number of road reflectors.

title: Guam - Asian Languages (Plonkit)
description: East Asian languages such as Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and even Russian are common to see in Guam.

title: Guam - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Coverage in Guam is fairly limited, particularly in the southern half, where there is almost no coverage inland.

title: Guam - Southern Hills (Plonkit)
description: Hills are mostly found on the southern half of the island.

title: Guam - Northern Flatness (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, the northern half of the island is mostly flat.

title: Guam - Apra View Yellow Post (Plonkit)
description: Some Signposts near the town of Apra View are coloured yellow.

title: Guam - LeoPalace Resort (Plonkit)
description: LeoPalace Resort can be recognised by the white, resort buildings with orange tiled roofs, which looks superficially similar to tiled roofs found on Java.

title: New Zealand - Road Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Bollards in New Zealand have a red strip which wraps around the top of the bollard. This strip wraps the whole way around the back and part of the front. The front or back of the bollard often contains a thin yellow or white reflector.

title: New Zealand - Black-White Plates (Plonkit)
description: New Zealand uses white licence plates with black text, which appears mostly white through the blur.

title: New Zealand - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: The most common pole type found in New Zealand is made of concrete and has one long indent which runs most of the way up the pole. Most concrete poles have small silver possum guards. Circular wooden poles can also be found, but are less common. You can also see concrete holey poles in New Zealand.

title: New Zealand - Give Way Signs (Plonkit)
description: Give-way signs in New Zealand have a white border and red text.

title: New Zealand - Give Way Triangles (Plonkit)
description: New Zealand intersections often use give-way triangles painted on the road.

title: New Zealand - Signposts (Plonkit)
description: The majority of directional and warning signs in New Zealand are held up by white posts. Warning signs are diamond-shaped and painted yellow.

title: New Zealand - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: New Zealand often uses blue street signs with white text, particularly in rural areas. While street signs of other colours can be often seen, blue is by far the most common.

title: New Zealand - Road Line Colors (Plonkit)
description: New Zealand normally uses white outer road lines. Yellow dashed outer road lines can be seen in populated areas. Roads with no outer lines can be seen on smaller roads. Inner lines are either a single dashed white line or unbroken double yellow lines.

title: New Zealand - Chevron Borders (Plonkit)
description: New Zealand uses black-on-yellow chevrons with a thin black border. White on black chevrons are very rarely used.

title: New Zealand - Directional Signs (Plonkit)
description: New Zealand uses green directional signs. If the sign is on a state highway, the highway number will always be shown in a red crest.

title: New Zealand - Bridge Markers (Plonkit)
description: Bridge markers can be found on most paved roads in New Zealand. If the sign is on a state highway, the highway number will always be shown in a red crest on a white marker. The yellow marker indicates the name of the river or bridge.

title: New Zealand - Ferns (Plonkit)
description: It is very common to see ferns growing in forested areas in New Zealand.

title: New Zealand - Two-digit State Highway (Plonkit)
description:
Two-digit state highway numbers follow a sequential pattern from North to South, making them easy to find. Single digit highways run through large parts of the country, but are easy to remember due to the small number of them.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: New Zealand - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description: New Zealand phone numbers are seven digits with a two-digit area code in front of it. Numbers starting with 02 are mobile numbers.

title: New Zealand - Lake Views (Plonkit)
description:
The first digit of Fonterra farm signs follows the regional pattern seen on the map.
This image was provided by snowf\lake and brainy. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: New Zealand - Bus Stop Designs (Plonkit)
description:
The cities of Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch all have unique bus stop signs.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: New Zealand - Several New Zealand (Plonkit)
description:
Several New Zealand cities have distinctive rubbish bins. The distinguishing feature of the bins are the council logos on the front. The colour of the bin lid varies within cities.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: New Zealand - Waikato Northland Hills (Plonkit)
description: The Waikato and Northland regions are characterised by their drier climate and rolling hills. In particular, the Northland region is quite hilly.

title: New Zealand - West Coast Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The West Coast and part of the Tasman region on the South Island can be recognized by its temperate rainforests and rugged landscape. This can be seen through the hundreds of tall hills and mountains, as well as the dark, compact greenery which is due to the area’s high level of rainfall.

title: New Zealand - Southland Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The flatter parts of the Southland and Otago regions can be recognised by their cold climate and sloping, alpine hills. The vegetation in this area is often quite stunted due to the climate.

title: New Zealand - Southern Alps (Plonkit)
description: The Southern Alps, a large, snowy mountain range, stretches throughout the majority of the South Island. Vegetation on the mountains becomes rarer the further south it is.

title: New Zealand - Hawke's Bay Hills (Plonkit)
description: Hawke’s Bay has dry, golden grassy hills, and in Generation 4 it will be sunny with a white Street View car.

title: New Zealand - Sandy Cliffs (Plonkit)
description: Bright sandy cliffs are a common sight in the central region of Manawatū-Whanganui. They may also be found in parts of Taranaki, Waikato and a road going into Hawke’s Bay.

title: New Zealand - Glacial Lakes (Plonkit)
description: The area of the Southern Alps, north and south of Queenstown, contains many glacial lakes, which can be recognized by their teal colours and clear waters.

title: New Zealand - Mount Taranaki Formerly (Plonkit)
description: Mount Taranaki, formerly known as Mount Egmont, is easily distinguished due to its relatively smooth slopes and its pointed, often snowy peak. It can frequently be identified from afar, as the surrounding area is flat.

title: New Zealand - Northland Gen 2 (Plonkit)
description: Generation 2 coverage and gravel roads are particularly common in the Northland region.

title: New Zealand - Tall Hedges (Plonkit)
description:
Tall hedge and tree rows are particularly common in the Canterbury region. They are mostly found in the Canterbury plains, which comprises very flat, large fields.
Due to Canterbury’s flat landscape, mountains can often be seen in the distance to the west.

title: New Zealand - Tauranga Hedges (Plonkit)
description: Very tall hedges are found in the Bay of Plenty, mainly around Tauranga.

title: New Zealand - Vineyards (Plonkit)
description: Vineyards are particularly common in the Marlborough and Hawke’s Bay regions.

title: New Zealand - Corn Fields (Plonkit)
description: Corn is almost exclusively found on the North Island.

title: New Zealand - Flax Rows (Plonkit)
description: While New Zealand flax can be found across the country, if you see them in long neat rows, you should consider Southland.

title: New Zealand - Marlborough Possum Guards (Plonkit)
description: Most utility poles in the Marlborough region have a long square shaped olive-brown possum guard. These can appear alongside the usual shorter silver possum guards.

title: New Zealand - Southland Cylindrical Guards (Plonkit)
description: Many of the utility poles in Southland feature a long cylindrical silver possum guard. These are also more rarely found in western Otago.

title: New Zealand - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Holey poles are found most commonly in Southland and around Auckland.

title: New Zealand - Square Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Square concrete poles without the usual indent are most common in Southland, but can also be found in Otago, Taranaki and Manawatū-Whanganui.

title: New Zealand - Uneven Crossbars (Plonkit)
description: Uneven crossbars, meaning they are off-centre, are found in Otago, Marlborough, Wellington and Taranaki.

title: New Zealand - Metal Bar Insulators (Plonkit)
description: Poles with the middle insulator being installed on top of a tall metal bar are often found along the Auckland Waikato border, as well as in other parts of Waikato.

title: New Zealand - White Painted Crossbars (Plonkit)
description: Some concrete poles in eastern Waikato and Whanganui city have white paint on the middle part of their wooden crossbars. This white painted crossbar can also be found in parts of western Bay of Plenty, Taranaki, Manawatū-Whanganui and eastern Wellington.

title: New Zealand - Gisborne Yellow Tag (Plonkit)
description: A yellow tag, similar in appearance to a cow-tag, is found on most poles in Gisborne. It is also found in a few spots on the South Island, as well as over the border in northern Hawke’s Bay.

title: New Zealand - Warning Sticker (Plonkit)
description: A warning sticker attached to poles, which has a yellow danger triangle between two white rectangles, is found in Hawke’s Bay, from lake Taupo to lake Rotorua, in northern Waikato and south of Auckland city.

title: New Zealand - 5 Digit Sticker (Plonkit)
description: A medium sized black vertical sticker with 5 digits is found in West Coast, Tasman, southern Canterbury and southern Northland.

title: New Zealand - 6 Digit Sticker (Plonkit)
description: A long black vertical sticker with 6 digits with a small black square beneath it, is found on most of the North Island, in Southland and in Otago. On the North Island the first digit will be a 3 or a 4, while on the South Island it starts with an 8.

title: New Zealand - Timaru Orange Paint (Plonkit)
description: Poles near Timaru often have a tall rectangle of orange paint on them with the text “DANGER LIVE WIRES”.

title: New Zealand - Black Horizontal Sticker (Plonkit)
description: A small black horizontal pole sticker, with several numbers, is often found in Taranaki and Wellington. The sticker may rarely be found in parts of Manawatū-Whanganui, Waikato, and southern Hawke's Bay.

title: New Zealand - White Horizontal Sticker (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, a small white horizontal pole sticker with several numbers is found in several parts of the North Island.

title: New Zealand - Gisborne Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Solid outer white lines without middle lines are most common in Gisborne, but can also be found in northern Hawke's Bay and Wellington.

title: New Zealand - Green Striped Bollard (Plonkit)
description: A typical bollard, but with a green stripe, is common in southern Canterbury, as well as in some pockets in eastern Southland.

title: New Zealand - Black Striped Bollard (Plonkit)
description: A typical bollard but with a black stripe instead of a red one is commonly found in Wellington, especially in older Generation 3 coverage.

title: New Zealand - Wooden Fences With (Plonkit)
description: Wooden fences with tightly packed fence posts are most common on the North Island and the north of the South Island, as well as on the Banks peninsula.

title: New Zealand - Wide Wooden Fences (Plonkit)
description: Wooden fences with a big gap in-between them are most common on the South island as well as in Taranaki.

title: New Zealand - Metal Fences (Plonkit)
description: Fences with thin metal fence posts are almost exclusive to the South island.

title: New Zealand - Short Fence Extensions (Plonkit)
description: Short pieces of wood attached to a fence post, slightly extending it, can often be found on fences in Hawke’s Bay and occasionally in Manawatū-Whanganui and Gisborne.

title: New Zealand - Long Fence Extensions (Plonkit)
description: Similar wooden extensions, which are significantly longer, are mainly found in Southland and Hawke’s Bay, but can also be seen in Otago.

title: New Zealand - White Blue Front Car (Plonkit)
description: This car with a white and blue front is mostly found on the North Island. It can occasionally be found In Canterbury and Marlborough, on the South Island.

title: New Zealand - Striped Car (Plonkit)
description: This Street View car features a white-blue-white pattern which is blurred out, and is mainly found on the South Island or around and north of Auckland.

title: New Zealand - North Island Street Signs (Plonkit)
description:
There are many town and city specific street signs in northern New Zealand, which can be seen in this graphic.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: New Zealand - South Island Street Signs (Plonkit)
description:
There are many town and city specific street signs in southern New Zealand, which can be seen in this graphic.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: New Zealand - Hilly Wellington (Plonkit)
description: An easy way to recognize the city of Wellington is by how hilly it is.

title: New Zealand - Stewart Island Gen 3 (Plonkit)
description: Stewart Island only has coverage around the settlement of Oban. It is easily recognized due to the distinct bay, which is often filled with small boats. There is only Generation 3 camera coverage.

title: New Zealand - Tongariro Park (Plonkit)
description: The area around Tongariro National Park is identifiable due to the low-lying volcanic vegetation in the area. Mount Ruapehu and Mount Tongariro are in the vicinity, and their tops are often covered by clouds.

title: New Zealand - Mount Ruapehu Mode (Plonkit)
description: Coverage on Mount Ruapehu is easily identifiable due to the dark volcanic landscape and distinct lack of vegetation.

title: New Zealand - Christchurch Earthquake (Plonkit)
description:
In 2011, Christchurch was hit by an earthquake. As a result, roads on coverage from 2012 often appear in quite bad shape. Water damage caused many driveways to be cut off from streets due to large puddles of water, dirt or mud.
Due to this reason, many residential houses in the city had to be removed, leading to several districts on newer coverage appearing like normal suburbs, but with almost no houses. This is noticeable when looking at where former driveways used to be.

title: New Zealand - Highway 85 Snow (Plonkit)
description: Part of State Highway 85 in Otago has light snow coverage, specifically between the towns of Becks and Morisson.

title: New Zealand - Hutt Valley (Plonkit)
description: The cities of Lower Hutt and Upper Hutt can be identified by the wide, green valley they are located in, which runs southwest to northeast.

title: New Zealand - Blenheim Hills (Plonkit)
description: Blenheim can be recognized by having a large range of hills to the north and the south of the city.

title: New Zealand - Fruit Farms (Plonkit)
description: Fruit farms covered in green netting are particularly common near Tauranga, but can also be seen near Gisborne.

title: New Zealand - Banks Peninsula Also (Plonkit)
description: Banks peninsula, also sometimes called Akaroa, due to the town, is rocky with grassy hills, and small patches of trees.

title: New Zealand - Marlborough Sounds (Plonkit)
description: The region of northern Marlborough, known as Marlborough Sounds, has densely forested mountains protruding from water.

title: New Zealand - Otago Peninsula (Plonkit)
description: The Otago peninsula east of Dunedin is recognizable from its combination of plants such as cabbage trees, yellow flowered bushes, small groves of cone-shaped pine trees, and New Zealand flax. Additionally, the peninsula’s poles often have off-centre crossbars.

title: New Zealand - Arthur's Pass Pickup (Plonkit)
description: State Highway 73, located near Arthur’s Pass, can be recognised by the almost dried out river with an abundance of gravel on the river bed. Additionally, the Street View car in Arthur’s Pass drove behind a black pickup truck with two ladders on its roof.

title: New Zealand - Milford Sound (Plonkit)
description: State Highway 94 is characterised by its dense red beech forest surrounded by snow-capped mountains.

title: New Zealand - Highway 80 (Plonkit)
description: State Highway 80 in the Southern Alps is recognizable by its north-south orientation up a glacial valley. The west side of the road is lined with snow-capped mountains, while the east side of the road runs alongside the Tasman River and Lake Pukaki.

title: New Zealand - Pirongia and Kakepuku (Plonkit)
description: The mountains of Pirongia and Kakepuku are often seen together in an otherwise mostly flat landscape. To the west, we have Mount Pirongia which is a long mountain range, with 2 distinct small bumps. Meanwhile Mount Kakepuku is to the south and has a volcanic cone shape.

title: New Zealand - Mount Putauaki (Plonkit)
description: The volcano of Putauaki in eastern Bay of Plenty has a seemingly cut-off top which vaguely resembles the shape of a frog, with two big “eyes” protruding on either side of the top.

title: New Zealand - Highway Numbering (Plonkit)
description: Two-digit state highway numbers follow a sequential pattern from North to South, making them easy to find. Single digit highways run through large parts of the country, but are easy to remember due to the small number of them.

title: New Zealand - Fonterra Farm Signs (Plonkit)
description:
The first digit of Fonterra farm signs follows the regional pattern seen on the map.

This image was provided by snowf_lake and brainy. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: New Zealand - Rubbish Bins (Plonkit)
description: Several New Zealand cities have distinctive rubbish bins. The distinguishing feature of the bins are the council logos on the front. The colour of the bin lid varies within cities.

title: New Zealand - Mount Taranaki (Plonkit)
description: Mount Taranaki, often referred to as Mount Egmont, is easily distinguished due to its relatively smooth slopes and its pointed, often snowy peak. It can frequently be identified from afar, as the surrounding area is flat.

title: New Zealand - Northern Fences (Plonkit)
description: Wooden fences with tightly packed fence posts are most common on the Northern Island and the north of the South Island, as well as on Akaroa.

title: New Zealand - Banks Peninsula (Plonkit)
description: Banks peninsula, also known as Akaroa, is rocky with grassy hills, and small patches of trees.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Location Map (Plonkit)
description: The Northern Mariana Islands is a United States overseas territory. As such, it is counted as the US for country streaks purposes.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Antenna Placement (Plonkit)
description: The entire Google car is blurred, however an antenna at the front right can be seen. The antenna is also noticeably closer to the camera than in the Guam Google car.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Wooden Poles (Plonkit)
description: Northern Mariana Islands have wooden poles, frequently with a crossbar at the top.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: The Northern Mariana Islands uses blue street signs, unlike Guam, which use green street signs.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Dense Vegetation (Plonkit)
description: Northern Mariana Islands have a tropical climate with a lot of dense and somewhat low vegetation.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Flame Tree (Plonkit)
description: Royal Poinciana, Flamboyant Tree or Flame Tree (Delonix Regia) is the official tree of the Northern Mariana Islands and very common to see in the territory. Its wide crown with bright red flowers is easy to recognize.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Reflector Spam (Plonkit)
description: Both Northern Mariana Islands and Guam often have a very large number of road reflectors.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Language Features (Plonkit)
description: East Asian languages such as Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and even Russian are common to see in the Northern Mariana Islands.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: The only island with car coverage is the main island of Saipan. The islands north of that have no coverage. Tinian and Sinapalu south of Saipan only have tripod coverage.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Commercial Areas (Plonkit)
description: Dense commercial areas can be found on the southern half of the west coast.

title: Northern Mariana Islands - Suicide Cliff (Plonkit)
description: The Suicide Cliff is a steep cliff with a lot of exposed rock near the northern tip of the island.

title: Pitcairn Islands - Location Map (Plonkit)
description: The Pitcairn Islands are a group of four islands in the South Pacific Ocean and a territory of the United Kingdom. As such, it is counted as the UK for country streaks purposes.

title: Pitcairn Islands - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Coverage is limited to two islands: Pitcairn Island and Henderson Island. The following clues will be focused on Pitcairn Island, as Henderson Island only has a very small amount of beach coverage.

title: Pitcairn Islands - Gen 3 Trekker (Plonkit)
description: All coverage was taken with a Generation 3 trekker.

title: Pitcairn Islands - Dirt Tracks (Plonkit)
description: Pitcairn Island is a semi-tropical and densely forested island, with most of the coverage being taken on small dirt tracks going through the forest.

title: Pitcairn Islands - Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: The soil is commonly very red.

title: Pitcairn Islands - Adamstown Concrete Roads (Plonkit)
description: Adamstown is the only settlement on Pitcairn Island, and is found near the northeastern shore. Some of the roads going through the town are made of concrete rather than dirt.

title: Pitcairn Islands - Henderson Island Coverage (Plonkit)
description: The coverage on Henderson Island is limited to two white sand beaches on the northern and eastern shore.

title: Pitcairn Islands - Adamstown Dock (Plonkit)
description: A dock with the POI “The Landing” containing a large number of small ATVs can be found at the eastern end of Adamstown.

title: Vanuatu - Location Map (Plonkit)
description: Vanuatu is an island nation located in the Pacific Ocean, northeast of Brisbane between the Solomon Islands, New Caledonia and Fiji.

title: Vanuatu - Gen 3 Trekker (Plonkit)
description: All coverage in Vanuatu was taken with a Generation 3 trekker.

title: Vanuatu - Volcanic Soil (Plonkit)
description: The coverage was taken on a volcanic island, and as such you will often see dark volcanic soil.

title: Vanuatu - Tropical Forest (Plonkit)
description: Vanuatu is a tropical island chain, with a significant part of the coverage being taken in a dense tropical forest.

title: Vanuatu - Ambrym Island Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Although Vanuatu consists of 13 primary islands, only Ambrym Island has coverage. Look for the ‘Port Vato’ label on the map, north of Port Vila, to find the island.

title: Vanuatu - Volcano Trekker (Plonkit)
description: This unique volcano trekker can be found in the middle of the island.

title: Vanuatu - Volcanic Plateau (Plonkit)
description: A distinct plateau with dark brown soil and patchy grass is seen east of the volcano.

title: Vanuatu - Jungle Trekker (Plonkit)
description: Tropical plants and many ferns can be seen in this jungle further to the east. A man with a red cap is also seen with the trekker.

title: Vanuatu - Black Sand Beach (Plonkit)
description: A beach with black sand can be seen on the east side of the island.

title: Vanuatu - Purple Soil Road (Plonkit)
description: This dirt road with tire tracks and slightly purple soil can be seen east of the beach.

title: Vanuatu - Endu Pahakol Village (Plonkit)
description: Endu Pahakol, the only village with coverage on Ambrym Island, can be recognized by the small thatched huts and dark soil.

title: Argentina - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Argentina uses two types of licence plates: a black one, which will be visible on street view with a black dot in the middle, and a white one with a blue bar at the top.

title: Argentina - Black Gen 3 Car (Plonkit)
description: Argentina has a black Google car in Generation 3 coverage.

title: Argentina - Argentina Also Has (Plonkit)
description: Argentina also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front.

title: Argentina - Alternating Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Round concrete poles sustaining three electricity lines in an alternating pattern are very common in Argentina.
Doubled up poles like in the second image is also a good clue for Argentina.

title: Argentina - Wooden A-Frame Poles (Plonkit)
description: Wooden poles are somewhat common in Argentina, they can be found either with a crossbar or without.

title: Argentina - Red-White Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Argentina typically uses white-and-red chevrons.

title: Argentina - Road Line Colors (Plonkit)
description: Road lines in Argentina are mainly dashed white, double yellow or a mix in between.

title: Argentina - Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: Argentinian kilometre markers are typically white with a black strip displaying the road number at the top.

title: Argentina - Red Guardrail Reflectors (Plonkit)
description: Yellow and red rectangular reflectors can often be seen on Argentinian guardrails.

title: Argentina - Flat Desolate Landscape (Plonkit)
description: While Argentina features a plethora of different landscapes, most of the country is relatively flat, mostly treeless, and sparsely populated. In the absence of better clues, you should consider Argentina when you see landscapes like this with a very “wide open”, desolate feel.

title: Argentina - City Taxi Designs (Plonkit)
description:
These Argentinian cities have unique and recognisable taxis.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Argentina - Western Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Far western Argentina typically features a mountainous landscape.

title: Argentina - Misiones Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: Red soil is typically found in the Misiones province.

title: Argentina - Chaco and Formosa Vegetation (Plonkit)
description: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.

title: Argentina - Grassland and Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Grassland with a few separated tree plantations is generally found in this area.

title: Argentina - Buenos Aires Lakes (Plonkit)
description: Small lakes near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.

title: Argentina - San Luis Red Roads (Plonkit)
description: Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.

title: Argentina - Central South Barren (Plonkit)
description: Flat and barren landscapes like this are typically found in central southern Argentina.

title: Argentina - Southern Grasslands (Plonkit)
description: If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.

title: Argentina - Entre Rios Plantations (Plonkit)
description: The majority of tree plantations in Argentina are located in the Entre Rios province.

title: Argentina - Tierra del Fuego Beech Forests (Plonkit)
description: Beech forests are commonly found in the state of Tierra del Fuego.

title: Argentina - Caranday Wax Palm (Plonkit)
description: Coperinicia alba, also known as the Caranday Wax Palm, have short, fan-like leaves that tend to grow in low-density, single-species forests. Most common in Formosa, they can also be found in Chaco, Corrientes and northern Santa Fe.

title: Argentina - Caranday Palm (Plonkit)
description: Trithrinax Campestris, or the caranday palm, not to be confused with the Caranday Wax Palm, is a rustic palm native to the Sierras de Córdoba with a broader distribution in San Luis and northern mountainous Argentina. It can be identified by its compact fan-like leaves with a trunk hidden by a coat of dead-leaves.

title: Argentina - Butia Yatay Palm (Plonkit)
description: The Butia yatay palm has arching, pinnate leaves and often grows at an incline with varying heights. It is most common in Corrientes and Parque Nacional El Palmar, Entre Rios.

title: Argentina - Totai Palm Has (Plonkit)
description: The Totai Palm has small thin leaves with a visible spear shaped top, and a smooth trunk. It can be found as a decorational plant all across Argentina, however in the wild it is most common in Formosa, Chaco and Misiones.

title: Argentina - Cardon Cactus (Plonkit)
description: Trichocereus atacamensis, or the cardón, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.

title: Argentina - Toothpick Cactus (Plonkit)
description: Stetsonia coryne, or the toothpick cactus, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.

title: Argentina - Wild Sunflowers (Plonkit)
description: Wild sunflowers (Tithonia tubaeformis) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and Tucumán.

title: Argentina - Calden Tree (Plonkit)
description: Prosopis caldenia, known as the caldén, is a decently large deciduous tree with small leaves and sinuous branches. It is mainly found in La Pampa.

title: Argentina - Pampas Grass (Plonkit)
description: Pampas grass (Cortaderia selloana) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads.

title: Argentina - Sugarcane Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Sugarcane plantations are most common in Tucumán, with hotspots appearing in Salta and Jujuy.

title: Argentina - Sorghum Fields (Plonkit)
description: Fields of sorghum can most commonly be seen in Santa Fe, Córdoba and Buenos Aires. It can be identified by its dark red flowerheads.

title: Argentina - Corn Fields Be (Plonkit)
description: Corn fields can be found in most of northern Argentina, however they are most common in Córdoba and Santiago del Estero.

title: Argentina - Sunflower Fields (Plonkit)
description: Fields of sunflowers are mainly found in southern Chaco, and less commonly in Buenos Aires and southern Córdoba.

title: Argentina - Poplar Tree Rows (Plonkit)
description: Single rows of poplar trees, characterised by their thin and tall appearance, are very common around Neuquén. The area is also very flat.

title: Argentina - Latvian Style Poles (Plonkit)
description: Within Argentina, these Latvian style wooden hook poles are unique to La Rioja and Mendoza.

title: Argentina - Mendoza Side Insulator (Plonkit)
description: In Mendoza, poles with a single insulator attached to the side of the pole can be found.

title: Argentina - Tucuman Pole Sticker (Plonkit)
description: White vertical pole stickers with several digits can be found in Tucumán.

title: Argentina - Cordoba Road Markers (Plonkit)
description: You can find these unique markers on provincial roads in Cordoba.

title: Argentina - La Pampa Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: T-Junctions in La Pampa sometimes have these yellow rectangular signs, with a chevron pattern on the bottom, and the Road Number(s) above, with an arrow on both sides.

title: Argentina - Northwest Red Bricks (Plonkit)
description: Red bricks, similar to what is common in Bolivia, can be found in the northwest of the country, especially in western Jujuy.

title: Argentina - Mar Del Plata Architecture (Plonkit)
description: In Mar Del Plata and surrounding cities (such as Miramar and Necochea), a unique style of architecture can be found. Its main features include quartzite stoned facades, orange tiled roofs, attached garages, and vault shaped porches.

title: Argentina - Jujuy Salt Pans (Plonkit)
description: Salt pans in Argentina are typically found in Jujuy.

title: Argentina - Salta Red Mountains (Plonkit)
description: These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.

title: Argentina - Catamarca Volcanic Rocks (Plonkit)
description: These volcanic rocks in Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the RP43 south of Antofagasta de la Sierra in northwestern Catamarca.

title: Argentina - RN65 Mountain Road (Plonkit)
description: The western part of the RN65 in western Tucumán can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains with its western part up in the clouds.

title: Argentina - Talampaya Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: Red soil with a barren landscape and mountain ranges, can often be seen on the RN76 in Parque Nacional Talampaya in western La Rioja.

title: Argentina - Cordoba Mountains (Plonkit)
description: These mountains are typically found west of Córdoba.

title: Argentina - San Juan Horse Trekker (Plonkit)
description: This horse trekker can be found in southwestern San Juan.

title: Argentina - Mendoza Vineyards (Plonkit)
description: If you see vineyards with mountains in the west and flatness in the east, you are most likely in the outskirts of Mendoza.

title: Argentina - Buenos Aires Hills (Plonkit)
description: Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of Bahía Blanca.

title: Argentina - Monkey Puzzle Tree (Plonkit)
description: The monkey puzzle tree can be found in western Neuquen. The most specimens are seen on state road 23.

title: Argentina - Neuquen Degraded Sunrise (Plonkit)
description: Sunrise coverage with degraded image quality is found on the RN40 just south of the Mendoza border with Neuquén.

title: Argentina - Rio Colorado Sunrise (Plonkit)
description: Sunrise coverage with bad image quality and multiple blurs is found on a short part of the RN251 and RN22, west of Río Colorado.

title: Argentina - Sawdust Car (Plonkit)
description: The “sawdust” car is found in centre-south Argentina and has a unique sandy dust on its visible black back.

title: Argentina - Chubut Rock Formations (Plonkit)
description: Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these rock formations.

title: Argentina - Comodoro Rivadavia (Plonkit)
description: Comodoro Rivadavia is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.

title: Argentina - Eastern Santa Cruz Snow (Plonkit)
description: This snow coverage is found on the eastern RP25 in eastern Santa Cruz.

title: Argentina - Southwestern Santa Cruz Snow (Plonkit)
description: Melting snow coverage is seen on the eastern RN293 close to the Chilean border in southwestern Santa Cruz.

title: Argentina - Ushuaia Mountains (Plonkit)
description: These snowy mountains to the north can only be found in Ushuaia.

title: Argentina - Macaw Palm (Plonkit)
description: The Macaw Palm has small thin leaves with a visible spear shaped top. It can be found as a decorational plant all across Argentina, however in the wild it is most common in Formosa, Chaco and Misiones.

title: Argentina - Corn Fields (Plonkit)
description: Corn fields can be found in most of northern Argentina, however they are most common in Córdoba, Buenos Aires and Santiago del Estero.

title: Argentina - Pink Trumpet Tree (Plonkit)
description: The Pink Trumpet Tree (Handroanthus impetiginosus) can be found in cities in northern Salta such as Orán, Tartagal and General Mosconi.

title: Bolivia - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Bolivia has short, white licence plates with blue text. The blue text can be hard to see through the blur, so plates might appear as plain white.

title: Bolivia - White Gen 3 Car (Plonkit)
description: Bolivia only has Generation 3 camera coverage. All of the country was covered by a solid white Google car with no antenna.

title: Bolivia - Unfinished Red Brick (Plonkit)
description: Many buildings in Bolivia consist of large red bricks. Buildings often have an ‘unfinished' look.

title: Bolivia - Road Line Colors (Plonkit)
description: Middle road lines can be all-yellow, yellow and white, or all-white, while outer road lines are always white.

title: Bolivia - Concrete Roads (Plonkit)
description: Bolivia has a lot of standard asphalt roads, but concrete slab roads are also fairly common.

title: Bolivia - Cobblestone Patterns (Plonkit)
description: There are also a lot of cobblestone roads. These roads often have a specific pattern, with several neat lines of stones separating the more disorganised cobblestones in between.

title: Bolivia - White Square Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Bolivia typically uses bulky, white square signposts.

title: Bolivia - Guardrail Markings (Plonkit)
description: Guardrails sometimes feature yellow and black markings. These markings always have the yellow stripes on the outside.

title: Bolivia - Pole Types (Plonkit)
description:
Two types of utility poles are common in Bolivia:
- Round concrete poles, often with small pinholes near the top.
- Wooden poles.
Poles in Bolivia are very inconsistent and should not be relied on too much. Poles can have a variety of pole tops. On rare occasions, you can find Argentina-style concrete poles.

title: Bolivia - Curvy Wooden Poles (Plonkit)
description: Many wooden utility poles, particularly in the eastern parts of Bolivia’s Street View coverage, are noticeably curvy and look like they are made from locally sourced tree trunks.

title: Bolivia - Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: Kilometre markers are black and white. The top part is black and features the abbreviation ‘Km’, while the bottom part is white and shows the distance. These markers do not have road numbers.

title: Bolivia - Traditional Clothing (Plonkit)
description: Many Bolivians wear traditional clothing, especially women. Folk dress for women typically consists of bowler hats, colourful shawls, and big pleated skirts (pollera).

title: Bolivia - Political Graffiti (Plonkit)
description:
At the time Bolivia was covered by Street View, its ruling political party was the Movimiento al Socialismo (MAS). Political graffiti often features the words MAS and Evo, short for then-president Evo Morales.
Additionally, many random objects are painted in the party’s colours: black, white, and a large blue field. This distinctive colour scheme is a good clue for Bolivia.

title: Bolivia - Wiphala Flag (Plonkit)
description: Bolivia has a second official flag, called the Wiphala. It is a square patchwork of seven diagonally arranged colours. It is sometimes seen on government buildings and project signs.

title: Bolivia - Tigo Ads (Plonkit)
description: In urban areas, you will often see ads for the telecom company Tigo, with its distinct blue logo. Crucially, this company does not operate in Peru, meaning it can help you solve urban 50-50s.

title: Bolivia - Reddish Tint (Plonkit)
description:
If all else fails, and you have a tough 50-50, it can help to look at the colour of the rocks and soil, which often have a distinct reddish tint in Bolivia, more so than the other Andean countries.
This information should be used with a fair amount of caution, as there are many variables. Only use it when you have no other clues available.

title: Bolivia - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Coverage in Bolivia is very limited, both in geographic scope and the density of roads covered.
Only the central and central-western parts of the country have coverage. Most coverage is found in and around the six main cities of La Paz or El Alto, Cochabamba, Oruro, Sucre, Potosi, and Santa Cruz.
These aforementioned six cities have in-depth side-street coverage. Outside these cities, coverage is mostly limited to main roads. Beware that “main road” is a relative concept in Bolivia: many of these, even some that are marked yellow on the map, have large unpaved sections.

title: Bolivia - Altiplano Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The Altiplano (“high plain”) is an immense highland plateau that dominates most of western Bolivia. It is covered in grasslands that range from green to arid. Some parts are suitable for agriculture, whereas other parts are extremely dry. Grass growing in tufts is common (sometimes referred to as “Bolivian hedgehogs” in the community).

title: Bolivia - Northern Altiplano (Plonkit)
description: The grasslands of the Altiplano tend to look more lush in the more northern half: the area close to El Alto and La Paz.

title: Bolivia - Southern Altiplano (Plonkit)
description: Conversely, the Altiplano looks more arid in the more southern half: around Oruro, and the roads going southwest towards Chile.

title: Bolivia - Lake Titicaca (Plonkit)
description:
Lake Titicaca, on the border with Peru, is the most significant body of water in Bolivia. It is located entirely within the Altiplano. It can be seen from two roads:
- The section of Ruta 1 between Desaguadero and Guaqui. Here, the lake will always be to your north.
- The section of Ruta 2 between San Pablo de Tiquina and Batallas. Here, the lake will mostly be to your south or west.
The landscape around Titicaca is very green, compared to most of the western half of Bolivia.

title: Bolivia - Andes Mountains (Plonkit)
description: If you are surrounded by tall mountains, you are likely in the Andes, which goes roughly northwest to southeast in between the Altiplano and the Amazon rainforest.

title: Bolivia - East of Andes (Plonkit)
description: The area east of the Andes is very green and tropical, with lots of agriculture – especially around Santa Cruz. This area is mostly very flat, though you will see large hills on some of the roads closer to the Andes. The soil tends to have a pink colour.

title: Bolivia - Santa Cruz Pink Soil (Plonkit)
description: Within this tropical area, coverage on unpaved roads is only found around Santa Cruz. These roads again prominently have the pink soil that is very characteristic of the area east of Andes.

title: Bolivia - Cobblestone Distribution (Plonkit)
description: Aside from being a useful identifier for the country, cobblestone roads are mainly found in and southeast of Cochabamba. They also appear around Sucre and, very rarely, in La Paz.

title: Bolivia - La Paz vs El Alto (Plonkit)
description: La Paz and El Alto are twin cities that together form one big metropolitan area. However, despite being located right next to each other, they each have a very different look. See the tips below for more information.

title: Bolivia - La Paz Green Hills (Plonkit)
description: La Paz is a very hilly city. Most of La Paz itself is situated in meandering valleys, surrounded by hills that often tend to be covered in green vegetation (as opposed to the more dry hillsides found in many other Bolivian urban areas).

title: Bolivia - Downtown La Paz (Plonkit)
description: Downtown La Paz is the only place in Bolivia where you will find very tall buildings (10+ storeys).

title: Bolivia - La Paz Sandstone Formations (Plonkit)
description:
In many parts of La Paz, you can see these heavily eroded, pillar-like rock formations on the hillsides. They consist of a very recognizable yellow-beige sandstone.
Of the big cities with coverage in Bolivia, these rock formations are essentially unique to La Paz.

title: Bolivia - El Alto Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
El Alto is situated on a very flat, highland plateau. It looks much drier and dustier than La Paz. The layout of its streets is also more regular and grid-like.
The city appears like an unending mess of semi-finished red brick buildings, even more so than other cities in Bolivia. Some neighbourhoods have a very rundown, desolate look.

title: Bolivia - El Alto Pavement (Plonkit)
description: This type of pavement, consisting of rectangular grey bricks with slightly wavy edges, is very common in El Alto.

title: Bolivia - Neo-Andean Architecture (Plonkit)
description: In El Alto, you can sometimes see a local type of architecture referred to as Neo-Andean. Buildings in this style are colourful, with elaborate, futuristic-looking façades. The style is really unique and is almost completely limited to El Alto.

title: Bolivia - El Alto Gradient Doors (Plonkit)
description: Gates and doors in El Alto are sometimes painted with a gradient pattern, usually dark green to light green, or red to yellow.

title: Bolivia - Cochabamba Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Cochabamba is situated in a large flat valley, where you will almost always see an imposing wall of mountains to your north. This is the single most useful and consistent way of distinguishing this city from other places in Bolivia.

title: Bolivia - Oruro Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
Of all the major cities in Bolivia, Oruro is situated in by far the most dry landscape.
In Oruro, you will also usually be able to see a large dry hill to your west, in an otherwise mostly flat and very arid landscape.

title: Bolivia - Sucre Hills (Plonkit)
description: Sucre is situated in a very hilly landscape, and as a result you can see many elevation changes in its streets. Uniquely, you can see these round, tree-covered hills in many parts of the city.

title: Bolivia - Sucre Historic Centre (Plonkit)
description: Sucre has a well-preserved historic city centre, with lots of old colonial buildings. The downtown area can be recognized by the white walls, orange tiled roofs, and generally more historic look than other places in Bolivia.

title: Bolivia - Potosi Arid Hills (Plonkit)
description: Potosí is also situated in a very hilly landscape, like Sucre. However, its landscape is much more arid, with little to no trees atop the hills.

title: Bolivia - Cerro Rico Potosi (Plonkit)
description: In many parts of Potosí, you can see this colossal pyramid-shaped mountain called Cerro Rico. It is famous for having massive quantities of silver ore, and as a result its surface is stripped bare by extensive mining – which is distinctly visible in the street view coverage.

title: Bolivia - Santa Cruz Tropical (Plonkit)
description:
Santa Cruz is the only large Bolivian city located in a tropical (and flat) landscape.
Note that there are several smaller towns around Santa Cruz that look essentially identical. Some of these have extensive side-road coverage too.

title: Bolivia - Ruta 1 Lake Views (Plonkit)
description:
Ruta 1 west of El Alto is a paved road that runs through green grasslands. The road itself is mostly flat, but you will usually see hills nearby. On the road, you will often see numbers marked in white paint.
Near the western end of the road, close to Desaguadero and the border with Peru, you will be able to see Lake Titicaca to your north.

title: Bolivia - Ruta 3 Pongo (Plonkit)
description: The section of Ruta 3 around Pongo, northeast of La Paz, can easily be recognised by the breathtaking views of enormous mountains, which are often surrounded by low-hanging clouds. The mountains are also recognizable by their dark grey rocks lightly covered in greenish grass.

title: Bolivia - Yungas Road (Plonkit)
description: The N Yungas Road (also popularly known as Death Road), is a bendy, small and unpaved road, high up in the mountains east of La Paz. The vegetation is very tropical. The coverage in the southern part of the road is very foggy. True to its unofficial name, this road looks like a very dangerous drive. You can sometimes see some daring cyclists.

title: Bolivia - Divided Highway 1 & 4 (Plonkit)
description:
Ruta 1 and 4 between La Paz and Oruro is a large divided highway that runs through the Altiplano landscape of western Bolivia.
It is the only large, divided highway in the entire country. There are smaller, divided roads in and near some urban areas, but those should be easily distinguishable based on landscape and road size.

title: Bolivia - Ruta 4 Square Smudge (Plonkit)
description: A long section of Ruta 4 has a distinctive square smudge on the front left of the camera. This coverage starts in the altiplano near Vila Vila, going east through Cochabamba, all the way to Buena Vista in the flat Amazonian part of Bolivia.

title: Bolivia - Morochata Road (Plonkit)
description:
Around Morochata, northwest of Cochabamba on Ruta 25, there is a small isolated piece of coverage that looks extremely similar to Peru. It is a dirt road that meanders through a mountainous landscape. Knowing this road can be extremely helpful for country streak purposes.
The western part of this road is located in a green mountain landscape, with fields on the mountain slopes and lots of eucalyptus trees around.
Towards the east, it transitions into a more arid high altitude landscape that still looks very similar to Peru.

title: Bolivia - Ruta 1 Snow (Plonkit)
description:
Ruta 1 between Machacamarca and Guindal runs through an arid landscape where you will often see patches of snow on the hilltops, and sometimes even next to the road. Weather conditions range from cloudy to fully overcast, lending this coverage a gloomy look.
The aforementioned road can be regionguessed even more precisely. See the next two tips.

title: Bolivia - North of Challapata (Plonkit)
description: The section north of Challapata runs in a general NNW direction, with straight roads in flat terrain, with hills on one or both sides. Weather conditions are a little bit better, with some of the sky visible, especially when looking south.

title: Bolivia - Southeast of Challapata (Plonkit)
description: The section southeast of Challapata tends to be more curvy and hilly. The weather is much worse, with grey skies.

title: Bolivia - Ruta 7 Glitch (Plonkit)
description: The section of Ruta 7 between Mairana and the outskirts of Santa Cruz has coverage with a camera bug that causes a visual glitch. It is a distinctive, neon-like discoloration, that (depending on the road angle) is usually more or less to your north.

title: Bolivia - Mataral Green Hills (Plonkit)
description:
The roads around the town of Mataral have recognizable coverage: a very green, hilly landscape, and sunny weather with only a couple of clouds. While the hills are very green, the vegetation is not very dense, and quite low.
This coverage is limited to Ruta 7 from Comarapa to Mairana, and Ruta 22 to Vallegrande. Other roads in Bolivia with similar vegetation tend to either have different weather (overcast) or terrain (more flat).

title: Bolivia - Mataral Vegetation (Plonkit)
description: In the aforementioned Mataral area, you will often see large cacti hiding between the bushes, as well as trees with yellow flowers.

title: Bolivia - Ruta 4 East (Plonkit)
description: The eastern section of Ruta 4, east of Santa Cruz, runs in a general east-west direction, through a mostly flat, green landscape. In some places, you can see some low hills. This road has both asphalt and concrete pad sections.

title: Bolivia - Ruta 5 Sunset (Plonkit)
description: The section of Ruta 5 around Chaco, just north of Sucre, has distinct sunset coverage. Most of this road has concrete pavement, and meanders through semi-arid hills.

title: Bolivia - Ruta 4 Grainy Asphalt (Plonkit)
description: The section of Ruta 4, southwest of Patacamaya, runs through a semi-arid grassland landscape. Many parts of that road between Patacamaya and Callapa have worn-down grainy asphalt.

title: Bolivia - Nevado Sajama (Plonkit)
description:
On the southwesternmost section of Ruta 4, you can usually see the Nevado Sajama, an isolated snow-capped volcano that is very distinct and unlike any other mountain in Bolivia.
When you see Sajama, you will always be south of Callapa and the Desaguadero River. However, you will not always be able to see it on this section of the road, as it is often hidden by hills.

title: Bolivia - Ruta 6 White Concrete (Plonkit)
description: The section of Ruta 6 between Tarabuco and Zudáñez is paved with extremely light-coloured concrete, bordering on white. This pavement is very recognizable and unique to this road.

title: Bolivia - Coipasa Salt Flat Road (Plonkit)
description:
Between the villages of Villa Vitalina and Coipasa, there is an isolated stretch of coverage where the Google car drove through extremely arid desert terrain. This small road is located close to the southwestern end of Ruta 12, near the Chilean border. It can be hard to spot on the map, because it blends in with the salt flat.
Closer to Villa Vitalina, the car drove over the salt flat. Closer to Coipasa, the car drove on an unpaved dirt road, where you can see cone-shaped volcanic hills. In both parts, there is virtually no vegetation.

title: Bolivia - Sajama National Park Car (Plonkit)
description:
Sajama National Park was covered by this unique Google car: it has a black roof rack with a series of metal bars.
The coverage is on an unpaved road surrounded by fluffy bushes. The Nevado Sajama volcano is always visible. The car briefly drove through the small village of Tomarapi, which can be recognized by its traditional buildings with adobe walls and thatched roofs.

title: Brazil - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Licence plates in Brazil were white until 2018. Now, a white plate with a blue stripe on top is used. Red is still used for commercial vehicles.

title: Brazil - Portuguese Influence (Plonkit)
description: Portuguese is spoken in Brazil, as opposed to most Latin American countries which speak Spanish. Compared to Spanish, some essential differences are that Portuguese uses -ão rather than -ón, -ch/-lh instead of -ll and -nh instead of -ñ.

title: Brazil - Red Soil Map (Plonkit)
description: Soil in most of Brazil is distinctly red. It can range from a light pink around Mato Grosso to a deep maroon near the Paraná river. The soil is usually not red in the North East, or in the majority of Rio Grande do Sul, however.

title: Brazil - Ladder Poles (Plonkit)
description: The most common poles in Brazil have some resemblance to a ladder in the bottom portion. They are rectangular, have long segments running through the bottom, and small holes near the top.

title: Brazil - Black Sign Backs (Plonkit)
description: Most Brazilian road signs have the backs painted black.

title: Brazil - Blue Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: Blue road markers with the road number and kilometre can be seen on the sides of roads.

title: Brazil - Yellow-Black Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Brazil uses yellow on black chevrons, as opposed to most of South America, which use black on yellow chevrons.

title: Brazil - Road Line Colors (Plonkit)
description: Roads in Brazil will usually feature double yellow middle lines, with white outer lines. Roads can occasionally have a single dashed yellow line.

title: Brazil - White Kerbs (Plonkit)
description: There are frequently white painted kerbs on Brazilian roads.

title: Brazil - Orange Tiled Roofs (Plonkit)
description: Many houses throughout Brazil have orange tiled roofs.

title: Brazil - Transparent Satellite Dishes (Plonkit)
description: It is fairly common to see transparent satellite dishes, which within Latin America is generally unique to Brazil.

title: Brazil - Fortlev Water Tanks (Plonkit)
description: Blue Fortlev water tanks are often seen on Brazilian roofs.

title: Brazil - Gen 3 Antenna Types (Plonkit)
description:
In Generation 3 coverage, you can see two different cars:
- A white car with a stubby antenna. There is a diagonal coil wrapped around the antenna.
- A white car with no antenna.
The car’s colour is not always visible, meaning you will often see either just the stubby antenna, or no hints of the car at all.
The stubby antenna with a diagonal coil can also be found in Ecuador, Colombia, and Mexico.

title: Brazil - Gen 4 Car Colors (Plonkit)
description:
The Generation 4 cars you can find in Brazil have a visible front, and have one of the following three colour patterns:
- Blue
- White with a blue stripe
- White

title: Brazil - Gen 4 Small Cam (Plonkit)
description: Brazil also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front.

title: Brazil - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Most of the coverage in Brazil is along the eastern half, with only sparse coverage in the Amazon.
It is useful for beginning players to start forming a rough mental map of where the (limited) coverage is in the western half. When you get Amazonian rounds, this can prevent you from wildly plonking hundreds of kilometres away from the nearest road.

title: Brazil - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description:
Area codes are common to see in Brazil. They are often notated using parentheses, or at minimum as two separate numbers. Phone numbers are sometimes without area codes, and without them will be 8 numbers long for landline and 9 for mobile.
The pattern for each of the states is very learnable and useful. The area codes are grouped by first digit, so even just learning those can already help a lot. Notably, area codes ending in 1 will always be around major cities and state capitals.

title: Brazil - State Acronyms (Plonkit)
description:
Each Brazilian state has a two-letter acronym. These show up most prominently in the numbers of state roads (found on kilometre markers). They can also be found in other contexts however.
The state acronyms show up when you zoom out a little bit on Google maps, which is also possible in the minimap while in-game. However, for quick and or competitive games, it can be very useful to learn them by heart anyway, as this can help a lot with eliminating scanning time.

title: Brazil - CEP Postcodes (Plonkit)
description: Postcodes (CEP) are seen frequently on street signs in Brazil (though sometimes hard to read). The first two numbers will depict an area, a state or multiple states. The numbers go anti-clockwise from São Paulo, ending in Rio Grande do Sul.

title: Brazil - Elevation Map (Plonkit)
description: Shown here is an elevation map of Brazil. It can help to have a rough mental map of where you can find mountains, and which regions are more flat. The highest mountains are generally found near the southeastern coast.

title: Brazil - Caatinga Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Northeastern Brazil can be identified by its dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga landscape). In rainy season coverage, the shrubs are still recognisable, but can be deceptively green.

title: Brazil - Amazon Rainforest (Plonkit)
description: The Amazon is a dense rainforest that comprises 40% of Brazil’s total area. Not many roads are within it, but those that are, mostly go through either biodiverse forest or grassy hills with sparse trees.

title: Brazil - Acre Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Acre has a unique landscape of small grass hills and sparsely growing trees. The roads often do not cut around the hills like in most of Brazil, but ride the hills instead. A similar landscape can also be seen near Maraba in the state of Pará.

title: Brazil - Roraima Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Rural locations in Roraima are mostly open grassy plains with large, distant mountains in the background. Occasionally, you are on roads within the mountains. Furthermore, the grass in Roraima is distinctly thin, and grows in bunches.

title: Brazil - Rio Grande do Sul Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The landscape in Rio Grande do Sul can be hilly or flat with lush, green fields. Southern areas can have some resemblance to Uruguay.

title: Brazil - Southeast Grassy Hills (Plonkit)
description: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo often have rolling grassy hills.

title: Brazil - Espirito Santo Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Espírito Santo, and the surrounding areas, often have large mountains with exposed rock.

title: Brazil - Parana Pines (Plonkit)
description: These distinct trees, called Paraná pines, have long horizontal branches with leaves only at the end. They grow mainly in the southern Brazilian states of Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.

title: Brazil - Coconut Palms (Plonkit)
