description: Coconut palm trees have long leaves, can grow very tall, and have thin trunks. They are common across the north eastern states and sometimes further west or south along the coast.

title: Brazil - Carnaúba Palms (Plonkit)
description: Carnaúba palms have short but strong fan-like leaves, and a trunk that is smooth at the top and spiked at the bottom. They are commonly seen in Ceará, Piauí, and Rio Grande de Norte, but are also around the town of Xique Xique in Bahia.

title: Brazil - Babassu Palms (Plonkit)
description: Babassu palms have long, robust leaves comprised of many leaflets. Trunk length can vary from short to tall. They are found throughout the Amazon, or more rarely, down the east coast.

title: Brazil - Acai Palms (Plonkit)
description: Açai palms produce fruits that are popular globally. Most of these palms are found near Belem, but can be seen across the Amazon. They are distinct in the way the leaflets droop downward along with their unusually thin trunks.

title: Brazil - Moriche Palms Have (Plonkit)
description: Moriche palms have leaves with a rounded fan shape, and often the bottom leaves can be seen dead and drooping down. They are most common in Roraima, Amazonas, Tocatins, Goias, and the Amazonian states, but random clusters can be found quite far away from this region.

title: Brazil - Macaw Palms (Plonkit)
description: Macaw palms have thin leaves compared to other palms, and often have a visible spear shaped top. They are very common around Mato Grosso do Sul, northern Tocantins, and around Belo Horizonte, but can be seen much further out sometimes. These palms should be used with caution, and single trees are much less of an indicator than multiple trees.

title: Brazil - Long Stem Plants (Plonkit)
description: This species of plant, with long stems and many leaves growing up, are very common in Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte, and Paraíba. In the dry season, you can still make out the distinct long stems without leaves.

title: Brazil - Tall Grass Region (Plonkit)
description: Very tall grass can be often seen in the centre of the country, most notably in the Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais states.

title: Brazil - Eucalyptus Grandis (Plonkit)
description: Eucalyptus Grandis, when fully grown, is a very tall tree with plantations all over Brazil. You can find them in both large and very small plantations., as well as randomly growing anywhere. You can see them all over the south, but there are some large plantations in Amapá too.

title: Brazil - Sugarcane Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Sugarcane plantations are by far most common in the state of São Paulo, and are common in Paraná, Mato Grosso do Sul, and in the coastal north eastern states.

title: Brazil - Soybean Fields (Plonkit)
description: Soybeans appear as small, leafy soil grown plants. They are most commonly grown in Mato Grosso, Paraná, and Goiás.

title: Brazil - Coffee Plantations (Plonkit)
description: Coffee beans are by far the most common in Minas Gerais, but also can be found in Espírito Santo and northeastern São Paulo.

title: Brazil - Round Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: Alongside ladder poles, round poles can often be found across the south of Brazil, especially São Paulo. These poles are cylindrical and made of concrete.

title: Brazil - Wooden Poles (Plonkit)
description: Some states also use wooden poles. They are most commonly seen in Rio Grande do Sul, Roraima, Amazonas, and Rio de Janeiro.

title: Brazil - Pole Supports (Plonkit)
description: Brazil often uses supports on its electricity poles that connect the crossbar to the stem of the pole. The frequency of pole supports varies greatly state-to-state. It is notably rare in the northeast.

title: Brazil - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles with a single support are most commonly found in the states of Tocantins, Santa Catarina, and Minas Gerais.

title: Brazil - Bahia and Pernambuco Pole ID (Plonkit)
description: Markings on poles are used by the electricity companies to identify them. This pole ID is long, yellow pole paint with a black code. The ones that start with a letter are found in Bahia and Pernambuco.

title: Brazil - Goias Pole ID (Plonkit)
description: Similar to the Bahia and Pernambuco poles, Goiás poles also use long, yellow pole paint with a black paint code, but it always starts with a number. They also have a rarer yellow on black pole ID, which can be either paint or a plate.

title: Brazil - RN and PE Pole ID (Plonkit)
description: This small yellow or orange plate attached onto the pole by thin metal or zip tie is found in Rio Grande do Norte and Pernambuco. This ID is usually much higher up the pole in Pernambuco than in Rio Grande do Norte.

title: Brazil - Parana Paint ID (Plonkit)
description: Pole IDs in Paraná are usually made up of black paint and yellow or white painted text.

title: Brazil - Maranhao Pole ID (Plonkit)
description: Most poles in Maranhão have a small beige plate with numbers built into the surface of the pole. This pole ID can be found in Pará and Piauí more rarely.

title: Brazil - Parana Street Names (Plonkit)
description: Utility poles in Paraná on intersections are sometimes painted with the street name. This can sometimes extend to Santa Catarina or Rio Grande do Sul if there are ladder poles in the city.

title: Brazil - Sao Paulo Poletop (Plonkit)
description: This poletop, consisting of an asymmetrical crossbar and a support reaching to the middle of the longer part of the crossbar, is the most common poletop in the state of São Paulo. It can also be frequently seen in the states of Rio Grande do Sul, Rio de Janeiro and Mato Grosso do Sul.

title: Brazil - Ceara and Rondonia Poletop (Plonkit)
description: This asymmetrical crossbar with no supports is exclusive to Ceara and Rondonia.

title: Brazil - Ceara and Roraima Poletop (Plonkit)
description: This pole configuration, featuring a zigzag-shaped top bar resting atop a flat crossbar, is exclusive to Ceara and Roraima. The pole is usually much larger than a regular electricity pole.

title: Brazil - Pencil Poles (Plonkit)
description: Poles that have a smooth cone on top, often called a pencil pole, are common in the state of Rio de Janeiro and rarely in Brasília and Manaus.

title: Brazil - Gamma Poles (Plonkit)
description: Gamma-shaped ("Γ") poles containing electricity boxes at the end of the bar are most commonly seen in the state of Rio de Janeiro and in the cities of Belém, Salvador, Fortaleza and Maceió.

title: Brazil - Electricity Counters (Plonkit)
description: You may frequently see electricity counters attached to the poles in Cuiabá, Macapá and large cities in the state of Pará.

title: Brazil - Mato Grosso Poletop (Plonkit)
description: Poles that have one insulator on top and alternating horizontal insulators can be found in Mato Grosso and southern Acre. It is also very rare in Rio Grande do Sul.

title: Brazil - Brown Mushroom Insulators (Plonkit)
description: Insulators that resemble brown mushrooms are only found in Pernambuco.

title: Brazil - White Mushroom Insulators (Plonkit)
description: Insulators that resemble white mushrooms are found in Bahia and rarely Brasília.

title: Brazil - Transparent Insulators (Plonkit)
description: Transparent insulators are mostly in Alagoas in the northeast, and Santa Catarina in the south. They can be seen rarely in Sergipe, Ceará, and Brasília.

title: Brazil - Spool Insulators (Plonkit)
description: These insulators have a shape resembling a spool of thread. They are found mostly in Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo, and have been seen in Ceará.

title: Brazil - Thin Insulators (Plonkit)
description: Insulators in Ceará can sometimes be uniquely long and thin. They are in Goiás too, but are rare.

title: Brazil - Para Horizontal Insulators (Plonkit)
description: Poles with horizontal insulators are very common in Pará and less so in Mato Grosso. They are rarely found in Acre, Amapá, Tocantins, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

title: Brazil - Long Grey Insulators (Plonkit)
description:
Long grey insulators, not including when they are horizontal, are most commonly found in Pará, Mato Grosso, Tocantins, Bahia, Mato Grosso do Sul, Paraná and Santa Catarina.
They are found rarely in Maranhão, Rio Grande do Norte, Alagoas, Sergipe, Rondônia, and Rio Grande do Sul. Other states have between 0 and 5%.

title: Brazil - Maranhao Trident Insulators (Plonkit)
description: Poles with these black double UFO-shaped insulators in a trident formation are common in Maranhão. The insulator itself is common across many states, but not in this configuration.

title: Brazil - Lollipop Insulators (Plonkit)
description: These insulators are spherical or cone shaped and suspended on a rod above the insulator bar. They are often referred to as “lollipop” insulators. They are very common in Rio Grande de Norte, Paraíba, Pernambuco, and more rarely, Sergipe.

title: Brazil - Santa Catarina Dark Insulators (Plonkit)
description: These dark brown insulators with grey bases are found almost exclusively in Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

title: Brazil - Metal vs Concrete Bins (Plonkit)
description: Brazil often uses metal trash baskets outside houses. In Acre and Rondônia, however, it is much more common to see them made of concrete.

title: Brazil - Two-Part Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Lamps in Minas Gerais and Goias will often feature two parts to them. They can also be found in Rio Grande do Norte, Ceará, Rio Grande do Sul as well as the Federal District.

title: Brazil - Parana No-Arm Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Lamps in urban northern Paraná sometimes have no lamp arm. Styles contrast, and are either colourful, plastic and industrial, or look fancy and ornate. Both versions are most commonly found in northwest Paraná.

title: Brazil - Attached Lamp Arms (Plonkit)
description: The vast majority of poles in Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Pará, Amapá, Rio Grande do Norte, Pernambuco and Santa Catarina have the lamp arm attached to the pole, as opposed to it being attached with a plate, which is much more common generally.

title: Brazil - Roraima Lamp Colors (Plonkit)
description: Lamps in Roraima have a similar style but have different colours in the main cities. Boa Vista, Normandia, and Mucajaí have red lamps, Rorainópolis has blue lamps, Pacaraima and Iracema have green, and Caracaraí has yellow.

title: Brazil - Ceara Colorful Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Lamps in Ceará often have a fancy and colourful arm, whether as lampposts or attached to utility poles. It sometimes says the town on the arm.

title: Brazil - Divided Highways (Plonkit)
description: São Paulo has far more divided highways than any other state.

title: Brazil - Phone Numbers on Markers (Plonkit)
description: Phone numbers can sometimes be seen underneath kilometre markers in São Paulo.

title: Brazil - Cobblestone Pavement (Plonkit)
description: Cobblestone pavement is most common in the northeast and in Rio Grande do Sul.

title: Brazil - Hexagonal Concrete Tiles (Plonkit)
description: Roads with hexagonal concrete tiles can be found across Brazil, but they are more common in Santa Catarina and Minas Gerais.

title: Brazil - Red Brick Roads (Plonkit)
description: Some roads in Acre are made of red brick.

title: Brazil - Random Stone Roads (Plonkit)
description: Cobblestone roads with randomly sized stones are most common in southeast Rio Grande do Sul and Minas Gerais.

title: Brazil - Uneven Square Stone Roads (Plonkit)
description: These uneven but mostly square stone roads are seen in western Rio Grande do Sul and west Santa Catarina. The soil will often be very dark in these regions too.

title: Brazil - Jagged Brown Tiles (Plonkit)
description: You can often see pavements in Rio Grande do Sul that have brown tiles but are either jagged and random, or square. This style can sometimes be seen in Santa Catarina.

title: Brazil - German Architecture (Plonkit)
description: Buildings in the southern states, mainly Santa Catarina, can be of European influence (typically vaguely German) in design and style.

title: Brazil - Stilt Houses (Plonkit)
description: Wooden houses on stilts are very common in the state of Acre.

title: Brazil - Piau Features (Plonkit)
description: Many roads in Piauí have red gravel on the side of the road. The gravel can appear spread above the tarmac shoulder or on roads with curbs.

title: Brazil - Amapa Roof Smudge (Plonkit)
description: In all Generation 4 coverage in Amapá, the front right of the camera is smudged. In addition, all Generation 4 coverage in Amapá features the white car with the blue stripe.

title: Brazil - Joao-de-Barro Nests (Plonkit)
description: These spheres on top of utility poles are João-de-Barro nests. They are common across the south of Brazil.

title: Brazil - Uiramuta Folded Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The landscape near the town of Uiramuta, in northern Roraima, features a very distinct landscape. It is dry, with large mountains containing numerous “folds.”

title: Brazil - RS Coastal Wetlands (Plonkit)
description: Coastal regions in Rio Grande do Sul are recognisable due to being a rare flat wetland, which is uncommon in Brazil.

title: Brazil - Coastal Coverage (Plonkit)
description: The 364 through Acre is very recognisable due to the rollercoaster-like landscape and road: the road uniquely rides the hills rather than snaking around them. There is usually no traffic, and is covered mostly by Generation 4 blue car.

title: Brazil - Amazonas 319 (Plonkit)
description: The Amazonas 319 has a very lush, bright green and tropical landscape, as it cuts through the Amazon rainforest. The road is flat and mostly unpaved, featuring bright orange soil. However, closer to Manaus the road becomes paved. There are wooden or ladder poles alongside the entire stretch. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

title: Brazil - Dry Hills (Plonkit)
description: The Pará section of the 163 is often hilly, curvy, dry, and sometimes hazy. It has a wide range of amazonian vegetation. The road is frequently trafficked, usually by transportation trucks. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car in the north and the Smallcam car in the south.

title: Brazil - Sao Paulo Pole ID (Plonkit)
description: São Paulo has a square, yellow pole ID paint. It has three letters on top followed by two numbers, a black line, and four more numbers. The three letters represent the municipality within São Paulo, but are rarely visible.

title: Brazil - Wrapped Sticker Signs (Plonkit)
description: Street signs in Campo Grande and Joinville are stickers wrapped around a pole at intersections. Campo Grande signs usually have extra information and a red and yellow stripe.

title: Brazil - Rio Curved Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Lamps in Rio de Janeiro are curved through the whole of the lamp arm, which is not seen anywhere else.

title: Brazil - Teresina Blue Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Teresina lamps are usually blue with an orange arm.

title: Brazil - Belem Orange Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Belém lamp heads are often orange.

title: Brazil - Cuiaba Green Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Cuiaba lamps are usually a light green, and is one of the few cities that has poles with multiple electricity metres, sometimes 6 to 12.

title: Brazil - MG Numbered Plaques (Plonkit)
description:
Lamps in Belo Horizonte and Uberaba in Generation 4 can have a white, numbered plaque attached to the lamp. In Belo Horizonte, the tag starts with 0 or 1, and in Uberaba, it starts with a 1 or 2.
Since this plaque is new, it may appear in other cities in Minas Gerais in the future.

title: Brazil - Caxias do Sul Zig-Zag Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Lamps in Caxias do Sul usually have a zig-zag bent pole and a yellow head.

title: Brazil - Florianopolis Pole Stripes (Plonkit)
description: Poles on Santa Catarina Island (Florianópolis) are painted white with blue and red stripes.

title: Brazil - Alagoas Rifts (Plonkit)
description: You can often see rifts in Alagoas Generation 3 coverage.

title: Brazil - NW Rio Grande glitch (Plonkit)
description: Northwest Rio Grande do Sul has coverage with this camera glitch in Generation 3.

title: Brazil - Amazonian Boat Trekker (Plonkit)
description: This Amazonian trekker combines boat and walking coverage on and near the Madeira and Aripuana rivers, south of the 319. They are seen travelling through dense rainforest and small villages.

title: Brazil - Maranhao National Park (Plonkit)
description: The beautiful National Park of Northeast Maranhão, known for its sand dunes with pools of water, has walking trekker and vehicle coverage. The truck is white with a black bed. The landscape can vary from beach to sandy wetland.

title: Brazil - Fernando de Noronha (Plonkit)
description: Ilha de Fernando de Noronha is a Brazilian island with official coverage approximately 340 kilometres northeast of Rio Grande do Norte, and the country itself. It is covered by a white buggy, which is visible at the front. The island is similar in vegetation to the closest part of mainland Brazil, and has large exposed rocks. There is also boat coverage around the island.

title: Brazil - Portuguese Language (Plonkit)
description: Portuguese is spoken in Brazil, as opposed to most Latin American countries which speak Spanish. Compared to Spanish, some essential differences are that Portuguese uses -ão rather than -ón, -ch instead of -ll and -nh instead of -ñ.

title: Brazil - Carnauba Palms (Plonkit)
description: Carnaúba palms have short but strong, fan-like leaves and a trunk that is smooth at the top and spiked at the bottom. They are common in Ceará but are also in Piauí and Rio Grande do Norte.

title: Brazil - Moriche Palms (Plonkit)
description: Moriche palms have leaves with a rounded fan shape. They are most common in Amazonas, Acre, and Roraima, but can be found in all of the Amazonian states.

title: Brazil - Piaui Red Gravel (Plonkit)
description: Most roads in Piauí have red gravel on the side of the road. Some roads in Generation 4 now have tarmac and kerbs, but some gravel shoulders remain.

title: Brazil - Acre 364 Rollercoaster (Plonkit)
description: The 364 through Acre is very recognisable due to the rollercoaster-like landscape and road: the road uniquely rides the hills rather than snaking around them. There is usually no traffic, and is covered mostly by Generation 3 with an antenna.

title: Brazil - Para 163 (Plonkit)
description: The Pará section of the 163 is often hilly, curvy, dry, and sometimes hazy. It has a wide range of amazonian vegetation. The road is frequently trafficked, usually by transportation trucks. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

title: Chile - Road Line Colors (Plonkit)
description:
Chilean road lines are either all white, or all yellow:
- All white road lines are most common. Within the Americas, they are a good clue for Chile, though not completely unique.
- All yellow road lines are seen in National Parks or areas of high snowfall. Within the Americas, these all yellow road lines are essentially unique to Chile.
You will almost never see a combination of the two colours, apart from a few rare exceptions.

title: Chile - Gen 3 Car Variants (Plonkit)
description:
Chile has a solid white Google Car with no antenna in Generation 3. There are two variants:
- A plain white car (left).
- A white car with a visible black section (right). This car is unique to Chile.
A blue Google Car can be seen in Generation 4.

title: Chile - Square Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Chile uses square concrete poles with an indent on both sides. They are somewhat similar to Brazilian poles, however have fewer horizontal supports in the indent. The upper part typically has small pinholes.
Wooden poles are also fairly common.

title: Chile - License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Regular vehicles have white licence plates, while commercial and taxi vehicles have orange plates.

title: Chile - Slotted Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Slots can often be seen at the top of signposts.

title: Chile - Yellow-Black Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Chile uses chevrons with a yellow base and black arrows.

title: Chile - Standard Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Chilean bollards are similar to Spanish style bollards, with a white reflector at the front and a yellow-orange reflector at the back. They are not super common.

title: Chile - Temporary Bollards (Plonkit)
description: While regular bollards are somewhat rare in Chile, you may sometimes find this orange, temporary bollard, with two white stripes at the top.

title: Chile - Red Fence Posts (Plonkit)
description: Bridges in Chile often have red painted fence posts.

title: Chile - Climate Map (Plonkit)
description:
Shown here is a Köppen climate map of Chile.
Chile is a long and narrow country that spans more than 4,000 kilometres from north to south, meaning that its climate varies significantly due to latitude.
The northern parts of the country, which lie in the tropical zone, are dry and arid, leading to a mild desert climate. In the centre, around the capital, the climate becomes less arid, leading to a temperate mediterranean climate. In the southernmost regions of Chile, which lie in the subantarctic zone, the climate is cold and wet, leading to a cool oceanic climate.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Chile - Road Naming System (Plonkit)
description: Chile uses a memorable regional road naming system, where the first letter increases between A and Y from north to south. For more information on specific regions, see here.

title: Chile - Phone Area Codes (Plonkit)
description: Chilean phone codes will sometimes have a two digit area code in front, followed by seven digits. The patterns of the codes are easily memorable. Most of the central states also have different area codes for specific provinces, which can help you make accurate guesses.

title: Chile - Atacama Desert (Plonkit)
description: The Atacama is an extremely arid desert covering the northern third of Chile. Some parts of it experience the lowest rainfall on the planet. As a result, many locations in this desert are almost completely devoid of any vegetation: you will often just see sand and bare rock without any plants in sight anywhere.

title: Chile - Arica Smooth Mountains (Plonkit)
description: The region of Arica y Parinacota can be recognized by the smooth, sandy mountains that may look slightly eroded, or have bulbous formations. Valleys are also common, which are rarely seen in other parts of Chile.

title: Chile - Atacama Rocky Mountains (Plonkit)
description: These rocky, uneven mountains are most commonly seen in Atacama and northern Coquimbo.

title: Chile - Atacama Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: This brownish red soil can sometimes be seen in Atacama region.

title: Chile - Valparaiso Eucalyptus (Plonkit)
description: Eucalyptus plantations combined with a somewhat dry climate are a good indicator that you are in southwestern Valparaíso.

title: Chile - Santiago Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The region around Santiago can be recognized by its semi-arid climate, having dry hills and scattered vegetation.

title: Chile - Maule Vineyards (Plonkit)
description: Compared to the area around Santiago, the Maule region has a similar look. However, it has a Mediterranean climate, and is generally greener. Vineyards are also commonly seen in this region.

title: Chile - Concepcion Pines (Plonkit)
description: Concepcion pines, scientifically named Pinus radiata, can be recognized by their puffy needles. They are most commonly found in Bio Bio, where the city of Concepcion is located, and less commonly in Ñuble and Araucania.

title: Chile - Narrow Tree-Lined Roads (Plonkit)
description: Narrow roads with trees on both sides can commonly be seen in the regions of Bio Bio and Araucania.

title: Chile - Monkey Puzzles (Plonkit)
description: Monkey puzzles, scientifically named Araucaria araucana, are found in far eastern Araucania.

title: Chile - Chiloe Agriculture (Plonkit)
description: A rolling, agricultural landscape, comparable to New Zealand, can be seen on Isla Grande de Chiloé.

title: Chile - Chilean Rhubarb (Plonkit)
description: Chilean rhubarb can commonly be found on Isla Grande, and on the mainland east of it. Chilean rhubarb can be recognized by its large, cabbage-like appearance.

title: Chile - Southern Valleys (Plonkit)
description: Lush green valleys, with rocky mountains and often overcast coverage, can be seen in southern Los Lagos and northern Aysén.

title: Chile - Aysen Autumn Colors (Plonkit)
description: Southern Aysén can be recognised by autumn coverage, having orange and red coloured vegetation. Keep in mind that not all coverage in this region will have fall colours.

title: Chile - Los Features (Plonkit)
description: Roadlines with dotted paint are common in Los Ríos and Aysén.

title: Chile - A-31 High Altitude (Plonkit)
description: The A-31 can be recognised by its high altitude, with a steep drop into a valley to the north. The road also has Gen 3 sunset coverage.

title: Chile - Ruta 21 Sunset (Plonkit)
description: Generation 4 sunset coverage can be seen on Ruta 21 from Calama to San Francisco de Chiu Chiu. In the west near Calama, the sun has just started to set, causing a giant white dome in the sky. In the east, the sky has a warm gradient, and the tops of the volcanoes are seen glowing pink.

title: Chile - B-710 Sunset (Plonkit)
description:
More Generation 4 Sunset coverage can be seen on B-710 and Ruta 5.
On the B-710, a slight ridge can be seen to the west, while Ruta 5 is more open. Make sure to use the road angle or other clues before guessing.

title: Chile - Ruta 1 Coast (Plonkit)
description:
Ruta 1 is a coastal road that is easily recognized by the wall of mountains to the east, and the Pacific Ocean to the west. This image shows the various weather conditions faced on the road to help you make closer guesses.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Chile - Ruta 41 Valley (Plonkit)
description: Part of Ruta 41 is located in a valley, with snowy mountains seen in the distance. Many trees and vineyards can commonly be seen toward the west. Triple yellow lines can also be seen from this point.

title: Chile - Large-leaved Lupines (Plonkit)
description: These purple flowers, named Large-leaved Lupines, can commonly be found along Ruta 240.

title: Chile - Magallanes Yellow Lines (Plonkit)
description: All yellow lines on a concrete road are a good indicator that you are on a paved road in the Magallanes region, in the very south of Chile. The landscape tends to be barren, grassy, and treeless.

title: Chile - Lauca National Park (Plonkit)
description: A distinct landscape consisting of a line of snow-capped mountains with two other isolated, symmetrical snow-capped volcanoes are seen in Lauca National Park. Most of the roads are newly paved and have a smooth, dark look.

title: Chile - Pampa del Tamarugal (Plonkit)
description: The northern section of Pampa del Tamarugal National Reserve can be recognized by the Tamarugo trees lining the road. The road itself is mediocre quality, and in a consistent north-west direction.

title: Chile - Alto Loa Reserve (Plonkit)
description: Alto Loa National Reserve can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to snow-capped volcanoes. The road running through the reserve is paved.

title: Chile - Los Flamencos Reserve (Plonkit)
description: Smooth mountains with a reddish tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines, with short dashes in the west.

title: Chile - Nevado Tres Cruces (Plonkit)
description:
In the west, Nevado Tres Cruces National Park can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to a line of mountains. The sand has a reddish tint.
In the east, the Google Car drives up a mountain pass with views of lightly snow-capped volcanoes and snow on the side of the road. The roads in the National Park are paved.

title: Chile - Llanos de Challe (Plonkit)
description: Llanos de Challe National Park can be recognized by the brown coloured dirt on the roadside, patches of light sand, juniper plants, and dark coloured mountains. The sky is overcast in most of the coverage.

title: Chile - Alto Bio Bio (Plonkit)
description: A vast, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and high altitude feel. Monkey puzzles are also seen toward the east.

title: Chile - Puyehue National Park (Plonkit)
description: Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and tar snakes are frequently seen. In the east, many dead trees can be seen with a lack of leaves.

title: Chile - Arica Sandy Ridge (Plonkit)
description: A slight, sandy ridge with a gradual incline can be seen in Arica.

title: Chile - Iquique Towering Ridge (Plonkit)
description: A larger, towering ridge can be seen in Iquique.

title: Chile - Antofagasta Uneven Ridge (Plonkit)
description: A rockier, and more uneven ridge can be seen in Antofagasta.

title: Chile - San Pedro Adobe Walls (Plonkit)
description: San Pedro de Atacama can be recognized by its clay brick walls, commonly with triangles at the top.

title: Chile - Lanco Orange Signs (Plonkit)
description: Orange street signs can be seen at almost every intersection in the city of Lanco, and occasionally in the nearby town of Malalhue.

title: Chile - Villa O'Higgins Wood (Plonkit)
description: Villa O’Higgins can be recognized by the large mountains located immediately to the east. To the west, snow-capped mountains are seen in the distance. Street signs, fences and many other structures throughout the village are made of orange-stained wood.

title: Chile - Orange Lamp Cities (Plonkit)
description: Orange lamps can most often be seen in Calama and Chañaral, and rarely in Antofagasta.

title: Chile - Copiapo Green Domes (Plonkit)
description: Lamps that look like green domes can be seen in Copiapo.

title: Chile - Santiago Photocells (Plonkit)
description: Lamps in Santiago very commonly have photocells. You will rarely find them in other cities such as Valparaiso, Osorno and Loncoche.

title: Chile - Talca Grey Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Grey lamps with a thin, flat top and a rounded underside can be found in Talca.

title: Chile - Concepcion Blue Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Blue rectangular lamps with a yellow stripe can be found in Concepción.

title: Chile - Silver Top Lamps (Plonkit)
description: This lamp, with a silver top and grey bottom, can be found in Puerto Montt and Temuco.

title: Chile - Atacama Pole Colors (Plonkit)
description: Poles in Arica feature white paint with a black number, while the other cities in the Atacama Desert feature poles with yellow paint. Keep in mind the paint may have faded, making it look white.

title: Chile - El Salvador Black Poles (Plonkit)
description: Round poles with black paint can be seen in the town of El Salvador.

title: Chile - Santiago Zoo Car (Plonkit)
description: The Google car can be seen towing a white and silver trailer with the word ‘Outback’ south of the Chilean National Zoo in Santiago.

title: Chile - Banos Morales Trekker (Plonkit)
description: A grey Toyota Hilux, with various gear loaded and a snorkel on the front right, can be seen from around Baños Morales to this point, where the trekker continues the journey on foot.

title: Chile - Conguillio White Truck (Plonkit)
description: Conguillio National Park can be recognized by this white truck with visible side mirrors and an antenna on the front right.

title: Chile - Puerto Williams Pickup (Plonkit)
description: Puerto Williams, the southernmost town covered by street view, can be recognized by this white pickup truck with visible side mirrors.

title: Chile - ALMA Radio Telescopes (Plonkit)
description: The Atacama Large Millimetre Array can be recognized by the many radio telescopes in a barren, snowy environment.

title: Chile - ALMA OSF Facilities (Plonkit)
description: ALMA OSF can be recognized by the large radio telescopes and rural facilities.

title: Chile - San Felipe Horse Trekker (Plonkit)
description: This horse trekker can be seen to the northeast of San Felipe.

title: Chile - Torres del Paine (Plonkit)
description: The Torres del Paine area can be recognized by the sharp peaked mountains, and the trekker walking on a glacier along with other people in orange helmets.

title: Colombia - Yellow License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Colombian licence plates are typically yellow.

title: Colombia - Antenna Car Variants (Plonkit)
description: In Generation 3 coverage, a short thick antenna is sometimes visible with a black, white or grey car. In Generation 4 coverage, a white or silver car is commonly found.

title: Colombia - White Cross Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Signposts in Colombia are made of white metal, and join to form a distinct cross on the back of signs.

title: Colombia - Kilometre Markers (Plonkit)
description: Colombia uses two types of kilometre markers: a tall green version with the letters “Pr” at the top, and the traditional stone marker with black lettering. Both designs are unique to the country.

title: Colombia - Striped Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description: Colombian poles are often marked with unique black-and-yellow or black-and-orange stripes.

title: Colombia - Wooden Fences (Plonkit)
description: Wooden fences are particularly common in Colombia.

title: Colombia - Yellow Taxis (Plonkit)
description: Colombian taxis are always this pastel yellow colour. As opposed to private vehicles, they have white licence plates, which are often printed on the side and roof. If unblurred, you will often see the city name.

title: Colombia - Concrete Pole Tops (Plonkit)
description:
Colombian poles are generally concrete with a variety of pole tops.
Moreover, dark-coloured poles are more common in Colombia than in neighbouring countries.

title: Colombia - Red Tiled Sidewalks (Plonkit)
description: In Colombia, it is particularly common for sidewalks to be decorated with reddish tiles.

title: Colombia - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description: Coverage in Colombia is mainly found in the north and west. The islands of Providencia and San Andrés, northwest of the mainland, also have coverage.

title: Colombia - Northern Arid Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The Northern part of the country is characterised by white, sandy soil and an arid landscape.

title: Colombia - Llanos Landscape (Plonkit)
description: East of the Andes lies a vast lowland called Llanos. It is characterised by open tropical grasslands, savannas with scattered trees, small areas of forest and seasonal flooding.

title: Colombia - Antioquia Pole Stripes (Plonkit)
description: These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.

title: Colombia - Pacific Coast Population (Plonkit)
description: As a result of slave trade, the Pacific coast of Colombia is home to an overwhelming majority of Afro-Colombians.

title: Colombia - Valle Sugarcane (Plonkit)
description: Sugar cane is grown along the Cauca river in Valle del Cauca and neighbouring departments.

title: Colombia - Southern Saturation Glitch (Plonkit)
description: A camera glitch that makes a part of the image look very saturated can be found in southern Colombia.

title: Colombia - La Guajira Landscape (Plonkit)
description:
This landscape is typical of the far Northern province of La Guajira: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti.
In addition, you can often recognise the Uribia-Puerto Bolivar road because of this landscape, the straightness and the train track always present to the East.

title: Colombia - Ruta 90 Landbridge (Plonkit)
description: You can recognise the narrow Ruta 90 landbridge between Barranquilla and Cienaga thanks to the dashed yellow lines and shallow bodies of water next to the road. Open ocean can often be seen to the north.

title: Colombia - Barranquilla Mojones (Plonkit)
description: Intersections in the coastal city of Barranquilla are commonly marked by small concrete poles (mojones) bearing street names. For example, this image was taken at the intersection of Carrera 42 and Calle 68.

title: Colombia - Leticia Vehicle (Plonkit)
description: This unique vehicle can be found in and around Leticia, the Southernmost town in Colombia.

title: Colombia - San Andres Car (Plonkit)
description: Coverage on the Caribbean island of San Andrés was taken by this distinct white car.

title: Colombia - Providencia Truck (Plonkit)
description: The island of Providencia, located roughly 90 kilometres North of San Andrés, is home to this unique grey truck.

title: Colombia - Providencia Street Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Providencia street lights are green and supported by a trapezoidal sheet of metal underneath.

title: Curaçao - Curacao Location (Plonkit)
description: Curaçao is a constituent country in the Kingdom of the Netherlands located north of western Venezuela in the Caribbean Sea. As such, for country streaks purposes, it is counted as the Netherlands.

title: Curaçao - Square White Plates (Plonkit)
description: Curaçao uses square licence plates that appear completely white through the blur.

title: Curaçao - Black Roof Rack Car (Plonkit)
description: This black car with a roof rack is unique to Curaçao.

title: Curaçao - Cacti Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Due to Curaçao’s semi-arid climate, cacti can commonly be seen.

title: Curaçao - Pastel Bungalows (Plonkit)
description: Much of the architecture on Curaçao consists of simple, one storey bungalows that are pastel coloured. Metal roofs are common on smaller shacks, while tiled roofs can be seen on more expensive houses. Additionally, multi storey villas can sometimes be seen.

title: Curaçao - Coloured Sign Backs (Plonkit)
description: The coloured border or road signs can typically be seen continuing onto the back of the signs. These will generally be red or blue.

title: Curaçao - Blue Street Signs (Plonkit)
description: Blue street signs attached to the top of yellow signposts are common in Curaçao.

title: Curaçao - Striped Traffic Posts (Plonkit)
description: White and black striped traffic light posts can be seen in urban areas.

title: Curaçao - Wooden Poles (Plonkit)
description: Wooden poles with three horizontal, alternating insulators are common.

title: Curaçao - Western Curacao Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The western half of Curaçao is characterised by a semi-arid rural landscape with green, but dry hills. Houses are spread apart, with the roads in the west quite narrow in width.

title: Curaçao - Wind Farm (Plonkit)
description: A line of wind turbines can be seen at this wind farm toward the southeast of Curaçao. The coverage is also notably rainy.

title: Curaçao - Queen Juliana Bridge (Plonkit)
description: The Queen Juliana Bridge is a wide four lane bridge in Willemstad. It can be recognised by the yellow and blue guardrails, and the view over the city.

title: Curaçao - Grote Berg Located (Plonkit)
description: Grote Berg, located in the centre of the island, can be recognised by the stick stuck to the front of the camera lens.

title: Curaçao - Queen Juliana Bridge (Plonkit)
description: The Queen Juliana Bridge is a wide four lane bridge in Willemstad. It can be recognized by the yellow and blue guardrails, and the view over the city.

title: Ecuador - License Plates
description:
The standard licence plates are white and can be short or long. In street view, you will often see a mix of both sizes.
Commercial vehicles, such as taxis or buses, can have older solid orange plates, or newer ones with an orange bar at the top.

*Ecuador is the only country in Latin America to use a mix of short and long licence plates.*

title: Ecuador - Gen4 Coverage
description:
All Gen4 coverage was captured using a white pickup truck with a black trunk and no antenna.

*The pickup truck in Panama and Costa Rica has an antenna on the front.*

title: Ecuador - Shitcam
description:
Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Ecuador.
This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”).
It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours.
You will sometimes see a unique red logo at the front of the car.

*Within Latin America, Ecuador is the only country that has shitcam coverage.*

title: Ecuador - Bollards
description:
Ecuador is one of the few Latin American countries where bollards are very common.
You will find two main types of bollards:
- A round bollard with two red stripes,
- A flat bollard with two red reflectors on black.

Many other bollards can be found, however, they will almost always have the same colour scheme and style.

*A similar rectangular bollard can sometimes be found in Malaysia.*

title: Ecuador - Double Guardrails
description:
**Double guardrails** are very commonly used.
This is much less common in other South American countries.

title: Ecuador - Chevron Spam
description:
Ecuador often uses a lot of chevrons in road curves (“chevron spam”), usually considerably more than most other Latin American countries.

*Colombia also occasionally uses a lot of chevrons in curves.*

title: Ecuador - Road Signs
description: Ecuador uses a lot of **square road signs with a white background**, of the design shown in the image.

title: Ecuador - Kilometre Markers
description: Kilometre markers are green and have the distinctive Ecuadorian **highway shields** on them.

title: Ecuador - Sign Backs
description:
Sometimes, the back of the signs are painted a teal blue colour.
The signposts are thin and made of metal.

*Ecuador is the only country in Latin America to use teal blue sign backs.*

title: Ecuador - Way Signs
description:
Ecuador uses these signs to indicate one or two-way streets. 

*The Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico are the only two other Latin American countries to use similar signs with text inside the arrow.*

title: Ecuador - Houses
description:
Most houses are made of grey bricks and have metal roofs.

*This is not unique to Ecuador, but is very common. Countries such as Peru, and especially Bolivia, commonly use red bricks.*

title: Ecuador - Hexagonal Pavement
description: In urban areas, you can sometimes find this pavement consisting of **hexagonal tiles**.

title: Ecuador - Banana Plants
description: **Banana plants**, and especially plantations, are most commonly found in the southwestern part of the country.

title: Ecuador - Dry Coastal Landscape
description: This **extremely dry landscape** is only found in the coastal region between Guayaquil and Manta.

title: Ecuador - Flat Landscape
description:
The **flattest region** is located around the city of Guayaquil.
This is most easily seen on the **E-25** and **E-48**.

title: Ecuador - Brownish Red Dirt
description:
The southern regions have many winding **mountain roads** and **exposed brownish red dirt**.
The central provinces can have similar roads, but the exposed dirt will usually not be found in these areas.

title: Ecuador - Chimborazo Landscape
description: The province of Chimborazo is **semi-arid**, and has an **abundance of pine trees**.

title: Ecuador - Guayas Guardrails
description: Guardrails are often **painted black-and-yellow**, as opposed to the generic silver or solid yellow versions.

title: Ecuador - E-40 Highway
description: The **E-40 between Salinas and Guayaquil** is one of the only **divided highways**, and the only one in the **dry area** near the southwestern coast.

title: Ecuador - Roadside Pipes
description: In the northeast of Ecuador you can find **metal pipes along some of the roads**

title: Ecuador - Galapagos Islands
description: The Galapagos Islands are an archipelago located west of mainland Ecuador. There are only trekkers and boat coverage on and around the islands. There is a wide variety of landscapes, including volcanic soil, low shrubbery, and craters (with Galapagos turtles onlooking).

title: Ecuador - Gen3 Coverage
description:
All **Gen3 coverage** is made with a **white car, with a short and thick antenna** (“stubby antenna”).
The antenna and or car are not always visible.

**This antenna on a black car** can only be found in **Colombia**, which can help with tough 50-50s with **Ecuador**.
Note that Colombia can also simply have a white car.

*Mexico, Brazil and Colombia can also have this same short antenna.*

title: Falkland Islands - Gen 3 Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
The Falkland Islands are a British Overseas Territory east of the Tierra del Fuego Province of Argentina. As such, for country streaks purposes, it is counted as the UK.
Coverage is very limited: there are only a couple of Generation 3 trekkers. The trekkers are all located on and around three islands in the western part of the territory:
- Carcass Island
- West Point Island
- New Island
Due to the sparse nature of the coverage, that is also entirely not on any streets, it is not useful to learn any territory identification metas. Instead, it is better to just memorise what the trekkers look like.

title: Falkland Islands - Carcass Island (Plonkit)
description: The Carcass Island trekker can be recognized by the open plains, with the ocean clearly visible. The ground may also get rocky.

title: Falkland Islands - West Point Island (Plonkit)
description: Open plains with slightly yellow grass can be seen on West Point Island. The ocean will not be clearly visible on this trekker.

title: Falkland Islands - Boat Trekker (Plonkit)
description: This boat trekker can be seen in the West Point Bay, with yellow hills in the distance with the MS National Geographic Explorer in the bay with the trekker.

title: Falkland Islands - New Island Beach (Plonkit)
description: This sandy beach with other people in red and blue jackets can be seen on New Island.

title: Falkland Islands - Inland New Island (Plonkit)
description: Inland New Island can be recognized by the dark brown soil. Tire tracks may also be visible.

title: Falkland Islands - New Island Cliffs (Plonkit)
description: Distinct steep cliffs can be seen on New Island.

title: Peru - Yellow License Plates (Plonkit)
description:
Peruvian licence plates are either white or yellow. In contrast to the white plates, yellow plates are less likely to be seen.
Additionally, taxis in Peru typically use licence plates that are yellow on the top and white on the bottom.

title: Peru - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
In Gen 3 coverage, Peru uses a solid black or white Google car.
- The black Google car is only found in Peru, Argentina and Uruguay.
- The white Google car is only found in Peru, Bolivia and Chile.

title: Peru - Large Pickup Truck (Plonkit)
description: An important thing to note is that Peru has Generation 4 Street View coverage, whereas the neighbouring country of Bolivia does not. While Ecuador does have some Generation 4 coverage, it will always have a large pickup truck.

title: Peru - Smallcam Coverage (Plonkit)
description: Peru also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front.

title: Peru - Road Line Standards (Plonkit)
description: Peruvian roads always have white outer lines. On highways, you will find either single yellow dashed or double yellow middle lines. On rural mountain roads, you will most likely see white outer lines without any centre line. On divided highways, the road lines may be completely white in colour.

title: Peru - Striped Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Peru is the only South American country to use black-and-white striped signposts. In some areas, black-and-yellow signposts can be seen.

title: Peru - Triangular Bollards (Plonkit)
description: Bollards in Peru are painted red or yellow, and the country mainly uses a variety of triangular-shaped concrete bollards. Occasionally you will also spot other designs, such as these circular concrete variants.

title: Peru - Striped Guardrails (Plonkit)
description: Black-and-yellow stripes on guardrails are seen throughout the country. You might sometimes find different designs, such as this sharp arrow design.

title: Peru - Concrete Markers (Plonkit)
description: Kilometre markers in Peru are made out of concrete and are painted black and white.

title: Peru - Signpost Concrete Base (Plonkit)
description: Peruvian metal signposts feature concrete blocks at the bottom.

title: Peru - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description: The country uses a variety of poles. They are made out of either concrete or wood, and sometimes feature distinct horizontal concrete bars.

title: Peru - Painted Poles (Plonkit)
description: Some poles in Peru have painted bottom sections. Most commonly they will be black or black-and-yellow.

title: Peru - Orange Bridges (Plonkit)
description: Bridges in Peru are commonly painted orange.

title: Peru - Semi-Arid Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Peru largely consists of semi-arid mountain ranges and valleys.

title: Peru - Mototaxis (Plonkit)
description: Tuk tuks, called mototaxis in Peru, are frequently seen in the country, especially in major cities such as Lima, Trujillo, Chiclayo, Piura, and Iquitos.

title: Peru - Red White Stickers (Plonkit)
description: Wide red and white stickers will typically be attached to the side of taxis and commercial vehicles.

title: Peru - Electricity Meters (Plonkit)
description: Peruvian electricity counters have a unique design: They are rectangular, metallic, and typically feature two or three horizontal slits.

title: Peru - Currency Sol (Plonkit)
description: Sol is the currency of Peru. You will occasionally spot it on street view and its symbol is S/.

title: Peru - Political Party Logos (Plonkit)
description: Peru has many political party logos and all of them are unique to the country. Here is a list with other parties in Peru.

title: Peru - Architecture Variety (Plonkit)
description:
Peru is home to diverse and somewhat unique architecture. Here are a few examples of types of buildings commonly seen in Peru; ranging from Colonial-era buildings, contemporary “boxy” buildings, and traditional red brick buildings.
Some of these styles are broken down further in Step 2 of this guide.

title: Peru - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Street View coverage in Peru is mostly located in the west and on main highways. There are some exceptions in the east near Iquitos and along the 30C.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Peru - Piura Desert (Plonkit)
description:
The country is generally flat in the east and mountainous in the west. However, an exception is the often flat desert near Piura in the northwest.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Peru - Climate Map (Plonkit)
description:
Peru has a diverse climate, dominated by a dry desert in the west, and a tropical rainforest in the east.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Peru - Highway Numbering (Plonkit)
description:
Highways in Peru are mainly located in the west, and the numbers increase from north to south. The 1, 3 and 5 are the longest and traverse through multiple departments.
You can click on the image to enlarge it.

title: Peru - Tumbes Landscape (Plonkit)
description: These three landscapes are typically found along offroads in Tumbes. You will always see sandy soil with either green or withered bushes.

title: Peru - Piura Southwest (Plonkit)
description: The southwestern landscape of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is mostly flat, but you will sometimes see rolling hills.

title: Peru - Piura Northwest (Plonkit)
description: Northwest of the city of Piura lies an area with similar vegetation to the area mentioned previously. However, this area is noticeably hillier.

title: Peru - Coastal Palms (Plonkit)
description: Coconut palms (and other species of tall palms) can sometimes be seen in coastal areas of Peru, mainly north of Lima. They are mainly found in the agricultural areas which are typically found around the major coastal cities.

title: Peru - Tacna Olives (Plonkit)
description: Olive tree plantations can be found in the far southern region of Tacna.

title: Peru - Sugar Cane Fields (Plonkit)
description: Most of the sugar cane production is found in the northern coastal regions of Peru near the cities of Chiclayo and Trujillo. Typically you see large fields of sugar cane in these areas. Smaller areas of sugar cane can be found further south in other valleys close to the Pacific coast.

title: Peru - Northern Banana Plants (Plonkit)
description: Similarly to sugar cane plants, banana plants are generally found in agricultural regions adjacent to the coast in the northern half of the country.

title: Peru - Puno Flat Mountains (Plonkit)
description: A flat landscape in the mountains of Peru is usually seen in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.

title: Peru - South Titicaca Landscape (Plonkit)
description: Low grass, a few hills, stone walls in villages and brown brick buildings are typical for the region south of Lake Titicaca in eastern Peru.

title: Peru - Northern Shrubby Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Far north Peru features mountains that are often covered in shrubby trees and bushes. Closer to the coast and the Ecuador border, these mountains are often quite dry in appearance.

title: Peru - High Elevation Pines (Plonkit)
description: Pine plantations are typically found in higher elevation areas of the country, away from the coastal deserts and Amazonian Regions. The most common types of pine trees planted are Pinus radiata and Pinus patula.

title: Peru - Tarapoto Landscape (Plonkit)
description: The areas adjacent to the northern Amazonian city of Tarapoto feature moderately tall foliage-covered mountains and can bear a similar resemblance to the hilly areas of Colombia or Brazil.

title: Peru - Rocky Outcrops (Plonkit)
description: In higher elevation areas near the centre of the country, exposed rocky outcroppings are commonly seen in the sides of hills and mountains. Some areas with the highest concentrations are near Lago Chinchaycocha (Junin District) stretching south towards the city of Ayacucho.

title: Peru - Spiky Mountains (Plonkit)
description: Similarly, taller mountains near the middle of the country often feature rocky and sharp mountain tops. The main region of these mountains stretches from near the city of Huaraz southward to the city of Cusco; generally away from the coast.

title: Peru - Green Lichen Rocks (Plonkit)
description: Patches of light green lichen can be seen covering rocks and growing on the ground in high elevation areas of central and southern Peru.

title: Peru - Dark Red Soil (Plonkit)
description: Dark red-tinted soil is found in several areas of Peru. Some notable areas include the areas near Cusco and Ayacucho in the south of the country, as well as areas near the northern cities of Cajamarca and Tarapoto. It can be found to a lesser extent in adjacent regions.

title: Peru - Southern Desert (Plonkit)
description: Areas near the cities of Ica, Arequipa, and Tacna feature barren and mostly flat desert landscapes that can resemble areas of northern Chile. You can typically see mountains in the distance, primarily while looking to the east.

title: Peru - Coastal Dry Valleys (Plonkit)
description: Coastal agricultural valleys in the middle and south are commonly sandwiched between dry mountains with no vegetation. The general orientation of these valleys are southwest-northeast.

title: Peru - Titicaca Brick Houses (Plonkit)
description: As a general rule, the closer you are to Lake Titicaca in Peru, houses and buildings made out of red brick become more common. This type of architecture resembles the predominant type of building seen in parts of western Bolivia, which is helpful for remembering where it is seen most commonly. Additionally, buildings with blue tinted glass can be seen most commonly in the same areas.

title: Peru - Northern Overhangs (Plonkit)
description: Buildings with overhanging roofs with wooden supports are mostly found in northern regions of Peru. These buildings are sometimes brightly coloured as well.

title: Peru - Utility Poles (Plonkit)
description:
Pole markings with yellow vertical numbers are commonly found in northern coastal Peru and Tacna.
Oftentimes, but not always, they will be accompanied by a horizontal pole marking starting with a 2 or 3 letter code corresponding to a city. For example, this horizontal sticker starts with CH for Chimbote.

title: Peru - Open Front Tuktuks (Plonkit)
description: Tuk-Tuks with open front compartments are primarily found in the northern half of Peru, and are especially common in northern Amazonian adjacent regions.

title: Peru - Street Lamps (Plonkit)
description:
Lamp posts in Lima and Lima Department often have a distinct, sweeping curve at the top, resembling an inverted "J" shape.
For other, more specific patterns, please see this document.

title: Peru - Moquegua Bollard (Plonkit)
description: This cylindrical bollard, with a black and yellow stripe at the top, is unique to the state of Moquegua, which is located in the south of Peru.

title: Peru - 1N Overcast Gen 3 (Plonkit)
description: The 1N near the Piura and Lambayeque border has a distinct looking landscape. It features a semidesert landscape and has overcast coverage in Generation 3. The new Generation 4 is drier but still looks somewhat similar.

title: Peru - Divided Highway 1 (Plonkit)
description: Highway 1N/S is divided in the highlighted area on the map.

title: Peru - 1S Coastal Desert (Plonkit)
description: The 1S south of the city of Ica is not divided and mostly follows the coast. The soil is often red or orange in these areas, and there is little-to-no vegetation. This road is also entirely covered with the Generation 4 camera.

title: Peru - Ruta 5N Rainforest (Plonkit)
description: Ruta 5N between the towns of San Alejandro and Esperanza is a relatively straight, flat road in good condition. This road primarily runs north-south through the rainforest.

title: Peru - Ruta 30C Gen 3 (Plonkit)
description: Ruta 30C in eastern Peru uses a white Street View car in Generation 3 between the cities of Planchon and Iñapari. It features dense forest, few villages, and resembles interior areas of Brazil. Some of this area has been overwritten with Generation 4. Most of this segment runs north to south.

title: Peru - Ruta 28B Valley (Plonkit)
description: Ruta 28B between the towns of Kimbiri and Echarate is a paved road with very faded or missing road lines. It is also characterised by being a relatively small road with Generation 4 coverage, which hugs the hillside and is located next to a river valley.

title: Peru - Jauja Huancayo Valley (Plonkit)
description: The valley connecting the cities of Jauja and Huancayo features a flat plain with plentiful trees, agricultural areas, and small villages. North-south oriented mountains can be seen on both edges of the valley.

title: Peru - Titicaca North Season (Plonkit)
description: The coverage on the north side of Lake Titicaca was taken during a significantly wetter season than the coverage taken on the south side of Lake Titicaca.

title: Peru - Lake Chinchaycocha (Plonkit)
description: North of the city of Huancayo lies a shallow lake called Lake Chinchaycocha (also referred to as ‘the middle lake.’). This lake is generally marshy and a range of mountains can be seen to the east of the lake. This lake can look similar to Lake Titicaca, but is generally less densely populated and features fewer trees.

title: Peru - Arequipa Volcanoes (Plonkit)
description: Volcanoes are often seen in and around the city of Arequipa.

title: Peru - Lima Boulevards (Plonkit)
description: Most of the boulevard-type streets in Peru are in the city of Lima. These boulevards are typically long, straight streets divided by concrete or a grassy berm.

title: Peru - Pucallpa Grid (Plonkit)
description: The east-central Amazonian city of Pucallpa, which lies close to the Brazil border, has a consistent street grid of WSW to ENE.

title: Peru - Iquitos Gen 3 (Plonkit)
description: Iquitos is a city in northeast Peru. It is an isolated city with only Generation 3 Street View coverage. Three-wheeled tuk-tuks, overcast skies, and rolling Amazonian landscapes are commonly seen in the area. This coverage is isolated from other areas of northern Peru.

title: Peru - Cusco Architecture (Plonkit)
description: The southern city of Cusco is recognizable by its prevalence of both red brick and Spanish colonial style buildings. Cusco is surrounded by mountains on all sides and features an airport in the middle of the city. Due to its proximity and similar architecture, Cusco superficially resembles the Bolivian city of La Paz.

title: Peru - Tacna Dry Ridge (Plonkit)
description: The city of Tacna in the far south of Peru has this distinct dry ridge to the north.

title: Peru - Motorcycle Taxi Drivers (Plonkit)
description: Motorcycle taxi drivers in the Amazonian city of Puerto Maldonado can often be seen wearing yellow safety vests.

title: Peru - Machu Picchu Car (Plonkit)
description: Within Peru, this white Street View car is found in central Cusco. It drives from the remote town of Aguas Calientes up to Machu Picchu.

title: Peru - Cusco Train Trekker (Plonkit)
description: A train track covered by a trekker is located between Aguas Calientes and Cusco.

title: Peru - Car Colors (Plonkit)
description: In Gen 3 coverage, Peru uses a solid black or white Google car.

title: Peru - Lima Curved Lamps (Plonkit)
description: Lamp posts in Lima and Lima Department often have a distinct, sweeping curve at the top, resembling an inverted "J" shape.

title: Uruguay - Stereotypical Landscape (Plonkit)
description: This is the stereotypical Uruguay round. The coverage often, but not always, features overcast weather. Most of the landscape consists of open grasslands with gentle hills. Occasionally, you might see separated tree plantations. Roads are generally in worse condition than in neighbouring countries.

title: Uruguay - White License Plates (Plonkit)
description: Uruguayan licence plates are plain white with black characters.

title: Uruguay - Gen 3 Coverage (Plonkit)
description:
Uruguay only has Generation 3 coverage. Coverage was taken by a black Google car without an antenna.
The car is not always visible.

title: Uruguay - Smudgy Camera (Plonkit)
description: In a lot of coverage, the camera quality is somewhat smudgy.

title: Uruguay - Thick Wooden Signposts (Plonkit)
description: Uruguay uses thick wooden signposts, which are typically painted white. They often have up to four rectangular notches at the back of the post.

title: Uruguay - Triple Road Lines (Plonkit)
description: Uruguay often has these triple road lines, that consist of double yellow roadlines with white dashes in between. This is a design not seen anywhere else in the Americas.

title: Uruguay - Other Road Lines (Plonkit)
description:
You can also find two other, non-unique road line patterns:
- Yellow-white lines (also found in Argentina)
- Simple white lines (found in many other places).

title: Uruguay - Uruguayan Bollards (Plonkit)
description: These white bollards, with one side often painted yellow, and stone barriers, are specific to Uruguay.

title: Uruguay - Trident Poles (Plonkit)
description: Uruguay uses a handful of different utility poles. One very common and useful one are the so-called trident poles, which get their name from their distinctive pole tops with three insulators that point upwards.

title: Uruguay - Concrete Poles (Plonkit)
description:
You can also see a variety of other pole designs, including:
- Round poles with a pole top consisting of flat metal sheets
- Square concrete poles.
Both of these pole designs are also good clues for Uruguay.
In addition, you might see simple wooden poles with one insulator, as well as very rarely some Argentina-style poles.

title: Uruguay - Red Reflector Guardrails (Plonkit)
description:
Uruguayan guardrails have a small, rectangular yellow or red reflector, which is the same as in Argentina. They can be differentiated by the shape of their support.
In Argentina, the supports are made up of three sides of a rectangle. Uruguayan supports have the same three sides, and additionally parts of the fourth side at the corners.

title: Uruguay - Green Stone Marker (Plonkit)
description: This green-painted stone kilometre marker is unique to Uruguay.

title: Uruguay - Yellow Black Chevrons (Plonkit)
description: Like most of Latin America, chevrons are yellow with black arrows.

title: Uruguay - Hilly Terrain (Plonkit)
description:
As mentioned before, most of Uruguay is slightly hilly, even though the overall elevation is fairly low. Although it is by no means a mountainous country, roads generally have at least a slight incline.
Take note that this hilliness is usually very subtle: don’t expect immense rolling hills in most of the country.

title: Uruguay - Many Parts Uruguay (Plonkit)
description:
In many parts of Uruguay, you can find reddish soil. The tint can range from light pink (pictured here) to deep red.
However, be cautious with using this meta in the inverse way: the absence of this type of soil does not exclude Uruguay, as you can still find a lot of generic white and brown soil throughout the country.

title: Uruguay - Boxy Concrete Houses (Plonkit)
description: Many Uruguayan houses are made out of concrete, and are somewhat cube-shaped. Walls often have drab colours and tend to look weathered. Flat roofs are relatively common.

title: Uruguay - Stocky Palm Trees (Plonkit)
description: Occasionally, you might see palm trees. These short and stocky species of palm tree are particularly common.

title: Uruguay - Cattle Farming (Plonkit)
description: Cattle farming is an important part of Uruguay’s agriculture. Cattle outnumber people four by one, so you will see a lot of them around in rural rounds.

title: Uruguay - Coverage Map (Plonkit)
description:
Coverage in Uruguay is somewhat limited. The densest coverage is in the south, in and around Montevideo. Outside of this area, most coverage is confined to yellow roads. This makes angle guessing a powerful tool to potentially get very close guesses.
For a zoomable overview of official street view coverage, see this site.

title: Uruguay - Elevation Map (Plonkit)
description:
Subtle differences in elevation can help when trying to region-guess Uruguay.
The highest hills are mostly concentrated around two areas:
- Near Minas, east of Montevideo.
- North of Tacuarembo, in the far north of the country.

title: Uruguay - Minas Hills (Plonkit)
description:
The landscape near the town of Minas is recognizable: some of the tallest hills in the country, with lots of exposed rocks, and often heavy bushland vegetation.
The image shown here is a fairly extreme example of this landscape, used for illustration purposes – usually it is more subtle. However, the exposed rock is always a good clue.

title: Uruguay - Northern Dark Hills (Plonkit)
description:
You can also find tall hills in the north of the country. These can be recognized by their noticeably darker soil. These hills also typically do not have the exposed rocks that are visible in the Minas hills.
The vegetation tends to be natural, and you will often see tree plantations.
This specific landscape tends to be most noticeable very close to the Brazil border, on Route 30 near Tranqueras.

title: Uruguay - Tree Plantations (Plonkit)
description:
Tree plantations are a defining feature of much of Uruguay’s countryside, but they are especially common in two areas in the north and northwest.
Note that the highest density of plantations is in these areas, but more isolated plantations can be found all over the country.

title: Uruguay - East Flatlands (Plonkit)
description: The region near Lagoa Mirim and the Brazil border in the southeast of the country is noticeably very flat, in contrast to the slight hills found in most of the rest of the country.

title: Uruguay - Divided Highways (Plonkit)
description:
There are only a couple of divided highways in Uruguay, all of which are close to Montevideo:
- Ruta 1 going west out of Montevideo, up until Colonia Valdense.
- Ruta IB going east out of Montevideo, up until Punta del Este.
- A short section of Ruta 5 going north out of Montevideo, up until Canelones.
The only exceptions to this are some divided avenues in urban areas, which should be easy to distinguish from actual highways.

title: Uruguay - Rocha Bins (Plonkit)
description: These bins with orange lids are specific to Rocha Department. However, you can still find these black bins in both the Rocha and Canelones Department.

title: Uruguay - Montevideo (Plonkit)
description:
Montevideo is by far the largest city in Uruguay. More than half the Uruguayan population lives within its metropolitan area.
Its relatively massive size may not always be as apparent in its suburbs. However, if you are in a densely populated, highly built-up area, consider guessing in downtown Montevideo, as there are very few places like that in other parts of Uruguay.

title: Uruguay - Punta del Este Pines (Plonkit)
description:
Punta del Este is a seaside resort town with a recognizable look. It is an affluent and touristic place with a developed downtown that consists of many tall, modern apartment buildings. Its main attraction is its large, sandy beach.
Further away from the downtown area, you will see less highrises, but still a lot of expensive-looking villa neighbourhoods. Here, you will often see distinctive tall pine trees.

title: Uruguay - Isla de Flores (Plonkit)
description: The small island of Isla de Flores is located off the coast of Montevideo. It has a trekker where you can see abandoned buildings, and usually also the lighthouse.

title: Uruguay - Cabo Polonio Car (Plonkit)
description:
This unique Google car is found in the coastal town of Cabo Polonio. It can be recognized by the orange strap on the left.
The coverage is an off-road trekker line on the map. The town that it drives through has a unique vibe, consisting of makeshift-looking shacks, scattered around the seaside landscape. In some of the coverage, the car drives on the beach.

title: Uruguay - Valle del Lunarejo Car (Plonkit)
description:
This unique Google car is found in the Valle del Lunarejo natural park, located west of the town of Tranqueras. The car has a white front and a curved black backside with a brown strap.
The coverage is an off-road trekker line on the map. The car drives on a small track through a grassy landscape.

title: Uruguay - Reddish Soil (Plonkit)
description: In many parts of Uruguay, you can find reddish soil. The tint can range from light pink (pictured here) to deep red.

title: Ecuador - Poles
description:
Most poles in Ecuador are round and made of concrete.
These poles are fairly generic and not all that useful to identify the country.

However, sometimes you will see another, more useful type of concrete pole: the ladder pole.
It has a lot of small indents – resembling the steps of a ladder.
Within Latin America, these poles are more or less unique to Ecuador.

*Brazilian waffle poles also have indents, but only a couple – as opposed to the large amount of indents that Ecuadorian ladder poles have.*

title: Ecuador - Roads
description: Concrete roads are relatively common in Ecuador.

title: Ecuador - Antennas
description:
The Google car antenna has two distinct variations:
- The “high” antenna (purple), where the wire around the antenna is entirely above the halfway line of the antenna.
- The “low” antenna (blue) where the majority of the wire is below the halfway point of the line, and there can be a small bit poking up at the very top.

This is most useful when you have the high antenna, since it will always be in the northern half of the country.

title: Ecuador - Volcanic Soil
description: **Volcanic soil** is mainly found between the Andes mountains

title: Ecuador - Amazon Landscape
description:
The **Amazon area** is very distinct.
It is **fairly flat**, and contains many of these trees with white bark (Cordia trichotoma), and oil palms.

*The vast majority of the coverage notably uses the rarer “high antenna”.*

description: The province of Esmeraldas can look similar to the Amazon region, but it is significantly hillier.
